title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text: 廣東鄉試錄嘉靖十九年
punctuated: 廣東鄉試錄，嘉靖十九年。
translation_en: Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination, the nineteenth year of the Jiajing reign (1540).

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
時維三年大比之期巡按監
察御史洪垣遵
制聘取繼皐與教諭劉康為考試
官教諭蕭彥陳光明甘汝孚
徐衍劉去矜王佩為同考試
官至期暨提調布政使楊銓
===
參議汪大受監試按察使歐
陽席僉事李文鳳入院飭事
合提學僉事吳鵬所簡士而
三試之旣畢繼皐當叙諸文
首夫文以闡道道以顯文道
者氣之中正者也文者道之
顯設者也文王之文純亦不
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

時維三年大比之期，巡按監察御史洪垣遵制，聘取繼皐與教諭劉康為考試官，教諭蕭彥、陳光明、甘汝孚、徐衍、劉去矜、王佩為同考試官。至期，暨提調布政使楊銓、參議汪大受，監試按察使歐陽席、僉事李文鳳入院飭事，合提學僉事吳鵬所簡士而三試之。旣畢，繼皐當叙諸文首。

夫文以闡道，道以顯文。道者，氣之中正者也；文者，道之顯設者也。文王之文，純亦不
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

It was the appointed time for the triennial examination. In obedience to the imperial decree, Hong Yuan, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, engaged me, Jigao, and Liu Kang, a School Instructor, as Examiners, and the School Instructors Xiao Yan, Chen Guangming, Gan Rufu, Xu Yan, Liu Qujin, and Wang Pei as Associate Examiners. When the appointed time arrived, we entered the examination compound to put affairs in order together with the Proctors—Provincial Administration Commissioner Yang Quan and Administrative Assistant Commissioner Wang Dashou—and the examination monitors—Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Ouyang Xi and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Li Wenfeng. We assembled the candidates selected by Wu Peng, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, and examined them in three sessions. Upon completion, it fell to me, Jigao, to write a preface to stand at the head of the essays.

Writing elucidates the Way, and the Way lends distinction to writing. The Way is that which is balanced and upright in vital energy; writing is the manifest expression of the Way. King Wen’s cultural virtue was pure and likewise did not …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
已夫子之文章性與天道者
也故文之高下類於風氣士
習焉符之氣之漓者其文散
氣之昌者其文華氣之朴者
其文簡氣之雄者其文確氣
之純者其文雅嶺南之風氣
其殆近昌以朴以雄不懈而
===
進於純者乎故其爲文爲直
方爲果毅直方果毅陽明之
象其變而至於純也爲近夫
純也者道也所謂氣之中正
者也故曰一陰一陽之謂道
其爲氣也近華而不豔近朴
而不野近確而不固苟損益
punctuated: 已。夫子之文章，性與天道者也。故文之高下，類於風氣，士習焉符之。氣之漓者，其文散；氣之昌者，其文華；氣之朴者，其文簡；氣之雄者，其文確；氣之純者，其文雅。嶺南之風氣，其殆近昌以朴以雄，不懈而進於純者乎？故其爲文，爲直方，爲果毅。直方果毅，陽明之象，其變而至於純也爲近。夫純也者，道也，所謂氣之中正者也。故曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」其爲氣也，近華而不豔，近朴而不野，近確而不固。苟損益
translation_en: …never ceases. The Master's literary expression embodies human nature and the Way of Heaven. Thus the higher and lower qualities of writing correspond to prevailing influences, and the habits of scholars accord with them [?]. When vital energy (qi) is diluted, writing is diffuse; when it flourishes, writing is splendid; when it is unadorned, writing is simple; when it is vigorous, writing is firm; when it is pure, writing is refined. Might the prevailing influences of Lingnan approach flourishing abundance, simplicity, and vigor, advancing unremittingly toward purity? Thus its writing is upright and square, resolute and steadfast. Uprightness, squareness, resolution, and steadfastness manifest the brightness of yang; from these, transformation toward purity is close at hand. Purity is the Way: what is called the balance and rectitude of vital energy. Hence it is said: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” In its vital energy, it approaches splendor without being gaudy, simplicity without being uncouth, and firmness without being rigid. If one were to diminish or augment…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之過與不及文之以道德化
而裁之存乎其人焉爾故曰
學以變化氣質氣質變化則
盛德日新而風氣不與焉矣
是故一變而爲唐張文獻公
九齡以功業著焉再變而爲
宋崔清獻公與之以節行著
===
焉功業清節以漸而歸之道
者蓋亦其風氣與時偕行也
夫今則又再變矣自宋而來
將五百歲
聖人敎化之盛氣運之隆厚蘊而
宏發之又豈無道德之士出
乎其間以當斯選者乎未可
punctuated: 之過與不及，文之以道德，化而裁之，存乎其人焉爾。故曰：「學以變化氣質。」氣質變化，則盛德日新，而風氣不與焉矣。是故一變而爲唐張文獻公九齡，以功業著焉；再變而爲宋崔清獻公與之，以節行著焉。功業清節，以漸而歸之道者，蓋亦其風氣與時偕行也夫！今則又再變矣。自宋而來，將五百歲，聖人敎化之盛，氣運之隆，厚蘊而宏發之，又豈無道德之士出乎其間，以當斯選者乎？未可
translation_en: …its excesses and deficiencies, embellishing it with moral virtue: its transformation and proper regulation depend upon the individual alone. Thus it is said, “Learning serves to transform one’s native endowment.” Once that endowment is transformed, abundant virtue is renewed daily, and the prevailing local influences no longer have a part in it. Thus, with one transformation there emerged Zhang Jiuling of the Tang, posthumously titled Duke Wenxian, who became distinguished for his achievements; with a further transformation there emerged Cui Yuzhi of the Song, posthumously titled Duke Qingxian, who became distinguished for his integrity and conduct. That achievement and unsullied integrity gradually came to accord with the Way was surely also a matter of the local ethos advancing with the times! Now it has undergone yet another transformation. Nearly five hundred years have passed since the Song. With the flourishing of the sage ruler’s civilizing instruction and the fullness of the age’s vital forces, deeply accumulated and grandly expressed, could there fail to emerge among us men of moral virtue worthy of selection in this examination? It cannot yet be…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知也今之觀道德之與功業
清節也孰觀哉觀其文焉言
焉已爾文有所言焉而所不
言者見焉是故君子觀言則
知默矣觀文則知質矣觀顯
則知隱矣觀動則知靜矣語
默文質隱顯動靜不失其正
===
焉而道德存乎其間矣故曰
觀今之功業清節之與道德
也必於文焉言焉觀之觀今
之文與言而其道德之蘊豈
無發越於其間而不可掩者
乎夫固未可知也顧諸生所
自期待何如耳期功業者必
punctuated: 知也。今之觀道德之與功業、清節也，孰觀哉？觀其文焉、言焉已爾。文有所言焉，而所不言者見焉。是故君子觀言則知默矣，觀文則知質矣，觀顯則知隱矣，觀動則知靜矣。語默、文質、隱顯、動靜，不失其正焉，而道德存乎其間矣。故曰：觀今之功業、清節之與道德也，必於文焉、言焉觀之。觀今之文與言，而其道德之蘊，豈無發越於其間而不可掩者乎？夫固未可知也，顧諸生所自期待何如耳。期功業者必
translation_en: …be known. In examining moral virtue alongside meritorious achievement and unblemished integrity today, what should one examine? Only a person's writings and words. Writings express certain things, yet through them what is left unsaid becomes apparent. Thus, by examining speech, the gentleman understands silence; by examining literary expression, he understands inner substance; by examining what is manifest, he understands what is hidden; and by examining activity, he understands stillness. When speech and silence, literary expression and inner substance, the hidden and the manifest, activity and stillness all maintain their proper balance, moral virtue resides among them. Thus I say: to examine meritorious achievement and unblemished integrity alongside moral virtue today, one must examine writings and words. When we examine the writings and words of today, might there not be stores of moral virtue that shine forth within them and cannot be concealed? This, indeed, cannot yet be known; it depends only on what you students expect of yourselves. Those who aspire to meritorious achievement will surely…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
止於功業期清節者必止於
清節正必之心累之也故志
學于道德則不期功業清節
而功業清節在其中矣是故
其才可以致相業矣又必觀
其有避相之心然後可焉其
志能以避相矣又必觀其有
===
聖賢之學然後可焉聖賢之
學文王之純亦不已夫子之
性與天道是也諸生皆誦法
文武孔子其必有爲聖賢之
志者乎否則雖博今古工文
辭篤行義君子以爲猶末學
也嘗觀自嶺以南多知學之
punctuated: 止於功業，期清節者必止於清節，正必之心累之也。故志學于道德，則不期功業清節，而功業清節在其中矣。是故其才可以致相業矣，又必觀其有避相之心，然後可焉；其志能以避相矣，又必觀其有聖賢之學，然後可焉。聖賢之學，文王之純亦不已，夫子之性與天道是也。諸生皆誦法文武孔子，其必有爲聖賢之志者乎？否則，雖博今古，工文辭，篤行義，君子以爲猶末學也。嘗觀自嶺以南，多知學之
translation_en: …stop at accomplishments; those who aspire to unsullied integrity will necessarily stop at unsullied integrity. It is precisely their insistence on a predetermined end that encumbers them. Thus, if one sets one's mind on studying the Way and virtue, one does not aim specifically at accomplishments or unsullied integrity, yet both are contained therein. Accordingly, even when someone's talents equip him to achieve the work of a grand councilor, one must also see whether he has the disposition to shun that office before approving him. Even when his resolve enables him to shun that office, one must also see whether he possesses the learning of the sages and worthies before approving him. The learning of the sages and worthies is exemplified by King Wen's unceasing purity and by the Master's teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven. You students all recite the teachings of, and take as your models, Kings Wen and Wu and Confucius. Surely you aspire to become sages and worthies? Otherwise, even if you are broadly versed in past and present, skilled in literary expression, and steadfast in righteous conduct, the gentleman regards this as still only peripheral learning. I have observed that south of the mountain ranges there are many who understand learning…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
士其所漸磨而造詣又若大
有所受者豈盡其風聲氣習
之所入乎哉今之有司或徒
以文觀之期以功業清節而
止焉則又何以仰副
聖君賢相之責望得夫德行道藝
之士以共成正大光明之業
===
也哉程子曰言學以道爲至
言人以聖爲至諸子初服自
待庶其在斯乎庶其在斯乎
茲舉也提督軍務兵部左侍
郎兼都御史蔡經都御史李
顯總兵官安遠侯柳珣豫宏
規制士庶聿興而協供庶務
punctuated:
士，其所漸磨而造詣，又若大有所受者，豈盡其風聲氣習之所入乎哉？今之有司，或徒以文觀之，期以功業清節而止焉，則又何以仰副聖君賢相之責望，得夫德行道藝之士，以共成正大光明之業也哉？程子曰：「言學以道爲至，言人以聖爲至。」諸子初服自待，庶其在斯乎！庶其在斯乎！
茲舉也，提督軍務兵部左侍郎兼都御史蔡經、都御史李顯、總兵官安遠侯柳珣，豫宏規制，士庶聿興，而協供庶務，
translation_en:
…men whose gradual cultivation and attainments suggest that they have received substantial instruction. Could these derive entirely from the influence of local reputation, disposition, and customary practice? If those now in authority judge them solely by their writing and expect no more than meritorious service and incorruptible conduct, how can they fulfill the expectations of our sagely ruler and worthy ministers, obtaining men of virtuous conduct and accomplishment in the Way and the arts, with whom to achieve an enterprise of uprightness and manifest integrity? Master Cheng said: “In speaking of learning, the Way is the highest attainment; in speaking of human beings, sagehood is the highest attainment.” As you gentlemen embark upon your vocation, may this be what you expect of yourselves! May this be what you expect of yourselves!
For this examination, Cai Jing, Superintendent of Military Affairs and Left Vice Minister of War concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief; Li Xian, Censor-in-Chief; and Liu Xun, Regional Commander and Marquis of Anyuan, made extensive arrangements beforehand, and scholars and commoners alike rose to the undertaking. As for those who cooperated in attending to its various affairs, …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則參政蕭晚周禥參議宋茂
熙周延副使陳大珊陳嘉謀
涂捷韓楷僉事趙維雍瀾林
希元劉廷範都指揮董廷玉
楊忻參將高誼程鑒各以其
職懋昭厥成蓋愼之也是故
文事章矣總督軍務總兵官
===
咸寧侯仇鸞參贊軍務兵部
尚書兼都察院右都御史毛
伯溫則又奉
命節鎮嶺南誕示威信以昭
文德而有懷之士勃勃然動忠悃
之思是故武事式矣文武合
一則道德存而儒者之功用
punctuated:
則參政蕭晚、周禥，參議宋茂熙、周延，副使陳大珊、陳嘉謀、涂捷、韓楷，僉事趙維、雍瀾、林希元、劉廷範，都指揮董廷玉、楊忻，參將高誼、程鑒，各以其職懋昭厥成，蓋愼之也。是故文事章矣。
總督軍務總兵官咸寧侯仇鸞、參贊軍務兵部尚書兼都察院右都御史毛伯溫，則又奉命節鎮嶺南，誕示威信，以昭文德，而有懷之士勃勃然動忠悃之思。是故武事式矣。文武合一，則道德存而儒者之功用
translation_en:
…As for those who cooperated in providing for the various tasks, Administration Vice Commissioners Xiao Wan and Zhou Qi; Administration Assistant Commissioners Song Maoxi and Zhou Yan; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Dashan, Chen Jiamou, Tu Jie, and Han Kai; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhao Wei, Yong Lan, Lin Xiyuan, and Liu Tingfan; Regional Military Commissioners Dong Tingyu and Yang Xin; and Assistant Regional Commanders Gao Yi and Cheng Jian each diligently fulfilled his office to bring this undertaking to a distinguished completion. Such was the care they devoted to it. Thus civil affairs flourished.
Qiu Luan, Marquis of Xianning, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs and Regional Commander, and Mao Bowen, Minister of War concurrently serving as Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and Counselor for Military Affairs, moreover received imperial orders to exercise command in Lingnan. They grandly displayed their authority and trustworthiness, thereby making manifest civil virtue, while men of aspiration were stirred with vigorous feelings of heartfelt loyalty. Thus military affairs were duly ordered. When civil and military affairs are united, the Way and its virtue endure, and the practical accomplishments of Confucian scholars …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
全諸士子逢茲
盛典其將有以自奮也夫
江西九江府儒學教授林繼
皐謹序
punctuated:
全。諸士子逢茲盛典，其將有以自奮也夫！
江西九江府儒學教授林繼皐謹序。
translation_en:
…is complete. Encountering this grand occasion, surely the candidates will find in it the means to spur themselves onward!
Lin Jigao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史洪垣〔峻之直隸婺源縣人壬辰進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使楊銓〔仲衡江西豐城縣人甲戌進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司右參議汪大受〔叔可直隸婺源縣人己丑進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使歐陽席〔崇珍江西泰和縣人戊辰進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事李文鳳〔廷儀廣西慶遠衛人壬辰進士〕
===
考試官
江西九江府儒學教授林繼皐〔德謨福建閩縣人己丑進士〕
河南汝寧府西平縣儒學教諭劉康〔汝和江西安福縣人甲午貢士〕
同考試官
直隸安慶府宿松縣儒學教諭蕭彥〔其士江西吉水縣人辛卯貢士〕
浙江台州府太平縣儒學教諭陳光明〔道昭福建莆田縣人乙酉貢士〕
江西九江府德安縣儒學教諭甘汝孚〔以德廣西桂平縣人丙子貢士〕
浙江台州府黃巖縣儒學教諭徐衍〔宗易福建龍溪縣人戊子貢士〕
湖廣鄖陽府鄖西縣儒學教諭劉去矜〔師禹四川富順縣人戊子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史洪垣〔峻之，直隸婺源縣人，壬辰進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使楊銓〔仲衡，江西豐城縣人，甲戌進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司右參議汪大受〔叔可，直隸婺源縣人，己丑進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使歐陽席〔崇珍，江西泰和縣人，戊辰進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司僉事李文鳳〔廷儀，廣西慶遠衛人，壬辰進士〕。

考試官：
江西九江府儒學教授林繼皐〔德謨，福建閩縣人，己丑進士〕。
河南汝寧府西平縣儒學教諭劉康〔汝和，江西安福縣人，甲午貢士〕。

同考試官：
直隸安慶府宿松縣儒學教諭蕭彥〔其士，江西吉水縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
浙江台州府太平縣儒學教諭陳光明〔道昭，福建莆田縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
江西九江府德安縣儒學教諭甘汝孚〔以德，廣西桂平縣人，丙子貢士〕。
浙江台州府黃巖縣儒學教諭徐衍〔宗易，福建龍溪縣人，戊子貢士〕。
湖廣鄖陽府鄖西縣儒學教諭劉去矜〔師禹，四川富順縣人，戊子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, the nineteenth year of Jiajing (1540).

Supervising Official:
Hong Yuan, Regional Inspecting Censor for Guangdong, had the courtesy name Junzhi and was a native of Wuyuan County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the renchen year.

Proctors:
Yang Quan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Zhongheng and was a native of Fengcheng County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Wang Dashou, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Shuke and was a native of Wuyuan County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.

Examination Overseers:

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子無終食之間違仁造次必於是顛沛
必於是
温故而知新敦厚以崇禮
聖人旣竭目力焉繼之以規矩準繩以爲
方員平直不可勝用也旣竭耳力焉繼
之以六律正五音不可勝用也旣竭心
思焉繼之以不忍人之政而仁覆天下
===
矣
易
臨剛浸而長說而順剛中而應大亨以正
天之道也
王假有廟王乃在中也
夫易廣矣大矣以言乎遠則不禦以言乎
邇則靜而正以言乎天地之間則備矣
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉
夫坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

君子無終食之間違仁，造次必於是，顛沛必於是。

温故而知新，敦厚以崇禮。

聖人旣竭目力焉，繼之以規矩準繩，以爲方員平直，不可勝用也；旣竭耳力焉，繼之以六律，正五音，不可勝用也；旣竭心思焉，繼之以不忍人之政，而仁覆天下矣。

易

臨，剛浸而長，說而順，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之道也。

王假有廟，王乃在中也。

夫易，廣矣大矣！以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正；以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉；夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The gentleman does not depart from benevolence even for the time it takes to eat a meal. Even in haste he abides by it; even in adversity he abides by it.

He reviews the old to understand the new, and cultivates generosity and sincerity to honor ritual propriety.

Having exerted their powers of sight to the utmost, the sages supplemented them with compasses, squares, levels, and marking cords to produce squares, circles, level surfaces, and straight lines; their uses are inexhaustible. Having exerted their powers of hearing to the utmost, they supplemented them with the six pitch standards to set the five notes aright; their uses are inexhaustible. Having exerted their powers of thought to the utmost, they supplemented them with government that could not bear to see others suffer, and benevolence spread over all under Heaven.

Book of Changes

In Lin (Approach), the firm gradually advances and grows. Joyous and yielding, the firm occupies the central position and finds a response. Great success comes through correctness: this is the Way of Heaven.

“The king approaches the ancestral temple”: the king is indeed in the center.

How broad and great is the Book of Changes! Speaking of what is distant, it has no bounds; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct; speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it embraces everything. Qian (the Creative), when still, is concentrated; when moving, it proceeds directly. Thus it generates greatness. Kun (the Receptive), when still, is closed; when moving, it opens. Thus it generates breadth.

安汝止惟幾惟康
惟木從繩則正后從諫則聖后克聖臣不
命其承疇敢不祗若王之休命
一曰正直二曰剛克三曰柔克
黍稷非馨明德惟馨
詩
春日載陽有鳴倉庚女執懿筐遵彼微行
===
爰求柔桑春日遲遲采蘩祁祁
物其多矣維其嘉矣物其旨矣維其偕矣
物其有矣維其時矣
泂酌彼行潦挹彼注茲可以餴饎豈弟君
子民之父母泂酌彼行潦挹彼注茲可
以濯罍豈弟君子民之攸歸泂酌彼行
潦挹彼注茲可以濯漑豈弟君子民之
攸墍
綏我眉壽介以繁祉旣右烈考亦右文母
punctuated:
君子脩此三者，故全也。

書
安汝止，惟幾惟康。
惟木從繩則正，后從諫則聖。后克聖，臣不命其承，疇敢不祗若王之休命？
一曰正直，二曰剛克，三曰柔克。
黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。

詩
春日載陽，有鳴倉庚。女執懿筐，遵彼微行，爰求柔桑。春日遲遲，采蘩祁祁。
物其多矣，維其嘉矣！物其旨矣，維其偕矣！物其有矣，維其時矣！
泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以餴饎。豈弟君子，民之父母。泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以濯罍。豈弟君子，民之攸歸。泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以濯漑。豈弟君子，民之攸墍。
綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。旣右烈考，亦右文母。
translation_en:
The gentleman cultivates these three things and thus achieves completeness.

Book of Documents (Shu)

Be secure in where you take your stand; attend to the first stirrings of events and to peace.

Wood that follows the marking cord becomes straight; a sovereign who follows remonstrance becomes sage. If the sovereign can become sage, his ministers will carry out his wishes without being commanded. Who would dare not reverently obey the king’s excellent commands?

The first is uprightness; the second, mastery through firmness; the third, mastery through gentleness.

It is not the millet offerings that are fragrant; it is luminous virtue that is fragrant.

Book of Odes (Shi)

The spring days grow warm; the orioles sing. A girl carries a fine basket and follows that narrow path, seeking tender mulberry leaves. The spring days lengthen; those gathering white southernwood come in crowds.

How abundant the provisions, and how fine! How delicious the provisions, and how complete! How plentiful the provisions, and how timely!

Draw that standing rainwater from afar; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used to steam grain for food. The gracious and kindly lord is the father and mother of the people. Draw that standing rainwater from afar; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used to wash wine jars. The gracious and kindly lord is the one to whom the people turn. Draw that standing rainwater from afar; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used for washing and rinsing. The gracious and kindly lord is the one with whom the people find repose.

Grant me long life, and aid me with abundant blessings. I have honored my illustrious departed father and also my accomplished mother.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋八月蔡季自陳歸于蔡〔桓公十有七年〕
春王正月宋公曹伯衞人邾人伐齊狄
救齊〔僖公十有八年〕春晉侯侵曹晉侯
伐衞〔僖公二十有八年〕楚子陳侯隨侯
許男圍蔡〔哀公元年〕
春公觀魚于棠〔隱公五年〕夏五月宋人及
楚人平〔宣公十有五年〕
叔孫舍至自晉〔昭公二十有四年〕
===
禮記
刑者侀也侀者成也一成而不可變故君
子盡心焉
禮之以少爲貴者以其内心也德産之致
也精微觀天下之物無可以稱其德者
如此則得不以少爲貴乎是故君子愼
其獨也
禮樂皆得謂之有德德者得也
是故其德盛者其志厚其志厚者其義章
punctuated:
春秋

秋八月，蔡季自陳歸于蔡。〔桓公十有七年〕
春王正月，宋公、曹伯、衞人、邾人伐齊。狄救齊。〔僖公十有八年〕春，晉侯侵曹。晉侯伐衞。〔僖公二十有八年〕楚子、陳侯、隨侯、許男圍蔡。〔哀公元年〕
春，公觀魚于棠。〔隱公五年〕夏五月，宋人及楚人平。〔宣公十有五年〕
叔孫舍至自晉。〔昭公二十有四年〕

禮記

刑者，侀也；侀者，成也。一成而不可變，故君子盡心焉。

禮之以少爲貴者，以其内心也。德産之致也精微，觀天下之物，無可以稱其德者。如此，則得不以少爲貴乎？是故君子愼其獨也。

禮樂皆得，謂之有德。德者，得也。

是故其德盛者，其志厚；其志厚者，其義章。
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, in the eighth month, Ji of Cai returned to Cai from Chen. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Huan〕
In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Cao, and men of Wei and Zhu attacked Qi. The Di came to Qi’s aid. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xi〕 In spring, the Marquis of Jin invaded Cao. The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕 The Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Sui, and the Baron of Xu besieged Cai. 〔First year of Duke Ai〕
In spring, the duke watched fishing at Tang. 〔Fifth year of Duke Yin〕 In summer, in the fifth month, the men of Song and the men of Chu made peace. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan〕
Shusun She arrived back from Jin. 〔Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao〕

Book of Rites

Punishment (xing 刑) means giving form (xing 侀); giving form means completing. Once completed, it cannot be changed. Thus the gentleman devotes his utmost care to it.

The reason ritual esteems small quantities is that it values the inner heart. What virtue brings forth is, at its utmost, exquisitely subtle; among all the things under Heaven, none can adequately match that virtue. This being so, how could small quantities fail to be esteemed? Thus the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.

To attain both ritual and music is called possessing virtue. Virtue (de 德) means attainment (de 得).

Thus, those whose virtue is abundant have profound purpose; those whose purpose is profound manifest righteousness…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其義章者其祭也敬祭敬則竟內之子
孫莫敢不敬矣
第貳場
論
孔子之謂集大成
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢以卓茂為太傅封褒德侯詔〔建武元年〕
擬唐以陸贄為翰林學士誥〔建中四年〕
擬宋廣州教授林勲上本政書表〔建炎三年〕
===

舉用有過官吏
檢踏災傷田糧
禁止師巫邪術
邊境申索軍需
軍民約會詞訟
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問三代而下惟漢得天下為正我
punctuated:
其義章者，其祭也敬；祭敬，則竟內之子孫莫敢不敬矣。

第貳場
論
孔子之謂集大成。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢以卓茂為太傅、封褒德侯詔〔建武元年〕。
擬唐以陸贄為翰林學士誥〔建中四年〕。
擬宋廣州教授林勲上本政書表〔建炎三年〕。

判語〔五條〕
舉用有過官吏。
檢踏災傷田糧。
禁止師巫邪術。
邊境申索軍需。
軍民約會詞訟。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：三代而下，惟漢得天下為正，我
translation_en:
…Those whose righteousness is manifest are reverent in their sacrifices. When sacrifices are performed reverently, none of the sons and grandsons within the territory dare fail to be reverent.

Second Session
Discourse
Confucius is said to have brought together the great accomplishments of the sages.

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials〔One question from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor appointing Zhuo Mao Grand Mentor and enfeoffing him as Marquis of Commended Virtue.〔First year of Jianwu〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of the Tang emperor appointing Lu Zhi Hanlin Academician.〔Fourth year of Jianzhong〕
Compose a memorial in the voice of Lin Xun, Professor of the Guangzhou prefectural school under the Song, submitting his Book on the Fundamentals of Government (Ben zheng shu).〔Third year of Jianyan〕

Legal Judgments〔Five items〕
Recommending and employing officials and clerks with prior offenses.
Inspecting fields damaged by disasters and assessing their grain-tax liabilities.
Prohibiting the heterodox arts of ritual masters and spirit mediums.
Requests from the frontier for military supplies.
Arranging joint hearings of lawsuits involving military personnel and civilians.

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕
Question: Since the Three Dynasties, only the Han gained All under Heaven legitimately. Our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明亦然昔班彪稱漢高帝之興有五
本朝學士宋濂稱我
太祖高皇帝之興有六其詳可得聞與
本朝得天下雖同於漢然漢得天下於亡秦
其時去古未遠先王紀綱制度猶有存
者高帝不能收拾補綴使先王典禮旣
亡而復存僅爲一時苟簡之治而已我
太祖高皇帝得天下於亡秦千載之後乃能法
古爲治使
===
一代典章文物煥然二帝三王之盛則其
神謨聖見度越漢高有前人之所未言者爾諸
生能詳言之與三代而下繼體之君表
章六經者或好大喜功致海內之虛耗
收復淮蔡者或器小易盈致美業之弗
終銳志更法者或委用非人釀天下之
禍亂未有卓然足稱中興之盛者肆我
皇上龍飛藩邸運際昌期
文武神聖全稟於天河清慶雲洊薦符瑞
punctuated: 明亦然。昔班彪稱漢高帝之興有五，本朝學士宋濂稱我太祖高皇帝之興有六，其詳可得聞與？本朝得天下雖同於漢，然漢得天下於亡秦，其時去古未遠，先王紀綱制度猶有存者。高帝不能收拾補綴，使先王典禮旣亡而復存，僅爲一時苟簡之治而已。我太祖高皇帝得天下於亡秦千載之後，乃能法古爲治，使一代典章文物煥然，二帝三王之盛。則其神謨聖見度越漢高，有前人之所未言者，爾諸生能詳言之與？三代而下，繼體之君表章六經者，或好大喜功，致海內之虛耗；收復淮蔡者，或器小易盈，致美業之弗終；銳志更法者，或委用非人，釀天下之禍亂。未有卓然足稱中興之盛者。肆我皇上龍飛藩邸，運際昌期，文武神聖，全稟於天，河清慶雲，洊薦符瑞。
translation_en:
…the same is true of our Ming dynasty. In former times, Ban Biao stated that there were five factors behind the rise of Emperor Gao of Han; Song Lian, an Academician of our dynasty, stated that there were six behind the rise of our Emperor Taizu Gao. May we hear the details? Although our dynasty acquired All under Heaven as the Han did, the Han acquired it upon the fall of Qin. That age was not far removed from antiquity, and some of the guiding principles and institutions of the former kings still survived. Emperor Gao could not gather together and restore these remnants, bringing back into existence the former kings’ institutions and rites once they had been lost. His rule amounted merely to makeshift arrangements for the moment. Our Emperor Taizu Gao acquired All under Heaven more than a thousand years after the fall of Qin, yet was able to model his government on antiquity, making the statutes, institutions, and cultural achievements of his dynasty shine with the splendor of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Thus his divine plans and sagely insight surpassed those of Emperor Gao of Han in ways that earlier writers have not discussed. Can you students explain these in detail?

Since the Three Dynasties, among rulers who succeeded to an established throne, one who honored and promoted the Six Classics nevertheless delighted in grand undertakings and military achievements, bringing depletion upon the realm; one who recovered Huai and Cai nevertheless possessed limited capacity and was easily satisfied, leaving his fine achievements unfinished; and one determined to reform the laws nevertheless entrusted affairs to unsuitable men, thereby breeding calamity and disorder throughout All under Heaven. None stood out sufficiently to merit being called a splendid restorer of his dynasty. Now our Emperor has risen like a dragon from his princely residence, his destiny coinciding with an age of flourishing fortune. His civil and martial virtues, his divine wisdom and sageliness, are all endowed by Heaven. The Yellow River has run clear, and auspicious clouds have appeared, repeatedly presenting favorable omens…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
臨御以來孜孜求治其所以經綸大業巍巍乎
足稱中興之盛有以度越漢唐宋之君
者有五爾諸生亦曾聞而誦之乎夫陶
鎔菁莪樸棫之化而鋪張敷揚
一代之盛亦臣子事也試一一為我言之
問移風易俗莫善於禮禮樂不興則刑罰
不中奢淫日蕩獄訟繁興是禮者天地
之紀而民之所以生者也今之牧民者
果能建萬世之長策舉
===
明主於三代之隆而不徒區區簿書聽訟如王
吉之言者乎夫外庭告冠聞者却立父
在學禮君子譏之此在賢者且然則古
禮之難復久矣然唐之牧守乃能獨行
於一郡之間至有百姓聞之而泣下者
又安在其為不可乎說者謂夫子作春
秋不存禮樂之制有志之士每動名實
之思故有請擇司馬光冠婚喪祭之儀
簡而易行布之民間者有請准令式行
punctuated:
臨御以來，孜孜求治，其所以經綸大業，巍巍乎足稱中興之盛，有以度越漢唐宋之君者有五。爾諸生亦曾聞而誦之乎？夫陶鎔菁莪樸棫之化，而鋪張敷揚一代之盛，亦臣子事也。試一一為我言之。
問：移風易俗，莫善於禮。禮樂不興，則刑罰不中。奢淫日蕩，獄訟繁興，是禮者天地之紀，而民之所以生者也。今之牧民者，果能建萬世之長策，舉明主於三代之隆，而不徒區區簿書聽訟，如王吉之言者乎？夫外庭告冠，聞者却立；父在學禮，君子譏之。此在賢者且然，則古禮之難復久矣。然唐之牧守，乃能獨行於一郡之間，至有百姓聞之而泣下者，又安在其為不可乎？說者謂夫子作春秋，不存禮樂之制。有志之士，每動名實之思，故有請擇司馬光冠婚喪祭之儀，簡而易行，布之民間者；有請准令式行
translation_en:
…Since ascending the throne, he has worked tirelessly to secure good government. In his ordering of the great affairs of state, five achievements are so exalted as to merit the designation of a flourishing restoration and to surpass those of the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song. Have you students also heard of and recounted them? To cultivate men through the transforming influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing e) and “Oak and Thorn” (Pu yu), and to proclaim and expound the glories of a dynasty, are also duties of a subject. Set these forth for me, one by one.
Question: Nothing excels ritual in transforming prevailing practices and changing customs. If ritual and music do not flourish, punishments will not fit the offenses. Extravagance and licentiousness grow more unrestrained each day, and lawsuits proliferate. Thus ritual is the ordering principle of Heaven and Earth and that by which the people sustain their lives. Can those who govern the people today truly establish an enduring policy for ten thousand generations and raise their enlightened sovereign to the heights of the Three Dynasties, rather than merely busy themselves with registers, documents, and hearing lawsuits, as Wang Ji said? When a capping ceremony was announced in the outer court, those who heard stepped back; when someone studied ritual while his father was alive, gentlemen criticized him. If even worthy men behaved thus, the difficulty of restoring ancient ritual is indeed longstanding. Yet a local governor under the Tang was able to put it into practice within a single prefecture, to the point that some commoners shed tears on hearing of it. How, then, can it be deemed impossible? Commentators say that when the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he did not preserve the institutions of ritual and music. Men of aspiration have often been moved to reflect upon names and realities. Thus some proposed selecting from Sima Guang’s ceremonies for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice those that were simple and easy to perform, and disseminating them among the people; others proposed following the ordinances and prescribed forms in carrying out…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮稍加獎勸以示風俗者有乞令教授
有出身官旦望就學講習新禮而督察
之者有欲請復古三科以興實學者使
今日酌而行之其致治成效必有可觀
然當時既能言之能行之而終不可以
復純王之治其弊又安在乎程子曰治
天下以正風俗得賢才為本諸士子以
賢才自負行當有風俗之責者如有用
爾其將何以副之
===
問出處去就乃士人出門第一步古先聖
賢不少放過學者所宜精察而不可苟
焉者也今以古人可議之迹與諸生論
之昔武王伐紂夷齊隱迹於首陽山遂
餓而死微子乃抱祭器歸周箕子又就
為之陳洪範焉夫異姓之臣則力全君
臣之義同姓之臣乃忘宗國以事之說
者以存祀傳道為言是矣然以武周之
聖其道未嘗不在殷之宗祀周家必無
punctuated:
禮，稍加獎勸，以示風俗者；有乞令教授、有出身官旦望就學講習新禮而督察之者；有欲請復古三科以興實學者。使今日酌而行之，其致治成效必有可觀。然當時既能言之，能行之，而終不可以復純王之治，其弊又安在乎？程子曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才為本。」諸士子以賢才自負，行當有風俗之責者，如有用爾，其將何以副之？

問：出處去就，乃士人出門第一步，古先聖賢不少放過，學者所宜精察而不可苟焉者也。今以古人可議之迹與諸生論之。昔武王伐紂，夷齊隱迹於首陽山，遂餓而死；微子乃抱祭器歸周，箕子又就為之陳洪範焉。夫異姓之臣，則力全君臣之義；同姓之臣，乃忘宗國以事之。說者以存祀傳道為言，是矣。然以武周之聖，其道未嘗不在；殷之宗祀，周家必無
translation_en:
…rites, and give some encouragement and rewards to guide popular customs; others petitioned that the Prefectural School Instructors and officials holding examination qualifications should attend the schools on the new- and full-moon days [?] to expound and study the new rites and supervise their observance; still others wished to request the restoration of the ancient three categories of selection to promote substantive learning. If these proposals were weighed and implemented today, they would surely produce notable results in achieving good government. Yet, although people at that time could both articulate and implement them, they ultimately could not restore the unalloyed government of the sage kings. Where, then, did the fault lie? Master Cheng said: “Governing the realm rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent.” You candidates pride yourselves on being worthy talents and will soon bear responsibility for popular customs. If someone were to employ you, how would you meet that expectation?

Question: Whether to enter office or remain in retirement, to withdraw or accept appointment, is the very first step a scholar takes upon going out into the world. The sages and worthies of antiquity never treated it lightly. It is something students must examine closely and cannot approach carelessly. Let us now discuss with you certain debatable actions of the ancients. When King Wu attacked Zhou 紂, Boyi and Shuqi withdrew to Mount Shouyang and eventually starved to death. Weizi, however, carried the sacrificial vessels with him and submitted to Zhou 周, while Jizi went so far as to expound the Great Plan (Hongfan) for its ruler. Thus, ministers of a different surname strove to preserve intact the obligations between ruler and minister, while ministers of the ruling lineage forgot their ancestral state and served its conqueror. Commentators explain this in terms of preserving ancestral sacrifices and transmitting the Way. That is sound. Yet, given the sageliness of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, the Way was never absent; as for the ancestral sacrifices of Yin, the house of Zhou would surely never…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
絕之之理豈待抱祭器歸周而后存乎
王莽易漢為新龔勝不食就斃武后易
唐為周狄仁傑乃俯首以事之說者又
謂仁傑之仕周將以為唐也然君子寧
功業之不建而不失身於匪人况中宗
之不足扶植武三思輩之不能有成不
待智者而后知仁傑之賢乃不知此何
與至若元以夷狄入主中國許衡應聘
而為臣劉因則屢聘之而不起或謂劉
===
高於許然愚觀渡江之賦乃快趙宋之
亡似非夷元不仕者許之仕元或謂將
變夷為華然王猛之仕秦能以東晉正
朔勸苻堅許衡之仕元乃不能以宋中
國勸世祖何與他如漢唐諸賢有以三
顧聘之而出以三公召之而不出有三
上宰相書而求出有下詔徵之而不出
者先儒論之詳矣然或謂求出者未必
為非不出者未必為正出者未必為時
punctuated: 絕之之理，豈待抱祭器歸周而后存乎？王莽易漢為新，龔勝不食就斃；武后易唐為周，狄仁傑乃俯首以事之。說者又謂仁傑之仕周，將以為唐也。然君子寧功業之不建，而不失身於匪人。况中宗之不足扶植，武三思輩之不能有成，不待智者而后知。仁傑之賢，乃不知此，何與？至若元以夷狄入主中國，許衡應聘而為臣，劉因則屢聘之而不起。或謂劉高於許，然愚觀《渡江之賦》，乃快趙宋之亡，似非夷元不仕者。許之仕元，或謂將變夷為華。然王猛之仕秦，能以東晉正朔勸苻堅；許衡之仕元，乃不能以宋中國勸世祖，何與？他如漢唐諸賢，有以三顧聘之而出，以三公召之而不出；有三上宰相書而求出，有下詔徵之而不出者。先儒論之詳矣。然或謂求出者未必為非，不出者未必為正，出者未必為時
translation_en:
…any reason to extinguish those ancestral sacrifices. How could their preservation have depended on his carrying the sacrificial vessels over to Zhou?

When Wang Mang replaced Han with Xin, Gong Sheng refused food and died. When Empress Wu replaced Tang with Zhou, Di Renjie bowed his head and served her. Commentators further say that Renjie served Zhou in order to act on behalf of Tang. Yet a gentleman would rather leave great achievements unrealized than compromise himself by serving an unworthy person. Moreover, one did not need to be wise to recognize that Zhongzong was not worth supporting and that Wu Sansi and his fellows could accomplish nothing. How could someone as worthy as Renjie have failed to understand this?

As for the Yuan, who entered and ruled the Central Lands as barbarians, Xu Heng accepted an invitation to serve as their subject, whereas Liu Yin repeatedly declined invitations to take office. Some say that Liu was superior to Xu. Yet in my humble reading of his “Rhapsody on Crossing the River,” he actually rejoiced at the fall of the Zhao house’s Song dynasty. He thus seems not to have been someone who refused office because he regarded the Yuan as barbarian. Of Xu’s service under Yuan, some say that he intended to transform the barbarians into bearers of Chinese civilization. Yet Wang Meng, while serving Qin, could urge Fu Jian to recognize the legitimate dynastic authority of the Eastern Jin. Why, then, could Xu Heng, while serving Yuan, not urge Shizu to recognize Song as the legitimate ruler of the Central Lands?

Among other worthy men of Han and Tang, there were those who took office after being invited through three personal visits, and those who refused to take office when summoned to serve as one of the Three Dukes. There were those who submitted letters to the chief councilor three times seeking office, and those who declined to serve even when summoned by imperial edict. Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed these matters in detail. Yet some say that seeking office was not necessarily wrong, that declining office was not necessarily right, and that taking office was not necessarily timely…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
召之而不出者乃又旣出而成伊傅之
業又何與此皆必有至公至大之義不
可以曲學俗士之說拘者亦諸生之所
當講也幸明言之庸占他日出處之槩
問聖賢間世而生常以五百歲為期故自
堯舜以來數千百年其所見聞而知之
者具有可稽觀數於今適逢其會而我
朝
列聖躬行之至
===
製作之盛獨步千古莫與之京而又我
皇上聰明睿智擴縱自天
敬一一箴直發前聖之所未發眞所謂聞而
知之者矣然漸濡旣久不見有得於禹
皐伊傅之傳以接斯道之緒者何與夫
道不墜地必有見者近世儒臣獨識此
意歷考當時造詣諸臣乃得十有五人
撮其行實各為編次名之曰
皇明理學名臣言行錄然則十有五人者果皆
punctuated:
召之而不出者，乃又旣出而成伊傅之業，又何與？此皆必有至公至大之義，不可以曲學俗士之說拘者，亦諸生之所當講也。幸明言之，庸占他日出處之槩。

問：聖賢間世而生，常以五百歲為期。故自堯舜以來數千百年，其所見聞而知之者，具有可稽。觀數於今，適逢其會，而我朝列聖躬行之至，製作之盛，獨步千古，莫與之京。而又我皇上聰明睿智，擴縱自天，《敬一》一箴，直發前聖之所未發，眞所謂聞而知之者矣。然漸濡旣久，不見有得於禹皐伊傅之傳，以接斯道之緒者，何與？夫道不墜地，必有見者。近世儒臣獨識此意，歷考當時造詣諸臣，乃得十有五人，撮其行實，各為編次，名之曰《皇明理學名臣言行錄》。然則十有五人者，果皆
translation_en:
…those who, when summoned, did not come forth nevertheless subsequently entered service and accomplished deeds like those of Yi Yin and Fu Yue—why was this? In all these cases there must be principles of the utmost impartiality and magnitude, which cannot be confined by the explanations of scholars of distorted learning and conventional men. These, too, are matters that you candidates ought to examine. Please explain them clearly, so that we may gauge the broad outlines of your future decisions to enter office or remain in retirement.

Question: Sages and worthies arise only at intervals, commonly reckoned as periods of five hundred years. Thus, over the thousands of years since Yao and Shun, those who attained understanding through seeing or hearing have all left evidence that can be examined. Considering this reckoning in relation to the present, we find ourselves precisely at such a juncture. The successive sage emperors of our dynasty have attained perfection in their personal conduct and magnificence in their institutions and ordinances, standing unrivaled through the ages, with none their equal. Moreover, our present Emperor possesses intelligence and sagely wisdom, bestowed in abundance by Heaven [?]. His Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jing yi) directly reveals what earlier sages had not yet revealed. He is truly what is meant by one who attains understanding through hearing. Yet, although we have long been steeped in this influence, we see no one who has grasped the tradition of Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue and thereby carried forward the thread of this Way. Why is this?

The Way has not fallen to the ground: surely there must be those who perceive it. A Confucian official of recent times uniquely recognized this point. Having examined in turn the attainments of the officials of the period, he identified fifteen men, excerpted accounts of their conduct, and arranged these individually into a compilation entitled Records of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Neo-Confucian Ministers of the August Ming (Huang Ming lixue mingchen yanxing lu). Now, were these fifteen men indeed all…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
見知之實而真有得於道統之正者誰
與且其言曰若薛瑄輩視程朱高弟豈
多讓之就如餘人亦不但僅如陳同父
輩而已卽斯論也果亦灼有所見而言
之否與周敦頤肇開宋學之源及其身
鮮有不疑之者而過時乃定然則今之
講求亦大率類此也與后之觀今猶今
之視古也諸士子將何觀乎幸毋高論
以對
===
問宋人有言欲天下之治在乎才者居職
欲才者居職在乎使其居閑之日少居
閑之日少在乎清入仕之源以今日觀
之歲貢科舉不增於舊員缺之冗率又
過之然赴部待選動至數千給假家居
恒逾二萬至有白首不得一命幸而得
之亦皆垂老志得之年正所謂莅官之
日淺居閑之日多以其莅官之所得而
為居閑仰給之資是以人才愈多治功
punctuated:
見知之實，而真有得於道統之正者誰與？且其言曰：「若薛瑄輩，視程朱高弟，豈多讓之？就如餘人，亦不但僅如陳同父輩而已。」卽斯論也，果亦灼有所見而言之否與？周敦頤肇開宋學之源，及其身，鮮有不疑之者，而過時乃定。然則今之講求，亦大率類此也與？后之觀今，猶今之視古也。諸士子將何觀乎？幸毋高論以對。

問：宋人有言：「欲天下之治，在乎才者居職；欲才者居職，在乎使其居閑之日少；居閑之日少，在乎清入仕之源。」以今日觀之，歲貢、科舉不增於舊，員缺之冗率又過之。然赴部待選，動至數千；給假家居，恒逾二萬。至有白首不得一命，幸而得之，亦皆垂老志得之年。正所謂莅官之日淺，居閑之日多，以其莅官之所得，而為居閑仰給之資。是以人才愈多，治功
translation_en:
…truly possessed knowledge gained through direct observation? And who among them truly grasped the orthodox transmission of the Way? Moreover, the author says: “Would men such as Xue Xuan concede much to the outstanding disciples of Cheng and Zhu? Even the others were not merely the equals of men such as Chen Tongfu.” Was this judgment indeed grounded in clear insight? Zhou Dunyi first opened the source of Song learning. During his lifetime, scarcely anyone was free of doubts about him; only afterward was his standing settled. Is the inquiry pursued today, then, largely similar? Later generations will view our age as we view antiquity. What judgment will you candidates make? Please do not answer with lofty generalities.

Question: A man of the Song said: “Bringing order to the realm depends on having talented men hold office; having talented men hold office depends on shortening their time without appointments; shortening their time without appointments depends on purifying the sources of entry into official service.” Looking at the present, the numbers entering through annual tribute and the examinations have not increased over former levels, while vacant posts are generally even more numerous [?]. Yet those who go to the Ministry to await selection routinely number in the thousands, and those granted leave to remain at home regularly exceed twenty thousand. Some reach white-haired old age without receiving a single appointment. Even those fortunate enough to obtain one achieve their ambition only when approaching old age. This is precisely what is meant by spending little time in office and much time without an appointment, and using what one acquires while in office to provide the means of support during periods without an appointment. Thus, the more talented men there are, the more the achievements of government…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
愈壞欲其飭已安民難矣立法以來不
聞有是猶至今日積壅日深爲銓司者
每欲疏通而不可得其故將安在乎蘇
軾嘗曰可畏者天下安危而嚚嚚者以
爲不可爲不足卹必欲變而通之是矣
然言變通者有曰四弊旣去則其源自
清有曰四色之人並行澄汰又曰必須
調停之使入仕者有實用之效汰退者
無失所之歎其道又安取乎尹洙之與
===
服飾陳襄之與折資差遣李東之與監
臨物務其亦調停之說尚可倣而用之
否乎爲官擇人不爲人設官此確論也
究竟其實不知終以何說爲然
alt_text:
愈壞欲其飭已安民難矣立法以來不
聞有是循至今日積壅日深爲銓司者
毎欲疏通而不可得其故將安在乎蘇
軾嘗曰可畏者天下安危而囂囂者以
爲不可爲不足恤必欲變而通之是矣
然言變通者有曰四弊旣去則其源自
清有曰四色之人並行澄汰又曰必須
調停之使入仕者有實用之效汰退者
無失所之歎其道又安取乎尹洙之與
===
服飾陳襄之與折資差遣李柬之與監
臨物務其亦調停之說尚可倣而用之
否乎爲官擇人不爲人設官此確論也
究竟其實不知終以何說爲然
punctuated: 愈壞，欲其飭已安民，難矣！立法以來，不聞有是，猶至今日，積壅日深。爲銓司者，每欲疏通而不可得，其故將安在乎？蘇軾嘗曰：「可畏者天下安危，而嚚嚚者以爲不可爲，不足卹。」必欲變而通之，是矣。然言變通者，有曰：「四弊旣去，則其源自清。」有曰：「四色之人，並行澄汰。」又曰：「必須調停之，使入仕者有實用之效，汰退者無失所之歎。」其道又安取乎？尹洙之與服飾，陳襄之與折資差遣，李東之與監臨物務，其亦調停之說，尚可倣而用之否乎？爲官擇人，不爲人設官，此確論也。究竟其實，不知終以何說爲然？
translation_en: …the worse government becomes; to expect them to discipline themselves and bring peace to the people is difficult indeed! Since these regulations were established, such a situation had not been heard of; yet by today the accumulated congestion grows daily more severe. Those responsible for personnel selection constantly wish to clear it but cannot. Where does the cause lie? Su Shi once said: “What warrants apprehension is the security or peril of the realm, yet the foolish and obstinate [?] consider that nothing can be done and that it is not worth concern.” The insistence that changes must be made to restore a workable system is right. Yet among those advocating reform, some say: “Once the four abuses are eliminated, the source will naturally become clear.” Others say: “All four categories of men should alike undergo scrutiny and elimination.” Still others say: “An accommodation must be reached, so that those entering office render effective service, while those eliminated and dismissed have no cause to lament losing their livelihood.” What means should be adopted to achieve this? Yin Zhu’s proposal to grant official attire, Chen Xiang’s to grant assignments at reduced seniority, and Li Dong’s [?] to grant posts supervising material affairs—are these also proposals for accommodation that might still be imitated and put into practice? Select men for offices; do not establish offices for men: this is a sound principle. But when the actual circumstances are thoroughly examined, which proposal should ultimately be judged correct?

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子無終食之間違仁造次必於是顛沛
必於是
蕭來鳳
同考試官教諭蕭批造次顛沛時功夫極難更詳之
考試官教諭劉批能體認
考試官教授林批明浄
君子體仁之功隨所寓而見其密焉夫仁者君
===
子所以成德者也體之於身而不以所寓遷焉
則其存養者不已密乎夫子之意以為君子審
擇於富貴貧賤而不苟者凡以求仁也仁其可
已乎哉是故終食者富貴貧賤之小者也君子
則自其不處不去者而精之時乎當取固致謹
矣而其為仁之心不以時取而始存時乎當舍
固致決矣而其克己之念不以時舍而始有蓋
其天德完備合大小以為功至理渾全貫心事
而成體曷嘗少離於一飯之頃乎至若造次而
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「君子無終食之間違仁，造次必於是，顛沛必於是。」

蕭來鳳

同考試官教諭蕭批：「造次顛沛時功夫極難，更詳之。」
考試官教諭劉批：「能體認。」
考試官教授林批：「明浄。」

君子體仁之功，隨所寓而見其密焉。夫仁者，君子所以成德者也。體之於身，而不以所寓遷焉，則其存養者不已密乎？夫子之意，以為君子審擇於富貴貧賤而不苟者，凡以求仁也。仁其可已乎哉？是故終食者，富貴貧賤之小者也。君子則自其不處不去者而精之。時乎當取，固致謹矣，而其為仁之心，不以時取而始存；時乎當舍，固致決矣，而其克己之念，不以時舍而始有。蓋其天德完備，合大小以為功；至理渾全，貫心事而成體。曷嘗少離於一飯之頃乎？至若造次而
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The gentleman does not depart from benevolence even for the duration of a meal. In haste he invariably cleaves to it; in adversity he invariably cleaves to it.”

Xiao Laifeng

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “The work of cultivation in haste and adversity is exceedingly difficult. Elaborate further on this.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Able to grasp it through personal understanding.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Clear and lucid.”

The thoroughness of the gentleman’s work of embodying benevolence becomes apparent in whatever circumstances he finds himself. Benevolence is that through which the gentleman perfects his virtue. If he embodies it in his own person and does not change with his circumstances, is his work of preserving and nurturing it not already thorough? The Master’s meaning is that the gentleman exercises considered judgment regarding wealth and honor, poverty and lowliness, and does not act heedlessly, solely because he seeks benevolence. Could benevolence ever be set aside?

Thus, the duration of a meal is a small instance of the circumstances of wealth and honor, poverty and lowliness. The gentleman refines the same practice by which he refuses to abide in the former or to depart from the latter. When it is time to accept, he certainly exercises the utmost care; yet his resolve to practice benevolence does not first come into being only at the moment of acceptance. When it is time to relinquish, he certainly acts with resolution; yet his intention to overcome the self does not first arise only at the moment of relinquishment. For his Heaven-endowed virtue is complete, bringing great and small together in the work of cultivation; ultimate principle is an undivided whole, uniting mind and affairs into one integral embodiment. When has he ever departed from it, even briefly, during the span of a single meal? As for moments of haste, when …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲急遽苟且之時則其時爲又近人之所易忽
者也君子則本體自然不容人力造次之心卽
其終食之心終食之心行於造次而不與焉固
無有惑之者自夫時而論之斯謂之造次云耳
顛沛而爲傾覆流離之際則其遇爲尤逆人之
所易動者也君子則本體固有不待人爲顛沛
之心卽其平居之心平居之心行於顛沛而不
與焉固無有變之者自夫遇而觀之殆謂之顛
沛云耳所以然者仁本無物故不可以有物戕
===
若見物而后覺焉則其於仁也遠矣功在事先
故不可以有事勝若臨事而后養焉則其於造
次顛沛也離矣此君子存養之功所以爲密而
不處不去之迹不足言也雖然不處不去固所
以爲仁矣然以原憲之貧子路之不恥與狐貉
者立而夫子不與其仁何也二子者未見夫仁
之體是以雖有所得猶不免於意必之心而未
大耳此夫子言取舍之分而必繼之以仁者以
此故曰見大則心泰心泰則無不足通於此者
punctuated:
爲急遽苟且之時，則其時爲又近，人之所易忽者也。君子則本體自然，不容人力，造次之心卽其終食之心。終食之心行於造次而不與焉，固無有惑之者。自夫時而論之，斯謂之造次云耳。顛沛而爲傾覆流離之際，則其遇爲尤逆，人之所易動者也。君子則本體固有，不待人爲，顛沛之心卽其平居之心。平居之心行於顛沛而不與焉，固無有變之者。自夫遇而觀之，殆謂之顛沛云耳。所以然者，仁本無物，故不可以有物戕；若見物而后覺焉，則其於仁也遠矣。功在事先，故不可以有事勝；若臨事而后養焉，則其於造次顛沛也離矣。此君子存養之功所以爲密，而不處不去之迹不足言也。
雖然，不處不去固所以爲仁矣，然以原憲之貧、子路之不恥與狐貉者立，而夫子不與其仁，何也？二子者未見夫仁之體，是以雖有所得，猶不免於意必之心，而未大耳。此夫子言取舍之分，而必繼之以仁者，以此。故曰：「見大則心泰，心泰則無不足。」通於此者
translation_en:
…being a time of haste and hurried expediency, the moment is still more immediate [?], and thus one in which people easily become neglectful. For the gentleman, however, the fundamental substance of his mind is naturally so and admits no contrived effort. His mind in haste is precisely his mind during a meal. The mind maintained during a meal operates amid haste without becoming implicated in it; nothing can bewilder it. It is merely from the standpoint of the occasion that this is called “haste.” When adversity brings ruin and displacement, the circumstances are especially hostile, and people are easily shaken by them. For the gentleman, however, the fundamental substance is inherent and does not depend upon deliberate contrivance. His mind in adversity is precisely his mind in ordinary life. The mind of ordinary life operates amid adversity without becoming implicated in it; nothing can alter it. It is only from the standpoint of the circumstances encountered that this may be called “adversity.” The reason is that benevolence is fundamentally free of external things, and therefore cannot be injured by them. If one becomes aware only upon encountering things, one is far from benevolence. The work of cultivation precedes events, and therefore cannot be overcome by them. If one begins nurturing the mind only when an event arises, one will be separated from benevolence amid haste and adversity. This is why the gentleman’s work of preserving and nurturing the mind is so thorough, while his outward acts of refusing to remain in wealth and rank or refusing to leave poverty and lowliness scarcely need mentioning.
Nevertheless, refusing to remain or to leave is indeed a means of practicing benevolence. Yet despite Yuan Xian’s poverty and Zilu’s feeling no shame at standing beside those wearing fox and raccoon furs, the Master did not grant them the designation of benevolent. Why was this? These two had not yet perceived the substance of benevolence. Thus, although they had attained something, they were still not free from a mind governed by conjecture and insistence, and had not yet attained greatness. This is why, when the Master spoke of the distinction between accepting and rejecting, he invariably followed it with benevolence. Hence the saying: “When one perceives what is great, the mind is at ease; when the mind is at ease, nothing is lacking.” Those who comprehend this…

嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
機會固不拂乎時措之宜且朋來無咎所以協
恭者有人矣夫當剛長之時備臨隂之善如此
故大亨者非偶然之故也蓋天者理而已矣理
之所當得天人相成之妙志氣交應之幾君子
安能以襲取哉利貞者非過為之防也蓋天者
正而已矣理之所當為天運而人從時起而事
應君子安能以逆天哉由是觀之世道固不能
以不復人謀亦不可以不臧幸乎天而人不繼
焉豈君子所以處道行之會也哉大抵盛衰相
===
推而運生焉安危相倚而機伏焉世道之不能
以常如一日也然圖回之機未始不於和順得
之任智以穿鑿挾權以急功恃勢以資姦其以
弊天下均也是故事未成而幾先泄功未就而
志已驕君子固病其驟也而陋前規以更張任
己意以推行者卒以啓禍亂之原安危治忽之
機君子可鑒矣
夫易廣矣大矣以言乎遠則不禦以言乎
邇則靜而正以言乎天地之間則備矣
punctuated:
機會固不拂乎時措之宜，且朋來無咎，所以協恭者有人矣。夫當剛長之時，備臨隂之善如此，故大亨者非偶然之故也。蓋天者理而已矣，理之所當得，天人相成之妙、志氣交應之幾，君子安能以襲取哉？利貞者非過為之防也。蓋天者正而已矣，理之所當為，天運而人從，時起而事應，君子安能以逆天哉？由是觀之，世道固不能以不復，人謀亦不可以不臧。幸乎天而人不繼焉，豈君子所以處道行之會也哉？大抵盛衰相推而運生焉，安危相倚而機伏焉，世道之不能以常如一日也。然圖回之機，未始不於和順得之。任智以穿鑿，挾權以急功，恃勢以資姦，其以弊天下均也。是故事未成而幾先泄，功未就而志已驕，君子固病其驟也。而陋前規以更張，任己意以推行者，卒以啓禍亂之原。安危治忽之機，君子可鑒矣。

夫易廣矣，大矣！以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正；以言乎天地之間，則備矣。
translation_en:
…the opportunity certainly accords with what is appropriate to timely action. Moreover, “friends come, and there is no blame”: there are thus people with whom to cooperate in reverent service. When the firm is increasing, the virtues needed to oversee the yin are so fully present; hence “great success” is no accidental outcome. Heaven is simply principle. What principle properly yields—the wondrous mutual fulfillment of Heaven and humanity, and the incipient workings through which purpose and vital energy respond to one another—how could the gentleman seize these for himself? “It is beneficial to remain correct” is no excessive precaution. Heaven is simply correctness. In doing what principle requires, humanity follows Heaven’s movements, and affairs respond as their proper times arise. How could the gentleman act against Heaven? Viewed in this light, the course of the world cannot fail to turn back toward the good, yet human plans must also be sound. To rely on Heaven’s favor without following it up through human effort—could this be how the gentleman meets an opportunity for the Way to prevail?

In general, flourishing and decline displace one another, giving rise to changing fortunes; security and danger depend on one another, concealing the beginnings of change. The world’s course cannot remain the same from day to day. Yet opportunities to bring about a recovery have always been found through harmony and accord. Relying on cleverness to devise strained contrivances, wielding power to hasten achievement, and depending on influence to facilitate wrongdoing all alike harm the world. Thus, before an undertaking is accomplished, its crucial designs are already divulged; before success is attained, ambition has already grown arrogant. The gentleman certainly deplores such haste. Those who disparage earlier rules and alter them, carrying out measures according to their own whims, ultimately open the source of calamity and disorder. The gentleman should take warning from these incipient causes of security and danger, order and disorder.

How broad and great is the Book of Changes! Speaking of what is distant, it reaches without limit; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct; speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉
夫坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉
高士楠
同考試官教諭王批說易廣大處不易見得
同考試官教諭劉批長題能收拾
同考試官教諭徐批模寫造化深見易理
考試官教諭劉批辭順理足
考試官教授林批純雅
大傳詳易理之廣大必推而本諸乾坤焉夫易
===
冒天下之道者也乾坤動靜之間而廣大見之
易其性命之書矣乎大傳之意若謂易者理之
會也乾坤者理之迹也人以易為卜筮之書非
知易者也易其至廣而无不包至大而无不有
者乎是故言乎遠而有所不達非廣大也易則
隨處充滿而无遠弗届夫孰得而禦之言乎近
而或有所遺非廣大也易則隨在各足而小大
有定不亦靜而正乎又自夫天地之間言之體
物或遺非廣大也吾見察於上下莫非陰陽之
punctuated:
夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。

高士楠

同考試官教諭王批：「說易廣大處，不易見得。」
同考試官教諭劉批：「長題能收拾。」
同考試官教諭徐批：「模寫造化，深見易理。」
考試官教諭劉批：「辭順理足。」
考試官教授林批：「純雅。」

大傳詳易理之廣大，必推而本諸乾坤焉。夫易，冒天下之道者也。乾坤動靜之間，而廣大見之，易其性命之書矣乎！大傳之意若謂：易者，理之會也；乾坤者，理之迹也。人以易為卜筮之書，非知易者也。易其至廣而无不包、至大而无不有者乎！是故言乎遠而有所不達，非廣大也；易則隨處充滿，而无遠弗届，夫孰得而禦之？言乎近而或有所遺，非廣大也；易則隨在各足，而小大有定，不亦靜而正乎？又自夫天地之間言之，體物或遺，非廣大也。吾見察於上下，莫非陰陽之
translation_en:
“Qian, in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct. Thus greatness arises. Kun, in stillness, gathers inward; in movement, it opens outward. Thus breadth arises.”

Gao Shinan 高士楠

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “It expounds the breadth and greatness of the Changes—qualities not easily discerned.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It brings a long topic into a coherent whole.”
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “It depicts creation and transformation, revealing deep insight into the principles of the Changes.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The language flows smoothly, and the reasoning is complete.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Pure and elegant.”

In explaining fully the breadth and greatness of the principles of the Changes, the Great Commentary necessarily traces them back to their foundation in Qian and Kun. The Changes encompasses the Way of all under Heaven. In the movement and stillness of Qian and Kun, its breadth and greatness become apparent. Surely the Changes is a book of human nature and destiny! The meaning of the Great Commentary seems to be this: the Changes is where principle converges; Qian and Kun are the manifestations of principle. Those who regard the Changes as a book of divination by tortoise shell and milfoil do not understand it. Is not the Changes so supremely broad that it embraces everything, and so supremely great that it contains everything?

Thus, speaking of the distant, if there were anything it could not reach, it would lack breadth and greatness. Yet the Changes fills every place, reaching everywhere however distant: what could possibly obstruct it? Speaking of the near, if anything were omitted, it would lack breadth and greatness. Yet the Changes is complete wherever it is present, and both small and great have their settled order: is it not still and correct? Again, speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, if it failed to embody any thing, it would lack breadth and greatness. I see that, examining what is above and below, there is nothing that is not of yin and yang …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
流行塞乎天地无非變化之妙用兼體不累其
至矣乎然易之所以廣大者何哉觀乾坤則知
易矣夫乾以生物爲心自其靜而別於坤誠之
所復專而一也及其動而與坤交焉推行不息
普天下而有莫禦之機是其周遍之體蓋實而
无所不統矣大不於是而生乎乾之大卽易之
大焉耳夫坤以成物爲心自其靜而別於乾機
之所入翕而聚也及其動而與乾交焉充周不
窮合群動而有難名之化是其含弘之量蓋虛
===
而无所不容矣廣不於是而生乎坤之廣卽易
之廣焉耳此易書所以爲至而聖人統天地之
心者以此學者苟不求之乾坤於心之動靜曷
足以知之哉大抵易書未作易在造化易書旣
作造化在易故天地之大事物之微无不出於
陰陽之變聖人亦因而模寫之而已後世洞極
有書潛虛有圖欲以擬易牽合附會自然之理
益晦焉無惑乎天下以卜筮而小吾易也
書經
punctuated:
流行，塞乎天地，无非變化之妙用，兼體不累，其至矣乎！然易之所以廣大者何哉？觀乾坤則知易矣。夫乾以生物爲心，自其靜而別於坤，誠之所復，專而一也；及其動而與坤交焉，推行不息，普天下而有莫禦之機，是其周遍之體，蓋實而无所不統矣。大不於是而生乎？乾之大，卽易之大焉耳。夫坤以成物爲心，自其靜而別於乾，機之所入，翕而聚也；及其動而與乾交焉，充周不窮，合群動而有難名之化，是其含弘之量，蓋虛而无所不容矣。廣不於是而生乎？坤之廣，卽易之廣焉耳。此易書所以爲至，而聖人統天地之心者以此。學者苟不求之乾坤，於心之動靜曷足以知之哉？大抵易書未作，易在造化；易書旣作，造化在易。故天地之大、事物之微，无不出於陰陽之變，聖人亦因而模寫之而已。後世《洞極》有書，《潛虛》有圖，欲以擬易，牽合附會，自然之理益晦焉。無惑乎天下以卜筮而小吾易也！

書經
translation_en:
…flow and circulation of yin and yang. All that fills Heaven and Earth is the wondrous working of transformation. Encompassing both without impediment—is this not perfection? Yet why is the Changes so broad and great? By contemplating Qian and Kun, one comes to understand the Changes. Qian takes the generation of things as its heart. In its stillness, when it is distinct from Kun, it is where sincerity returns, concentrated and single. When it moves and joins with Kun, it advances without cease, possessing an impulse that nothing throughout the world can resist. Its all-pervading constitution is thus full, leaving nothing outside its command. Does not greatness arise from this? The greatness of Qian is precisely the greatness of the Changes. Kun takes the completion of things as its heart. In its stillness, when it is distinct from Qian, it is where the incipient impulse enters, closing and gathering together. When it moves and joins with Qian, it fills everything without limit, uniting all movements in a transformation difficult to name. Its capacious magnitude is thus empty, leaving nothing it cannot accommodate. Does not breadth arise from this? The breadth of Kun is precisely the breadth of the Changes.

This is why the book of Changes is supreme, and it is through this that the sage comprehends the heart of Heaven and Earth. Unless learners seek this in Qian and Kun, how can they adequately understand it in the movement and stillness of their own hearts? Generally speaking, before the book of Changes was composed, the Changes resided in the process of creation and transformation; once the book was composed, creation and transformation resided in the Changes. Thus, from the greatness of Heaven and Earth to the minutiae of affairs and things, nothing fails to arise from the transformations of yin and yang. The sage merely followed these and depicted them. In later ages, there was the book Penetrating the Ultimate (Dongji), and there were the diagrams of Latent Emptiness (Qianxu). These sought to emulate the Changes, but through forced connections and strained correspondences they only further obscured the principles of what is naturally so. No wonder the world belittles our Changes as merely a work of divination!

Classic of Documents

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
安汝止惟幾惟康
林繼習
同考試官教諭蕭批〔以惟幾惟康為安汝止之實亦是〕
考試官教諭劉批〔理明詞暢〕
考試官教授林批〔純正〕
事適本原之善而致謹於發用之間大臣告君
之脩己也蓋君心主天下之善而審之於為則
得之矣聖禹以此箴帝舜之謹位也有以哉想
其意豈不曰人君居天位而致治安者在乎事
===
為之善而事之善非在事也蓋吾之一心萬善
咸備事之所取無窮而吾之付之也各因其則
若有所定於中而其不可遷者是之謂止其止
也惟懼夫欲之為奪者矣帝也日覲萬化其必
以道心為主而帝德昭然其廣運使凡動靜云
為之發莫不各取其固有於吾道心而止焉如
天之運而日月星辰各得其麗也日臨萬幾其
必守中心無為而淵衷穆然其靜定使凡事事
物物之來莫不各還其本善於吾中心而安焉
punctuated:
安汝止，惟幾惟康。
林繼習
同考試官教諭蕭批〔以惟幾惟康為安汝止之實，亦是。〕
考試官教諭劉批〔理明詞暢。〕
考試官教授林批〔純正。〕
事適本原之善，而致謹於發用之間，大臣告君之脩己也。蓋君心主天下之善，而審之於為，則得之矣。聖禹以此箴帝舜之謹位也，有以哉！想其意，豈不曰：人君居天位而致治安者，在乎事為之善，而事之善非在事也。蓋吾之一心，萬善咸備，事之所取無窮，而吾之付之也，各因其則，若有所定於中，而其不可遷者，是之謂止。其止也，惟懼夫欲之為奪者矣。帝也日覲萬化，其必以道心為主，而帝德昭然其廣運，使凡動靜云為之發，莫不各取其固有於吾道心而止焉，如天之運，而日月星辰各得其麗也。日臨萬幾，其必守中心無為，而淵衷穆然其靜定，使凡事事物物之來，莫不各還其本善於吾中心而安焉。
translation_en:
“Be secure in your resting place; attend to incipient stirrings and to well-being.”
Lin Jixi
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔Taking attention to incipient stirrings and well-being as the substance of “be secure in your resting place” is also sound.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear reasoning and fluent expression.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔Pure and correct.〕
To make affairs accord with the goodness of their original source, and to exercise care as that goodness comes into operation: this is a great minister’s counsel to his ruler concerning self-cultivation. The ruler’s mind presides over all goodness under Heaven; if he scrutinizes it in his actions, he will attain it. The sage Yu had good reason to admonish Emperor Shun in these terms to be circumspect in his position! If we imagine his meaning, would he not have said: A ruler occupies Heaven’s appointed position and brings about order and peace through the goodness of his actions. Yet the goodness of affairs does not reside in the affairs themselves. Within this single mind of mine, every goodness is fully present. What affairs draw from it is inexhaustible, and what I impart to each follows its proper standard. There is, as it were, something settled within that cannot be shifted: this is what is called a resting place. Once resting there, one fears only that desires may wrest it away.
You, Emperor, daily behold the myriad transformations. You must take the moral mind as your master, so that your imperial virtue shines forth in its expansive operation. Thus, whatever issues forth in activity or stillness, speech or action, will draw upon what is inherently present in your moral mind and rest there. This is like the movement of Heaven, in which the sun, moon, and stars each find their proper attachment. Daily you preside over the myriad incipient stirrings of affairs. You must preserve your inner mind in nonaction, keeping your profound inward thoughts serenely still and settled, so that every affair and thing that comes before you returns to its original goodness within your mind and rests securely there …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
如地之容而山川人物各奠其居也是之謂安
汝止然所以能使之安者果何如哉蓋事之欲
爲而發動所由謂之幾幾分善惡在毫釐之間
惟己所獨知者矣帝於此必致審其念慮之發
眞所以昭德致理也而罔有飾僞之私則從而
發之如其未然則禦寇之剛不可不厲也事之
旣爲而適當其理謂之康康成於幾則微著以
著理無所容其僞矣帝於此又必致省於事爲
之迹果足以達善宣猷也而匪爲違道之行則
===
從而安之如其未然則改圖之功所不容已也
夫審幾以達外則察之精而其善爲必行考成
以觀內則守之一而其善爲益固如此而事有
不得其所止者哉事得其止則治化益隆天位
可保於無窮矣帝其可不念哉抑聖禹幾康之
說是卽精一之旨舜所受之堯者厥後舜之禪
禹其所命精一之言亦卽幾康之意三聖相授
共守一道於此可見而幾之一字尤虞廷之所
致謹焉者故皐陶陳謨有曰一日二日萬幾舜
punctuated:
如地之容，而山川人物各奠其居也，是之謂安汝止。然所以能使之安者，果何如哉？蓋事之欲爲，而發動所由，謂之幾。幾分善惡，在毫釐之間，惟己所獨知者矣。帝於此必致審其念慮之發，眞所以昭德致理也，而罔有飾僞之私，則從而發之。如其未然，則禦寇之剛不可不厲也。事之旣爲，而適當其理，謂之康。康成於幾，則微著以著，理無所容其僞矣。帝於此又必致省於事爲之迹，果足以達善宣猷也，而匪爲違道之行，則從而安之。如其未然，則改圖之功所不容已也。
夫審幾以達外，則察之精而其善爲必行；考成以觀內，則守之一而其善爲益固。如此，而事有不得其所止者哉？事得其止，則治化益隆，天位可保於無窮矣。帝其可不念哉？抑聖禹幾康之說，是卽精一之旨，舜所受之堯者。厥後舜之禪禹，其所命精一之言，亦卽幾康之意。三聖相授，共守一道，於此可見。而幾之一字，尤虞廷之所致謹焉者。故皐陶陳謨有曰：「一日二日萬幾。」舜
translation_en:
…just as the earth accommodates all things, and mountains, rivers, people, and other creatures each settle in their proper dwelling. This is what is meant by “rest securely in your proper stopping place.” But how, indeed, can one bring about this security? When an undertaking is about to be carried out, the incipient impulse from which its activation proceeds is called ji. At this incipient stage, good and evil diverge by the slightest margin, discernible to oneself alone. Here the emperor must scrutinize the emergence of his thoughts with the utmost care. If they truly serve to manifest virtue and bring about good government, without any selfish impulse toward pretense or deceit, he should give them expression. If they do not, he must sharpen his resolve as firmly as if resisting bandits. When an undertaking has been carried out and accords precisely with its proper principle, this is called kang, a state of good order. Good order takes shape from incipient impulses; what was subtle thus becomes manifest [?], and principle leaves no room for falsity. Here the emperor must also examine with the utmost care the traces left by his actions. If they truly suffice to extend goodness and give effect to sound plans, and are not conduct that violates the Way, he should rest securely in them. If they do not, the work of revising his plans must not cease.
By scrutinizing incipient impulses so as to give them outward expression, his discernment becomes exact and his good actions are sure to be carried out. By examining completed results so as to observe what lies within, his adherence becomes single-minded and his good actions grow still more firmly established. With matters handled thus, could any undertaking fail to attain its proper stopping place? When each undertaking attains its proper stopping place, government and moral transformation flourish increasingly, and the throne may be preserved without end. How could the emperor fail to give this thought? Moreover, the sage Yu’s teaching concerning incipient impulses and good order embodies precisely the purport of refined discernment and single-mindedness that Shun received from Yao. Later, when Shun abdicated in favor of Yu, his injunction concerning refined discernment and single-mindedness likewise expressed the meaning of incipient impulses and good order. Here we can see that the three sages transmitted their teaching to one another and together upheld a single Way. The single word ji, “incipient impulses,” especially commanded the utmost vigilance at the court of Yu—that is, Shun. Thus, when Gao Yao presented his counsels, he said: “In one day, in two days, there are ten thousand incipient impulses.” Shun…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之作歌亦曰勅天之命惟時惟幾蓋天下之治
忽天人之去留誠於此係焉聖君賢臣所以兢
業而不敢忽而其警戒之言猶不忘於盛治之
時有由然也是故觀其道之同可以知往聖之
心學會其幾之審可以開萬世之太平
黍稷非馨明德惟馨
蕭來鳳
同考試官教諭蕭批發出周公之意無遺
考試官教諭劉批明整
考試官教授林批簡古
===
賢王舉聖訓著格神之本以命大臣也蓋至治
馨香則神之所格者誠不在於黍稷矣此周公
精微之訓而成王述之以告君陳也且昔周公
之意若曰祀以感神為極而治以明德為本有
其德則神易於感矣今夫君子脩明禋以事天
萃精神以假廟粢盛旣具於靜嘉則黍稷必列
於昭薦當是時也對越者無言奏假而感神明
之來享駿奔者顒若裸將而接靈貺之若通孰
punctuated:
之作歌亦曰：「勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」蓋天下之治忽，天人之去留，誠於此係焉。聖君賢臣所以兢業而不敢忽，而其警戒之言猶不忘於盛治之時，有由然也。是故觀其道之同，可以知往聖之心學；會其幾之審，可以開萬世之太平。
黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。
蕭來鳳
同考試官教諭蕭批：發出周公之意無遺。
考試官教諭劉批：明整。
考試官教授林批：簡古。
賢王舉聖訓，著格神之本，以命大臣也。蓋至治馨香，則神之所格者，誠不在於黍稷矣。此周公精微之訓，而成王述之以告君陳也。且昔周公之意若曰：祀以感神為極，而治以明德為本，有其德則神易於感矣。今夫君子脩明禋以事天，萃精神以假廟，粢盛旣具於靜嘉，則黍稷必列於昭薦。當是時也，對越者無言，奏假而感神明之來享；駿奔者顒若，裸將而接靈貺之若通。孰
translation_en:
…in his song also said: “Attend reverently to Heaven’s mandate; heed the times and the incipient signs.” For the order or disorder of All under Heaven, and whether Heaven and the people withdraw or remain, truly depend upon this. There is thus a reason why sage rulers and worthy ministers remain vigilant and dare not be negligent, and why they do not forget their words of warning even in times of flourishing government. Hence, by observing the unity of their Way, one may understand the learning of the mind of the sages of old; by grasping their careful discernment of incipient signs, one may inaugurate peace for ten thousand generations.
“It is not the millet that is fragrant; enlightened virtue alone is fragrant.”
Xiao Laifeng 蕭來鳳
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Brings out the Duke of Zhou’s meaning without omission.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Clear and well ordered.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: “Concise and antique in style.”
The worthy king cites a sage’s instruction, making clear the foundation for bringing the spirits near, in order to charge a great minister. For perfect government has a sweet fragrance: what brings the spirits near truly does not lie in the millet. This was the Duke of Zhou’s subtle and profound teaching, which King Cheng repeated in his charge to Jun Chen.
Now the Duke of Zhou’s meaning in former times was as if to say: the ultimate purpose of sacrifice is to move the spirits, while the foundation of government lies in enlightened virtue. With that virtue, the spirits are readily moved. Consider how the gentleman performs pure sacrifices to serve Heaven and gathers his spiritual energies as he approaches the ancestral temple. Once the sacrificial grain has been prepared in purity and excellence, the millet must be arrayed as a splendid offering. At this moment, those facing the divine presence remain wordless, presenting their offerings and moving the spirits to come and partake; those hastening to their duties are reverent, presenting libations and receiving divine blessings as though communion had been established. title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不以為黍稷之馨而致然也殊不知簠實特所
以羞神而祀有不求於備物略儀文之末節求
苾芬之實體夫豈專在於黍稷之具而已哉誠
以至治成於有本而康乂之休莫非至德之薰
蒸大化神於不顯而太和之美莫非明德之融
液敷聞在下則昭升于上上帝時歆其鬯達固
不待黍稷之陳矣而况禮行於郊社有不降監
者乎精華旁達則馨香發聞百神胥悅其和氣
固出於黍稷之外矣而况祀事之孔明有不昭
===
格者乎周公之訓如此則知不能明德以治民
者不可以事神君陳之尹東郊有神民之寄可
不懋昭周公之訓以自明其德而化訓殷民以
求無斁於神乎抑殷民為梗周公誕保之而東
郊之尹繼以君陳將舉周公之政必師周公之
德而後可故成王命君陳首以周公之訓為言
欲其近法而不違襲德而不貳庶漸濡相繼頑
民懷服無異於周公時也下文式時猷訓敬典
在德之言成王復為君陳丁寧之卒之殷民式
punctuated: 不以為黍稷之馨而致然也？殊不知簠實特所以羞神，而祀有不求於備物。略儀文之末節，求苾芬之實體，夫豈專在於黍稷之具而已哉？誠以至治成於有本，而康乂之休莫非至德之薰蒸；大化神於不顯，而太和之美莫非明德之融液。敷聞在下，則昭升于上，上帝時歆，其鬯達固不待黍稷之陳矣，而况禮行於郊社，有不降監者乎？精華旁達，則馨香發聞，百神胥悅，其和氣固出於黍稷之外矣，而况祀事之孔明，有不昭格者乎？周公之訓如此，則知不能明德以治民者，不可以事神。君陳之尹東郊，有神民之寄，可不懋昭周公之訓，以自明其德，而化訓殷民，以求無斁於神乎？抑殷民為梗，周公誕保之，而東郊之尹繼以君陳。將舉周公之政，必師周公之德而後可。故成王命君陳，首以周公之訓為言，欲其近法而不違，襲德而不貳，庶漸濡相繼，頑民懷服，無異於周公時也。下文「式時猷訓，敬典在德」之言，成王復為君陳丁寧之。卒之殷民式
translation_en:
…would not think that the fragrance of the sacrificial millet had brought this about? Yet they fail to understand that the contents of the grain vessels serve merely as offerings to the spirits, and that sacrifice does not seek its fulfillment in the completeness of the offerings. If we set aside the minor details of ceremonial forms and seek the true substance of sacrificial fragrance, how could it reside solely in the provision of millet?

Indeed, perfect government is achieved through having a foundation: the blessings of peace and good order all arise from the pervasive influence of consummate virtue. Great transformation works wondrously in the unseen: the beauty of supreme harmony all arises from the permeation of luminous virtue. When its renown spreads here below, it rises resplendently above, and the Lord on High delights in it. Its unobstructed influence assuredly does not depend on setting out millet. How much more, then, when rites are performed at the suburban altar and the altar of the soil: could he fail to descend and behold them? When the essence of virtue reaches everywhere, its fragrance becomes manifest, and the hundred spirits all rejoice. Its harmonious influence assuredly extends beyond the millet itself. How much more, then, when the sacrificial service is conducted with utmost splendor: could the spirits fail to come in manifest presence?

Such was the Duke of Zhou’s instruction. We may therefore understand that one who cannot make virtue manifest in governing the people cannot serve the spirits. In governing the eastern suburb, Jun Chen was entrusted with responsibility for both spirits and people. Could he fail diligently to illuminate the Duke of Zhou’s instruction, thereby making his own virtue manifest and transforming and instructing the people of Yin, so that the spirits might never weary of him?

Moreover, the people of Yin had been recalcitrant, and the Duke of Zhou had greatly protected them. Jun Chen then succeeded him in governing the eastern suburb. To carry forward the Duke of Zhou’s government, he first had to take the Duke of Zhou’s virtue as his model. Thus, in commissioning Jun Chen, King Cheng began by speaking of the Duke of Zhou’s instruction. He wished Jun Chen to follow this recent exemplar without deviation and to inherit his virtue without wavering, so that its gradual, permeating influence might continue uninterrupted, and the obstinate people might cherish him and submit, just as in the Duke of Zhou’s time. In the words that follow, “Follow these counsels and instructions; reverence for the constant norms rests in virtue,” King Cheng again earnestly admonished Jun Chen. In the end, the people of Yin thus…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
化世變風移君陳和中之治端有力焉而成王
之因時制宜命德命治憂勤馴擾之心不少置
焉嗚呼繼體守成之君其有賢於成王哉
詩
物其多矣維其嘉矣物其旨矣維其偕矣
物其有矣維其時矣
蒙詔
同考試官教諭甘批辭不費而事理詳盡
同考試官教諭陳批優商之情宛然可見
===
考試官教諭劉批才思清妙
考試官教授林批精槩
觀主人優賓之意自夫物之曲全見之矣夫燕
飲之禮以備物為尚也主人燕賓而能曲全焉
是不可以觀敬乎哉此燕饗通用之樂歌以為
燕也者所以昭嘉會之禮洽賓主之情者也儀
不及物是曰不享然享非多儀無乃太簡乎是
故物有以多為貴者多而不嘉雖多奚以為也
今君子有酒多且旨吾見嘉寓於多焉尊罍盈
punctuated:
化，世變風移，君陳和中之治端有力焉。而成王之因時制宜，命德命治，憂勤馴擾之心不少置焉。嗚呼！繼體守成之君，其有賢於成王哉？
詩
物其多矣，維其嘉矣。物其旨矣，維其偕矣。物其有矣，維其時矣。
蒙詔
同考試官教諭甘批：辭不費而事理詳盡。
同考試官教諭陳批：優商之情宛然可見。
考試官教諭劉批：才思清妙。
考試官教授林批：精槩。
觀主人優賓之意，自夫物之曲全見之矣。夫燕飲之禮，以備物為尚也。主人燕賓而能曲全焉，是不可以觀敬乎哉？此燕饗通用之樂歌，以為燕也者，所以昭嘉會之禮，洽賓主之情者也。儀不及物，是曰不享。然享非多儀，無乃太簡乎？是故物有以多為貴者，多而不嘉，雖多奚以為也？今君子有酒，多且旨，吾見嘉寓於多焉。尊罍盈
translation_en:
…transformed; society changed and customs shifted. Jun Chen’s government, harmonious and balanced, certainly contributed to this. Yet King Cheng never for a moment set aside his anxious, diligent concern to adapt measures to the times, give instructions concerning virtue and government, and gradually bring the people into willing obedience. Ah! Among rulers who inherited the throne and preserved their predecessors’ achievements, was any worthier than King Cheng?
Book of Odes
“The provisions are abundant indeed, and truly excellent. The provisions are delicious indeed, and truly complete. The provisions are present indeed, and truly seasonable.”
Meng Zhao
Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: “The wording is economical, yet the matters and principles are fully explained.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The feeling of generosity toward merchants [?] is vividly apparent.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “His literary imagination is lucid and subtle.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Refined and succinct.”
The host’s intention to treat his guests generously can be seen in the thorough completeness of his provisions. For the rites of convivial drinking prize the full provision of everything required. When a host entertains his guests and attends completely to every detail, can we not see his respect in this? This is a song used alike at convivial gatherings and formal feasts. Its meaning is that a banquet serves to display the rites of a joyous gathering and bring host and guests into harmony. When ceremonial observances lack material offerings, this is called a failure to present hospitality. Yet if hospitality does not include abundant ceremonial offerings, would it not be excessively simple? Thus provisions are valued for their abundance. But if they are abundant without being excellent, what use is their abundance? Now, ‘the gentleman has wine, abundant and delicious’: I see excellence embodied in abundance. The zun and lei wine vessels brim…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
椒飶之芳也籩豆著靜嘉之美也勸酬之下足
以昭燕衎之光而弗嘉非所患矣物有以旨爲
貴者旨而弗偕雖旨猶未備也今君子有酒旨
且多吾見偕寓於旨焉食之飲之無缺儀也旣
戒旣平皆陳饋也獻酢之餘足以明盡物之敬
而弗齊非所患矣乃若物以有爲貴有而弗時
是徒有也非君子之所以厚賓也今則無一物
之不具則亦無一而不時焉以洽百禮順時物
之宜以和五味亶芳臭之薦酌言嘗之真足以
===
稱嘉美之會而無尚焉者矣又何患于弗時也
哉夫其物之曲全如此優賓之意於是乎至固
非以私惠爲德者其相孚之情可知矣抑嘗觀
之易曰天道下濟而光明地道卑而上行成周
之時衆賢和於朝而萬物和於野其君臣上下
恩禮交洽以至昆蟲闓澤協氣濡潤一時燕饗
通用之樂與笙詩相間歌者有魚麗嘉魚南山
有臺諸作可以見上下感應之機可以見厚倫
敦化之道此周之治所以爲盛也聖人以是錄
punctuated: 椒飶之芳也，籩豆著靜嘉之美也。勸酬之下，足以昭燕衎之光，而弗嘉非所患矣。物有以旨爲貴者，旨而弗偕，雖旨猶未備也。今君子有酒，旨且多，吾見偕寓於旨焉。食之飲之，無缺儀也；旣戒旣平，皆陳饋也。獻酢之餘，足以明盡物之敬，而弗齊非所患矣。乃若物以有爲貴，有而弗時，是徒有也，非君子之所以厚賓也。今則無一物之不具，則亦無一而不時焉。以洽百禮，順時物之宜；以和五味，亶芳臭之薦。酌言嘗之，真足以稱嘉美之會，而無尚焉者矣。又何患于弗時也哉？夫其物之曲全如此，優賓之意於是乎至，固非以私惠爲德者，其相孚之情可知矣。抑嘗觀之，《易》曰：「天道下濟而光明，地道卑而上行。」成周之時，衆賢和於朝，而萬物和於野。其君臣上下，恩禮交洽，以至昆蟲闓澤，協氣濡潤。一時燕饗通用之樂，與笙詩相間歌者，有《魚麗》、《嘉魚》、《南山有臺》諸作，可以見上下感應之機，可以見厚倫敦化之道。此周之治所以爲盛也。聖人以是錄
translation_en: …the fragrance of pepper; the bamboo and wooden offering vessels display the beauty of pure and excellent fare. As the guests are urged to drink and cups are exchanged, these things amply manifest the splendor of a joyful banquet: there is no need to fear any lack of excellence. Among provisions, some are prized for their fine flavor; yet if fine flavor is not accompanied by completeness, even delicious fare remains inadequate. Now the gentleman has wine, delicious and plentiful, and I see completeness embodied in its deliciousness. In feeding his guests and giving them drink, no ceremony is omitted; everything is prepared and duly arranged, all set out for their enjoyment. Through the offering and return of cups, the reverence expressed by providing everything is fully made clear: there is no need to fear any lack of completeness. As for valuing provisions simply because they are available, if they are available but out of season, this is mere possession, not the gentleman’s way of treating his guests generously. Now, however, no provision is lacking, and none is out of season. To fulfill the hundred rites, he observes what is fitting for the season’s produce; to harmonize the five flavors, he offers truly fragrant fare. Pour and taste it: it truly merits being called an excellent and beautiful gathering, unsurpassed by any other. Why, then, fear that anything is out of season? With his provisions so complete in every particular, his intention to honor his guests reaches its fullest expression. Certainly he is not one who takes private favors for virtue; the mutual trust between host and guests is plain to see. Moreover, I have considered this saying in the Book of Changes: “The Way of Heaven reaches downward and shines brightly; the Way of Earth lies low and moves upward.” In the flourishing age of Zhou, the many worthy men were harmonious at court, and all things were harmonious in the countryside. Between ruler and ministers, those above and those below, kindness and ritual courtesy flowed freely in both directions; even insects shared in the beneficence, and harmonious vital energy nourished all. Among the musical works then used for both informal and formal banquets, sung alternately with the sheng-accompanied poems, were “Fish in the Weir” (Yu li), “Fine Fish” (Jia yu), and “The Southern Mountain Has Terrace Plants” (Nanshan you tai). In these one can see how those above and below respond to one another, and the way to strengthen human relationships and deepen moral transformation. This is why Zhou’s government flourished. For this reason, the sage recorded…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之於經後世猶有流連之行至忘設醴者惜哉
以是詩告之
綏我眉壽介以繁祉旣右烈考亦右文母
劉格
同考試官教諭甘批〔正大〕
同考試官教諭陳批〔文王昌後武王歸德處意明〕
考試官教諭劉批〔得稱頌體〕
考試官教授林批〔典實〕
周王之祀親也必徵其昌後之慶極其隆焉夫
===
克昌厥後先王之澤所以爲盛也後王奉先而
以是徵之可以觀孝矣此爲武王祀文王之詩
意謂皇考一德格天固有以昌後人而綏孝子
矣然其實何如也彼畀之以福而壽弗綏猶爲
徒福也今則綏我以眉壽焉錫以難老優游泮
奐以延有道之長履大業而致盛治非皇考所
以陰隲於予者乎與之以壽而祉弗隆猶爲徒
壽也今則助我以多福焉俾以戬穀單厚多益
以衍無疆之緒饗宗廟而保子孫非皇考所以
punctuated:
之於經。後世猶有流連之行，至忘設醴者，惜哉！以是詩告之。
綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。旣右烈考，亦右文母。
劉格
同考試官教諭甘批〔正大〕
同考試官教諭陳批〔文王昌後武王歸德處意明〕
考試官教諭劉批〔得稱頌體〕
考試官教授林批〔典實〕
周王之祀親也，必徵其昌後之慶，極其隆焉。夫克昌厥後，先王之澤所以爲盛也。後王奉先而以是徵之，可以觀孝矣。此爲武王祀文王之詩，意謂皇考一德格天，固有以昌後人而綏孝子矣。然其實何如也？彼畀之以福而壽弗綏，猶爲徒福也。今則綏我以眉壽焉，錫以難老，優游泮奐，以延有道之長，履大業而致盛治，非皇考所以陰隲於予者乎？與之以壽而祉弗隆，猶爲徒壽也。今則助我以多福焉，俾以戬穀，單厚多益，以衍無疆之緒，饗宗廟而保子孫，非皇考所以
translation_en:
…in the Classic. Yet in later ages there were still those who indulged in idle wandering, even forgetting to provide sweet wine for their guests. How regrettable! Let this poem admonish them.
“Grant me venerable longevity, and augment it with abundant blessings. Having honored my illustrious deceased father, I also honor my cultured mother.”
Liu Ge
Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: 〔Upright and broad in conception.〕
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning is clear where King Wen brings prosperity to his descendants and King Wu attributes the beneficence to him.〕
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Successfully captures the form of a eulogy.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔Grounded in the classics and substantial.〕
When the king of Zhou sacrificed to his parents, he necessarily took the blessings that made their descendants prosper as evidence of their beneficence, and honored them to the utmost. For the ability to bring prosperity to descendants is what makes the former king’s bounty so abundant. When the succeeding king serves his ancestors and adduces this as evidence, his filial devotion may be seen. This is a poem about King Wu’s sacrifice to King Wen. Its meaning is that my august deceased father, through his undivided virtue, reached Heaven; thus he assuredly had the means to make his descendants prosper and bring peace to his filial son. But how is this realized in practice?
If he bestowed good fortune without also granting longevity, it would be good fortune alone. Now, however, he grants me venerable longevity, bestowing freedom from the infirmities of age and ease and spacious contentment, so that I may long continue in possession of the Way, carry on the great undertaking, and achieve flourishing government. Is this not how my august deceased father gives me his unseen protection?
If he granted longevity without abundant blessings, it would be longevity alone. Now, however, he assists me with many blessings, granting me goodness and prosperity, fullness, abundance, and ever greater benefit, so that I may extend the succession without limit, present offerings in the ancestral temple, and safeguard my descendants. Is this not how my august deceased father…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
左右於予者乎夫福壽之庇吾固以身蒙其休
矣今日光於前人孰非其所遺者也是故明堂
啓而祀事行旣右我烈考焉駿奔對越有以合
萬國之歡心凡行其禮奏其樂煥乎天子之制
而非周邦之舊矣使先王莫開于前吾何以右
之也哉不但是也清廟開而廣牡薦亦右我文
母焉饗祀妥侑有以備四方之禮物凡昭其度
致其文巍乎母后之儀而非立國之初矣使先
王弗昌其後又何以右之也哉然此非倖致者
===
也皆我先王之德之庇也今日克承其休以纘
前業敢忘所自乎嗟夫武王可謂知重其本而
為孝之純也已不自矜其功不自大其德表章
前業世德作求蓋非幸其成而淺於自待者故
孔子稱之曰武王其達孝矣乎惟其孝之達是
以業益弘而慶益萃也集蒼姬之緒而畢未竟
之功夫豈適然者哉記曰惟孝子為能饗親讀
是詩而知武王之孝也
春秋
punctuated:
左右於予者乎？夫福壽之庇，吾固以身蒙其休矣。今日光於前人，孰非其所遺者也？是故明堂啓而祀事行，旣右我烈考焉，駿奔對越，有以合萬國之歡心。凡行其禮、奏其樂，煥乎天子之制，而非周邦之舊矣。使先王莫開于前，吾何以右之也哉？不但是也，清廟開而廣牡薦，亦右我文母焉。饗祀妥侑，有以備四方之禮物。凡昭其度、致其文，巍乎母后之儀，而非立國之初矣。使先王弗昌其後，又何以右之也哉？然此非倖致者也，皆我先王之德之庇也。今日克承其休，以纘前業，敢忘所自乎？嗟夫！武王可謂知重其本，而為孝之純也已。不自矜其功，不自大其德，表章前業，世德作求，蓋非幸其成而淺於自待者。故孔子稱之曰：「武王其達孝矣乎！」惟其孝之達，是以業益弘而慶益萃也。集蒼姬之緒，而畢未竟之功，夫豈適然者哉？記曰：「惟孝子為能饗親。」讀是詩而知武王之孝也。

春秋
translation_en:
…is this not how he sustains and assists me? Through the protection of his blessings and longevity, I have indeed personally received his beneficence. Of all that brings glory to my predecessors today, what has not been bequeathed by him? Thus the Hall of Enlightenment is opened and the sacrifices performed, honoring my illustrious deceased father. Those who hasten to serve and stand reverently before his spirit unite the joyful hearts of the myriad states. The rites performed and the music played display the splendor of the Son of Heaven’s institutions, surpassing the former practices of the Zhou state. Had the former king not opened the way before me, how could I thus honor him?

Nor is this all. The Pure Temple is opened and large bulls are offered, honoring also my cultured mother. Through sacrificial offerings, the settling of the spirits, and the urging of them to partake, the ritual gifts of the four quarters are fully assembled. The rules made manifest and the ceremonial adornments fully displayed present the lofty ceremonial dignity of a queen mother, surpassing that of the state’s beginnings. Had the former king not brought prosperity to his descendants, how could I thus honor her? Yet this was not attained by mere good fortune: it is all the protection afforded by our former king’s virtue. Now that I can receive his beneficence and continue his earlier work, dare I forget its source?

Ah! King Wu may indeed be said to have understood the importance of his roots and to have practiced filial piety in its purity. He neither boasted of his achievements nor exalted his own virtue. He made manifest his predecessors’ accomplishments and sought to carry forward the virtue of successive generations. He was surely no one who merely enjoyed his success through good fortune and expected little of himself. Thus Confucius praised him, saying: “How consummate was King Wu’s filial piety!” Precisely because his filial piety was consummate, his undertaking grew ever greater and blessings gathered ever more abundantly. He brought together the inherited legacy of the venerable Ji house of Zhou and completed its unfinished work. Could this possibly have happened by chance? The Record of Rites says: “Only a filial son can make offerings to his parents.” Reading this poem, we come to understand King Wu’s filial piety.

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春王正月宋公曹伯衞人邾人伐齊狄
救齊〔僖公十有八年〕春晉侯侵曹晉侯
伐衞〔僖公二十有八年〕楚子陳侯隨侯
許男圍蔡〔哀公元年〕
曾迪
考試官敎諭劉批〔得傳旨〕
考試官敎授林批〔有斷制〕
列國報兵之情異春秋隨事而立法焉夫兵一
也是非則存乎其事春秋曲直之準其容以無
===
辯乎嘗考衞之伐齊狄之救齊晉之侵曹伐衞
楚之圍蔡而知人情之得失若是乎其相遠焉
何則楚丘有城衞文之受德於桓也已深聶北
見却齊桓之遺恨於狄也已久夫情之厚者每
懷人之德於不忘而多偏繫之私者則又計小
忿而不釋何衞與狄之異耶一則乘其喪也而
奉少以奪其長一則憫其難也而率衆以解其
危怨隆於可報之恩義急於仇讐之人其得失
果何如耶君子曰情貴乎厚而惡乎薄薄則忍
punctuated:
春，王正月，宋公、曹伯、衞人、邾人伐齊，狄救齊。〔僖公十有八年〕春，晉侯侵曹，晉侯伐衞。〔僖公二十有八年〕楚子、陳侯、隨侯、許男圍蔡。〔哀公元年〕
曾迪
考試官敎諭劉批〔得傳旨〕
考試官敎授林批〔有斷制〕
