列國報兵之情異，春秋隨事而立法焉。夫兵一也，是非則存乎其事。春秋曲直之準，其容以無辯乎？嘗考衞之伐齊、狄之救齊、晉之侵曹伐衞、楚之圍蔡，而知人情之得失，若是乎其相遠焉。何則？楚丘有城，衞文之受德於桓也已深；聶北見却，齊桓之遺恨於狄也已久。夫情之厚者，每懷人之德於不忘；而多偏繫之私者，則又計小忿而不釋。何衞與狄之異耶？一則乘其喪也，而奉少以奪其長；一則憫其難也，而率衆以解其危。怨隆於可報之恩，義急於仇讐之人，其得失果何如耶？君子曰：情貴乎厚，而惡乎薄。薄則忍
translation_en:
“In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Cao, men of Wei, and men of Zhu attacked Qi. The Di came to Qi’s rescue.” 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Xi〕 “In spring, the Marquis of Jin invaded Cao. The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei.” 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕 “The Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Sui, and the Baron of Xu besieged Cai.” 〔First year of Duke Ai〕
Zeng Di
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the purport of the commentary.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔Shows decisive judgment.〕
The motives underlying the various states’ military reprisals differed; the Spring and Autumn Annals establishes its standards according to each event. Warfare is one and the same activity, but its rightness or wrongness lies in the particular circumstances. As the standard of right and wrong, could the Spring and Autumn Annals permit these to go undistinguished? I have examined Wei’s attack on Qi, the Di’s rescue of Qi, Jin’s invasion of Cao and attack on Wei, and Chu’s siege of Cai, and have thereby understood how widely human sentiments can diverge in their propriety and failings.
Why is this? The walls built at Chuqiu show how deeply Duke Wen of Wei had benefited from Duke Huan. The repulse at Niebei shows how long the resentment left by Duke Huan of Qi had endured among the Di. Those whose feelings are generous always remember others’ kindness without forgetting it; those much governed by selfish partiality instead dwell on petty resentments and will not let them go. How different were Wei and the Di! One exploited Qi’s bereavement, supporting the younger son to dispossess the elder; the other pitied Qi’s troubles and led troops to deliver it from danger. In one case, resentment outweighed kindness that deserved repayment; in the other, a sense of duty impelled urgent aid to an enemy. What, then, should we make of their respective merits and failings?
The gentleman says: Generosity of feeling is to be valued, and meanness of feeling detested. Meanness leads to ruthlessness…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而犯順厚則同而無我伐齊之兵其忍心之無
忌救齊之旅其得同物之仁乎故書伐以責衞
書救以許狄者非偏也曲直之不可欺也豈故
伸夷而抑夏歟若塊裸之侮曹衞之獲戾於晉
也可畧宗廟之壞蔡昭之駕禍於楚也實淫夫
心之廣者每矜人之過於不校而無自强之志
者則又委重怨於不圖何晉與楚之異耶一則
懷其侮也而侵伐之必加一則計其暴也而遷
徙之不怨可矜之小過必問終天之重怨不忘
===
其是非果何如耶君子曰心貴乎公而病於私
私則隘而不宏公則正而不拂曹衞之侵其褊
心之所使蔡都之遷其得人情之公乎故書爵
以責晉紀子以予楚者非私也是非之不可枉
也豈故重外而輕內歟是則晉衞俱可惡也而
負德者爲尤楚狄俱可取也而恤患者爲最因
人示法春秋之義精矣抑於是而猶有憾焉無
虧孝公之分可易耶不可易耶桓乃囑人以私
而欲以愛惡定廢置卒之柩方在殯國被危辱
punctuated: 而犯順，厚則同而無我。伐齊之兵，其忍心之無忌；救齊之旅，其得同物之仁乎？故書伐以責衞，書救以許狄者，非偏也，曲直之不可欺也。豈故伸夷而抑夏歟？若塊裸之侮，曹衞之獲戾於晉也，可畧；宗廟之壞，蔡昭之駕禍於楚也，實淫。夫心之廣者，每矜人之過於不校，而無自强之志者，則又委重怨於不圖。何晉與楚之異耶？一則懷其侮也，而侵伐之必加；一則計其暴也，而遷徙之不怨。可矜之小過必問，終天之重怨不忘，其是非果何如耶？君子曰：「心貴乎公，而病於私。私則隘而不宏，公則正而不拂。曹衞之侵，其褊心之所使；蔡都之遷，其得人情之公乎？」故書爵以責晉，紀子以予楚者，非私也，是非之不可枉也。豈故重外而輕內歟？是則晉衞俱可惡也，而負德者爲尤；楚狄俱可取也，而恤患者爲最。因人示法，《春秋》之義精矣。抑於是而猶有憾焉：無虧、孝公之分，可易耶？不可易耶？桓乃囑人以私，而欲以愛惡定廢置。卒之柩方在殯，國被危辱。
translation_en:
…and violate the proper order, whereas generosity brings fellow feeling and freedom from selfishness. Did not the troops attacking Qi display unrestrained cruelty, and the army rescuing Qi attain the benevolence of fellow feeling for others? Thus, recording “attacked” to censure Wei and “rescued” to commend the Di is no partiality: right and wrong cannot be concealed. How could this be a deliberate attempt to exalt the non-Chinese and disparage the Chinese?

As for the insult involving nakedness [?], the offense that Cao and Wei gave Jin could have been overlooked; but the destruction of ancestral temples—the calamity that Zhao of Cai brought upon Chu [?]—was truly excessive. Those of broad sympathies often pity others’ faults and refrain from taking them to task; yet those without the resolve to strengthen themselves also leave grave grievances unattended. How different were Jin and Chu! One brooded over its humiliation and insisted on launching an attack; the other considered the violence it had suffered yet bore no resentment over the relocation [?]. A minor fault deserving indulgence was invariably punished, while a lifelong, grievous wrong was not forgotten [?]. What, then, were the rights and wrongs of these actions?

The gentleman says: “The mind is valued for its impartiality and impaired by selfishness. Selfishness makes it narrow and ungenerous; impartiality makes it upright and free from perversity. Was not the invasion of Cao and Wei driven by narrow-mindedness, while the relocation of Cai’s capital attained the impartiality proper to human feeling?” Thus, recording Jin’s ruler by his rank to censure him, and recording Chu’s ruler as ‘Viscount’ to commend him, is no private favoritism: right and wrong cannot be distorted. How could this be a deliberate attempt to esteem outsiders and slight those within the Chinese realm?

Thus Jin and Wei both deserve condemnation, but the one that betrayed a benefaction is the worse; Chu and the Di both deserve approval, but the one that showed compassion in another’s distress is the better. By using particular persons to reveal standards, the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses its principles with subtle precision.

Yet there remains something to regret here. Could the respective positions of Wukui and Duke Xiao be reversed, or could they not? Duke Huan nevertheless entrusted others with his private wishes, seeking to determine deposition and installation through personal likes and dislikes. In the end, while his coffin still awaited burial, his state suffered peril and humiliation.…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
功利之效其及也淺矣若曹衛與蔡之禍固其
自取然斂盂之盟可重絕耶申胥之賢可少無
耶君子以是知棄人不可以大甚而有國家之
責者甚無比之匪人乎
叔孫舍至自晉昭公二十有四年
康建勳
考試官敎諭劉批典雅
考試官敎授林批謹嚴
春秋於大夫之歸國特表其制行以賢之焉夫
===
執禮以維其身懷忠以衞其主舍之所以爲賢
也君子特表之以示勸也爲宜且夫執叔舍者
晉之逆也其歸舍者晉之順也去逆效順晉若
可嘉矣而以之賢叔舍也何賢乎謂其持身有
禮而事君以忠也何則天下之可畏者莫如强
安於靡而罔克自振者辱也遠辱有道禮莫先
焉彼其坐列於邾夷賂責於范鞅晉之無道亦
甚矣怵於其勢者命斯順其誰能抗之而舍則
能秉禮者是故陳之以周制以却其坐也取之
punctuated:
功利之效，其及也淺矣。若曹衛與蔡之禍，固其自取，然斂盂之盟可重絕耶？申胥之賢可少無耶？君子以是知棄人不可以大甚，而有國家之責者，甚無比之匪人乎！
叔孫舍至自晉。昭公二十有四年。
康建勳
考試官敎諭劉批：典雅。
考試官敎授林批：謹嚴。
春秋於大夫之歸國，特表其制行以賢之焉。夫執禮以維其身，懷忠以衞其主，舍之所以爲賢也。君子特表之以示勸也，爲宜。且夫執叔舍者，晉之逆也；其歸舍者，晉之順也。去逆效順，晉若可嘉矣，而以之賢叔舍也，何賢乎？謂其持身有禮，而事君以忠也。何則？天下之可畏者莫如强，安於靡而罔克自振者辱也。遠辱有道，禮莫先焉。彼其坐列於邾夷，賂責於范鞅，晉之無道亦甚矣！怵於其勢者，命斯順，其誰能抗之？而舍則能秉禮者。是故陳之以周制，以却其坐也；取之
translation_en:
…The effects of pursuing achievement and advantage reach only a little way. As for the calamities of Cao, Wei, and Cai, these states certainly brought them upon themselves. Yet could the covenant at Lianyu [?] be broken yet again? Could the worthiness of Shen Xu be dispensed with even briefly? From this the gentleman knows that one must not go too far in casting others aside, and that those responsible for a state must be especially wary of associating with unworthy men [?].
“Shusun She arrived from Jin.” The twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.
Kang Jianxun.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Careful and rigorous.”
When recording this grand master’s return to his state, the Spring and Autumn Annals especially highlights his conduct in order to commend his worthiness. Holding fast to ritual propriety to sustain his own integrity, and cherishing loyalty to protect his ruler: these are what made She worthy. It is fitting that the gentleman should single him out as an encouragement to others. Now, detaining Shu She was Jin’s act of defiance against what was right; sending She home was Jin’s compliance with it. In abandoning defiance and following what was right, Jin might seem deserving of praise. Yet the text instead uses this occasion to commend Shu She. What was worthy about him? It was that he conducted himself with ritual propriety and served his ruler loyally. Why is this so? Nothing in the world is more fearsome than superior power. To acquiesce in weakness and fail to rouse oneself brings humiliation. There is a way to keep humiliation at a distance, and nothing takes precedence over ritual propriety.
He was assigned a seat alongside the Yi of Zhu, and Fan Yang demanded a bribe from him: Jin’s disregard for the Way had indeed gone far! Those intimidated by its power would obey its commands; who could resist it? Yet She was able to uphold ritual propriety. Thus he set forth the institutions of Zhou to refuse the seat assigned to him; he drew upon …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以冠法而罔狥其求也蓋曰晉之所以辱我者
勢我之所恃以不辱者禮抗節不回君子之所
以係國輕重者也委靡之風熾矣而猶有不畏
强禦如舍者不亦幸哉天下之可懷者莫如君
志於奸而匪克夾義者亂也遠奸有道忠莫先
焉彼其奪政柄而下移逐主君而外播季之不
軌亦甚矣甘於其黨者謀斯協其誰能折之而
舍則能懷忠者是故責之以逐君以正其奸也
祈之以祝宗而罔受其欺也蓋曰君之所以榮
===
我者爵我之所恃以自榮者忠正色立朝君子
之所以能爲有無者也跋扈之習甚矣而猶有
不忘君父如舍者尚亦利哉夫維觀舍之執禮
而后有以見晉人之無禮觀舍之愛君而后有
以顯意如之無君執足以壯國之勢歸足以係
國之危臣道罔戾厥惟賢哉春秋特表其姓氏
而不比於意如之歸之例者得非彰其賢以示
勸乎雖然國有賢臣惟福之植然而揚州乾侯
之禍終不能免豈賢者無益於人國耶良由昭
punctuated: 以冠法而罔狥其求也。蓋曰：「晉之所以辱我者，勢；我之所恃以不辱者，禮。」抗節不回，君子之所以係國輕重者也。委靡之風熾矣，而猶有不畏强禦如舍者，不亦幸哉！天下之可懷者莫如君，志於奸而匪克夾義者，亂也。遠奸有道，忠莫先焉。彼其奪政柄而下移，逐主君而外播，季之不軌亦甚矣。甘於其黨者，謀斯協，其誰能折之？而舍則能懷忠者。是故責之以逐君，以正其奸也；祈之以祝宗，而罔受其欺也。蓋曰：「君之所以榮我者，爵；我之所恃以自榮者，忠。」正色立朝，君子之所以能爲有無者也。跋扈之習甚矣，而猶有不忘君父如舍者，尚亦利哉！夫維觀舍之執禮，而后有以見晉人之無禮；觀舍之愛君，而后有以顯意如之無君。執足以壯國之勢，歸足以係國之危，臣道罔戾，厥惟賢哉！春秋特表其姓氏，而不比於意如之歸之例者，得非彰其賢以示勸乎？雖然，國有賢臣，惟福之植，然而揚州乾侯之禍終不能免，豈賢者無益於人國耶？良由昭
translation_en:
…He appealed to the rules governing caps [?] and would not comply with their demands. It was as though he said: “What Jin uses to humiliate me is power; what I rely upon to escape humiliation is ritual propriety.” Upholding his integrity without wavering—this is how a gentleman determines the standing of his state. The habit of feeble submission was rampant, yet there was still someone like She who did not fear the powerful and overbearing. Was this not fortunate?

Of all under Heaven who deserve devoted regard, none surpasses one’s ruler. To set one’s heart on treachery and fail to uphold righteousness is disorder. There is a way to keep clear of treachery, and nothing takes precedence over loyalty. Seizing the reins of government and transferring authority downward, driving out his sovereign and sending him into exile—the lawlessness of Ji was extreme indeed. Those content to belong to his faction joined in his plots; who could thwart him? Yet She was able to remain loyal. Thus he reproached Ji for expelling his ruler, exposing his treachery; he appealed through the ancestral invocators [?] and would not be taken in by his deception. It was as though he said: “What my ruler uses to honor me is rank; what I rely upon to bring myself honor is loyalty.” Standing at court with a resolute countenance—this is how a gentleman makes his presence or absence consequential. The habit of domineering arrogance was severe, yet there was still someone like She who did not forget his ruler and father. Was this not a benefit after all?

Only by observing She’s adherence to ritual propriety can we perceive the men of Jin’s lack of propriety; only by observing She’s love for his ruler can we reveal Yiru’s disregard for his ruler. In captivity he was able to strengthen his state’s standing; on returning he was able to bear upon its peril. Never deviating from the proper way of a minister, was he not indeed worthy? The Spring and Autumn Annals expressly records his surname and personal name, rather than treating his return according to the precedent of Yiru’s return. Was this not to make his worth manifest and encourage others?

Nevertheless, having a worthy minister plants the seeds of good fortune for a state, yet the calamities of Yangzhou [?] and Qianhou could not ultimately be averted. Can it be that worthy men bring no benefit to a state? The true reason lay with Zhao…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
公任之不專信之不篤是以强臣之逼卒不可
制千乘之尊求爲一匹夫而不可得矣噫昭之
弗克厥終不足惜也併舍之賢而無以自效君
子重爲之三歎焉
禮記
禮之以少爲貴者以其内心也德產之致
也精微觀天下之物無可以稱其德者
如此則得不以少爲貴乎是故君子愼
其獨也
===
譚維鼎
考試官敎諭劉批〔說理詳盡〕
考試官敎授林批〔明整〕
記者原禮有宜於存誠者因著君子存誠之故
焉夫天地妙生物之德而君子之祀亦難乎其
爲報矣然則不以物而以誠也有以哉禮器君
子蓋謂禮不同或豐或殺惟其稱而已矣是故
君子之行禮也郊以報天而不尚夫多儀社以
神地而不貴於備物者誠以恭敬不足又何牲
punctuated:
公任之不專，信之不篤，是以强臣之逼卒不可制，千乘之尊求爲一匹夫而不可得矣。噫！昭之弗克厥終，不足惜也；併舍之賢而無以自效，君子重爲之三歎焉。

禮記
禮之以少爲貴者，以其内心也。德產之致也精微，觀天下之物，無可以稱其德者。如此，則得不以少爲貴乎？是故君子愼其獨也。

譚維鼎
考試官敎諭劉批〔說理詳盡〕
考試官敎授林批〔明整〕

記者原禮有宜於存誠者，因著君子存誠之故焉。夫天地妙生物之德，而君子之祀亦難乎其爲報矣。然則不以物而以誠也，有以哉！禮器君子蓋謂禮不同，或豐或殺，惟其稱而已矣。是故君子之行禮也，郊以報天而不尚夫多儀，社以神地而不貴於備物者，誠以恭敬不足，又何牲
translation_en:
…Duke Zhao did not entrust him with undivided authority or place firm confidence in him. Thus the pressure exerted by powerful ministers ultimately could not be checked, and even with the dignity of a ruler of a thousand chariots, he could not obtain his wish to become an ordinary man. Alas! That Duke Zhao failed to bring his course to a successful end is not itself cause for regret; but that even She, worthy as he was, had no means to prove his effectiveness makes the gentleman sigh deeply for him again and again.

Record of Rites
“Where ritual values small quantities, it does so because of the inner heart. The utmost expression of generative virtue is subtle and refined; among all things under Heaven, none can match that virtue. This being so, how could small quantities fail to be prized? Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.”

Tan Weiding
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The reasoning is thorough and exhaustive.〕
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: 〔Clear and orderly.〕

The compiler of the Record traces the reason why certain features of ritual are suited to preserving sincerity, and thereby makes clear why the gentleman preserves sincerity. Heaven and Earth exercise their wondrous virtue in bringing living things into being, and even the gentleman’s sacrifices can scarcely repay it. There is thus good reason to rely on sincerity rather than material offerings! The gentleman of the “Ritual Vessels” chapter [?] presumably means that rites differ: some are elaborate and others reduced, but all that matters is their fittingness. Thus, when the gentleman performs rites, he offers the suburban sacrifice to repay Heaven without esteeming a multiplicity of ceremonies, and sacrifices at the altar of the soil to honor Earth as divine without valuing a full array of offerings. This is truly because, if reverence is insufficient, what can sacrificial animals …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
幣之足云而內志允孚自致神祇之來格矣所
以然者蓋有以見天地之德雖極於至大而無
外而其發育之妙則入於至密而無形故盈天
下之物皆天之所生也然其所以生者孰得而
測其機緘哉皆地之所產也然其所以產者孰
得而窺其蘊奧哉夫天地之德密緻精微如此
縱盡取天下之物以報其功吾見物有盡而功
無窮其能稱其德也乎孰若竭內志之誠以少
為貴使實意孚而幽明達庶或盡吾心焉耳以
===
故行禮君子燔柴於泰壇虛文弗事也瘞埋於
泰折縟禮弗尚也防物訖欲而小心以昭事上
帝者豫養於對越之先閑邪存誠而齋戒以神
明其德者慎獨於駿奔之始則精明之德至而
將享之道盡矣尚何事於盡物也哉由是觀之
則知行禮者不在於儀文而在於誠心之感也
今之君子宜知所法矣抑君子無弗誠也祭祀
為至祭祀無弗誠也郊社為至故禮行於郊而
百神受職禮行於社而百貨可極誠而已矣誠
punctuated: 幣之足云，而內志允孚，自致神祇之來格矣。所以然者，蓋有以見天地之德，雖極於至大而無外，而其發育之妙，則入於至密而無形。故盈天下之物，皆天之所生也，然其所以生者，孰得而測其機緘哉？皆地之所產也，然其所以產者，孰得而窺其蘊奧哉？夫天地之德密緻精微如此，縱盡取天下之物以報其功，吾見物有盡而功無窮，其能稱其德也乎？孰若竭內志之誠，以少為貴，使實意孚而幽明達，庶或盡吾心焉耳。以故行禮君子，燔柴於泰壇，虛文弗事也；瘞埋於泰折，縟禮弗尚也。防物訖欲，而小心以昭事上帝者，豫養於對越之先；閑邪存誠，而齋戒以神明其德者，慎獨於駿奔之始。則精明之德至，而將享之道盡矣，尚何事於盡物也哉？由是觀之，則知行禮者，不在於儀文，而在於誠心之感也。今之君子宜知所法矣。抑君子無弗誠也，祭祀為至；祭祀無弗誠也，郊社為至。故禮行於郊，而百神受職；禮行於社，而百貨可極。誠而已矣。誠
translation_en:
…what could offerings of silk avail? When the inward purpose is truly sincere, it naturally brings the spirits of Heaven and Earth into attendance. The reason is that, although the potency of Heaven and Earth extends to the utmost vastness, with nothing beyond it, the marvel of their nourishing and developing things reaches into the utmost intricacy and has no visible form. Thus, all the things that fill the world are generated by Heaven; yet who can fathom the hidden workings by which it generates them? They are all produced by Earth; yet who can discern the profound mysteries by which it produces them? The potency of Heaven and Earth is so intricate, refined, and subtle that, even if one gathered everything in the world to repay their achievements, I see that these things would be exhausted while those achievements remained inexhaustible. Could such offerings be commensurate with their potency? How much better to expend fully the sincerity of one’s inward purpose, valuing few offerings, so that genuine intent finds a response and communication passes between the unseen and visible realms! In this way, perhaps, one may fully express one’s heart.

For this reason, the gentleman performing ritual burns wood on the Great Altar, without attending to empty formalities; he buries offerings at the Great Square Altar, without esteeming elaborate rites. Guarding against external distractions and curbing desires [?], he carefully and reverently serves the Lord on High, cultivating this disposition beforehand, before standing in His presence. Keeping out deviance and preserving sincerity, he fasts and observes abstinence to render his virtue spiritually luminous, remaining watchful over himself even when alone, before hastening to perform his service. Then the virtue of purity and illumination reaches its fullest extent, and the way of presenting offerings is completely fulfilled. What further need is there to exhaust all material things? Viewed thus, the performance of ritual clearly rests upon the response elicited by a sincere heart. The gentlemen of today should know what to emulate.

Moreover, the gentleman is sincere in everything, but sincerity reaches its height in sacrifice. All sacrifices require sincerity, but it reaches its height in the suburban sacrifice to Heaven and the sacrifice to the soil. Thus, when the suburban rites are performed, the many spirits receive their appointed duties; when the rites to the soil are performed, the abundance of all goods can be brought to its fullest extent. It is sincerity alone. Sincerity…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則天地斯格矣格則百順斯備矣弗誠弗敬不
能以交人而况鬼神乎書曰鬼神無常享享于
克誠易曰東鄰殺牛不如西鄰之禴祭蓋言誠
也
禮樂皆得謂之有德德者得也
黃榜
考試官教諭劉批典則
考試官教授林批理到
記者原德之所由名而申其義以見君子知樂
===
之妙也蓋禮樂之道大矣兼而有之則有德之
名歸之矣尚有待於外哉且夫一貫而無二者
禮樂之情同也會通以成德者善體禮樂者也
君子蓋嘗審音知樂而幾於禮矣由是禮之寓
於倫理者匪徒知其物采之施而已也神而明
之有以析其奧樂之發於聲音者匪徒知其器
數之宣而已也默而識之有以通其微夫惟析
禮之奧則有得乎禮矣會道器而體之而治躬
之妙豈有遺乎通樂之微則有得乎樂矣兼情
punctuated:
則天地斯格矣，格則百順斯備矣。弗誠弗敬，不能以交人，而况鬼神乎？《書》曰：「鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」《易》曰：「東鄰殺牛，不如西鄰之禴祭。」蓋言誠也。

禮樂皆得謂之有德德者得也

黃榜

考試官教諭劉批：典則。
考試官教授林批：理到。

記者原德之所由名，而申其義，以見君子知樂之妙也。蓋禮樂之道大矣，兼而有之，則有德之名歸之矣，尚有待於外哉？且夫一貫而無二者，禮樂之情同也；會通以成德者，善體禮樂者也。君子蓋嘗審音知樂而幾於禮矣。由是禮之寓於倫理者，匪徒知其物采之施而已也，神而明之，有以析其奧；樂之發於聲音者，匪徒知其器數之宣而已也，默而識之，有以通其微。夫惟析禮之奧，則有得乎禮矣，會道器而體之，而治躬之妙豈有遺乎？通樂之微，則有得乎樂矣，兼情
translation_en:
…then Heaven and Earth are moved to respond. When they respond, every favorable condition is fully present. Without sincerity and reverence, one cannot establish communion even with other people—how much less with ghosts and spirits! The Book of Documents says: “Ghosts and spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those of one who can be sincere.” The Book of Changes says: “The eastern neighbor’s slaughter of an ox is inferior to the western neighbor’s modest yue sacrifice.” These passages speak of sincerity.

“When ritual and music are both attained, this is called possessing virtue; virtue means attainment.”

Huang Bang

Examiner Liu, Instructor in a county Confucian school, comments: “Classical and exemplary.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor in a prefectural Confucian school, comments: “The principles are fully grasped.”

The compiler of the Record of Rites traces the origin of the designation ‘virtue’ and elaborates its meaning, thereby revealing the subtlety of the gentleman’s understanding of music. The Way of ritual and music is indeed great. When someone possesses both, the designation ‘possessor of virtue’ belongs to him. What further need has he to depend on anything external? What runs through them as a single thread, without division, is the shared underlying substance of ritual and music. Those who bring them together into a comprehensive understanding and thereby perfect their virtue are those who excel at embodying ritual and music. The gentleman has indeed examined tones, understood music, and thereby approached an understanding of ritual.

Thus, concerning ritual as it inheres in the ordered relationships of human life, he does more than merely understand the deployment of its objects and ornamentation: through a spiritually penetrating understanding, he can discern its profundities. Concerning music as it issues in sounds, he does more than merely understand its expression through instruments and numerical measures: through silent apprehension, he can comprehend its subtleties. Only by discerning the profundities of ritual does he attain ritual. Bringing together the Way and its concrete manifestations and embodying them, could he leave anything unmastered in the subtle art of ordering his own conduct? By comprehending the subtleties of music, he attains music. Embracing its inner feelings…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文而有之而治心之理其咸備乎合和序於一
致而粹然無偏達於禮而不達於樂者固不得
而擬之也混中和於一途而渾然無迹達於樂
而不達於禮者固不得而名之也不謂之有德
乎然是德也非襲取而強名也蓋至道克篤於
庸行而允蹈實踐各造其精微之域融會貫通
和序之妙其心領之矣至理恒熟於素履而極
深研幾咸達於性安之境交暢洋溢中和之實
其神會之矣故曰德者得也舍是不足以言德
===
矣何以盡知樂之妙也哉大抵禮樂一致也和
序一機也自一身而達之天下皆是物也能全
之者在有諸已而已有諸已則可以察倫可以
知政可以格神可以易俗而其用溥矣否則其
理昧其志荒聽古樂則唯恐卧而心迹之判遠
矣故曰士之所難者在有諸已又曰待其人而
後行
第貳場
論
punctuated:
文而有之，而治心之理其咸備乎？合和序於一致，而粹然無偏，達於禮而不達於樂者，固不得而擬之也。混中和於一途，而渾然無迹，達於樂而不達於禮者，固不得而名之也。不謂之有德乎？然是德也，非襲取而強名也。蓋至道克篤於庸行，而允蹈實踐，各造其精微之域，融會貫通，和序之妙，其心領之矣。至理恒熟於素履，而極深研幾，咸達於性安之境，交暢洋溢，中和之實，其神會之矣。故曰：「德者，得也。」舍是不足以言德矣，何以盡知樂之妙也哉？大抵禮樂一致也，和序一機也，自一身而達之天下，皆是物也。能全之者，在有諸已而已。有諸已，則可以察倫，可以知政，可以格神，可以易俗，而其用溥矣。否則其理昧，其志荒，聽古樂則唯恐卧，而心迹之判遠矣。故曰：「士之所難者，在有諸已。」又曰：「待其人而後行。」

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…and its outward forms, possessing them together: would not the principles for ordering the mind then be fully present? He unites harmony and order into a single whole, pure and free of partiality; one who understands ritual but not music certainly cannot compare with him. He blends equilibrium and harmony into a single course, seamlessly and without trace; one who understands music but not ritual certainly cannot be described in these terms. Should he not be called a man of virtue? Yet this virtue is neither borrowed from elsewhere nor given that name by force.

For he firmly establishes the utmost Way in everyday conduct and faithfully puts it into practice, reaching the most subtle depths of each aspect. Comprehending and connecting them throughout, he grasps in his heart the marvels of harmony and order. The highest principles become thoroughly familiar through his habitual conduct; plumbing the depths and examining the subtlest beginnings, he reaches in every respect the state in which his nature rests at ease. As these principles flow freely together and overflow, he apprehends in spirit the substance of equilibrium and harmony. Thus it is said: “Virtue means attainment.” Apart from this, there is no adequate basis for speaking of virtue. How, then, could one fully understand the marvels of music?

In general, ritual and music form a unity; harmony and order share a single mainspring. From one’s own person to all under Heaven, it is this same thing throughout. The ability to preserve it whole lies simply in possessing it within oneself. Possessing it within oneself, one can discern human relationships, understand government, reach the spirits, and transform customs: its application is far-reaching indeed. Otherwise, one’s understanding of its principles is obscure and one’s aspirations are neglected; when listening to ancient music, one fears only falling asleep, and the gulf between one’s mind and outward conduct is wide indeed. Thus it is said: “What is difficult for a scholar is to possess it within himself.” It is also said: “It awaits the right person before it can be put into practice.”

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孔子之謂集大成
梁式
同考試官教諭王批以大成為本體足見深造
同考試官教諭劉批俱自胸中流出
同考試官教諭徐批集大成處發得精新似非文
章之士
考試官教諭劉批是學孔孟而有得者
考試官教授林批不蹈襲
夫子之道不可以名言者也夫可名言者則有
===
迹有迹則小不可名言者則無迹無迹則大大
者理也夫子之道具眾理而無迹是以見其用
而不見其體見其出之之時而不見其所以時
出之妙又烏可以名言哉不可名言而謂之曰
孔子之謂集大成而後不可名言者益見矣夫
大成何為者也孟子以夫子之道至大難形故
借樂以形之而非以為真有所成也嘗為之說
曰可器者則有成不器者則無成有所成者則
泥無所成者則通夫子通乎晝夜之道而知故
punctuated:
孔子之謂集大成
梁式
同考試官教諭王批：以大成為本體，足見深造。
同考試官教諭劉批：俱自胸中流出。
同考試官教諭徐批：集大成處發得精新，似非文章之士。
考試官教諭劉批：是學孔孟而有得者。
考試官教授林批：不蹈襲。
夫子之道，不可以名言者也。夫可名言者則有迹，有迹則小；不可名言者則無迹，無迹則大。大者，理也。夫子之道具眾理而無迹，是以見其用而不見其體，見其出之之時而不見其所以時出之妙，又烏可以名言哉？不可名言，而謂之曰：「孔子之謂集大成。」而後不可名言者益見矣。夫大成何為者也？孟子以夫子之道至大難形，故借樂以形之，而非以為真有所成也。嘗為之說曰：可器者則有成，不器者則無成；有所成者則泥，無所成者則通。夫子通乎晝夜之道而知，故
translation_en:
“Confucius Is Said to Have Gathered Together the Great Consummation”
Liang Shi
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “He takes the great consummation as the fundamental substance: this amply demonstrates profound attainment.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It all flows from his own heart.”
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “His exposition of ‘gathering together the great consummation’ is incisive and fresh. He seems to be more than a mere man of letters.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who has studied Confucius and Mencius and gained real understanding.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “He does not follow established formulas.”
The Master’s Way cannot be named or expressed in words. Whatever can be named and expressed has traces; what has traces is limited. Whatever cannot be named or expressed has no traces; what has no traces is great. This greatness is principle. The Master’s Way encompasses all principles yet leaves no traces. Thus we see its functioning but not its substance; we see the occasions on which he brings it forth, but not the subtle workings by which he brings it forth at the fitting time. How, then, could it be named or expressed? Although it cannot be named or expressed, one says of it: “Confucius is said to have gathered together the great consummation.” Only then does what cannot be named or expressed become still more apparent. What, then, is this great consummation? Mencius considered the Master’s Way so supremely great that it was difficult to give it form, and therefore borrowed music to give it form. He did not mean that it truly possessed some fixed completion. I have sought to explain it thus: what can be made into a vessel has a fixed completion; what is not confined to a vessel has no fixed completion. What has a fixed completion is constrained; what has no fixed completion is all-pervading. The Master comprehends the Way of day and night and possesses understanding; therefore …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以所撰本政書上
獻者伏以
賢君觀萬化之原因時立政忠臣思一得之益
隨事昌言稽往牒以成編本生民之急務
敢塵
黼扆庸效芻蕘臣勳誠惶誠恐頓首稽首竊
惟
國保於民
皇建有極所其無逸知小人稼穡之依率由舊
===
章爲王業艱難之故實帝王心法之要爲
民生衣食之源自井牧肇于黃虞經制已
備至貢助行之湯禹法度爲詳以迄成周
尤重民事風歌七月鴻鴈無中澤之哀雅
善三單草莽皆在公之役分田制祿足用
安邊經界正而井地均什一行而頌聲作
慨秦之世阡陌旣開由唐以來兵農遂二
趙過搜粟無補海内空虛陳靖司農祗益
編氓耗竭反裘以負涸澤而漁何有乎正
punctuated:
以所撰《本政書》上獻者。伏以，賢君觀萬化之原，因時立政；忠臣思一得之益，隨事昌言。稽往牒以成編，本生民之急務，敢塵黼扆，庸效芻蕘。
臣勳誠惶誠恐，頓首稽首。竊惟，國保於民，皇建有極。所其無逸，知小人稼穡之依；率由舊章，爲王業艱難之故實。帝王心法之要，爲民生衣食之源。自井牧肇于黃虞，經制已備；至貢助行之湯禹，法度爲詳。以迄成周，尤重民事。風歌七月，鴻鴈無中澤之哀；雅善三單，草莽皆在公之役。分田制祿，足用安邊。經界正而井地均，什一行而頌聲作。慨秦之世，阡陌旣開；由唐以來，兵農遂二。趙過搜粟，無補海内空虛；陳靖司農，祗益編氓耗竭。反裘以負，涸澤而漁，何有乎正
translation_en:
…concerning the presentation to the throne of the Book on the Foundations of Governance (Ben zheng shu), which I have composed. I humbly submit: a worthy ruler observes the source of all transformations and establishes government suited to the times; a loyal minister considers how even one useful insight might benefit the realm and speaks forthrightly as circumstances require. Consulting earlier records to compile this work, I have taken the people's urgent needs as its foundation. I venture to trouble Your Majesty's august presence with it, thereby offering the humble counsel of a grass cutter or wood gatherer.
Your servant Xun, in deepest fear and trepidation, bows his head and knocks his forehead upon the ground. I humbly reflect that the state is preserved through its people, and the sovereign establishes the supreme standard. Making freedom from ease his dwelling, he understands the farming upon which common people depend; following the old statutes, he takes the difficulties of founding royal rule as historical precedents. The essentials of the sovereigns' teaching of the mind are the source of the people's clothing and food. From the inception of the well-field and pastoral land systems under Huangdi and Shun, institutions were already fully established; when the tribute and labor-assistance systems were practiced under Tang and Yu, their regulations became detailed. By the flourishing Zhou, the people's affairs received particular attention. The Airs sang of “The Seventh Month,” and the wild geese had no cause to lament amid the marshes; the Court Hymns praised “three dan” [?], and even those in the grassy wilds served in public labor. Fields were apportioned and stipends regulated, supplies made sufficient and the frontiers secured. When field boundaries were properly fixed, well-field allotments were equitable; when the tithe was practiced, songs of praise arose. Alas, in Qin times the field boundaries were opened up; from the Tang onward, soldiers and farmers became separate groups. Zhao Guo's grain collection did nothing to remedy the depletion of the realm; Chen Jing's administration of agriculture only further exhausted the registered common people. This was like wearing a fur coat inside out to carry a load, or draining a marsh to catch its fish. How could there be any rectification …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
德利用厚生惡在爲勞來旋定安集潢池
兆釁石壕吏之朘削尤深碩鼠傷殘安上
門之流離具在
近自建炎之歲
上遡開國之初兩稅之征數已增于七倍九
伐之法人不知者百年皆緣經理之疎未
獲雍熙之效惟
明哲以庶績其凝爲泰在農夫以百畝不易爲
憂久激愚衷曷酬
===
洪造兹蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
繼天駿命
垂世丕圖民安而視若未安
治先邦本道至而望猶未至
功妙時幾從善如圜進人加膝故自忘其固
陋爰陳本政之書亦願
察於細微壹明王者之制夫一而占田五十
畝井一而爲夫十六人由兵馬以及餘夫皆
punctuated:
德、利用、厚生，惡在爲勞來、旋定、安集？潢池兆釁，石壕吏之朘削尤深；碩鼠傷殘，安上門之流離具在。近自建炎之歲，上遡開國之初，兩稅之征，數已增于七倍；九伐之法，人不知者百年。皆緣經理之疎，未獲雍熙之效。惟明哲以庶績其凝爲泰，在農夫以百畝不易爲憂。久激愚衷，曷酬洪造？
兹蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，繼天駿命，垂世丕圖。民安而視若未安，治先邦本；道至而望猶未至，功妙時幾。從善如圜，進人加膝。故自忘其固陋，爰陳本政之書，亦願察於細微，壹明王者之制。夫一而占田五十畝，井一而爲夫十六人，由兵馬以及餘夫，皆
translation_en:
…rectifying virtue, promoting useful resources, and enriching the people's livelihood—where are the efforts to encourage them, bring them back, settle them, and gather them in peace? Trouble brews at Huangchi; the exactions exemplified by the bailiff of Shihao grow still more severe. The great rats ravage the people, and the displaced at Anshang Gate are all there to see. From the more recent Jianyan years, tracing back to the founding of the dynasty, the amount collected under the Two-Tax system has already increased sevenfold; the rules for the nine kinds of punitive campaigns have been unknown to people for a hundred years. All this results from neglect in administration, which has failed to achieve harmony and prosperity. The enlightened ruler regards the consolidation of all achievements as peace; the farmer worries that his hundred mu cannot be properly tended. These matters have long stirred my ignorant heart. How can I repay Your Majesty's immense beneficence?
Now, reverently encountering [four circles in the text: 〇〇〇〇], who succeeds to Heaven's great mandate and transmits a grand design to future generations: though the people are secure, you regard them as not yet secure, giving priority in government to the foundation of the state. Though the Way has been attained, you aspire as though it were not yet attained; your accomplishments lie in discerning the subtle beginnings of events. You follow good counsel as readily as a circle turns and raise worthy men as though placing them upon your knees. Thus, forgetting my own narrowness and ignorance, I submit this writing on the fundamentals of government. I also hope that you will examine its fine details and make fully clear the institutions of the true king. Each man is to hold fifty mu of land, and each well-field unit is to comprise sixteen men. From the troops and horses to the surplus adult males, all …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
自隷農而至匹婦斂散有節適緩急之宜
勞逸相均便分番之直足兵足食有土有
財是謂因略致詳復井田之舊庶幾以人
立政增
祖武之光事在可行言皆有據臣業慙學稼教
不逮於蘇湖祿過代耕志欲裨於海嶽雖
非
帝籍不刊之典誠為平生獨得之愚行以十年
化未三代者未之有也伏願
===
端本善則
明物察倫
先天下之憂
謹日中之戒
儆於有位
養賢以及萬民
紹乃前聞
雪恥而酬
九廟
punctuated: 自隷農而至匹婦，斂散有節，適緩急之宜；勞逸相均，便分番之直。足兵足食，有土有財，是謂因略致詳，復井田之舊。庶幾以人立政，增祖武之光。事在可行，言皆有據。臣業慙學稼，教不逮於蘇湖；祿過代耕，志欲裨於海嶽。雖非帝籍不刊之典，誠為平生獨得之愚。行以十年，化未三代者，未之有也。伏願端本善則，明物察倫，先天下之憂，謹日中之戒，儆於有位，養賢以及萬民，紹乃前聞，雪恥而酬九廟。
translation_en:
…from dependent cultivators down to ordinary women. Collection and distribution would be regulated to meet needs both routine and urgent; toil and rest would be apportioned evenly, facilitating service in rotating shifts. With sufficient troops and sufficient food, with land and wealth, this is what is meant by working from a general outline toward detailed arrangements and restoring the old well-field system. Thus, perhaps, government could be established through the right people, adding glory to the footsteps of Your Majesty’s ancestors. These measures are practicable, and every assertion has grounds.

Your servant is ashamed of his attainments in learning agriculture; his teaching falls short of that of Suzhou and Huzhou. His stipend exceeds what would suffice in place of farming, yet his ambition is to contribute something to the seas and mountains of Your Majesty’s realm. Although this is no immutable canon of the imperial records [?], it is truly a humble insight independently attained over a lifetime. Were it implemented for ten years, there could be no failure to attain a transformation matching that of the Three Dynasties.

I humbly beseech Your Majesty to rectify the foundations and perfect the standards; distinguish things and discern human relationships; take concern for the world’s troubles before others do; heed the warning implicit in the sun at noon; admonish those holding office; nourish the worthy and extend that care to all the people; carry forward your ancestors’ renown; and wipe away humiliation to requite the ancestors in the nine ancestral temples…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
垂衣致治
卑服即功
調玉燭於氤氳占太平之有象
鼓仁風以披拂衍
盛世於無疆臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以本政書十三篇奉
表隨
進以
===
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
蕭來鳳
同考試官教諭蕭 批 不但善陳
聖善德且忠愛之心見於言外
考試官教諭劉 批 大雅之作
考試官教授林 批 有胸襟
punctuated:
垂衣致治，卑服即功，調玉燭於氤氳，占太平之有象；鼓仁風以披拂，衍盛世於無疆。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以本政書十三篇奉表隨進以聞。
第叁場，策，第一問。
蕭來鳳。
同考試官教諭蕭批：不但善陳聖善德，且忠愛之心見於言外。
考試官教諭劉批：大雅之作。
考試官教授林批：有胸襟。
translation_en:
…Let good government be achieved with robes hanging loosely, and let work be undertaken in humble clothing. Bring the seasons into harmonious order amid the mingling cosmic energies, discerning therein manifest signs of Great Peace; stir the winds of benevolence to spread everywhere, extending this flourishing age without limit. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and profound trepidation. I respectfully submit the thirteen chapters of the Book on the Fundamentals of Government (Benzheng shu), accompanied by this memorial, for Your Majesty’s attention.
Third Session. Policy Essays. First Question.
Xiao Laifeng.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “He not only skillfully expounds the sage’s excellent virtues [?]; his loyal devotion is also apparent beyond the words themselves.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “A work of great elegance.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: “He has breadth of mind.”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝王之創業垂統也當有以昭曠代之宏
規而其繼體守成也當有以隆中興之大
業夫創業之君嗣王是法必宏規有立而
後人為可繼繼體之君先烈是揚必大業
克隆而前人為益光於乎此我
太祖高皇帝之法古為治而典章文物追蹤於
二帝三王之盛
皇上之經綸大業巍巍足稱中興之盛歟粤昔
秦失其鹿天下競逐漢高起自豐沛手提
===
三尺不五載而成帝業故史臣班彪贊其
所以興者有五曰帝王之苗裔曰體貌多
竒異曰神武有徵應曰寛明而仁恕曰知
人善任使言其取天下於亡秦者以是也
有宋不競元夷猾夏我
太祖高皇帝不階尺土奮起布衣亦不十餘年
而正大統故
當代文臣宋濂述
聖祖之所以興者有六曰功高萬古曰得國之
punctuated: 帝王之創業垂統也，當有以昭曠代之宏規；而其繼體守成也，當有以隆中興之大業。夫創業之君，嗣王是法，必宏規有立，而後人為可繼；繼體之君，先烈是揚，必大業克隆，而前人為益光。於乎！此我太祖高皇帝之法古為治，而典章文物追蹤於二帝三王之盛，皇上之經綸大業巍巍，足稱中興之盛歟！粤昔秦失其鹿，天下競逐，漢高起自豐沛，手提三尺，不五載而成帝業。故史臣班彪贊其所以興者有五：曰帝王之苗裔，曰體貌多竒異，曰神武有徵應，曰寛明而仁恕，曰知人善任使。言其取天下於亡秦者，以是也。有宋不競，元夷猾夏，我太祖高皇帝不階尺土，奮起布衣，亦不十餘年而正大統。故當代文臣宋濂述聖祖之所以興者有六：曰功高萬古，曰得國之
translation_en:
When emperors and kings found a dynasty and establish its succession, they must make manifest a grand design outstanding across the ages; when they inherit the throne and preserve what has been achieved, they must advance the great undertaking of dynastic resurgence. A founding ruler is the model for succeeding kings: only when his grand design has been established can later generations carry it forward. A ruler who inherits the throne exalts his predecessors’ achievements: only when the great undertaking flourishes do those predecessors gain still greater glory. Ah! Thus our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, modeled his government on antiquity, and his institutions and cultural accomplishments followed in the footsteps of the flourishing age of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. His Majesty’s great undertaking of ordering the realm is lofty indeed—surely it merits being called a glorious dynastic resurgence!

In former times, Qin lost its deer—the empire—and all under Heaven competed to pursue it. Gaozu of Han rose from Feng and Pei, wielding a three-foot sword, and in fewer than five years established his imperial dominion. Thus the historian Ban Biao, in praising him, identified five reasons for his rise: he was descended from emperors and kings; his physique and appearance displayed many extraordinary features; his divine martial prowess was attested by signs; he was generous, discerning, humane, and forgiving; and he understood men and employed them well. These, he said, were the reasons he took the empire from the fallen Qin.

The Song proved weak, and the Yuan barbarians threw the Chinese realm into disorder. Our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, rose vigorously from the common people without so much as a foot of territory to build upon; he too established the legitimate imperial succession within little more than a decade. Thus Song Lian, a civil official of that time, set forth six reasons for the Sacred Ancestor’s rise: first, his achievements surpassed those of all ages; second, the manner in which he acquired the realm …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
正曰獨稟全智曰敬天勤民曰家法之嚴
曰兵政有統言其復我中國帝王之統者
以是也夫我
太祖高皇帝之取天下得國之正雖與漢高同
而其復華夏於腥羶挽起生民於塗炭者
厥功尤偉固非漢高之所可同矣故曰功
高萬古者也然而漢高代秦之興去古未
遠先王之典則尚存六經之遺籍未散高
帝不能收拾補綴其殘壞以追三代之隆
===
而以苟簡之規模自足三章約法之外一
切承襲秦舊無所建明卒使先王典禮湮
而不章論治者不無遺恨於高帝也若我
太祖高皇帝之興乃在亡秦千載之後矣觀其
草創之初首建
宗社以重邦國之本繼立庠序以先郡縣之化
大業既定稽古立法制禮以序倫作樂以
宣化建官以分職明教以齊俗凡所制作
盡反元政典章文物直追前古之隆有非
punctuated:
正，曰獨稟全智，曰敬天勤民，曰家法之嚴，曰兵政有統，言其復我中國帝王之統者以是也。夫我太祖高皇帝之取天下，得國之正雖與漢高同，而其復華夏於腥羶、挽起生民於塗炭者，厥功尤偉，固非漢高之所可同矣。故曰功高萬古者也。然而漢高代秦之興，去古未遠，先王之典則尚存，六經之遺籍未散。高帝不能收拾補綴其殘壞，以追三代之隆，而以苟簡之規模自足。三章約法之外，一切承襲秦舊，無所建明，卒使先王典禮湮而不章。論治者不無遺恨於高帝也。
若我太祖高皇帝之興，乃在亡秦千載之後矣。觀其草創之初，首建宗社，以重邦國之本；繼立庠序，以先郡縣之化。大業既定，稽古立法，制禮以序倫，作樂以宣化，建官以分職，明教以齊俗。凡所制作，盡反元政，典章文物直追前古之隆，有非
translation_en:
…the legitimacy of his acquisition of the realm; another, his unique endowment with complete wisdom; another, his reverence for Heaven and diligence on behalf of the people; another, the strictness of his dynastic household regulations; and another, the unified direction of military administration. These, he said, were the reasons he restored the succession of emperors and kings in our central realm. Now, although our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, equaled Gaozu of Han in the legitimacy with which he won All-under-Heaven and acquired the realm, his achievement in rescuing Huaxia from the rank stench of alien rule and lifting the people out of utter misery was still greater. In this, Gaozu of Han certainly could not equal him. Hence the statement that his achievement surpassed all antiquity. Yet when Gaozu of Han rose to replace Qin, antiquity was not yet far distant: the statutes and standards of the former kings still survived, and the surviving texts of the Six Classics had not yet been dispersed. Emperor Gao failed to gather these up and repair their damaged remnants so as to recapture the flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties. Instead, he was content with makeshift and rudimentary institutions. Apart from his three-article compact of laws, he inherited everything from the old Qin arrangements, establishing and elucidating nothing anew. In the end, this caused the canonical rites of the former kings to fall into obscurity and remain unmanifest. Those who discuss government cannot but regret this failing of Emperor Gao.
The rise of our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, by contrast, came a thousand years after Qin’s fall. Consider how, at the very beginning of his founding work, he first established the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, thereby giving due weight to the foundations of the state. He next established schools, making moral transformation the foremost concern in the prefectures and counties. Once his great enterprise was secured, he examined antiquity and established laws; instituted rites to order human relationships; created music to spread moral transformation; established offices to apportion duties; and clarified moral instruction to bring customs into accord. Everything he instituted reversed Yuan governance. His statutes, institutions, and cultural accomplishments directly emulated the flourishing achievements of antiquity, with some beyond …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一時儒臣播誦之所能盡者此豈漢高之
所可得而並論哉所以然者蓋漢高得天
下於馬上不事詩書又嫚而侮人不喜儒
生當時為之議禮者僅以叔孫通鄙儒而
帝方命之曰令易知度吾所能行為之則
帝誠非有復古之心而真知垂統之大計
者其安於苟簡也固宜我
太祖高皇帝本以
天授神聖之資應運而出兵戈倥傯即能延訪
===
鴻儒以置帷幄購求遺書以備
省閱其所得於講論聞見者既深且廣故能
見超千古慮周萬世創制立法盡善盡美
有以昭曠代之宏規也夫作之於前者固
不可無久大之業而守之於後者尤不可
無充拓之功歷觀前代繼體之君如漢之
武帝能表章六經有功斯道矣而窮奢黷
武卒致海內之虛耗唐之憲宗能收復淮
蔡威震强藩矣而驕心一起反令美業之
punctuated:
一時儒臣播誦之所能盡者。此豈漢高之所可得而並論哉？所以然者，蓋漢高得天下於馬上，不事詩書，又嫚而侮人，不喜儒生。當時為之議禮者，僅以叔孫通鄙儒，而帝方命之曰：「令易知，度吾所能行為之。」則帝誠非有復古之心而真知垂統之大計者，其安於苟簡也固宜。我太祖高皇帝本以天授神聖之資，應運而出，兵戈倥傯，即能延訪鴻儒以置帷幄，購求遺書以備省閱。其所得於講論聞見者，既深且廣，故能見超千古，慮周萬世，創制立法，盡善盡美，有以昭曠代之宏規也。
夫作之於前者，固不可無久大之業，而守之於後者，尤不可無充拓之功。歷觀前代繼體之君，如漢之武帝，能表章六經，有功斯道矣，而窮奢黷武，卒致海內之虛耗；唐之憲宗，能收復淮蔡，威震强藩矣，而驕心一起，反令美業之
translation_en:
…beyond what the Confucian ministers of the time could fully celebrate and recount. How could Gaozu of Han possibly be discussed on equal terms with him? The reason is that Gaozu won the realm on horseback, paid no attention to the Odes and Documents, and was moreover arrogant and insulting toward others, with no liking for Confucian scholars. The man who deliberated on ritual for him at the time was merely the mediocre scholar Shusun Tong, and the emperor instructed him: “Make it easy to understand, and devise it according to what you judge I can carry out.” Thus the emperor truly had neither the intention to restore antiquity nor a genuine understanding of the great plan of transmitting the dynastic succession. It was only to be expected that he should rest content with makeshift simplicity. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with divine sagacity, arose in response to the destined moment. Even amid the turmoil of warfare, he sought out eminent Confucian scholars and brought them into his command tent, and purchased surviving books for his own perusal. What he gained through discussion, hearing, and observation was both profound and extensive. Hence his vision surpassed a thousand ages, and his deliberations encompassed ten thousand generations. His establishment of institutions and laws attained complete excellence and perfection, manifesting a grand design unequalled through the ages.
Those who first establish a dynasty must certainly leave an enduring and great achievement; those who subsequently preserve it have an even greater need to enlarge and extend it. Surveying the rulers who inherited the throne in earlier dynasties, Emperor Wu of Han honored and promoted the Six Classics and rendered service to this Way. Yet his extreme extravagance and wanton warfare ultimately exhausted the resources of the realm. Emperor Xianzong of Tang recovered Huai and Cai, and his might awed the powerful regional military commands. Yet once pride arose in his heart, he instead caused his splendid achievement to…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不終宋之神宗銳意更法勵精求治矣而
委用者無經世之學紛紛制作卒釀靖康
之亂惡在其爲中興也我
聖祖創大業於前
列聖紹鴻休於後奕葉相承有隆無替至我
皇上龍飛藩邸運際昌期禀
文武聖神之資備剛健中正之德
御極以來孜孜圖治其所以經綸大業
議禮考文足以建萬世之長策而綿億萬年
===
無疆之休者未能悉數而其卓然爲世大
法度越漢唐宋之君者則有五事可言定
圜丘方澤之制而分祀之議以一也著
明倫大典之書而繼統之禮以明也
留神經術則
經筵日御以研聖賢之旨尊崇孔子則正號
毁像而洗因循之陋察
先朝之遺弊革中官之出鎮若此者皆前人講
求之所未定智慮之所不及或牽於欲而
punctuated: 不終。宋之神宗銳意更法，勵精求治矣，而委用者無經世之學，紛紛制作，卒釀靖康之亂，惡在其爲中興也？我聖祖創大業於前，列聖紹鴻休於後，奕葉相承，有隆無替。至我皇上龍飛藩邸，運際昌期，禀文武聖神之資，備剛健中正之德。御極以來，孜孜圖治，其所以經綸大業、議禮考文，足以建萬世之長策，而綿億萬年無疆之休者，未能悉數。而其卓然爲世大法、度越漢唐宋之君者，則有五事可言：定圜丘方澤之制，而分祀之議以一也；著《明倫大典》之書，而繼統之禮以明也；留神經術，則經筵日御，以研聖賢之旨；尊崇孔子，則正號毁像，而洗因循之陋；察先朝之遺弊，革中官之出鎮。若此者，皆前人講求之所未定、智慮之所不及，或牽於欲而
translation_en:
…was not brought to completion. Emperor Shenzong of the Song was intent on reforming the laws and devoted his energies to good government. Yet those he entrusted with office lacked learning in statecraft; their profusion of institutions and enactments ultimately brewed the calamity of the Jingkang era. How could this constitute a restoration?

Our sagely founding ancestor established the great enterprise, and the succession of sage sovereigns carried forward his magnificent blessings. Generation succeeded generation, with increasing prosperity and no decline. Then our present Emperor rose like a dragon from his princely residence, encountering an auspicious age. Endowed with civil and martial gifts, sagacity and spiritual insight, he possesses the virtues of strength, vigor, balance, and rectitude. Since ascending the throne, he has labored tirelessly for good government. His ordering of the great enterprise, deliberations on ritual, and scrutiny of cultural standards suffice to establish enduring plans for ten thousand generations and perpetuate boundless blessings for countless ages; these achievements cannot all be enumerated. Yet five deeds may be cited in which he has conspicuously established great standards for the world and surpassed the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song.

He established the arrangements for the Circular Mound and Square Marsh altars, thereby settling debate over the separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. He compiled the Great Compendium Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian), thereby elucidating the rites governing succession to the imperial line. Attentive to classical learning, he attends the Classics Colloquium daily to investigate the meaning of the sages and worthies. Honoring Confucius, he corrected his title and destroyed his images, thereby sweeping away the shortcomings of unthinking adherence to precedent. Examining abuses inherited from preceding reigns, he abolished the dispatch of eunuchs to serve as regional defenders.

These were all matters that his predecessors’ inquiries had failed to settle and their deliberations had failed to encompass, or in which, constrained by their desires, they…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不能爲或制於內而不敢爲者而我
皇上稽古因心右文體道
濬哲淵衷超然遠覽
神謨聖斷毅然裁正有不待儒臣之賛一詞者
猗歟盛哉中興之業前代未之有比也所
以然者蓋我
皇上聰明睿智超越千古而又以
敬一之學上接堯舜禹湯文武周公孔子道
統之傳凡其見諸事天法祖者率皆裁以
===
往聖之心法故能剖析群疑脗合至道考
衷立度盡制盡倫有以隆中興之大業也
愚生生長遐陬沾濡
聖澤其所得於典籍之傳樂育之化者不過如
此何能以鋪張敷揚其萬一哉雖然愚嘗
聞諸先儒韓愈有言曰莫爲於前雖美弗
彰莫爲於後雖盛弗傳蓋創業者爲其可
繼燕翼之仁也守成者光昭前烈繼述之
孝也我
punctuated:
不能爲，或制於內而不敢爲者。而我皇上稽古因心，右文體道，濬哲淵衷，超然遠覽，神謨聖斷，毅然裁正，有不待儒臣之賛一詞者。猗歟盛哉！中興之業，前代未之有比也。所以然者，蓋我皇上聰明睿智，超越千古，而又以敬一之學，上接堯舜禹湯文武周公孔子道統之傳。凡其見諸事天法祖者，率皆裁以往聖之心法，故能剖析群疑，脗合至道，考衷立度，盡制盡倫，有以隆中興之大業也。

愚生生長遐陬，沾濡聖澤，其所得於典籍之傳、樂育之化者，不過如此，何能以鋪張敷揚其萬一哉？雖然，愚嘗聞諸先儒，韓愈有言曰：「莫爲於前，雖美弗彰；莫爲於後，雖盛弗傳。」蓋創業者爲其可繼，燕翼之仁也；守成者光昭前烈，繼述之孝也。我
translation_en:
…could not undertake, or, constrained from within, dared not undertake. Yet our Emperor examines antiquity and acts from his own heart, honors civil learning and embodies the Way. With profound wisdom and depth of mind, he surveys distant prospects from a lofty vantage. Through his divine counsels and sage decisions, he resolutely adjudicates and rectifies matters, sometimes without awaiting a single word of assistance from his Confucian ministers. Ah, how splendid! The achievement of this restoration has no equal in former dynasties. This is because our Emperor’s intelligence and sagacity surpass those of all past ages, and because, through his learning of reverent singleness of mind, he directly continues the transmission of the Way from Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. All that he manifests in serving Heaven and emulating his ancestors is judged by the teachings of the former sages concerning the mind. Thus he can resolve the many doubts, accord perfectly with the highest Way, ascertain the proper mean and establish standards, bringing institutions and human relationships to their fullest realization, thereby exalting the great enterprise of restoration.

I, an ignorant student born and raised in a remote corner of the realm, have been steeped in the beneficence of the sage sovereign. What I have gained from the transmission of the classics and the transforming influence of his delight in nurturing talent amounts to no more than this. How could I elaborate and proclaim even one ten-thousandth of it? Nevertheless, I have heard this from earlier Confucian scholars. Han Yu said: “If none acts before, even beauty will not be made manifest; if none acts afterward, even greatness will not be transmitted.” For those who found an enterprise make it capable of being continued: this is the benevolence of providing for their descendants. Those who preserve established achievements illuminate the glorious deeds of their predecessors: this is the filial devotion of carrying on and fulfilling their work. Our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝之興有六以建不世之大功我
皇上之度越前代有五以隆萬世之大業其功
大則其德厚而澤遠有以衍無窮之緒仁
之昭也其業隆則其氣振而運昌有以延
無疆之休孝之大也於乎創之以仁守之
以孝我
國家之盛當視成周八百之歷而遠過之矣
詩曰君子萬年永錫祚胤敬為
皇上頌之雖然愚生又有聞焉昔魏徵事唐太
===
宗於晚年有十漸不克終之陳而太宗實
嘉納之蓋人心易荒於逸樂而至治常虞
於盛隆以數者成之而不足以其一壞之
而有餘我
皇上總攬
乾剛裁決萬幾政權未嘗一日下移固無不克
終之漸而愚生私憂過計有不能忘情於
聖明之世者執事儻與其進尚能有言為
聖天子陳之
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝之興，有六以建不世之大功；我皇上之度越前代，有五以隆萬世之大業。其功大，則其德厚而澤遠，有以衍無窮之緒，仁之昭也；其業隆，則其氣振而運昌，有以延無疆之休，孝之大也。於乎！創之以仁，守之以孝，我國家之盛，當視成周八百之歷而遠過之矣。《詩》曰：「君子萬年，永錫祚胤。」敬為皇上頌之。
雖然，愚生又有聞焉。昔魏徵事唐太宗，於晚年有十漸不克終之陳，而太宗實嘉納之。蓋人心易荒於逸樂，而至治常虞於盛隆。以數者成之而不足，以其一壞之而有餘。我皇上總攬乾剛，裁決萬幾，政權未嘗一日下移，固無不克終之漸。而愚生私憂過計，有不能忘情於聖明之世者。執事儻與其進，尚能有言為聖天子陳之。
translation_en:
…The rise of our Emperor Taizu Gao had six features through which he established achievements unequalled in his age; our present Emperor’s surpassing of former dynasties has five features through which he magnifies the great undertaking of ten thousand generations. The greatness of those achievements means that virtue is deep and beneficence far-reaching, providing the means to perpetuate an unending succession: this is benevolence made manifest. The flourishing of that undertaking means that its vitality is invigorated and its fortunes prosper, providing the means to prolong boundless blessings: this is the greatness of filial piety. Ah! Founded through benevolence and preserved through filial piety, the flourishing of our dynasty should far exceed even the eight-hundred-year span of the Zhou. The Book of Odes says: “May the lord live ten thousand years, forever blessed with descendants.” I respectfully offer these words in praise of His Majesty.
Nevertheless, this humble student has also heard the following. When Wei Zheng served Emperor Taizong of the Tang, in the emperor’s later years he submitted an account of ten gradual failings that threatened his ability to finish well, and Taizong graciously accepted it. For the human heart readily grows heedless amid ease and pleasure, and even the best government must always fear danger at the height of its prosperity. Several measures together may be insufficient to bring it to fruition, while a single failing is more than enough to ruin it. Our Emperor holds supreme sovereign authority, personally deciding the myriad affairs of government; political power has never for a single day passed into subordinate hands. Certainly, there are no gradual failings that threaten his ability to finish well. Yet this humble student, in his private anxiety and excessive concern, cannot cease caring about this age of sagely and enlightened rule. If you, honored examiners, should approve his advancement, he still has words that he can set forth before the sagely Son of Heaven.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第二問
譚維鼎
考試官教諭劉批〔議論根據〕
考試官教授林批〔條答〕
執事之間以禮不以刑愚生則曰用禮者
當如用刑焉用禮如刑則禮重禮重則民
心革安處善欲驅之而為惡也不可得已
何哉善固民之心也重之以禮者非强其
所無也特教之無素則發動之機塞而無
===
以觸其懿美之衷於是乎有物而不化者
苟浸漬之既久而又時執其機以振作之
如今之用刑焉民固有勃然興起而日趨
於善者三代教化之隆率此而已舎此而
徒以法度把縛拘拘於簿書訟獄之間吾
見上繁於刑民敢於悍將有刑之所不能
禁者以此為治終苟而已於乎此禮樂之
所以當興而刑法之不足恃歟請因問而
詳言之天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣
punctuated:
第二問
譚維鼎
考試官教諭劉批〔議論根據〕
考試官教授林批〔條答〕
執事之間以禮不以刑，愚生則曰：用禮者當如用刑焉。用禮如刑，則禮重；禮重，則民心革，安處善，欲驅之而為惡也不可得已。何哉？善固民之心也，重之以禮者，非强其所無也。特教之無素，則發動之機塞，而無以觸其懿美之衷，於是乎有物而不化者。苟浸漬之既久，而又時執其機以振作之，如今之用刑焉，民固有勃然興起而日趨於善者。三代教化之隆，率此而已。舎此而徒以法度把縛，拘拘於簿書訟獄之間，吾見上繁於刑，民敢於悍，將有刑之所不能禁者。以此為治，終苟而已。於乎！此禮樂之所以當興，而刑法之不足恃歟？請因問而詳言之。天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣。
translation_en:
Second Policy Question
Tan Weiding
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The argument has a sound basis.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔Answers point by point.〕
Your question [?] concerns governing through ritual rather than punishment. I, an unworthy student, would say: those who employ ritual should do so as they employ punishment. If ritual is employed like punishment, ritual carries weight; when ritual carries weight, the people's hearts are transformed and they dwell contentedly in goodness. Even if one wished to drive them to do evil, one could not. Why is this? Goodness is inherent in the people's hearts. Giving it weight through ritual does not force upon them something they lack. It is simply that, when instruction has not been sustained, the impulse that would stir them to action is obstructed, and there is no means of touching the beauty and goodness within their hearts. Thus there are people who remain untransformed [?]. If they have long been steeped in instruction, and one also seizes timely opportunities to rouse them, just as punishment is employed today, the people will indeed rise with enthusiasm and advance daily toward goodness. The flourishing moral instruction of the Three Dynasties followed precisely this course.
If one abandons this and merely binds people with laws and regulations, becoming narrowly preoccupied with registers, documents, lawsuits, and criminal cases, I foresee those above multiplying punishments and the people growing brazen in their defiance. There will then be conduct that punishment cannot restrain. To govern in this manner is ultimately no more than expediency. Alas! Is this not why ritual and music must be promoted, and penal law cannot be relied upon? Allow me to explain in detail in response to the question. Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct, and the ordering of ritual operates. …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉古先聖王
所以繼天立極垂世立教者莫大於是故
其精神心術之蘊寓於三千三百之儀冠
婚喪祭朝聘鄉射之禮行於君臣父子兄
弟夫婦朋友之間者不過庸言庸行而已
是故形而下也不離於飲食器服之用形
而上也則極於無聲無臭之微由唐虞以
及三代罔不由是損益故當是時教化休
明治隆俗美雖有刑罰無所用之下至亡
===
秦焚滅典籍禮樂崩頹遂使後世言治率
多苟簡在上者畏於檢束或擇令易行或
謙讓未遑既無以脩復古昔節文度數之
詳與夫道德性命之體在下者苟隨時好
或綿蕞雜就或廢罷儀禮亦無以建立萬
世之長策而舉
明主於三代之隆然則刻期簿書而獄訟繁興
穿鑿於俗吏之苟且詐僞萌生而質朴日
消泛濫於刑罰之無極又烏怪乎王吉之
punctuated: 流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。古先聖王所以繼天立極、垂世立教者，莫大於是。故其精神心術之蘊，寓於三千三百之儀；冠婚喪祭、朝聘鄉射之禮，行於君臣、父子、兄弟、夫婦、朋友之間者，不過庸言庸行而已。是故形而下也，不離於飲食器服之用；形而上也，則極於無聲無臭之微。由唐虞以及三代，罔不由是損益。故當是時，教化休明，治隆俗美，雖有刑罰，無所用之。下至亡秦，焚滅典籍，禮樂崩頹，遂使後世言治，率多苟簡。在上者畏於檢束，或擇令易行，或謙讓未遑，既無以脩復古昔節文度數之詳，與夫道德性命之體；在下者苟隨時好，或綿蕞雜就，或廢罷儀禮，亦無以建立萬世之長策，而舉明主於三代之隆。然則刻期簿書，而獄訟繁興，穿鑿於俗吏之苟且；詐僞萌生，而質朴日消，泛濫於刑罰之無極，又烏怪乎王吉之
translation_en:
…flowing without cease, joining in unity and undergoing transformation, and music arises therein. Nothing was more important than these for the sage kings of antiquity in carrying on Heaven’s work, establishing the supreme standard, and transmitting their teachings to succeeding generations. Thus, the depths of their spiritual understanding and inner cultivation were embodied in the three thousand and three hundred ritual observances. The rites of capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, court audience, diplomatic visits, village gatherings, and archery, practiced among ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friends, were nothing beyond everyday speech and conduct. Thus, in their concrete aspect, they never departed from the uses of food and drink, utensils and clothing; in their metaphysical aspect, they reached the utmost subtlety of what has neither sound nor scent. From Tang and Yu through the Three Dynasties, all made their modifications on this basis. Hence, in those times, moral instruction was splendid and enlightened, government flourished, and customs were excellent. Although punishments existed, there was no occasion to employ them.

By the time of the doomed Qin dynasty, the canonical writings were burned and destroyed, and ritual and music fell into ruin. Consequently, later discussions of government were mostly makeshift and superficial. Those above feared restraints: some selected ordinances that were easy to implement [?], while others deferred modestly, claiming they had not yet had time. They were thus unable to restore either the detailed forms and measures of ancient ritual or the underlying substance of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny. Those below merely followed current preferences: some cobbled together makeshift ceremonies, while others abolished ceremonial rites. They too were unable to establish a lasting policy for all generations and raise an enlightened ruler to the eminence of the Three Dynasties. Consequently, deadlines were imposed for registers and documents while lawsuits multiplied, amid the strained contrivances and expedients of ordinary officials [?]; deceit arose while simplicity and sincerity dwindled daily, amid the unchecked proliferation of punishments. Why, then, should one be surprised that Wang Ji’s…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蓋禮樂之感於外而精神之發於中也禮
果不可復乎禮之根於人心也大矣聖人
本因其心而制節之固非強世之物也自
後世禮樂之敎不行天下日流於鄙俗之
敝故說者慨夫子之作春秋不存禮樂之
制博士顏復至有虛名失實之歎豈非探
本之論乎古人有見於此斷斷乎以禮之
必可爲國民之不可無禮故裴耀卿之在
唐玄宗朝也則請乞令天下大州每年各
===
備禮儀准令式行禮稍加勸奬以示風俗
使民習禮聞樂上奉君親下安鄉族自然
和氣浹洽化理清平而不任刑法矣胡銓
之在宋寧宗朝也則請以司馬光冠婚喪
祭之儀乞詔禮官討論擇其要而易行者
布之民間使耆儒宿學轉相傳授而武夫
悍將亦令通行欲使民知禮則知尊君親
上奉先思孝而天下不足治矣若夫五禮
新儀下頒州郡有司慮其推行之不及也
punctuated: 蓋禮樂之感於外，而精神之發於中也。禮果不可復乎？禮之根於人心也大矣！聖人本因其心而制節之，固非強世之物也。自後世禮樂之敎不行，天下日流於鄙俗之敝，故說者慨夫子之作春秋不存禮樂之制，博士顏復至有虛名失實之歎，豈非探本之論乎？古人有見於此，斷斷乎以禮之必可爲國，民之不可無禮。故裴耀卿之在唐玄宗朝也，則請乞令天下大州每年各備禮儀，准令式行禮，稍加勸奬，以示風俗，使民習禮聞樂，上奉君親，下安鄉族，自然和氣浹洽，化理清平，而不任刑法矣。胡銓之在宋寧宗朝也，則請以司馬光冠婚喪祭之儀，乞詔禮官討論，擇其要而易行者，布之民間，使耆儒宿學轉相傳授，而武夫悍將亦令通行。欲使民知禮，則知尊君親上，奉先思孝，而天下不足治矣。若夫五禮新儀，下頒州郡，有司慮其推行之不及也，
translation_en:
…For rites and music exert their influence from without, while the spirit issues from within. Can rites truly not be restored? How deeply rites are rooted in the human heart! The sages originally followed that heart in establishing rules to regulate it; rites were certainly not something forcibly imposed upon the world. In later ages, instruction in rites and music ceased to be practiced, and the world slid daily into the corruptions of vulgar custom. Thus commentators lamented that when the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he did not preserve the institutions of rites and music. The Erudite Yan Fu even lamented that empty names remained while their substance had been lost. Was this not an argument that probed the root of the matter?

The ancients understood this and firmly believed that rites could indeed be used to govern a state, and that the people could not do without them. Thus, when Pei Yaoqing served at the court of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang, he requested that every large prefecture throughout the empire be ordered each year to make preparations for ritual ceremonies and perform them according to the statutes and regulations. Some encouragement and rewards should be added to guide popular customs, enabling the people to practice rites and hear music, to serve their sovereign and parents above, and to live peacefully among their fellow villagers and clansmen below. A spirit of harmony would naturally permeate society, moral transformation and governance would bring purity and peace, and there would be no reliance on penal law.

When Hu Quan served at the court of Emperor Ningzong of the Song [?], he requested that ritual officials be commanded to examine and discuss Sima Guang’s ceremonies for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice, select those that were essential and easy to perform, and disseminate them among the people. Elderly Confucian scholars and seasoned men of learning were to transmit them to one another, while even fighting men and fierce generals were to be ordered to practice them universally. The intention was that, by knowing rites, the people would know to honor their sovereign and regard their superiors with affection, serve their ancestors, and give thought to filial piety; then the realm would be insufficiently governed [?]. As for the New Ceremonies for the Five Rites, these were promulgated to prefectures and commanderies, and the responsible officials worried that their implementation might not reach far enough…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其議論可知巳其始也以權其成也以正
豈直心在唐巳哉吕温謂其蒙恥奮忠以
權大謀世亦謂之知言而大儒朱子感興
詩亦曰向非狄張徒誰辦取日功愚嘗觀
此未嘗不服仁傑沉幾潜運獨立物表區
區匹夫之諒烏足以知之是故可以觀智
矣至若元以夷人入主中國此世道大變
之極也當時儒者許衡乃應聘而爲臣劉
因則屢聘而不起以迹擬之劉信高於許
===
矣然戰則爲王降則爲奴渡江賦之所誇
揚似乎欣幸趙宋之亡者劉之心毋乃未
嘗以元夷爲非者耶然以靜脩之賢甘心
爲之不以爲諱而又丕爲之臣其在當時
必有所見果合於至公至大之義未可知
也五胡亂華姚弋仲老羌耳尚言胡人之
不當據有中土正朔相承王景略臨終尤
以勸符堅之不當圖晉許以一世大儒得
君行道將欲以華變夷乃曾無一言以存
punctuated:
其議論可知巳。其始也以權，其成也以正，豈直心在唐巳哉？吕温謂其蒙恥奮忠，以權大謀，世亦謂之知言。而大儒朱子《感興詩》亦曰：「向非狄張徒，誰辦取日功？」愚嘗觀此，未嘗不服仁傑沉幾潜運，獨立物表，區區匹夫之諒，烏足以知之？是故可以觀智矣。
至若元以夷人入主中國，此世道大變之極也。當時儒者許衡乃應聘而爲臣，劉因則屢聘而不起。以迹擬之，劉信高於許矣。然「戰則爲王，降則爲奴」，《渡江賦》之所誇揚，似乎欣幸趙宋之亡者。劉之心，毋乃未嘗以元夷爲非者耶？然以靜脩之賢，甘心爲之，不以爲諱，而又丕爲之臣，其在當時必有所見，果合於至公至大之義，未可知也。五胡亂華，姚弋仲老羌耳，尚言胡人之不當據有中土。正朔相承，王景略臨終，尤以勸符堅之不當圖晉。許以一世大儒，得君行道，將欲以華變夷，乃曾無一言以存
translation_en:
…his views can thus be understood. At the outset he acted through expedient measures; in bringing his undertaking to completion, he acted according to what was right. Could it merely have been that his heart remained with the Tang? Lü Wen said that he endured disgrace and exerted his loyalty, using expedient measures to advance a great design; people likewise regarded this as an insightful judgment. The great Confucian master Zhu Xi also wrote in his Poems of Reflection (Ganxing shi): “Had it not been for men like Di and Zhang, who could have accomplished the recovery of the sun?” Whenever I have considered this, I have invariably admired Di Renjie’s profound discernment of incipient developments and his concealed workings, standing alone above worldly concerns. How could the petty fidelity of an ordinary man suffice to comprehend him? Thus, this allows us to discern his wisdom.
As for the Yuan, who entered and ruled China as outsiders, this was the utmost upheaval in the ordering of the world. The Confucian scholar Xu Heng accepted their invitation and became their subject, whereas Liu Yin repeatedly declined invitations to take office. Judging by their outward conduct, Liu was indeed superior to Xu. Yet “fight and become a king; surrender and become a slave”—what his Rhapsody on Crossing the River (Dujiang fu) extols seems to express delight at the fall of the Zhao house’s Song dynasty. Could it be that, in his heart, Liu never regarded rule by the Yuan outsiders as wrong? Yet a man as worthy as Jingxiu [Liu Yin] willingly wrote this without regarding it as something to conceal, while nevertheless not becoming their subject [?]. He must have had some particular insight at the time; whether it truly accorded with the most impartial and encompassing righteousness cannot be known.
When the Five Hu threw China into disorder, Yao Yizhong, merely an old Qiang, nevertheless said that the Hu ought not to occupy the central lands. As for the legitimate succession of dynasties, Wang Jinglüe, on his deathbed, particularly urged Fu Jian not to attempt the conquest of Jin. Xu, a great Confucian scholar of his age, found a ruler under whom he could put the Way into practice and intended to transform the outsiders through Chinese civilization; yet he never uttered even a single word to preserve…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有見而知之者則必有聞而知之者此固
氣機之潛運而上下之相爲感者尤不可
誣也是故上有隆儒重道之君而後下有
懷道秉德之士上得其人而聖人之道行
天下不患無善治下得其人而聖人之學
傳天下不患無眞儒同時者得於見知之
的後時者亦得上有所考而與聞乎心法
之要焉此其所以上下同德而世敎休美
也有以哉執事策試諸生而以當世道統
===
之傳下詢蓋有望於諸生者不淺也夫道
何統乎堯之授舜曰惟精惟一允執厥中
此千聖傳心之要法而道之所由宗也然
聖賢不世出則其出也有時故孟軻氏曰
五百年必有王者興其間必有名世者由
堯舜至於湯五百餘歲若禹皐陶見而知
之若湯聞而知之由湯至於文王五百餘
歲若伊尹萊朱見而知之若文王聞而知
之由文王至於孔子五百餘歲若太公望
punctuated:
有見而知之者，則必有聞而知之者。此固氣機之潛運，而上下之相爲感者，尤不可誣也。是故上有隆儒重道之君，而後下有懷道秉德之士。上得其人，而聖人之道行，天下不患無善治；下得其人，而聖人之學傳，天下不患無眞儒。同時者得於見知之的，後時者亦得上有所考，而與聞乎心法之要焉。此其所以上下同德而世敎休美也，有以哉！執事策試諸生，而以當世道統之傳下詢，蓋有望於諸生者不淺也。
夫道何統乎？堯之授舜曰：「惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此千聖傳心之要法，而道之所由宗也。然聖賢不世出，則其出也有時。故孟軻氏曰：「五百年必有王者興，其間必有名世者。」由堯舜至於湯，五百餘歲，若禹、皐陶，見而知之；若湯，聞而知之。由湯至於文王，五百餘歲，若伊尹、萊朱，見而知之；若文王，聞而知之。由文王至於孔子，五百餘歲，若太公望
translation_en:
Where there are those who understand through seeing, there must also be those who understand through hearing. This is indeed the unseen operation of the workings of vital energy; still less can the mutual influence of those above and those below be denied. Thus, only when there is a ruler above who exalts Confucian scholars and esteems the Way are there men below who cherish the Way and uphold virtue. When the right person is found above, the Way of the sages prevails, and the world need not fear a lack of good government. When the right people are found below, the learning of the sages is transmitted, and the world need not fear a lack of true Confucian scholars. Contemporaries gain the certainty of understanding through direct observation; those of later times can also look back for evidence and learn the essentials of the teaching of the mind. There is good reason, then, that those above and below share the same virtue and that moral instruction in the world flourishes! You, honored examiners, test us students with policy questions and graciously inquire about the transmission of the succession of the Way in our own age. Surely your expectations of us are considerable.
What, then, constitutes the succession of the Way? In transmitting it to Shun, Yao said: “Be discerning, be single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the Mean.” This is the essential method by which the myriad sages transmitted the teaching of the mind, and the guiding principle of the Way. Yet sages and worthies do not appear in every generation; their emergence has its appointed times. Thus Meng Ke said: “Every five hundred years a true king must arise, and in the interval there must be men renowned in their age.” From Yao and Shun to Tang was more than five hundred years. Men such as Yu and Gao Yao understood through seeing; Tang understood through hearing. From Tang to King Wen was more than five hundred years. Men such as Yi Yin and Lai Zhu understood through seeing; King Wen understood through hearing. From King Wen to Kongzi was more than five hundred years. Men such as Taigong Wang…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
散宜生見而知之若孔子聞而知之軻嘗
私淑於孔子之門人蓋與乎見而知之者
矣軻之死不得其傳秦漢以來天下之士
莫知所以為學是以天理不明而人欲熾
正學不傳而異端起彛倫之在人心者雖
不可泯而斯道一脉亦且不絕如綫矣延
至有宋一元恊運五星聚奎上之人知所
以敎下之人知所以學濂溪周敦頤作著
太極圖通書以示學者刋落繁蕪直究道
===
體真有以闡夫陰陽五行之奧而天下之
為中正仁義者得以知其所自來言聖學
之有要而下學者知勝私復禮之可以馴
致於上達明天下之有本而言治者知誠
心端緒之可以舉而措之於天下其所以
上接洙泗千載之統下啓河洛百世之傳
者脉絡分明規模亦宏遠矣由宋迄今適
逢其會胡元運竭
聖人篤生於是我
punctuated:
散宜生見而知之，若孔子聞而知之。軻嘗私淑於孔子之門人，蓋與乎見而知之者矣。軻之死，不得其傳。秦漢以來，天下之士莫知所以為學，是以天理不明而人欲熾，正學不傳而異端起。彛倫之在人心者雖不可泯，而斯道一脉亦且不絕如綫矣。
延至有宋，一元恊運，五星聚奎，上之人知所以敎，下之人知所以學。濂溪周敦頤作著《太極圖》《通書》以示學者，刋落繁蕪，直究道體，真有以闡夫陰陽五行之奧，而天下之為中正仁義者得以知其所自來；言聖學之有要，而下學者知勝私復禮之可以馴致於上達；明天下之有本，而言治者知誠心端緒之可以舉而措之於天下。其所以上接洙泗千載之統，下啓河洛百世之傳者，脉絡分明，規模亦宏遠矣。
由宋迄今，適逢其會，胡元運竭，聖人篤生，於是我
translation_en:
…San Yisheng knew it through seeing, while Confucius knew it through hearing. Meng Ke once privately cultivated himself through the teachings of Confucius’s disciples, and thus may be counted among those who knew it through seeing. When Meng Ke died, no one received his transmission. From the Qin and Han onward, scholars throughout the realm did not know how to pursue learning. Consequently, heavenly principle remained obscure while human desires blazed; orthodox learning went untransmitted while heterodox doctrines arose. Although the enduring moral relationships inherent in the human heart could not be erased, this single line of transmission of the Way barely survived, like a slender thread.
When the Song dynasty arrived, the primordial unity harmonized with the cycle of destiny, and the five planets gathered in the Kui constellation. Those above knew how to teach, and those below knew how to learn. Zhou Dunyi of Lianxi composed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and the Penetrating the Book of Changes to instruct learners. Stripping away tangled elaboration, he investigated directly the substance of the Way. He truly elucidated the mysteries of yin and yang and the Five Phases, enabling all who practiced centrality, correctness, benevolence, and righteousness to understand their source. He explained that sagely learning had an essential core, so that those beginning with ordinary learning understood that overcoming selfishness and returning to ritual propriety could gradually lead to higher understanding. He made clear that all under Heaven had a root, so that those discussing governance understood that the beginnings of sincerity in the heart could be extended and applied throughout the realm. In this way he carried forward the thousand-year succession of the Zhu and Si rivers—the tradition of Confucius—and opened the transmission of the He and Luo rivers—the tradition of the Cheng brothers—for a hundred generations to come. Its connections were clear, and its scope was vast and far-reaching.
From the Song down to the present, the opportune conjunction of circumstances duly arrived: the alien Yuan dynasty’s allotted fortune was exhausted, and a sage was born. Thereupon our …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝龍飛九五作萬世君師之極嘗謂
禮部侍郎曾魯曰帝王之治莫盛於堯舜
觀其授受其要在允執厥中而病儒者講
之雖精未免背馳於行事又曰人君一心
治化之本存於中者無堯舜之心欲施於
治者有堯舜之治決不可得而務存心立
政以成堯舜之事功
成祖文皇帝繼統尤切儆戒其覽學士解縉進
呈大學正心章講義則曰人君誠不可有
===
所好樂一有好樂泥而不返則慾必勝理
若心能靜虛事來則應事去如明鏡止水
自然純是天理朕每朝默坐未嘗不思管
束此心爲切要是哉
祖宗創業垂統之初即有以啓斯道之眞傳於
上而其所以明世敎淑人心者有以媲美
於唐虞矣
列聖相承躬行體道代有
制作蓋獨步千古而莫之與京洪惟我
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝龍飛九五，作萬世君師之極。嘗謂禮部侍郎曾魯曰：「帝王之治，莫盛於堯舜。觀其授受，其要在允執厥中。」而病儒者講之雖精，未免背馳於行事。又曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，欲施於治者有堯舜之治，決不可得。」而務存心立政，以成堯舜之事功。
成祖文皇帝繼統，尤切儆戒。其覽學士解縉進呈《大學》正心章講義，則曰：「人君誠不可有所好樂。一有好樂，泥而不返，則慾必勝理。若心能靜虛，事來則應，事去如明鏡止水，自然純是天理。朕每朝默坐，未嘗不思管束此心爲切要。」是哉！祖宗創業垂統之初，即有以啓斯道之眞傳於上，而其所以明世敎、淑人心者，有以媲美於唐虞矣。
列聖相承，躬行體道，代有制作，蓋獨步千古而莫之與京。洪惟我
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, rose like a dragon to the sovereign’s place and established the supreme standard of ruler and teacher for all ages. He once told Zeng Lu, Vice Minister of Rites: “No imperial government flourished more greatly than that of Yao and Shun. When we examine their transmission and reception of sovereignty, its essential principle lay in sincerely holding fast to the Mean.” He deplored the fact that Confucian scholars, though precise in explaining this principle, nevertheless departed from it in their conduct. He also said: “The ruler’s mind alone is the foundation of government and moral transformation. If what he harbors within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes his administration to achieve the government of Yao and Shun, this is utterly impossible.” He therefore devoted himself to preserving his moral mind and establishing good government, so as to accomplish deeds like those of Yao and Shun.
Chengzu, the Wen Emperor, succeeded to the imperial line and was especially earnest in vigilance and self-admonition. On reading the exposition of the Great Learning’s chapter on rectifying the mind submitted by Academician Xie Jin, he said: “A ruler truly must not have objects of partiality or delight. Once he has such preferences and becomes mired in them without turning back, desire will inevitably overcome principle. If the mind can remain still and empty, it responds when affairs arise; when they pass, it is like a bright mirror or still water, naturally consisting wholly of Heaven’s principle. Every morning I sit silently, invariably considering the restraint of this mind to be the most urgent task.” How true! From the time when our imperial ancestors founded the dynasty and handed down its succession, they thus opened the true transmission of this Way from above. In illuminating moral instruction in the world and improving people’s hearts, they rivaled the age of Yao and Shun.
The successive sage emperors carried on this inheritance, personally practicing and embodying the Way. Each reign produced institutions and ordinances, standing unrivaled through the ages, with none to equal them. Reverently we reflect upon our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
勉綱紀以造就乎四方者深矣然漸濡
聖化者乃未嘗有得於禹臯伊傅之緒以為名
世之望成見知之盛者豈有之而未見耶
抑尚有待於薫陶之既久而後出耶夫天
理民彝不可泯沒況上有累朝
列聖作人之功今日
皇上躬行之化百七十餘年間儒臣隱逸豈無
造詣誠確神會心得以垂衍斯道之一脉
者乎近世儒臣楊廉獨識此意乃歷考當
===
時諸臣如力行好古進趨有程有若河津
之薛瑄堅忍貧賤進脩不倦有若崇仁之
吳與弼或仕或不仕皆銳志理學而潜心
於聖賢者也端嘿沉靜慕回如愚有若布
衣陳真晟學求自得勿助勿忘有若白沙
陳獻章或著作與不著作皆絕意舉業而
返求於心學者也以至胡居仁之議論的
當根據程朱布政使陳選之講明正學務
實近裏侍郎張元禎之反躬研理侍講納
punctuated: 勉綱紀以造就乎四方者深矣。然漸濡聖化者，乃未嘗有得於禹臯伊傅之緒，以為名世之望、成見知之盛者，豈有之而未見耶？抑尚有待於薫陶之既久而後出耶？夫天理民彝不可泯沒，況上有累朝列聖作人之功、今日皇上躬行之化，百七十餘年間，儒臣隱逸豈無造詣誠確、神會心得，以垂衍斯道之一脉者乎？近世儒臣楊廉獨識此意，乃歷考當時諸臣。如力行好古，進趨有程，有若河津之薛瑄；堅忍貧賤，進脩不倦，有若崇仁之吳與弼：或仕或不仕，皆銳志理學而潜心於聖賢者也。端嘿沉靜，慕回如愚，有若布衣陳真晟；學求自得，勿助勿忘，有若白沙陳獻章：或著作與不著作，皆絕意舉業而返求於心學者也。以至胡居仁之議論的當，根據程朱；布政使陳選之講明正學，務實近裏；侍郎張元禎之反躬研理；侍講納
translation_en:
…his efforts to strengthen the guiding principles and bring people throughout the realm to maturity have been profound. Yet among those steeped in the sage ruler’s transforming influence, none has yet attained the legacy of Yu, Gao, Yi, and Fu so as to become an eminent figure of the age and bring to fruition the flourishing tradition of understanding the sages through personal encounter. Could such people exist but remain unrecognized? Or must they emerge only after a longer period of cultivation? Heaven’s principles and the enduring moral norms of the people cannot be effaced. Moreover, above there have been the achievements of the sage emperors of successive reigns in nurturing talent, and today there is the transforming influence of His Majesty’s personal example. Over these more than 170 years, could there have been no Confucian officials or recluses whose attainments were sincere and sure, who grasped the Way intuitively and apprehended it in their hearts, thereby transmitting and extending this thread of the Way?

The recent Confucian official Yang Lian alone recognized this significance and accordingly examined, one by one, the officials of that time. For vigorous practice and devotion to antiquity, with orderly progress in learning, there was Xue Xuan of Hejin; for steadfast endurance of poverty and humble circumstances, and tireless advancement in self-cultivation, there was Wu Yubi of Chongren. Whether they held office or remained outside it, they resolutely devoted themselves to the Learning of Principle and concentrated their minds on the sages and worthies. For upright reserve and deep tranquillity, emulating Yan Hui’s seeming simplicity, there was the commoner Chen Zhensheng; for seeking personal understanding through study, neither forcing growth nor neglecting it, there was Chen Xianzhang of Baisha. Whether they produced writings or not, all abandoned ambitions in examination studies and turned inward to seek the learning of the mind. There were also Hu Juren, whose discussions were precise and well founded in the teachings of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi; Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xuan, who expounded orthodox learning and pursued substance and inward depth; Vice Minister Zhang Yuanzhen, who examined himself and investigated principle; and Expositor Na…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忠聞望輝映於後先也羅倫之氣節竒偉
任道甚力布政使周瑛之每事檢心學求
自得郎中莊㫤之博學大志温醇和易互
相為羽翼也以至急流引退究心理學則
有重內輕外篤信朱子如章懋飭躬勵行
深明易理如蔡清者焉遭時星變抗疏直
言則有卓然自立如張吉篤志聖賢如鄒
智名並四諫竒氣踈節如黃仲昭者焉凡
一十五人撮其行實各為編次名之曰
===
皇明理學名臣言行錄其意盖亦慮夫理學之
失傳而所以扶持世道於不廢者就中論
之如薛瑄之學貴踐履性與天通陳獻章
之主一養心造詣充裕以至吳與弼之分
別聖學俗學是皆奮起乎百世之下倡明
斯道之統以為天下法程雖若不敢遽謂
其俱有見知之實然考其脩身慎行明道
立言由下學以至上達卑不遺於事物高
不淪於空虛粹然一出於正回視游黃諸
punctuated: 忠，聞望輝映於後先也。羅倫之氣節竒偉，任道甚力，布政使周瑛之每事檢心，學求自得，郎中莊㫤之博學大志，温醇和易，互相為羽翼也。以至急流引退，究心理學，則有重內輕外，篤信朱子如章懋，飭躬勵行，深明易理如蔡清者焉。遭時星變，抗疏直言，則有卓然自立如張吉，篤志聖賢如鄒智，名並四諫，竒氣踈節如黃仲昭者焉。凡一十五人，撮其行實，各為編次，名之曰《皇明理學名臣言行錄》。其意盖亦慮夫理學之失傳，而所以扶持世道於不廢者。就中論之，如薛瑄之學貴踐履，性與天通，陳獻章之主一養心，造詣充裕，以至吳與弼之分別聖學俗學，是皆奮起乎百世之下，倡明斯道之統，以為天下法程。雖若不敢遽謂其俱有見知之實，然考其脩身慎行，明道立言，由下學以至上達，卑不遺於事物，高不淪於空虛，粹然一出於正。回視游黃諸
translation_en:
…Zhong: their renown shone forth, earlier and later figures lending brilliance to one another. Luo Lun possessed extraordinary moral integrity and devoted great effort to upholding the Way; Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhou Ying examined his own heart in every matter and sought understanding for himself in learning; and Bureau Director Zhuang Chang possessed broad learning and lofty aspirations, and was gentle, sincere, amiable, and approachable. They lent support to one another. Among those who withdrew from the swift current of official life and devoted their minds to the study of principle were Zhang Mao, who valued inner cultivation above external concerns and firmly trusted Master Zhu, and Cai Qing, who disciplined himself, diligently cultivated his conduct, and deeply understood the principles of the Book of Changes. Among those who, when celestial anomalies occurred, submitted forthright memorials were Zhang Ji, who stood firmly on his own convictions; Zou Zhi, who resolutely aspired to the sages and worthies; and Huang Zhongzhao, ranked among the Four Remonstrators, whose spirit was extraordinary and whose conduct was unconstrained [?]. The deeds of these fifteen men were summarized and separately arranged in a compilation entitled Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Neo-Confucian Ministers of the August Ming.

The intention was presumably also to guard against the loss of the transmission of the learning of principle, thereby sustaining the moral order of the world and preventing its collapse. To consider particular figures within it: Xue Xuan’s learning prized putting principles into practice, and his nature was in communion with Heaven; Chen Xianzhang nurtured the mind through concentration on unity and attained abundant understanding; and Wu Yubi distinguished the learning of the sages from conventional learning. All these men rose up a hundred generations later to elucidate the succession of this Way and provide a standard for all under Heaven. Although one might hesitate to assert immediately that they all possessed genuine understanding through direct insight, an examination of their self-cultivation, careful conduct, elucidation of the Way, and establishment of enduring teachings shows that they proceeded from learning ordinary matters below to comprehending higher principles above. At the ordinary level they neglected no affairs or things; at the higher level they did not lapse into vacuity. Everything issued purely from what was correct. Looking back at such masters as You and Huang…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
子親炙程朱之門而其後不能無少謬者
殆為過之暨如羅倫之好善惡惡心事如
青天白日胡居仁之學主忠信排斥異端
章懋之精極義理身體力行莊㫤之慷慨
豪邁樂取人善以及鄒智之雅負竒氣守
義據經皆卓然有以自立以為四方表雖
若不敢盡謂其涵養弘深各造其極然尚
論一時之清風勁節才識忠款志之必為
君子而不為小人學之必為道德而不苟
===
利禄端使海內之士想望風采可仰而不
可及回視陳同父輩之出入於義利王伯
之間而不免以豪傑自逞者其不猶有可
議矣乎於乎道之不明也久矣流俗之難
挽人心之難覺也今世果無其人乎固有
篤於深造而不求人知者蓋偶未之見耳
昔周敦頤肇開宋學之源當時見其政事
精絕者則以為宦業過人見其有山林之
志者則以為襟懷灑落世有知其學者則
punctuated:
子親炙程朱之門，而其後不能無少謬者，殆為過之。暨如羅倫之好善惡惡，心事如青天白日；胡居仁之學主忠信，排斥異端；章懋之精極義理，身體力行；莊㫤之慷慨豪邁，樂取人善；以及鄒智之雅負竒氣，守義據經，皆卓然有以自立，以為四方表。雖若不敢盡謂其涵養弘深，各造其極，然尚論一時之清風勁節、才識忠款，志之必為君子而不為小人，學之必為道德而不苟利禄，端使海內之士想望風采，可仰而不可及。回視陳同父輩之出入於義利王伯之間，而不免以豪傑自逞者，其不猶有可議矣乎？
於乎！道之不明也久矣，流俗之難挽，人心之難覺也！今世果無其人乎？固有篤於深造而不求人知者，蓋偶未之見耳。昔周敦頤肇開宋學之源，當時見其政事精絕者，則以為宦業過人；見其有山林之志者，則以為襟懷灑落；世有知其學者，則
translation_en:
…those masters who received personal instruction in the schools of Cheng and Zhu, yet later could not remain entirely free of error, were probably surpassed by them. Then there were Luo Lun, who loved goodness and hated evil, whose heart and deeds were as clear as the blue sky and bright sun; Hu Juren, whose learning centered on loyalty and trustworthiness and who rejected heterodox teachings; Zhang Mao, who investigated moral principles to their utmost refinement and personally put them into practice; Zhuang Chang, who was spirited and bold and delighted in adopting others’ good qualities; and Zou Zhi, long endowed with an extraordinary spirit, who upheld righteousness and grounded himself in the Classics. All stood firmly on their own and served as exemplars throughout the realm. Although one might hesitate to say that all possessed broad and profound self-cultivation and had each attained its utmost heights, consider their pure influence and steadfast integrity, their talent, discernment, and sincere loyalty in their own time: their resolve was always to become gentlemen rather than petty men, and their learning always pursued the Way and virtue rather than careless acquisition of profit and official emoluments.
