They truly caused scholars throughout the empire to yearn for their bearing, which could be admired but scarcely equaled. Looking back at Chen Tongfu and his like, who moved between righteousness and profit, between the kingly way and hegemonic rule, and could not avoid making a display of their heroic talents, do they not still leave grounds for criticism?
Alas! The Way has long been obscured. How difficult it is to turn back prevailing vulgar customs and awaken people’s hearts! Does the present age truly lack such men? Surely there are those devoted to profound attainment who do not seek recognition; it is merely that we happen not to have encountered them. Formerly, when Zhou Dunyi first opened the source of Song learning, those of his contemporaries who saw the consummate excellence of his administration considered his achievements in office superior to others’; those who saw his aspiration to retire among mountains and forests considered him free and untrammeled in spirit. As for those in his day who knew of his learning, they …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
又或疑其出於希夷而未甞知其有道必
至身沒而后道始章名始定今之論者毋
亦類此歟然則論我
朝見知之學而有以得其正傳者詢名責實
固有俟於後之君子也方今
聖天子學有緝熈凡所
講明制作以昭著於天下者無非斯道之實
用公卿而下以及士庶沾濡
聖澤者亦皆丕變維新凡所措之身心以爲化
===
民成俗之本者亦皆體道之實功將見上
有善治以行聖人之道致天下於仁義禮
樂之域下有真儒以明聖人之學上接夫
周程張朱道統之傳固當應期而出以徽
柔
一代治教之盛者矣愚何幸身親見之
第五問
曾迪
考試官教諭劉批〔非泛言者〕
punctuated:
又或疑其出於希夷，而未甞知其有道，必至身沒而后道始章，名始定。今之論者毋亦類此歟？然則論我朝見知之學，而有以得其正傳者，詢名責實，固有俟於後之君子也。方今聖天子學有緝熈，凡所講明制作，以昭著於天下者，無非斯道之實用。公卿而下，以及士庶，沾濡聖澤者，亦皆丕變維新。凡所措之身心，以爲化民成俗之本者，亦皆體道之實功。將見上有善治，以行聖人之道，致天下於仁義禮樂之域；下有真儒，以明聖人之學，上接夫周程張朱道統之傳，固當應期而出，以徽柔一代治教之盛者矣。愚何幸身親見之！

第五問
曾迪
考試官教諭劉批〔非泛言者〕
translation_en:
…some also suspected that his learning derived from Xiyi, yet never recognized that he possessed the Way. Only after his death did his Way become manifest and his reputation become established. Are those who pass judgment today not much the same? Thus, in assessing the learning of those known to us firsthand in our dynasty and determining who has received its authentic transmission, investigating reputations and demanding substantive proof must indeed await gentlemen of later generations.

Now our sagely Son of Heaven continually advances in luminous learning. Everything he elucidates through discussion and establishes through institutions, making it manifest throughout the realm, is a practical application of this Way. From the dukes and ministers down to scholars and commoners, all who are steeped in his sagely beneficence have likewise undergone great transformation and renewal. Everything they put into practice in body and mind as the foundation for transforming the people and shaping their customs is likewise genuine work in embodying the Way. We shall see good government above putting the sages’ Way into effect and bringing all under Heaven into the realm of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music; below, there will be true Confucians elucidating the sages’ learning and carrying forward the transmission of the succession of the Way from Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi. Surely they will emerge at the appointed time to embellish and bring harmony to this dynasty’s flourishing government and moral instruction. How fortunate I, in my humble station, am to witness this in person!

Fifth Policy Question
Zeng Di
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔These are no mere generalities.〕

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授林批有見
用人者貴於公天下之法而不必盡天下
之情入仕者在於端致用之本而不可計
一身之利蓋人有不可盡之情而法無可
必盡之術吾惟持之以公則情之不得盡
者與我皆無憾也而又何嫌於法耶士有
欲用世之志而法無可倖進之理吾惟俟
之以正則身之難於進者於法固相安也
而又何急於利耶審如此則入仕者不患
===
其居閑之日多而掌銓者亦何憂其積壅
之日深也哉維昔羲后以物命官推擇之
典邈矣無聞爰洎唐虞建官惟百夏商官
倍當其時疇咨明揚考言詢事旁招俊乂
列于庶位上以道求下以行應無常法也
逮于成周大司徒以鄉三物敎萬民攷其
德行道藝而賓之于王曰選士曰俊士曰
造士曰進士論定而後官任官而後爵位
定而後祿擇才取士始爲詳矣然猶未有
punctuated:
考試官敎授林批：有見。

用人者貴於公天下之法，而不必盡天下之情；入仕者在於端致用之本，而不可計一身之利。蓋人有不可盡之情，而法無可必盡之術。吾惟持之以公，則情之不得盡者與我皆無憾也，而又何嫌於法耶？士有欲用世之志，而法無可倖進之理。吾惟俟之以正，則身之難於進者於法固相安也，而又何急於利耶？審如此，則入仕者不患其居閑之日多，而掌銓者亦何憂其積壅之日深也哉！維昔羲后以物命官，推擇之典邈矣無聞。爰洎唐虞，建官惟百，夏商官倍。當其時，疇咨明揚，考言詢事，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。上以道求，下以行應，無常法也。逮于成周，大司徒以鄉三物敎萬民，攷其德行道藝而賓之于王，曰選士，曰俊士，曰造士，曰進士。論定而後官，任官而後爵，位定而後祿，擇才取士始爲詳矣，然猶未有
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Lin, an Education Official: “Insightful.”

Those who appoint men to office should above all administer the laws of the realm impartially; they need not accommodate every individual circumstance. Those entering official service must rectify the foundation of their fitness to serve, and must not calculate their personal advantage. Human circumstances cannot all be accommodated, and the law has no means of ensuring that every circumstance is met. If I uphold it impartially, then those whose circumstances cannot be fully accommodated and I alike will have no cause for regret. What grounds, then, are there for resentment against the law? Scholars aspire to serve the world, but the law provides no warrant for advancement through mere good fortune. If I await appointment with rectitude, then even when advancement proves difficult, I can remain at peace with the law. Why, then, be impatient for personal gain? If this is truly so, those entering service will not worry about spending many days without an appointment, and those responsible for personnel selection need not fear an ever-growing backlog of candidates.

Long ago, the sovereign Fuxi named offices after things; the institutions by which men were recommended and selected are so remote that nothing of them is known. By the time of Tang and Yu—that is, Yao and Shun—only a hundred offices were established; under the Xia and Shang, their number doubled. In those days, inquiries were made and worthy men openly recommended; their words were examined and their deeds investigated. Outstanding men were summoned from far and wide and placed in the various offices. Those above sought them according to the Way, and those below responded through their conduct: there were no fixed procedures. By the Zhou dynasty, the Minister of Education instructed all the people through the three categories of township teaching, examined their virtue, conduct, learning, and skills, and presented them as honored guests to the king. They were designated “selected scholars” (xuanshi), “outstanding scholars” (junshi), “accomplished scholars” (zaoshi), and “advanced scholars” (jinshi). Only after their assessment was settled were they appointed to office; only after appointment were they granted rank; and only after their positions were fixed were they granted stipends. The selection of talent and recruitment of scholars thus began to become detailed. Yet there was still no…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
銓選之法也至漢成帝立常侍曹尚書一
人以主公卿之選立二千石曹尚書一人
以主郡國之選而選法始起光武改常侍
曹為吏部尚書以總三曹之事而選法專
隸之吏部矣自時厥後魏有九品中正之
法唐有三曹選法宋有國初之選法有元
豐之銓法然皆愈詳愈敝愈敝愈變用中
正者膏粱閥閱坐登仕版而寒素有不得
進之滯循資格者闒茸讒諂立升要路而
===
豪傑有不得伸之歎故崔亮嘗變中正矣
而停解之法賢愚同貫或咎亮之失才魏
玄同張九齡嘗欲停資格矣而選舉之制
迄不可復終莫能遂其志此宋人調停之
說所由起也恭惟我
朝稽古定制設吏部尚書佐以侍郎有郎中
員外郎主事為之屬有文選司以掌文官
銓選之法蓋古之資格也用之
累朝得人為治至我
punctuated:
銓選之法也。至漢成帝，立常侍曹尚書一人，以主公卿之選；立二千石曹尚書一人，以主郡國之選，而選法始起。光武改常侍曹為吏部尚書，以總三曹之事，而選法專隸之吏部矣。自時厥後，魏有九品中正之法，唐有三曹選法，宋有國初之選法，有元豐之銓法。然皆愈詳愈敝，愈敝愈變。用中正者，膏粱閥閱坐登仕版，而寒素有不得進之滯；循資格者，闒茸讒諂立升要路，而豪傑有不得伸之歎。故崔亮嘗變中正矣，而停解之法，賢愚同貫，或咎亮之失才；魏玄同、張九齡嘗欲停資格矣，而選舉之制迄不可復，終莫能遂其志。此宋人調停之說所由起也。
恭惟我朝稽古定制，設吏部尚書，佐以侍郎，有郎中、員外郎、主事為之屬，有文選司以掌文官銓選之法，蓋古之資格也。用之累朝，得人為治。至我
translation_en:
…a system for selecting and appointing officials. Under Emperor Cheng of the Han, one Director of the Imperial Secretariat was appointed to the Section for Regular Attendants to oversee the selection of the highest ministers, and another to the Section for Officials of Two Thousand Bushels to oversee selection for the commanderies and kingdoms. Thus began a system of selection. Emperor Guangwu changed the Section for Regular Attendants into the post of Minister of Personnel, with overall responsibility for the affairs of the three sections; selection thereby came exclusively under the Ministry of Personnel. Thereafter, the Wei had the nine-rank system of Rectifiers, the Tang had selection through three sections, and the Song had both its early dynastic selection system and the appointment system of the Yuanfeng era. Yet the more elaborate these became, the more abuses arose; the more abuses arose, the more they were altered. Under the Rectifiers, scions of wealthy, distinguished families entered the official rolls without effort, while men of humble background were held back from advancement. Under selection by prescribed qualifications and seniority, the base and incompetent, slanderers and flatterers, rose at once to powerful posts, while outstanding men lamented that they could not fulfill their potential. Thus Cui Liang once altered the system of Rectifiers, but his system of ‘suspending release’ [?] treated the worthy and foolish alike, and some blamed him for failing to secure men of talent. Wei Xuantong and Zhang Jiuling once sought to abolish selection by qualifications and seniority, but the earlier system of selection and recommendation could never be restored, and neither ultimately achieved his aim. This was the origin of the Song writers’ proposals for reconciling the systems.
We reverently reflect that our dynasty examined antiquity to establish its institutions. It instituted a Minister of Personnel, assisted by Vice Ministers, with Bureau Directors, Vice Directors, and Secretaries as subordinate officials. Its Bureau of Civil Appointments administers the selection and appointment of civil officials, essentially following the earlier system of qualifications and seniority. Employed through successive reigns, it has secured suitable men to carry on government. Now, under our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上殫心化理尤愼用人家宰之官不輕授任
常慮選法爲滯重以
天語丁寧宜乎仕路清通人才彙進矣而執事
猶曰赴部待選動至數千給假家居恒逾
二萬至有白首不得一命幸而得之亦皆
垂老志得之年深歎夫壅滯之弊而欲求
變通之計者何也將謂入仕之源有未清
歟愚觀今
國家入仕之途不過歲貢科舉吏員三者而
===
已外此則有蔭補之冑納粟之例而已然
歲貢科舉定額未增于舊蔭補胥吏資格
不混其常納貲入監非爲常例其視上官
均之所謂四弊曰雜流曰特奏曰資蔭曰
入流者不待去而自無惡在其爲仕源之
不清也將謂冗濫之員未盡去歟考自
皇上臨治以來屢
勅吏部通查天下凡官之事簡可兼及因時添
設者盡從裁革至今停選而又有六察嚴
punctuated:
皇上殫心化理，尤愼用人，家宰之官不輕授任，常慮選法爲滯，重以天語丁寧。宜乎仕路清通，人才彙進矣。而執事猶曰：「赴部待選，動至數千；給假家居，恒逾二萬。至有白首不得一命，幸而得之，亦皆垂老志得之年。」深歎夫壅滯之弊，而欲求變通之計者，何也？將謂入仕之源有未清歟？
愚觀今國家入仕之途，不過歲貢、科舉、吏員三者而已。外此，則有蔭補之冑、納粟之例而已。然歲貢、科舉，定額未增于舊；蔭補、胥吏，資格不混其常；納貲入監，非爲常例。其視上官均之所謂四弊，曰雜流，曰特奏，曰資蔭，曰入流者，不待去而自無。惡在其爲仕源之不清也？
將謂冗濫之員未盡去歟？考自皇上臨治以來，屢勅吏部通查天下，凡官之事簡可兼及因時添設者，盡從裁革，至今停選。而又有六察嚴
translation_en:
…His Majesty devotes his whole mind to governance and moral transformation and is especially cautious in employing men. He does not lightly confer the office of Minister of Personnel. Ever concerned that the selection procedures cause delays, he has repeatedly issued earnest imperial admonitions. One would therefore expect the path to office to be clear and unobstructed, with talented men advancing together. Yet you, the examiners, still say: “Those who report to the ministry awaiting selection frequently number several thousand; those granted leave to remain at home regularly exceed twenty thousand. Some reach old age without receiving a single appointment; even those fortunate enough to obtain one fulfill their ambitions only when they are approaching old age.” Why do you so deeply lament the harm caused by this congestion and seek a means of reform? Is it that the sources of recruitment into office remain impure?
In my humble view, the state now has only three routes into office: annual tribute students, the civil-service examinations, and clerical service. Beyond these, there are only descendants appointed through hereditary privilege and the provisions for appointment through grain contributions. Yet the established quotas for annual tribute students and examination graduates have not increased over their former levels; the eligibility requirements for those entering through hereditary privilege and clerical service retain their regular distinctions; and admission to the Directorate of Education through monetary contributions is not a standing practice. Compared with what Shangguan Jun called the four abuses—miscellaneous avenues of recruitment, special recommendations to the throne, hereditary privilege, and admission to ranked official service—these abuses are absent of themselves, without needing to be eliminated. Where, then, is the alleged impurity in the sources of recruitment?
Is it that superfluous and excessive posts have not all been eliminated? Since His Majesty began his reign, he has repeatedly ordered the Ministry of Personnel to conduct a comprehensive review throughout the realm. All posts whose duties were light enough to be combined with others, and those added to meet temporary circumstances, have been abolished, and appointments to them remain suspended to this day. Moreover, the six censorial divisions strictly…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
糾劾於監臨吏部明考察於朝
覲其視歐陽脩之所謂四色曰年老曰患病曰
貪汙曰不才者已皆汰而不留烏在其爲
冗員之未去也然則變通之法將無用乎
愚嘗思之厥初生民寡鮮大地爲墟爰自
三代養育以迄于今齒類益繁猶皆各奠
攸居未聞有巢棲而穴處者乘除消長之
數天固有自然之妙而非人之所能與也
銓選之法何以異是嘗觀今之需選者科
===
貢率十餘年而得官胥吏十五年而得官
蔭補者半之若進士之選則又速矣循資
之外又有揀選遠方之例家貧親老者得
就此以申其願若不爲壅矣其間歲貢出
身之人容或有皓首膺命之悲蓋其所成
之時則然也固無害其爲選法之通矣又
竊嘗觀之天之生物洪纖巨細各惟其質
遲速榮悴各惟其時夭札久固各惟其氣
不能强之而使同是雖父母之於子有不
punctuated:
糾劾於監臨，吏部明考察於朝覲。其視歐陽脩之所謂四色，曰年老，曰患病，曰貪汙，曰不才者，已皆汰而不留，烏在其爲冗員之未去也？然則變通之法將無用乎？

愚嘗思之：厥初生民寡鮮，大地爲墟。爰自三代養育，以迄于今，齒類益繁，猶皆各奠攸居，未聞有巢棲而穴處者。乘除消長之數，天固有自然之妙，而非人之所能與也。銓選之法，何以異是？嘗觀今之需選者，科貢率十餘年而得官，胥吏十五年而得官，蔭補者半之。若進士之選，則又速矣。循資之外，又有揀選遠方之例，家貧親老者得就此以申其願，若不爲壅矣。其間歲貢出身之人，容或有皓首膺命之悲，蓋其所成之時則然也，固無害其爲選法之通矣。

又竊嘗觀之：天之生物，洪纖巨細，各惟其質；遲速榮悴，各惟其時；夭札久固，各惟其氣，不能强之而使同。是雖父母之於子，有不
translation_en:
…conduct impeachments in the course of supervision, while the Ministry of Personnel rigorously evaluates officials when they attend court audience. As for the four categories identified by Ouyang Xiu—those who are old, ill, corrupt, or incompetent—all have already been dismissed, with none retained. How, then, can it be said that superfluous officials have not been removed? Does this mean that measures of adaptation and reform have no use?

I have often reflected on this: when humankind first arose, people were few, and the vast earth lay empty. From the nurturing of the people under the Three Dynasties down to the present, the population has steadily multiplied. Yet everyone still has a settled dwelling; we do not hear of people living in nests or caves. In the patterns of increase and decrease, decline and growth, Heaven possesses a natural subtlety in which human beings cannot intervene. How does the system of official selection differ from this? I have observed that among those now awaiting selection, examination and tribute candidates generally obtain office after more than ten years, clerks after fifteen years, and those appointed through hereditary privilege after half that time. Selection for metropolitan graduates (jinshi) is faster still. Besides appointment according to seniority and qualifications, there is also a provision for selecting men for distant posts. Those whose families are poor and whose parents are old can use this provision to fulfill their wishes; thus there seems to be no blockage. Among those who entered through annual tribute, some may indeed suffer the sorrow of receiving an appointment only when their hair has turned white. But this results from the time at which they attained their qualification; it certainly does not detract from the effective operation of the selection system.

I have also privately observed that, among the living things Heaven produces, whether vast or minute, large or small, each follows its own inherent nature. Whether they flourish or wither, early or late, each follows its own season. Whether they die prematurely or endure, each depends on its own vital endowment. They cannot be forced to become alike. In this, even parents in dealing with their children cannot always…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
監臨物務以利誘人者不以自待其身則
靖恭之下行誼已章雖終身未沾一命而
其所榮者不旣多乎如此則蘇軾之所謂
以蒞官之所得爲居閑仰給之資者非所
恤於上矣然而掌銓者何難於用法也昔
在唐宋有墨勅之官有內降之除皆自宮
闈而出倖濫之輩溷我清流此猶可諉曰
衡之未平天子奪之也今
皇上於吏部尚書簡任責成未嘗侵職愼惜名
===
器不輕授予而今之士人猶有囂囂於銓
部者豈所居之者敦尚勤儉甄别清通如
毛玠山濤者未得其人耶抑豈所謂天地
之大人猶有所憾者耶嗚呼吾果至公如
天則人言不恤可也如或未然得無有厘
於位乎而入仕者又何難於守正也古之
時公卿大夫之子弟皆自幼年入學至四
十方仕士脩其學學至而君求之故其行
備業全事理績茂秦漢以降乃異於斯其
punctuated:
監臨物務，以利誘人者，不以自待其身，則靖恭之下，行誼已章。雖終身未沾一命，而其所榮者不旣多乎？如此，則蘇軾之所謂以蒞官之所得爲居閑仰給之資者，非所恤於上矣。然而掌銓者何難於用法也？昔在唐宋，有墨勅之官，有內降之除，皆自宮闈而出，倖濫之輩溷我清流。此猶可諉曰：「衡之未平，天子奪之也。」今皇上於吏部尚書簡任責成，未嘗侵職，愼惜名器，不輕授予，而今之士人猶有囂囂於銓部者，豈所居之者敦尚勤儉、甄别清通，如毛玠、山濤者，未得其人耶？抑豈所謂天地之大，人猶有所憾者耶？嗚呼！吾果至公如天，則人言不恤可也。如或未然，得無有厘於位乎？

而入仕者又何難於守正也？古之時，公卿大夫之子弟皆自幼年入學，至四十方仕。士脩其學，學至而君求之，故其行備業全，事理績茂。秦漢以降，乃異於斯，其
translation_en:
…in overseeing affairs, if one does not apply to oneself the inducements of profit used to entice others [?], then beneath one’s quiet reverence, upright conduct is already manifest. Even if one never receives an official appointment throughout one’s life, are not the honors one possesses already abundant? If so, what Su Shi spoke of—using the proceeds of holding office as the means of support in retirement—would not be a concern for those above. Yet why should those responsible for selecting officials find it difficult to apply the rules? In the Tang and Song, there were officials appointed by ink-written imperial orders and appointments issued directly from the inner palace. All these came from the palace precincts; men favored without merit or appointed indiscriminately polluted our pure ranks. One could still excuse this by saying: “The balance was not even because the Son of Heaven took the decision out of our hands.” Now His Majesty selects and appoints the Minister of Personnel and holds him responsible for results, without ever encroaching upon his duties. He carefully safeguards titles and offices and does not bestow them lightly. Yet scholars today still clamor against the Ministry of Personnel. Is it that suitable men have not been found to occupy its posts—men like Mao Jie and Shan Tao, who esteemed diligence and frugality and were discerning, impartial, and perceptive in assessing candidates? Or is this what is meant by saying that, vast though Heaven and Earth are, people still find grounds for dissatisfaction? Alas! If we truly are as impartial as Heaven, we may disregard what people say. But if we are not, might there be some fault in our discharge of office [?]?

And why should those entering official service find it difficult to uphold rectitude? In ancient times, the sons and younger relatives of dukes, ministers, and grandees all entered school in childhood and did not take office until forty. Scholars cultivated their learning; when their learning was mature, the ruler sought them out. Thus their conduct was fully formed and their studies complete; affairs were well ordered and their achievements abundant. From the Qin and Han onward, things were different: their…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
行敎也不深其取材也務速人才愈多治
功愈壞職此之由今之需選於銓部者胥
吏雜流無容深議其出於科貢入貲者皆
謂之士人我
國家旣養之於庠序董之以憲臣比其有成
則又晉之國學廣其聞見敎之不爲不豫
矣而猶有汲汲於求仕敗德於授官者豈
所敎之者身先孝弟敦尚行實如陽城安
定者未得其人耶抑亦執德不固見義未
===
明脩之於家而壞之於庭耶嗚呼吾知窮
達有命則守正以俟可也如其未然得無
有負於敎乎執事曰變通之法以疏壅滯
愚則曰非壅滯之足患也要在掌銓者之
秉其公執事曰莅官之資以給居閑愚則
曰非資給之足恤也要在入仕者之安於
敎然則銓選之法終無可言乎曰入貲之
例以濟時艱不宜於數開田里之賢盡收
科目無庸於辟舉資格以待常品則不亂
punctuated:
行敎也不深，其取材也務速，人才愈多，治功愈壞，職此之由。今之需選於銓部者，胥吏雜流，無容深議；其出於科貢、入貲者，皆謂之士人。我國家旣養之於庠序，董之以憲臣，比其有成，則又晉之國學，廣其聞見，敎之不爲不豫矣。而猶有汲汲於求仕、敗德於授官者，豈所敎之者身先孝弟、敦尚行實，如陽城、安定者，未得其人耶？抑亦執德不固，見義未明，脩之於家而壞之於庭耶？嗚呼！吾知窮達有命，則守正以俟可也。如其未然，得無有負於敎乎？

執事曰：「變通之法，以疏壅滯。」愚則曰：「非壅滯之足患也，要在掌銓者之秉其公。」執事曰：「莅官之資，以給居閑。」愚則曰：「非資給之足恤也，要在入仕者之安於敎。」然則銓選之法，終無可言乎？曰：「入貲之例，以濟時艱，不宜於數開；田里之賢，盡收科目，無庸於辟舉；資格以待常品，則不亂
translation_en:
…their implementation of instruction lacked depth, and their recruitment of talent sought speed. The more numerous the men of talent became, the worse the achievements of government grew: this was precisely the cause. Among those now awaiting selection by the Ministry of Personnel, clerks and men from miscellaneous recruitment streams need not be discussed at length. Those who enter through examinations, tribute recommendation, or monetary contributions are all called scholars. Our dynasty has already nurtured them in local schools and supervised them through censorial officials. Once they have attained proficiency, it further advances them to the National University to broaden their knowledge and experience. Its instruction can hardly be said to lack preparation. Yet there are still those who anxiously pursue office and undermine their virtue upon receiving appointments. Is this because suitable teachers have not been found—men like Yang Cheng and Anding [Hu Yuan], who personally exemplified filial piety and fraternal respect and earnestly esteemed substantive moral conduct? Or is it that these scholars hold virtue insecurely and do not yet clearly discern righteousness, cultivating themselves at home only to undo that cultivation at court? Alas! If I know that adversity and advancement are determined by fate, I need only maintain rectitude and wait. If I do otherwise, would I not betray the instruction I have received?

You say: “Adapt the procedures to relieve the backlog.” I humbly reply: “The backlog is not what should cause concern. What matters is that those responsible for personnel selection uphold impartiality.” You say: “The resources obtained through holding office can support those awaiting appointment.” I humbly reply: “Material provision is not what should cause anxiety. What matters is that those entering office rest content in the teachings they have received.” Does this mean, then, that nothing at all can be said about the procedures for personnel selection? I reply: “The provision for entry through monetary contributions serves to relieve the difficulties of the times; it should not be opened repeatedly. Worthy men from the countryside should all be recruited through the examinations; there is no need for recruitment by invitation and recommendation. Eligibility requirements should govern the treatment of men of ordinary ability, so that they do not disrupt …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
序於私親超用以待異才匪為徇法於權
貴獎拔恬退則奔競者自抑崇尚清節則
請謁者羞為此在掌銓者加之意而已若
夫慎簡其人是在吾
君吾相之權衡人物也草茅之言不知忌諱惟
執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 序於私親；超用以待異才，匪為徇法於權貴。獎拔恬退，則奔競者自抑；崇尚清節，則請謁者羞為。此在掌銓者加之意而已。若夫慎簡其人，是在吾君吾相之權衡人物也。草茅之言，不知忌諱，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …the order of precedence out of favoritism toward relatives; appointments beyond the usual grades should accommodate exceptional talent, rather than bend the rules for the powerful and eminent [?]. If the modest and retiring are rewarded and promoted, those who scramble for advancement will restrain themselves; if integrity is esteemed, those who solicit favors will be ashamed to do so. This requires only that those responsible for selecting officials give it their attention. As for carefully choosing those responsible, that rests upon our ruler and our chief ministers in weighing men’s qualities. These words from a man of the countryside take no account of taboos. I would count it a great kindness if you, sir, would receive me and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
嘉靖十九年秋八月廣東鄉
試錄成康以執事當序諸末
簡乃復申勗多士曰古稱虎
嘯而風冽龍興而致雲世有
明聖之君必有賢良之臣睹
諸虞夏商周可尚也已惟我
===
皇明列聖繼作禮樂聲敎之澤漸
濡浸潤積百有數十餘年今
上紹承鴻緒
文明濬哲道化丕隆溢於四海章
逢之士衣被薰育雖在疏逖
莫不窮經學古磨濯淬礪以
賢良事業自期待易曰聖人
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

嘉靖十九年秋八月，廣東鄉試錄成。康以執事，當序諸末簡，乃復申勗多士曰：「古稱虎嘯而風冽，龍興而致雲。世有明聖之君，必有賢良之臣，睹諸虞夏商周，可尚也已。惟我皇明列聖繼作，禮樂聲敎之澤，漸濡浸潤，積百有數十餘年。今上紹承鴻緒，文明濬哲，道化丕隆，溢於四海。章逢之士，衣被薰育，雖在疏逖，莫不窮經學古，磨濯淬礪，以賢良事業自期待。《易》曰：『聖人
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the nineteenth year of Jiajing (1540), the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination was completed. I, Kang, having served in the examination, was charged with composing a postface for its final leaves. I therefore once again exhorted the assembled scholars, saying:

“The ancients said that when the tiger roars, the wind blows fiercely, and when the dragon rises, clouds gather. When the world has an enlightened and sagely ruler, it must have worthy and good ministers. We see this in the ages of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou: they are indeed worthy of admiration. In our august Ming, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another, and the beneficent influence of rites, music, and moral instruction has steadily permeated the realm for more than a hundred and several tens of years. His present Majesty has inherited this grand legacy. His cultural brilliance and profound wisdom have brought the transforming power of the Way to great flourishing, extending throughout the Four Seas. Scholars wearing Confucian robes and caps, enveloped and nurtured by this influence, even in remote places, all investigate the classics exhaustively, study antiquity, and polish, cleanse, temper, and hone themselves, aspiring to the accomplishments of worthy and good men. The Book of Changes says: ‘The sage …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
久於其道而天下化成其弗
信矣乎今獲選而進之
天子之庭奮庸熈載固其會也康
於多士竊猶有餘懼焉夫文
辭藝也道德實也古之進也
以道德今之進也以辭章爾
多士以辭章進自今觀之固
===
有光明俊偉建功樹業庶幾
豪傑者出乎其間亦豈無脂
韋淟涊與時乾没始慎而終
以悖謬者是非辭章之罪不
善用者之過也夫聖人之道
入乎耳存乎心蘊之爲德行
行之爲事業故六經爲文之
punctuated: 久於其道而天下化成」，其弗信矣乎？今獲選而進之天子之庭，奮庸熈載，固其會也。康於多士，竊猶有餘懼焉。夫文辭，藝也；道德，實也。古之進也以道德，今之進也以辭章爾。多士以辭章進，自今觀之，固有光明俊偉、建功樹業、庶幾豪傑者出乎其間，亦豈無脂韋淟涊、與時乾没、始慎而終以悖謬者？是非辭章之罪，不善用者之過也。夫聖人之道，入乎耳，存乎心，蘊之爲德行，行之爲事業，故六經爲文之
translation_en: “…abides long in his Way, and the world is transformed and brought to fulfillment.” Is this not indeed true? Now, having been selected and advanced to the Son of Heaven’s court, they assuredly have their opportunity to exert their abilities and bring their duties to fruition. Yet I, Kang, still harbor some apprehension concerning these many scholars. Literary composition is an art; moral cultivation is the substance. In antiquity, men advanced through moral cultivation; today, they advance through literary composition alone. Judging from the present, among the many scholars who advance through literary composition, there will certainly emerge men of integrity and outstanding talent who establish achievements and careers, approaching the stature of heroes. Yet will there not also be men who are pliant and servile, sullied and shameless, pursuing gain as circumstances permit—men who begin cautiously but end in perversity and error? This is no fault of literary composition; it is the fault of those who fail to put it to good use. The Way of the sages enters through the ears and abides in the heart. Stored within, it becomes virtuous conduct; put into practice, it becomes achievement. Thus the Six Classics are, for literary composition, …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宗孔孟爲道德之宗皐夔稷
契伊傅周召爲事業之宗諸
士子亦既明六經誦法孔孟
欲見諸事業矣究其所用或
昧焉康也能無懼乎今夫勾
粤之榦鏃礪羽栝遇射疏及
遠則有功以之棓箠則與槁
===
樸無擇也湛盧干將之劍氣
凌紫蜆煇奪白日遇斷犀彖
蕩爭寇則有功以之刲穫則
與鉛刃無擇也是故器一也
用之於此則善於彼則不善
諸士產於粤猶粤榦神劍也
不務道德而第以辭章爲工
punctuated: 宗，孔孟爲道德之宗，皐夔稷契伊傅周召爲事業之宗。諸士子亦既明六經，誦法孔孟，欲見諸事業矣。究其所用，或昧焉，康也能無懼乎？今夫勾粤之榦鏃，礪羽栝，遇射疏及遠則有功；以之棓箠，則與槁樸無擇也。湛盧干將之劍，氣凌紫蜆，煇奪白日，遇斷犀彖、蕩爭寇則有功；以之刲穫，則與鉛刃無擇也。是故器一也，用之於此則善，於彼則不善。諸士產於粤，猶粤榦神劍也。不務道德，而第以辭章爲工，
translation_en:
…the guiding source; Confucius and Mencius are the guiding sources of moral virtue, and Gao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Yi, Fu, Zhou, and Shao are the guiding exemplars of practical achievement. You scholars have already understood the Six Classics, recited and emulated Confucius and Mencius, and wish to manifest this learning in practical achievements. Yet when one examines how you put it to use, some remain uncertain. Can I, Kang, be without apprehension?

Consider the arrow shafts and arrowheads of Gou and Yue, sharpened, feathered, and nocked. When used to shoot distant targets, they prove effective; used as clubs or rods, they are no different from withered pieces of wood. The swords Zhanlu and Ganjiang have an aura that rises above the purple [?], and a radiance that outshines the sun. Used to cut through rhinoceroses and swine [?] or sweep away hostile raiders, they prove effective; used for cutting and harvesting, they are no different from leaden blades. Thus the implement is the same: employed for one purpose it serves well, but for another it does not.

You scholars, born in Yue, are like its arrow shafts and divine swords. If you do not devote yourselves to moral virtue, but merely seek mastery of literary composition…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
時維三年大比之期巡按監
察御史洪垣遵
制聘取繼皐與教諭劉康爲考試
官教諭蕭彦陳光明甘汝孚
徐衍劉去矜王佩爲同考試
官至期曁提調布政使楊銓
===
參議汪大受監試按察使歐
陽席僉事李文鳳入院飭事
合提學僉事吳鵬所簡士而
三試之旣畢繼皐當叙諸文
首夫文以闡道道以顯文道
者氣之中正者也文者道之
顯設者也文王之文純亦不
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

時維三年大比之期，巡按監察御史洪垣遵制，聘取繼皐與教諭劉康爲考試官，教諭蕭彦、陳光明、甘汝孚、徐衍、劉去矜、王佩爲同考試官。至期，曁提調布政使楊銓、參議汪大受、監試按察使歐陽席、僉事李文鳳入院飭事，合提學僉事吳鵬所簡士而三試之。旣畢，繼皐當叙諸文首。

夫文以闡道，道以顯文。道者，氣之中正者也；文者，道之顯設者也。文王之文，純亦不
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

It was the appointed time for the triennial grand examination. Hong Yuan, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, acting in obedience to the imperial decree, engaged Jigao and Liu Kang, Instructor, as Examiners, and the Instructors Xiao Yan, Chen Guangming, Gan Rufu, Xu Yan, Liu Qujin, and Wang Pei as Associate Examiners. When the appointed time arrived, they entered the examination compound to put affairs in order together with the Proctors, Yang Quan, Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Wang Dashou, Administration Vice Commissioner, and the examination supervisors, Ouyang Xi, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Li Wenfeng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner. They assembled the candidates selected by Wu Peng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, and examined them in three sessions. When these were completed, it fell to Jigao to compose a preface to stand at the head of the collected essays.

Writing elucidates the Way, and the Way gives distinction to writing. The Way is that which is central and correct in vital energy; writing is the visible manifestation of the Way. The cultural accomplishment of King Wen was pure and likewise did not…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
巳夫子之文章性與天道者
也故文之高下類於風氣士
習焉符之氣之漓者其文散
氣之昌者其文華氣之朴者
其文簡氣之雄者其文確氣
之純者其文雅嶺南之風氣
其殆近昌以朴以雄不懈而
===
進於純者乎故其爲文爲直
方爲果毅直方果毅陽明之
象其變而至於純也爲近夫
純也者道也所謂氣之中正
者也故曰一陰一陽之謂道
其爲氣也近華而不豔近朴
而不野近確而不固苟損益
punctuated: 巳。夫子之文章，性與天道者也。故文之高下類於風氣，士習焉符之。氣之漓者，其文散；氣之昌者，其文華；氣之朴者，其文簡；氣之雄者，其文確；氣之純者，其文雅。嶺南之風氣，其殆近昌以朴以雄，不懈而進於純者乎？故其爲文，爲直方，爲果毅。直方果毅，陽明之象，其變而至於純也爲近。夫純也者，道也，所謂氣之中正者也。故曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」其爲氣也，近華而不豔，近朴而不野，近確而不固。苟損益
translation_en: …unceasing. The literary expression of Confucius embodies human nature and the Way of Heaven. Thus, the relative quality of writing corresponds to the prevailing ethos, and scholars’ habits accord with it. Where vital energy (qi) is diluted, writing is diffuse; where it flourishes, writing is ornate; where it is unadorned, writing is simple; where it is vigorous, writing is firm; where it is pure, writing is refined. Might the prevailing ethos of Lingnan approach flourishing abundance, simplicity, and vigor, advancing tirelessly toward purity? Thus, its writing is upright and principled, resolute and steadfast. Uprightness, principle, resolution, and steadfastness are manifestations of yang brightness; their transformation toward purity is therefore close at hand. Purity is the Way: what is called the balanced and correct condition of vital energy. Hence the saying: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” Such vital energy approaches ornateness without gaudiness, simplicity without coarseness, and firmness without rigidity. If one were to diminish and augment…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之過與不及文之以道德化
而裁之存乎其人焉爾故曰
學以變化氣質氣質變化則
盛德日新而風氣不與焉矣
是故一變而為唐張文獻公
九齡以功業著焉再變而為
宋崔清獻公與之以節行著
===
焉功業清節以漸而歸之道
者蓋亦其風氣與時偕行也
夫今則又再變矣自宋而來
將五百歲
聖人教化之盛氣運之隆厚蘊而
宏發之又豈無道德之士出
乎其間以當斯選者乎未可
punctuated:
之過與不及，文之以道德，化而裁之，存乎其人焉爾。故曰：「學以變化氣質。」氣質變化，則盛德日新，而風氣不與焉矣。是故一變而為唐張文獻公九齡，以功業著焉；再變而為宋崔清獻公與之，以節行著焉。功業清節，以漸而歸之道者，蓋亦其風氣與時偕行也夫！
今則又再變矣。自宋而來，將五百歲，聖人教化之盛，氣運之隆，厚蘊而宏發之，又豈無道德之士出乎其間，以當斯選者乎？未可
translation_en:
…their excesses and deficiencies, refining them through the Way and virtue: transforming and regulating them rests with the individual alone. Thus it is said: “Learning serves to transform one’s innate disposition.” When that disposition is transformed, abundant virtue is renewed daily, and the prevailing local ethos no longer has a part in it. Thus, with one transformation there appeared Zhang Jiuling of the Tang, honored posthumously as Lord Wenxian, who was renowned for his achievements; with a further transformation there appeared Cui Yuzhi of the Song, honored posthumously as Lord Qingxian, who was renowned for his integrity and conduct. That achievements and incorruptible integrity gradually come into accord with the Way is surely also a matter of the local ethos advancing with the times!
Now there has been yet another transformation. Nearly five hundred years have passed since the Song. With the flourishing of the sage ruler’s moral instruction and the fullness of the age’s vital forces, deeply accumulated and grandly expressed, could there be no men of the Way and virtue emerging among them who are worthy of selection in this examination? It cannot yet be…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知也今之觀道德之與功業
清節也孰觀哉觀其文焉言
焉已爾文有所言焉而所不
言者見焉是故君子觀言則
知默矣觀文則知質矣觀顯
則知隱矣觀動則知靜矣語
默文質隱顯動靜不失其正
===
焉而道德存乎其間矣故曰
觀今之功業清節之與道德
也必於文焉言焉觀之觀今
之文與言而其道德之蘊豈
無發越於其間而不可掩者
乎夫固未可知也顧諸生所
自期待何如耳期功業者必
punctuated: 知也。今之觀道德之與功業、清節也，孰觀哉？觀其文焉、言焉已爾。文有所言焉，而所不言者見焉。是故君子觀言則知默矣，觀文則知質矣，觀顯則知隱矣，觀動則知靜矣。語默、文質、隱顯、動靜，不失其正焉，而道德存乎其間矣。故曰：觀今之功業、清節之與道德也，必於文焉、言焉觀之。觀今之文與言，而其道德之蘊，豈無發越於其間而不可掩者乎？夫固未可知也。顧諸生所自期待何如耳。期功業者必
translation_en: …be known. In assessing moral virtue alongside public achievement and unsullied integrity today, what should we examine? Simply a person’s writings and words. Writing expresses certain things, yet what it does not express also becomes apparent within it. Thus, by observing speech, the gentleman understands silence; by observing outward refinement, he understands inner substance; by observing the manifest, he understands the hidden; and by observing activity, he understands stillness. When speech and silence, refinement and substance, the hidden and the manifest, activity and stillness all remain true to what is right, moral virtue resides among them. Thus I say: to assess public achievement and unsullied integrity alongside moral virtue today, one must examine writings and words. When we examine the writings and words of the present day, might there not be inward stores of moral virtue that shine forth within them and cannot be concealed? This indeed cannot yet be known. It depends only on what you students expect of yourselves. Those who aspire to public achievement will surely…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
止於功業期清節者必止於
清節正必之心累之也故志
學于道德則不期功業清節
而功業清節在其中矣是故
其才可以致相業矣又必觀
其有避相之心然後可焉其
志能以避相矣又必觀其有
===
聖賢之學然後可焉聖賢之
學文王之純亦不已夫子之
性與天道是也諸生皆誦法
文武孔子其必有為聖賢之
志者乎否則雖博今古工文
辭篤行義君子以為猶未學
也嘗觀自嶺以南多知學之
punctuated: 止於功業，期清節者必止於清節，正必之心累之也。故志學于道德，則不期功業清節，而功業清節在其中矣。是故其才可以致相業矣，又必觀其有避相之心，然後可焉；其志能以避相矣，又必觀其有聖賢之學，然後可焉。聖賢之學，文王之純亦不已，夫子之性與天道是也。諸生皆誦法文武孔子，其必有為聖賢之志者乎？否則，雖博今古、工文辭、篤行義，君子以為猶未學也。嘗觀自嶺以南，多知學之
translation_en: …go no further than accomplishments; those who aspire to unsullied integrity will necessarily go no further than unsullied integrity. It is precisely their insistence on a predetermined outcome that encumbers them. Thus, if one sets one’s heart on studying the Way and virtue, one need not aspire to accomplishments or unsullied integrity: both will be contained therein. Therefore, even when someone has the talent to achieve great things as a grand councilor, one must also see whether he has the disposition to shun that office before judging him worthy. Even when his resolve enables him to shun that office, one must also see whether he possesses the learning of the sages and worthies before judging him worthy. The learning of the sages and worthies is exemplified by King Wen’s unceasing purity and by the Master’s teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven. You students all recite the teachings of and take as your models Kings Wen and Wu and Confucius. Surely among you there are those resolved to become sages and worthies? Otherwise, even if you are widely versed in past and present, skilled in literary composition, and steadfast in righteous conduct, the gentleman considers you not yet to have learned. I have observed that south of the mountains there are many who understand learning …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
士其所漸磨而造詣又若大
有所受者豈盡其風聲氣習
之所入乎哉今之有司或徒
以文觀之期以功業清節而
止焉則又何以仰副
聖君賢相之責望得夫德行道藝
之士以共成正大光明之業
===
===
也哉程子曰言學以道爲至
言人以聖爲至諸子初服自
待庶其在斯乎庶其在斯乎
兹舉也提督軍務兵部左侍
郎兼都御史蔡經都御史李
顯總兵官安遠侯柳珣豫宏
規制士庶聿興而恊供庶務
punctuated:
士，其所漸磨而造詣，又若大有所受者，豈盡其風聲氣習之所入乎哉？今之有司，或徒以文觀之，期以功業清節而止焉，則又何以仰副聖君賢相之責望，得夫德行道藝之士，以共成正大光明之業也哉？程子曰：「言學以道爲至，言人以聖爲至。」諸子初服自待，庶其在斯乎！庶其在斯乎！
兹舉也，提督軍務兵部左侍郎兼都御史蔡經、都御史李顯、總兵官安遠侯柳珣，豫宏規制，士庶聿興；而恊供庶務，
translation_en:
…scholars. Through gradual cultivation, their attainments seem to reflect a substantial intellectual inheritance. Could these derive entirely from the influence of local traditions and habits? If officials today judge them solely by their writing, expecting no more than achievements in office and unsullied integrity, how can they fulfill the expectations of our sage sovereign and worthy ministers, obtain men of virtuous conduct and mastery of the Way and the arts, and together accomplish an undertaking of uprightness and radiance? Master Cheng said: “In speaking of learning, the Way is the highest attainment; in speaking of human beings, sagehood is the highest attainment.” You gentlemen, at the outset of your careers, should surely set your aspirations here! Surely set your aspirations here!
For this examination, Cai Jing, superintendent of military affairs and left vice minister of War concurrently serving as censor-in-chief; Li Xian, censor-in-chief; and Liu Xun, regional commander and Marquis of Anyuan, made extensive arrangements in advance. Scholars and commoners thereupon rose to the occasion; as for those who cooperated in attending to the various practical duties…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則叅政蕭晚周釋叅議宋茂
熈周延副使陳大珊陳嘉謀
涂揵韓楷僉事趙維雍瀾林
希元劉廷範都指揮董廷玉
楊忻叅將高誼程鑒各以其
職懋昭厥成蓋慎之也是故
文事章矣總督軍務總兵官
咸寧侯仇鸞叅賛軍務兵部
尚書兼都察院右都御史毛
伯温則又奉
命節鎮嶺南誕示威信以昭
文德而有懷之士勃勃然動忠悃
之思是故武事式矣文武合
一則道德存而儒者之功用
punctuated: 則叅政蕭晚、周釋，叅議宋茂熈、周延，副使陳大珊、陳嘉謀、涂揵、韓楷，僉事趙維、雍瀾、林希元、劉廷範，都指揮董廷玉、楊忻，叅將高誼、程鑒，各以其職懋昭厥成，蓋慎之也。是故文事章矣。總督軍務總兵官咸寧侯仇鸞、叅賛軍務兵部尚書兼都察院右都御史毛伯温，則又奉命節鎮嶺南，誕示威信，以昭文德，而有懷之士勃勃然動忠悃之思。是故武事式矣。文武合一，則道德存，而儒者之功用
translation_en:
…there were the Provincial Administration Vice Commissioners Xiao Wan and Zhou Shi; the Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners Song Maoxi and Zhou Yan; the Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Dashan, Chen Jiamou, Tu Jian, and Han Kai; the Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhao Wei, Yong Lan, Lin Xiyuan, and Liu Tingfan; the Regional Military Commissioners Dong Tingyu and Yang Xin; and the Assistant Regional Commanders Gao Yi and Cheng Jian. Each, through his own office, diligently brought this undertaking to a distinguished completion: such was the care they took. Thus civil affairs flourished.

Qiu Luan, Marquis of Xianning, Regional Commander and Supreme Commander of Military Affairs, and Mao Bowen, Minister of War and concurrently Right Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, charged with assisting in military affairs, further received the imperial command to exercise military authority over Lingnan. They amply displayed their authority and trustworthiness, thereby making manifest the virtues of civil government. Men of aspiration were thus stirred with vigorous feelings of heartfelt loyalty. Thus military affairs, too, were properly ordered. When the civil and military are united, the Way and virtue endure, and the practical achievements of Confucian scholars…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
全諸士子逢茲
盛典其將有以自奮也夫
江西九江府儒學教授林繼
皐謹序
punctuated:
全。諸士子逢茲盛典，其將有以自奮也夫！
江西九江府儒學教授林繼皐謹序。
translation_en:
…is fully realized. Encountering this grand occasion, the examination candidates will surely find inspiration to exert themselves!
Respectfully prefaced by Lin Jigao, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jiujiang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子無終食之間違仁造次必於是顛沛
必於是
温故而知新敦厚以崇禮
聖人旣竭目力焉繼之以規矩準繩以為
方員平直不可勝用也旣竭耳力焉繼
之以六律正五音不可勝用也旣竭心
思焉繼之以不忍人之政而仁覆天下
===
矣
易
臨剛浸而長說而順剛中而應大亨以正
天之道也
王假有廟王乃在中也
夫易廣矣大矣以言乎遠則不禦以言乎
邇則靜而正以言乎天地之間則備矣
夫乾其靜也專其動也直是以大生焉
夫坤其靜也翕其動也闢是以廣生焉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

君子無終食之間違仁，造次必於是，顛沛必於是。

温故而知新，敦厚以崇禮。

聖人旣竭目力焉，繼之以規矩準繩，以為方員平直，不可勝用也；旣竭耳力焉，繼之以六律，正五音，不可勝用也；旣竭心思焉，繼之以不忍人之政，而仁覆天下矣。

易

臨，剛浸而長，說而順，剛中而應，大亨以正，天之道也。

王假有廟，王乃在中也。

夫易，廣矣，大矣！以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正；以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉；夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The gentleman does not depart from benevolence even for the time it takes to finish a meal. In haste and urgency he necessarily abides in it; in distress and adversity he necessarily abides in it.

He reviews what he has learned and thereby gains new understanding; he cultivates generosity and sincerity in order to honor ritual propriety.

Having exerted their eyesight to the utmost, the sages supplemented it with compasses, squares, levels, and marking lines, thereby making squares, circles, level surfaces, and straight lines in inexhaustible application. Having exerted their hearing to the utmost, they supplemented it with the six pitch standards to regulate the five notes, likewise in inexhaustible application. Having exerted their minds to the utmost, they supplemented their thought with government that could not bear to see others suffer, and benevolence thus spread over all under Heaven.

Book of Changes

In Lin (Approach), the firm gradually grows. Joyous and yielding, the firm occupies the central position and finds a response. Great success through correctness: this is the Way of Heaven.

“The king approaches the ancestral temple”: the king is indeed in the center.

How broad and great is the Book of Changes! Speaking of what is distant, it knows no bounds; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct; speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything. Qian (the Creative), in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct. Thus it gives rise to greatness. Kun (the Receptive), in stillness, closes; in movement, it opens. Thus it gives rise to breadth. …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
君子脩此三者故全也
書
安汝止惟幾惟康
惟木從繩則正后從諫則聖后克聖臣不
命其承疇敢不祗若王之休命
一曰正直二曰剛克三曰柔克
黍稷非馨明德惟馨
詩
春日載陽有鳴倉庚女執懿筐遵彼微行
===
爰求柔桑春日遲遲采蘩祁祁
物其多矣維其嘉矣物其旨矣維其偕矣
物其有矣維其時矣
泂酌彼行潦挹彼注茲可以餴饎豈弟君
子民之父母泂酌彼行潦挹彼注茲可
以濯罍豈弟君子民之攸歸泂酌彼行
潦挹彼注茲可以濯溉豈弟君子民之
攸墍
綏我眉壽介以繁祉旣右烈考亦右文母
punctuated:
君子脩此三者，故全也。

書
安汝止，惟幾惟康。
惟木從繩則正，后從諫則聖。后克聖，臣不命其承，疇敢不祗若王之休命？
一曰正直，二曰剛克，三曰柔克。
黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。

詩
春日載陽，有鳴倉庚。女執懿筐，遵彼微行，爰求柔桑。春日遲遲，采蘩祁祁。
物其多矣，維其嘉矣！物其旨矣，維其偕矣！物其有矣，維其時矣！
泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以餴饎。豈弟君子，民之父母。泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以濯罍。豈弟君子，民之攸歸。泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以濯溉。豈弟君子，民之攸墍。
綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。旣右烈考，亦右文母。
translation_en:
…The gentleman cultivates these three things and thus preserves himself intact.

Book of Documents

Be settled in your proper place; attend to the first stirrings of events and to maintaining peace.

Just as wood becomes straight by following the marking cord, a ruler becomes sage by following remonstrance. If the ruler can become sage, his ministers will carry out his wishes without being commanded. Who would dare not reverently obey the king’s excellent commands?

The first is uprightness; the second, governing through firmness; the third, governing through gentleness.

It is not the millet offerings that are fragrant; luminous virtue alone is fragrant.

Book of Odes

The spring days grow warm; the orioles sing. The women carry fine baskets and follow those narrow paths, seeking tender mulberry leaves. The spring days lengthen; those gathering white southernwood throng together.

The provisions are abundant, and excellent indeed! The provisions are delicious, and complete in their variety! The provisions are available, and appropriate to the season!

Draw water from those distant roadside pools; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used to steam the sacrificial grain. The gracious, amiable gentleman is the father and mother of the people. Draw water from those distant roadside pools; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used to wash wine jars. The gracious, amiable gentleman is the one to whom the people turn. Draw water from those distant roadside pools; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used to wash and rinse vessels. The gracious, amiable gentleman is the one in whom the people find repose.

Grant me long life, and aid me with abundant blessings. Having honored my illustrious deceased father, honor also my accomplished mother.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
秋八月蔡季自陳歸于蔡桓公十有七年
春王正月宋公曹伯衞人邾人伐齊狄
救齊僖公十有八年春晉侯侵曹晉侯
伐衞僖公二十有八年楚子陳侯隨侯
許男圍蔡哀公元年
春公觀魚于棠隱公五年夏五月宋人及
楚人平宣公十有五年
叔孫舍至自晉昭公二十有四年
===
禮記
刑者侀也侀者成也一成而不可變故君
子盡心焉
禮之以少爲貴者以其内心也德産之致
也精微觀天下之物無可以稱其德者
如此則得不以少爲貴乎是故君子慎
其獨也
禮樂皆得謂之有德德者得也
是故其德盛者其志厚其志厚者其義章
punctuated:
春秋

「秋八月，蔡季自陳歸于蔡。」桓公十有七年。「春王正月，宋公、曹伯、衞人、邾人伐齊。狄救齊。」僖公十有八年。「春，晉侯侵曹。晉侯伐衞。」僖公二十有八年。「楚子、陳侯、隨侯、許男圍蔡。」哀公元年。

「春，公觀魚于棠。」隱公五年。「夏五月，宋人及楚人平。」宣公十有五年。

「叔孫舍至自晉。」昭公二十有四年。

禮記

刑者，侀也；侀者，成也。一成而不可變，故君子盡心焉。

禮之以少爲貴者，以其内心也。德産之致也，精微。觀天下之物，無可以稱其德者。如此，則得不以少爲貴乎？是故君子慎其獨也。

禮樂皆得，謂之有德。德者，得也。

是故其德盛者，其志厚；其志厚者，其義章。
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In autumn, in the eighth month, Ji of Cai returned to Cai from Chen.” Seventeenth year of Duke Huan.
“In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Cao, and men of Wei and Zhu attacked Qi. The Di came to Qi’s aid.” Eighteenth year of Duke Xi.
“In spring, the Marquis of Jin invaded Cao. The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei.” Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.
“The Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Sui, and the Baron of Xu besieged Cai.” First year of Duke Ai.

“In spring, the duke watched the fishing at Tang.” Fifth year of Duke Yin.
“In summer, in the fifth month, the men of Song and the men of Chu made peace.” Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.

“Shusun She arrived back from Jin.” Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.

Book of Rites

Punishment (xing) means giving form (xing); giving form means completing. Once completed, it cannot be altered. Thus the gentleman devotes his utmost care to it.

Where ritual values small quantities, it does so because it values the inner heart. The fullest expression of what virtue produces is subtle and refined. Looking at all things under Heaven, none can adequately match that virtue. This being so, how could small quantities fail to be valued? Thus the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.

To attain both ritual and music is called possessing virtue. Virtue (de) means attainment (de).

Thus, those whose virtue is abundant have deeply earnest intentions; those whose intentions are deeply earnest manifest their righteousness…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其義章者其祭也敬祭敬則竟內之子
孫莫敢不敬矣
第貳場
論
孔子之謂集大成
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢以卓茂爲太傅封褒德侯詔建武元年
擬唐以陸贄爲翰林學士誥建中四年
擬宋廣州教授林勲上本政書表建炎三年
===
判語五條
舉用有過官吏
檢踏災傷田糧
禁止師巫邪術
邊境申索軍需
軍民約會詞訟
第叁場
策五道
問三代而下惟漢得天下爲正我
punctuated:
其義章者，其祭也敬；祭敬，則竟內之子孫莫敢不敬矣。

第貳場
論：孔子之謂集大成。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢以卓茂爲太傅、封褒德侯詔，建武元年。
擬唐以陸贄爲翰林學士誥，建中四年。
擬宋廣州教授林勲上本政書表，建炎三年。

判語五條：舉用有過官吏；檢踏災傷田糧；禁止師巫邪術；邊境申索軍需；軍民約會詞訟。

第叁場
策五道。
問：三代而下，惟漢得天下爲正。我
translation_en:
…Those whose righteousness is manifest are reverent in their sacrifices; when sacrifices are conducted reverently, none of the sons and grandsons within the territory dares to be irreverent.

Second Session
Discourse: Confucius is said to have brought together the great achievements of his predecessors.
One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty appointing Zhuo Mao Grand Preceptor and enfeoffing him as Marquis of Commended Virtue: first year of Jianwu [25 CE].
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Lu Zhi a Hanlin Academician: fourth year of Jianzhong [783].
Compose a memorial in the voice of Lin Xun, Instructor of Guangzhou under the Song dynasty, submitting his Book on the Foundations of Government (Ben zheng shu): third year of Jianyan [1129].

Five legal judgment topics:
Recommending and appointing officials and clerks with past offenses.
Inspecting disaster-damaged farmland and its grain-tax assessments.
Prohibiting shamans and their heterodox arts.
Requests from frontier regions for military supplies.
Military personnel and civilians arranging joint litigation.

Third Session
Five policy questions.
Question: Since the Three Dynasties, only the Han gained All under Heaven legitimately. Our …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明亦然昔班彪稱漢高帝之興有五
本朝學士宋濂稱我
太祖高皇帝之興有六其詳可得聞與
本朝得天下雖同於漢然漢得天下於亡秦
其時去古未遠先王紀綱制度猶有存
者高帝不能收拾補綴使先王典禮旣
亡而復存僅爲一時苟簡之治而已我
太祖高皇帝得天下於亡秦千載之後乃能法
古爲治使
===
一代典章文物煥然二帝三王之盛則其
神謨聖見度越漢高有前人之所未言者爾諸
生能詳言之與三代而下繼體之君表
章六經者或好大喜功致海內之虛耗
收復淮蔡者或器小易盈致美業之弗
終銳志更法者或委用非人釀天下之
禍亂未有卓然足稱中興之盛者肆我
皇上龍飛藩邸運際昌期
文武神聖全稟於天河清慶雲洊薦符瑞
punctuated: 明亦然。昔班彪稱漢高帝之興有五，本朝學士宋濂稱我太祖高皇帝之興有六，其詳可得聞與？本朝得天下雖同於漢，然漢得天下於亡秦，其時去古未遠，先王紀綱制度猶有存者。高帝不能收拾補綴，使先王典禮旣亡而復存，僅爲一時苟簡之治而已。我太祖高皇帝得天下於亡秦千載之後，乃能法古爲治，使一代典章文物煥然二帝三王之盛，則其神謨聖見度越漢高，有前人之所未言者，爾諸生能詳言之與？三代而下，繼體之君表章六經者，或好大喜功，致海內之虛耗；收復淮蔡者，或器小易盈，致美業之弗終；銳志更法者，或委用非人，釀天下之禍亂。未有卓然足稱中興之盛者。肆我皇上龍飛藩邸，運際昌期，文武神聖全稟於天，河清慶雲洊薦符瑞。
translation_en:
…Ming is likewise. Formerly, Ban Biao stated that there were five grounds for the rise of Emperor Gao of Han; Song Lian, an Academician of our dynasty, stated that there were six grounds for the rise of our Emperor Taizu Gao. May we hear these in detail? Although our dynasty gained All-under-Heaven in the same manner as the Han, the Han gained it upon the fall of Qin. That age was not far removed from antiquity, and some of the guiding principles and institutions of the former kings still survived. Emperor Gao could not gather and repair them, restoring the former kings’ canonical rites after their loss; he achieved only an expedient and rudimentary government for his own time. Our Emperor Taizu Gao gained All-under-Heaven a thousand years after Qin’s fall, yet was able to model his government on antiquity, making the dynasty’s institutions and cultural achievements shine with the splendor of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. His divine plans and sagely insight thus surpassed those of Emperor Gao of Han in ways that earlier writers have not discussed. Can you candidates explain these in detail?

Since the Three Dynasties, among rulers who inherited the throne, one who exalted the Six Classics was nevertheless grandiose and eager for achievements, exhausting the resources of the realm; one who recovered Huai and Cai was nevertheless limited in capacity and easily satisfied, failing to bring his admirable undertaking to completion; and one determined to reform the laws nevertheless entrusted responsibilities to unsuitable men, fomenting calamity and disorder throughout All-under-Heaven. None stood out sufficiently to merit acclaim for the splendor of a dynastic restoration. Now our Emperor has risen like a dragon from his princely residence, his destiny coinciding with an age of flourishing fortune. His civil and martial virtues, divine wisdom, and sageliness are all fully endowed by Heaven. The Yellow River running clear and auspicious clouds have repeatedly presented favorable portents…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
臨御以來孜孜求治其所以經綸大業巍巍乎
足稱中興之盛有以度越漢唐宋之君
者有五爾諸生亦曾聞而誦之乎夫陶
鎔菁莪棫樸之化而鋪張敷揚
一代之盛亦臣子事也試一一為我言之
問移風易俗莫善於禮禮樂不興則刑罰
不中奢淫日蕩獄訟繁興是禮者天地
之紀而民之所以生者也今之牧民者
果能建萬世之長策舉
===
明主於三代之隆而不徒區區簿書聽訟如王
吉之言者乎夫外庭告冠聞者却立父
在學禮君子譏之此在賢者且然則古
禮之難復久矣然唐之牧守乃能獨行
於一郡之間至有百姓聞之而泣下者
又安在其為不可乎說者謂夫子作春
秋不存禮樂之制有志之士每動名實
之思故有請擇司馬光冠婚喪祭之儀
簡而易行布之民間者有請准令式行
punctuated:
臨御以來，孜孜求治，其所以經綸大業，巍巍乎足稱中興之盛，有以度越漢唐宋之君者有五。爾諸生亦曾聞而誦之乎？夫陶鎔菁莪棫樸之化，而鋪張敷揚一代之盛，亦臣子事也。試一一為我言之。
問：移風易俗，莫善於禮。禮樂不興，則刑罰不中，奢淫日蕩，獄訟繁興。是禮者，天地之紀，而民之所以生者也。今之牧民者，果能建萬世之長策，舉明主於三代之隆，而不徒區區簿書聽訟，如王吉之言者乎？夫外庭告冠，聞者却立；父在學禮，君子譏之。此在賢者且然，則古禮之難復久矣。然唐之牧守，乃能獨行於一郡之間，至有百姓聞之而泣下者，又安在其為不可乎？說者謂夫子作春秋，不存禮樂之制。有志之士，每動名實之思，故有請擇司馬光冠婚喪祭之儀，簡而易行，布之民間者；有請准令式行
translation_en:
…Since ascending the throne, he has worked tirelessly for good government. Among the means by which he has ordered his great undertaking, so lofty as fully to deserve the designation of a flourishing restoration, there are five in which he surpasses the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song. Have you students also heard and recited them? To cultivate the transforming influence celebrated in the Odes “Luxuriant Southernwood” (Jing e) and “Oak and Thorn” (Yu pu), and to set forth and proclaim the flourishing achievements of a dynasty, are also duties of a subject. Explain these matters to me one by one.
Question: For transforming prevailing practices and changing customs, nothing excels ritual. If ritual and music do not flourish, punishments fail to fit the offenses, extravagance and licentiousness grow daily more unrestrained, and criminal cases and lawsuits multiply. Thus ritual is the ordering principle of Heaven and Earth and the means by which the people live. Can those who govern the people today truly establish a lasting policy for ten thousand generations and raise their enlightened sovereign to the heights of the Three Dynasties, rather than merely busying themselves with registers, documents, and hearing lawsuits, as Wang Ji said?
When a capping ceremony was announced in the outer court, the man who heard it stepped back; when a man studied ritual while his father was still alive, the gentleman criticized him. If even worthy men encountered such difficulties, restoring ancient ritual has long been hard indeed. Yet a prefect in the Tang was able to put it into practice independently within a single prefecture, so successfully that some common people shed tears on hearing of it. On what grounds, then, can it be considered impossible?
Commentators say that when the Master compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he did not preserve the institutions of ritual and music. Men of aspiration have often been stirred to consider the relationship between names and realities. Thus some requested that those of Sima Guang’s procedures for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice that were simple and easy to carry out be selected and disseminated among the people; others requested that, in accordance with the ordinances and regulations, there be put into practice…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
禮稍加獎勸以示風俗者有乞令敎授
有出身官旦望就學講習新禮而督察
之者有欲請復古三科以興實學者使
今日酌而行之其致治成效必有可觀
然當時旣能言之能行之而終不可以
復純王之治其弊又安在乎程子曰治
天下以正風俗得賢才爲本諸士子以
賢才自負行當有風俗之責者如有用
爾其將何以副之
===
問出處去就乃士人出門第一步古先聖
賢不少放過學者所宜精察而不可苟
焉者也今以古人可議之迹與諸生論
之昔武王伐紂夷齊隱迹於首陽山遂
餓而死微子乃抱祭器歸周箕子又就
爲之陳洪範焉夫異姓之臣則力全君
臣之義同姓之臣乃忘宗國以事之說
者以存祀傳道爲言是矣然以武周之
聖其道未嘗不在殷之宗祀周家必無
punctuated:
禮，稍加獎勸，以示風俗者；有乞令敎授、有出身官旦望就學講習新禮而督察之者；有欲請復古三科以興實學者。使今日酌而行之，其致治成效必有可觀。然當時旣能言之，能行之，而終不可以復純王之治，其弊又安在乎？程子曰：「治天下以正風俗、得賢才爲本。」諸士子以賢才自負，行當有風俗之責者，如有用爾，其將何以副之？

問：出處去就，乃士人出門第一步，古先聖賢不少放過，學者所宜精察而不可苟焉者也。今以古人可議之迹與諸生論之。昔武王伐紂，夷齊隱迹於首陽山，遂餓而死；微子乃抱祭器歸周，箕子又就爲之陳洪範焉。夫異姓之臣則力全君臣之義，同姓之臣乃忘宗國以事之，說者以存祀傳道爲言，是矣。然以武周之聖，其道未嘗不在，殷之宗祀，周家必無
translation_en:
…rites, with some additional rewards and encouragement to provide an example for prevailing customs; others requested that prefectural school instructors and officials possessing examination qualifications attend the schools on the first and fifteenth days of each month to study and discuss the new rites and oversee their practice; still others wished to request the restoration of the ancient three categories of selection to promote substantive learning. If these proposals were weighed and implemented today, their effectiveness in bringing about good government would surely be noteworthy. Yet, although people at that time could both advocate and implement them, they ultimately could not restore government wholly guided by the kingly way. Where, then, did the failing lie? Master Cheng said: “Governing the realm rests upon rectifying customs and obtaining worthy talent.” You examination candidates pride yourselves on your worth and talent and will soon bear responsibility for public customs. If someone were to employ you, how would you meet that responsibility?

Question: Whether to enter office or remain in retirement, to leave service or remain in it—these constitute the scholar’s very first step into public life. The sages and worthies of antiquity never treated them lightly. Students must examine them closely and must not be careless about them. Let us now discuss with you candidates some debatable actions of the ancients. When King Wu attacked Zhou, the ruler of Shang, Boyi and Shuqi withdrew into seclusion on Mount Shouyang and eventually starved to death. Weizi, however, took the sacrificial vessels and submitted to the Zhou dynasty, while Jizi went on to expound the Great Plan for its ruler. Thus ministers of a different surname strove to preserve fully the obligations between ruler and minister, whereas ministers of the royal surname forgot their ancestral state and served its conqueror. Commentators explain this in terms of preserving ancestral sacrifices and transmitting the Way. That is indeed reasonable. Yet, given the sagehood of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou, the Way was never absent; as for the ancestral sacrifices of Yin, the house of Zhou surely would never…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
絕之之理豈待抱祭器歸周而后存乎
王莽易漢為新龔勝不食就斃武后易
唐為周狄仁傑乃俯首以事之說者又
謂仁傑之仕周將以為唐也然君子寧
功業之不建而不失身於匪人况中宗
之不足扶植武三思輩之不能有成不
待智者而后知仁傑之賢乃不知此何
與至若元以夷狄入主中國許衡應聘
而為臣劉因則屢聘之而不起或謂劉
===
高於許然愚觀渡江之賦乃快趙宋之
亡似非夷元不仕者許之仕元或謂將
變夷為華然王猛之仕秦能以東晉正
朔勸符堅許衡之仕元乃不能以宋中
國勸世祖何與他如漢唐諸賢有以三
顧聘之而出以三公召之而不出有三
上宰相書而求出有下詔徵之而不出
者先儒論之詳矣然或謂求出者未必
為非不出者未必為正出者未必為時
punctuated: 絕之之理，豈待抱祭器歸周而后存乎？王莽易漢為新，龔勝不食就斃；武后易唐為周，狄仁傑乃俯首以事之。說者又謂仁傑之仕周，將以為唐也。然君子寧功業之不建，而不失身於匪人。况中宗之不足扶植、武三思輩之不能有成，不待智者而后知。仁傑之賢乃不知此，何與？至若元以夷狄入主中國，許衡應聘而為臣，劉因則屢聘之而不起。或謂劉高於許，然愚觀《渡江之賦》，乃快趙宋之亡，似非夷元不仕者。許之仕元，或謂將變夷為華，然王猛之仕秦，能以東晉正朔勸符堅；許衡之仕元，乃不能以宋中國勸世祖，何與？他如漢唐諸賢，有以三顧聘之而出、以三公召之而不出，有三上宰相書而求出，有下詔徵之而不出者。先儒論之詳矣，然或謂求出者未必為非，不出者未必為正，出者未必為時
translation_en:
…have had any reason to extinguish those sacrifices. Could their preservation really have depended on his carrying the sacrificial vessels with him when he submitted to Zhou? When Wang Mang replaced Han with Xin, Gong Sheng refused food and died; when Empress Wu replaced Tang with Zhou, Di Renjie bowed his head and served her. Commentators further maintain that Renjie served Zhou in order to act on behalf of Tang. Yet a gentleman would rather fail to establish great achievements than compromise himself by serving an unworthy person. Moreover, one need not be wise to recognize that Zhongzong was not worth supporting and that Wu Sansi and his kind could accomplish nothing. How could someone as worthy as Renjie have failed to understand this?

As for the Yuan, who entered and ruled China as barbarians, Xu Heng accepted an invitation to serve and became their subject, whereas Liu Yin repeatedly declined invitations to take office. Some say that Liu was superior to Xu. Yet in my humble reading of his Rhapsody on Crossing the River, he actually rejoiced at the fall of the Zhao family's Song dynasty. He thus seems not to have been someone who refused office because he regarded the Yuan as barbarians. Some say that Xu served the Yuan in order to transform the barbarians into bearers of Chinese civilization. Yet Wang Meng, while serving Qin, could urge Fu Jian to recognize the legitimate dynastic authority of Eastern Jin. Why, then, could Xu Heng, while serving the Yuan, not urge Shizu to recognize Song as the legitimate Chinese realm?

Among other worthy men of Han and Tang, there were those who entered office after being invited through three personal visits, and those who declined a summons to serve as one of the Three Dukes. There were those who submitted letters to the chief councilor three times in pursuit of office, and those who declined to serve even when summoned by imperial edict. Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed these cases in detail. Yet some say that seeking office is not necessarily wrong, that declining office is not necessarily right, and that entering office is not necessarily timely…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
召之而不出者乃又旣出而成伊傅之
業又何與此皆必有至公至大之義不
可以曲學俗士之說拘者亦諸生之所
當講也幸明言之庸占他日出處之槩
問聖賢間世而生常以五百歲為期故自
堯舜以來數千百年其所見聞而知之
者具有可稽觀數於今適逢其會而我
朝
列聖躬行之至
===
製作之盛獨步千古莫與之京而又我
皇上聰明睿智擴縱自天
敬一一箴直發前聖之所未發眞所謂聞而
知之者矣然漸濡旣久不見有得於禹
臯伊傅之傳以接斯道之緒者何與夫
道不墜地必有見者近世儒臣獨識此
意歷考當時造詣諸臣乃得十有五人
撮其行實各為編次名之曰
皇明理學名臣言行錄然則十有五人者果皆
punctuated:
召之而不出者，乃又旣出而成伊傅之業，又何與？此皆必有至公至大之義，不可以曲學俗士之說拘者，亦諸生之所當講也。幸明言之，庸占他日出處之槩。

問：聖賢間世而生，常以五百歲為期。故自堯舜以來，數千百年，其所見聞而知之者，具有可稽。觀數於今，適逢其會，而我朝列聖躬行之至、製作之盛，獨步千古，莫與之京。而又我皇上聰明睿智，擴縱自天，敬一一箴，直發前聖之所未發，眞所謂聞而知之者矣。然漸濡旣久，不見有得於禹臯伊傅之傳，以接斯道之緒者，何與？夫道不墜地，必有見者。近世儒臣獨識此意，歷考當時造詣諸臣，乃得十有五人，撮其行實，各為編次，名之曰《皇明理學名臣言行錄》。然則十有五人者，果皆
translation_en:
…Those who did not come forth when summoned nevertheless subsequently entered service and accomplished deeds like those of Yi Yin and Fu Yue: why was this? In all these cases there must have been principles of the utmost impartiality and magnitude, which cannot be confined within the arguments of narrow scholars and conventional men. These too are matters you students ought to discuss. Please explain them clearly, so that we may gauge the general course you will follow in entering service or remaining in retirement in years to come.

Question: Sages and worthies arise only at intervals, commonly reckoned at five hundred years. Thus, over the thousands of years since Yao and Shun, those who attained understanding through seeing or hearing have all left evidence that can be examined. Considering this numerical cycle, our own time coincides precisely with its appointed moment. The consummate personal practice and magnificent institutions of the successive sage emperors of our dynasty stand unrivalled throughout the ages; none can equal them. Moreover, our reigning emperor possesses intelligence and sagely wisdom, his expansive capacities bestowed by Heaven [?]. His single Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi) directly reveals what earlier sages had not revealed. He truly is what is meant by one who attains understanding through hearing. Yet, although this influence has long permeated the realm, we see no one who has grasped the transmission of Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue and thereby continued the thread of this Way. Why is this?

The Way has not fallen to the ground; surely there must be those who perceive it. A Confucian official of recent times uniquely recognized this significance. He examined in turn the attainments of the officials of his day and identified fifteen men. Selecting accounts of their conduct, he arranged these into separate compilations, entitled Records of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Neo-Confucian Officials of the August Ming (Huang Ming lixue mingchen yanxing lu). Were these fifteen men, then, truly all…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
見知之實而真有得於道統之正者誰
與且其言曰若薛瑄輩視程朱高第豈
多讓之就如餘人亦不但僅如陳同父
輩而已卽斯論也果亦灼有所見而言
之否與周敦頤肇開宋學之源及其身
鮮有不疑之者而過時乃定然則今之
講求亦大率類此也與后之觀今猶今
之視古也諸士子將何觀乎幸毋高論
以對
===
問宋人有言欲天下之治在乎才者居職
欲才者居職在乎使其居閑之日少居
閑之日少在乎清入仕之源以今日觀
之歲貢科舉不增於舊員缺之冗率又
過之然赴部待選動至數千給假家居
恒逾二萬至有白首不得一命幸而得
之亦皆垂老志得之年正所謂莅官之
日淺居閑之日多以其莅官之所得而
為居閑仰給之資是以人才愈多治功
punctuated:
見知之實，而真有得於道統之正者誰與？且其言曰：「若薛瑄輩，視程朱高第，豈多讓之？就如餘人，亦不但僅如陳同父輩而已。」卽斯論也，果亦灼有所見而言之否與？周敦頤肇開宋學之源，及其身，鮮有不疑之者，而過時乃定。然則今之講求，亦大率類此也與？后之觀今，猶今之視古也。諸士子將何觀乎？幸毋高論以對。

問：宋人有言：「欲天下之治，在乎才者居職；欲才者居職，在乎使其居閑之日少；居閑之日少，在乎清入仕之源。」以今日觀之，歲貢、科舉不增於舊，員缺之冗率又過之。然赴部待選，動至數千；給假家居，恒逾二萬。至有白首不得一命，幸而得之，亦皆垂老志得之年。正所謂莅官之日淺，居閑之日多，以其莅官之所得，而為居閑仰給之資。是以人才愈多，治功
translation_en:
…truly knew through seeing? And who genuinely grasped the orthodox transmission of the Way? Moreover, the author says: “Would men such as Xue Xuan concede much to the outstanding disciples of Cheng and Zhu? Even the others were not merely on a level with men such as Chen Tongfu.” Was this judgment indeed based on clear insight? Zhou Dunyi first opened the wellspring of Song learning. During his lifetime, few did not doubt him; only afterward was his standing settled. Is present-day inquiry into these matters, then, broadly similar? Later generations will view our time just as we view antiquity. What view will you candidates take? Please answer without lofty, abstract pronouncements.

Question: A man of the Song said: “Bringing order to the realm depends on placing talented men in office. Placing talented men in office depends on shortening the time they spend without appointments. Shortening that time depends on purifying the sources of entry into official service.” Looking at the present, the numbers entering through annual tribute studentship and the examinations have not increased over earlier levels, while the abundance of official posts and vacancies generally exceeds that of the past [?]. Yet those who go to the ministry to await selection readily number several thousand, and those granted leave to remain at home regularly exceed twenty thousand. Some even reach white-haired old age without receiving a single appointment. Those fortunate enough to receive one likewise attain their ambition only as they approach old age. This is precisely what is meant by spending little time in office and much time without an appointment, and using what one acquires while serving as the means of support during one's years out of office. Thus, the more numerous the talented men, the more the accomplishments of government…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
愈壞欲其飭已安民難矣立法以來不
聞有是猶至今日積壅日深為銓司者
每欲疏通而不可得其故將安在乎蘇
軾嘗曰可畏者天下安危而囂囂者以
為不可為不足卹必欲變而通之是矣
然言變通者有曰四弊既去則其源自
清有曰四色之人並行澄汰又曰必須
調停之使入仕者有實用之效汰退者
無失所之歎其道又安取乎尹洙之與
===
服飾陳襄之與折資差遣李柬之與監
臨物務其亦調停之說尚可仿而用之
否乎為官擇人不為人設官此確論也
究竟其實不知終以何說為然
punctuated: 愈壞，欲其飭已安民，難矣。立法以來，不聞有是，猶至今日，積壅日深，為銓司者每欲疏通而不可得，其故將安在乎？蘇軾嘗曰：「可畏者天下安危，而囂囂者以為不可為，不足卹。」必欲變而通之，是矣。然言變通者，有曰：「四弊既去，則其源自清。」有曰：「四色之人，並行澄汰。」又曰：「必須調停之，使入仕者有實用之效，汰退者無失所之歎。」其道又安取乎？尹洙之與服飾，陳襄之與折資差遣，李柬之與監臨物務，其亦調停之說，尚可仿而用之否乎？為官擇人，不為人設官，此確論也。究竟其實，不知終以何說為然？
translation_en: …the more governance deteriorates; to expect them to discipline themselves [?] and bring peace to the people is difficult indeed. Since these regulations were established, such a situation was unheard of; yet by the present day the accumulated congestion has grown ever worse. Those responsible for official selection repeatedly seek to clear it but cannot. Where does the cause lie? Su Shi once said: “What deserves apprehension is the security or peril of the realm, yet those who clamour regard it as something about which nothing can be done and which merits no concern.” To insist on changing the system so that it functions smoothly is indeed right. Yet among those who advocate change, some say: “Once the four abuses are removed, the source will clear itself.” Others say: “All four categories of men should undergo screening and elimination together.” Still others say: “An accommodation must be reached, so that those entering office can render effective service, while those eliminated and dismissed have no cause to lament losing their livelihood.” By what means, then, can this be achieved? Yin Zhu’s proposal to grant official attire [?], Chen Xiang’s proposal to grant assignments with reduced seniority requirements, and Li Jianzhi’s proposal to grant posts overseeing goods and fiscal affairs—were these also proposals for accommodation, and might they still be imitated and put into practice? To select men for offices, rather than create offices for men: this is a sound principle. But when the practical circumstances are thoroughly examined, which view should ultimately be judged correct?
