Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: “The wording is economical, yet the matters and principles are fully explained.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The feeling of generous solicitude for the guests is vividly apparent.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The talent and thought are lucid and subtle.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Refined and concise.”

The host’s intention to treat his guests generously can be seen in the meticulous completeness of his provisions. For the rites of banqueting esteem the full provision of everything required. When a host entertains his guests and can make every detail complete, does this not reveal his respect? This is a ceremonial song used for both informal and formal banquets. Its meaning is that banqueting serves to manifest the rites of a felicitous gathering and bring the feelings of host and guests into harmony. If the ceremonial observances do not extend to material offerings, this is called a failure to entertain. Yet if the entertainment lacks abundant ceremonial offerings, would it not be excessively meager? Thus, provisions are valued for their abundance. But if they are abundant without being excellent, what use is abundance? Now the gentleman has wine, abundant and delicious: I see excellence embodied in abundance. The zun and lei wine vessels are all…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
椒餼之芳也籩豆著靜嘉之美也勸酬之下足
以昭燕衎之光而弗嘉非所患矣物有以旨爲
貴者旨而弗偕雖旨猶未備也今君子有酒旨
且多吾見偕寓於旨焉食之飲之無缺儀也旣
戒旣平皆陳饋也獻酢之餘足以明盡物之敬
而弗齊非所患矣乃若物以有爲貴有而弗時
是徒有也非君子之所以厚賓也今則無一物
之不具則亦無一而不時焉以洽百禮順時物
之宜以和五味亶芳臭之薦酌言嘗之眞足以
===
稱嘉美之會而無尚焉者矣又何患于弗時也
哉夫其物之曲全如此優賓之意於是乎至固
非以私惠爲德者其相孚之情可知矣抑嘗觀
之易曰天道下濟而光明地道卑而上行成周
之時衆賢和於朝而萬物和於野其君臣上下
恩禮交洽以至昆蟲闓澤恊氣濡潤一時燕饗
通用之樂與笙詩相間歌者有魚麗嘉魚南山
有臺諸作可以見上下感應之機可以見厚倫
敦化之道此周之治所以爲盛也聖人以是錄
punctuated:
椒餼之芳也，籩豆著靜嘉之美也。勸酬之下，足以昭燕衎之光，而弗嘉非所患矣。物有以旨爲貴者，旨而弗偕，雖旨猶未備也。今君子有酒，旨且多，吾見偕寓於旨焉。食之飲之，無缺儀也；旣戒旣平，皆陳饋也。獻酢之餘，足以明盡物之敬，而弗齊非所患矣。乃若物以有爲貴，有而弗時，是徒有也，非君子之所以厚賓也。今則無一物之不具，則亦無一而不時焉。以洽百禮，順時物之宜；以和五味，亶芳臭之薦。酌言嘗之，眞足以稱嘉美之會，而無尚焉者矣。又何患于弗時也哉？夫其物之曲全如此，優賓之意於是乎至，固非以私惠爲德者，其相孚之情可知矣。
抑嘗觀之，《易》曰：「天道下濟而光明，地道卑而上行。」成周之時，衆賢和於朝，而萬物和於野。其君臣上下，恩禮交洽，以至昆蟲闓澤，恊氣濡潤。一時燕饗通用之樂，與笙詩相間歌者，有《魚麗》《嘉魚》《南山有臺》諸作，可以見上下感應之機，可以見厚倫敦化之道。此周之治所以爲盛也。聖人以是錄
translation_en:
…fragrant with pepper-scented provisions [?], while the bamboo and wooden offering vessels display the beauty of pure and excellent fare. As the guests are urged to drink and cups are exchanged, all this sufficiently manifests the splendor of convivial feasting; there is no cause to fear any lack of excellence. Among provisions, some are valued for their fine flavor. Yet if fine flavor is not accompanied by completeness, even delicious fare remains inadequate. Now the gentleman has wine, both delicious and plentiful: I see completeness embodied in its fine flavor. In feeding his guests and giving them drink, he omits no ceremony; everything is prepared and arranged, all the offerings set out. Through the presentation and return of cups, he fully manifests the reverence expressed by providing everything; there is no cause to fear any lack of completeness. As for valuing provisions simply because they are available, if they are available but out of season, this is mere possession, not the means by which a gentleman treats his guests generously. Now, since no provision is lacking, none is out of season either. To fulfill the hundred rites, he accords with the suitability of seasonal produce; to harmonize the five flavors, he presents truly fragrant offerings. Pour the wine and taste it: this truly deserves to be called a gathering of excellence and beauty, beyond which nothing could surpass it. Why, then, fear anything being out of season? His provisions are thus complete in every particular, bringing his intention to honor his guests to its fullest expression. Certainly he is not one who treats private favors as virtue; the feelings of mutual trust can be understood from this.
I have also considered this saying in the Book of Changes: “The Way of Heaven descends to aid below and shines brightly; the Way of Earth is lowly yet moves upward.” In the time of the fully established Zhou, the many worthy men were in harmony at court, and the myriad things were in harmony in the countryside. Between ruler and ministers, superiors and inferiors, favor and ritual courtesy flowed in mutual accord, reaching even the insects, which received beneficence [?], while harmonious vital energies moistened and nourished all. Among the musical pieces then used alike for informal feasts and ceremonial banquets, sung alternately with the sheng-accompanied poems, were Fish Abound (Yu li), Fine Fish (Jia yu), and On the Southern Mountain There Are Terraces (Nanshan you tai). In these one can perceive the workings of mutual influence and response between those above and below, and the way of strengthening human relationships and deepening moral transformation. This is why Zhou governance flourished. For this reason, the sage recorded…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之於經後世猶有流連之行至忘設醴者惜乎
以是詩告之
綏我眉壽介以繁祉旣右烈考亦右文母
劉格
同考試官教諭甘批正大
同考試官教諭陳批文王昌后武王歸德處意明
考試官教諭劉批得稱頌體
考試官教授林批典實
周王之祀親也必徵其昌後之慶極其隆焉夫
===
克昌厥後先王之澤所以為盛也後王奉先而
以是徵之可以觀孝矣此為武王祀文王之詩
意謂皇考一德格天固有以昌後人而綏孝子
矣然其實何如也彼畀之以福而壽弗綏猶為
徒福也今則綏我以眉壽焉錫以難老優游泮
奐以延有道之長履大業而致盛治非皇考所
以陰隲於予者乎與之以壽而祉弗隆猶為徒
壽也今則助我以多福焉俾以戬穀單厚多益
以衍無疆之緒饗宗廟而保子孫非皇考所以
punctuated:
之於經，後世猶有流連之行，至忘設醴者，惜乎！以是詩告之。
綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。旣右烈考，亦右文母。
劉格
同考試官教諭甘批：正大。
同考試官教諭陳批：文王昌后、武王歸德處，意明。
考試官教諭劉批：得稱頌體。
考試官教授林批：典實。
周王之祀親也，必徵其昌後之慶，極其隆焉。夫克昌厥後，先王之澤所以為盛也。後王奉先而以是徵之，可以觀孝矣。此為武王祀文王之詩，意謂皇考一德格天，固有以昌後人而綏孝子矣。然其實何如也？彼畀之以福而壽弗綏，猶為徒福也。今則綏我以眉壽焉，錫以難老，優游泮奐，以延有道之長，履大業而致盛治，非皇考所以陰隲於予者乎？與之以壽而祉弗隆，猶為徒壽也。今則助我以多福焉，俾以戬穀，單厚多益，以衍無疆之緒，饗宗廟而保子孫，非皇考所以
translation_en:
…it in the Classic. Yet in later ages there were still those who lingered in their pleasures [?], even forgetting to provide sweet wine for their guests. What a pity! Let this poem serve to admonish them.
“Grant me long life, and aid me with abundant blessings. Having honored my illustrious deceased father, I also honor my cultured mother.”
Liu Ge
Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: “Upright and elevated.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The meaning is clear where King Wen brings prosperity to his descendants and King Wu attributes the beneficence to him.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Captures the manner of a panegyric.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Grounded in the classics and substantial.”
When the king of Zhou sacrificed to his parents, he necessarily bore witness to their blessings in bringing prosperity to their descendants and accorded them the highest honor. For the former king’s beneficence was great precisely because it could bring prosperity to his descendants. When the succeeding king served his ancestors and bore witness to this, his filial devotion could be seen. This is a poem about King Wu’s sacrifice to King Wen. Its meaning is: “My august deceased father, through his undivided virtue, reached Heaven; he assuredly possessed the means to bring prosperity to his descendants and bring peace to his filial son. Yet how is this realized in practice? If he bestowed blessings without granting longevity, these would be blessings alone. Now, however, he grants me long life, bestowing freedom from the infirmities of age, ease and expansive contentment, so that I may prolong the years of one who possesses the Way, carry forward the great undertaking, and achieve flourishing government. Is this not how my august deceased father secretly protects me? If he granted longevity without abundant blessings, this would be longevity alone. Now, however, he aids me with manifold blessings, granting me happiness and goodness, fullness, abundance, and ever greater benefits, so that I may extend an unending succession, offer sacrifices in the ancestral temple, and safeguard my descendants. Is this not how my august deceased father …”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
左右於予者乎夫福壽之庇吾固以身蒙其休
矣今日光於前人孰非其所遺者也是故明堂
啓而祀事行旣右我烈考焉駿奔對越有以合
萬國之歡心凡行其禮奏其樂煥乎天子之制
而非周邦之舊矣使先王莫開于前吾何以右
之也哉不但是也清廟開而廣牡薦亦右我文
母焉饗祀妥侑有以備四方之禮物凡昭其度
致其文巍乎母后之儀而非立國之初矣使先
王弗昌其後又何以右之也哉然此非倖致者
===
也皆我先王之德之庇也今日克承其休以纘
前業敢忘所自乎嗟夫武王可謂知重其本而
為孝之純也已不自矜其功不自大其德表章
前業世德作求蓋非幸其成而淺於自待者故
孔子稱之曰武王其達孝矣乎惟其孝之達是
以業益弘而慶益萃也集蒼姬之緒而畢未竟
之功夫豈適然者哉記曰惟孝子為能饗親讀
是詩而知武王之孝也
春秋
punctuated:
左右於予者乎？夫福壽之庇，吾固以身蒙其休矣。今日光於前人，孰非其所遺者也？是故明堂啓而祀事行，旣右我烈考焉，駿奔對越，有以合萬國之歡心。凡行其禮、奏其樂，煥乎天子之制，而非周邦之舊矣。使先王莫開于前，吾何以右之也哉？不但是也，清廟開而廣牡薦，亦右我文母焉。饗祀妥侑，有以備四方之禮物。凡昭其度、致其文，巍乎母后之儀，而非立國之初矣。使先王弗昌其後，又何以右之也哉？然此非倖致者也，皆我先王之德之庇也。今日克承其休，以纘前業，敢忘所自乎？嗟夫！武王可謂知重其本而為孝之純也已。不自矜其功，不自大其德，表章前業，世德作求，蓋非幸其成而淺於自待者。故孔子稱之曰：「武王其達孝矣乎！」惟其孝之達，是以業益弘而慶益萃也。集蒼姬之緒而畢未竟之功，夫豈適然者哉？記曰：「惟孝子為能饗親。」讀是詩而知武王之孝也。

春秋
translation_en:
…assists me? Under this protection of blessings and longevity, I have indeed personally received his beneficence. Of the glory that today reflects upon our predecessors, what has not been bequeathed by him? Thus, when the Hall of Light is opened and the sacrifices performed, I honor my illustrious deceased father. Those who hasten reverently to attend and respond to his spirit unite the joyful hearts of the myriad states. The rites performed and the music played display the resplendent institutions of the Son of Heaven, no longer the old usages of the state of Zhou. Had the former king not opened the way before me, how could I thus honor him? Nor is this all. When the Pure Temple is opened and great bulls are offered, I also honor my accomplished mother. The sacrificial offerings, the settling of the spirits, and the urging of them to partake bring together the full array of ritual gifts from the four quarters. The standards displayed and the ceremonial refinements fully expressed constitute the majestic ritual honors of a queen mother, unlike those at the founding of the state. Had the former king not brought prosperity to his descendants, how could I thus honor her? Yet this has not come about by mere good fortune. It is entirely the protection afforded by the virtue of my former king. Today, enabled to receive his beneficence and continue his former enterprise, dare I forget its source?

Ah! King Wu may indeed be said to have understood the importance of honoring his roots and to have practiced filial piety in its purity. He neither boasted of his achievements nor exalted his own virtue; he made manifest the enterprise of his predecessors and sought to perpetuate the virtue transmitted through the generations. Surely he was no man who merely enjoyed the good fortune of success while expecting little of himself. Thus Confucius praised him, saying, “How consummate was King Wu’s filial piety!” Precisely because his filial piety was consummate, his enterprise grew ever greater and blessings gathered ever more abundantly. He brought together the inherited undertakings of the august Ji house and completed its unfinished work. Could this have happened by chance? The Record of Rites says, “Only a filial son can offer sacrifice acceptably to his parents.” Reading this poem, we understand King Wu’s filial piety.

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春王正月宋公曹伯衞人邾人伐齊狄
救齊僖公十有八年春晉侯侵曹晉侯
伐衞僖公二十有八年楚子陳侯隨侯
許男圍蔡哀公元年
曾迪
考試官敎諭劉批得傳旨
考試官敎授林批有斷制
列國報兵之情異春秋隨事而立法焉夫兵一
也是非則存乎其事春秋曲直之準其容以無
===
辯乎甞考衞之伐齊狄之救齊晉之侵曹伐衞
楚之圍蔡而知人情之得失若是乎其相遠焉
何則楚丘有城衞文之受德於桓也已深聶北
見却齊桓之遺恨於狄也已乆夫情之厚者每
懷人之德於不忘而多偏繫之私者則又計小
忿而不釋何衞與狄之異耶一則乘其喪也而
奉少以奪其長一則憫其難也而率衆以解其
危怨隆於可報之恩義急於仇讐之人其得失
果何如耶君子曰情貴乎厚而惡乎薄薄則忍
punctuated:
「春，王正月，宋公、曹伯、衞人、邾人伐齊，狄救齊。」僖公十有八年。「春，晉侯侵曹。晉侯伐衞。」僖公二十有八年。「楚子、陳侯、隨侯、許男圍蔡。」哀公元年。
曾迪。
考試官敎諭劉批：得傳旨。
考試官敎授林批：有斷制。
列國報兵之情異，春秋隨事而立法焉。夫兵一也，是非則存乎其事。春秋曲直之準，其容以無辯乎？甞考衞之伐齊、狄之救齊、晉之侵曹伐衞、楚之圍蔡，而知人情之得失若是乎其相遠焉。何則？楚丘有城，衞文之受德於桓也已深；聶北見却，齊桓之遺恨於狄也已乆。夫情之厚者，每懷人之德於不忘；而多偏繫之私者，則又計小忿而不釋。何衞與狄之異耶？一則乘其喪也，而奉少以奪其長；一則憫其難也，而率衆以解其危。怨隆於可報之恩，義急於仇讐之人，其得失果何如耶？君子曰：情貴乎厚，而惡乎薄，薄則忍
translation_en:
“In spring, in the first month of the royal calendar, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Cao, men of Wei, and men of Zhu attacked Qi. The Di came to Qi’s rescue.” Eighteenth year of Duke Xi. “In spring, the Marquis of Jin invaded Cao. The Marquis of Jin attacked Wei.” Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi. “The Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Sui, and the Baron of Xu besieged Cai.” First year of Duke Ai.
Zeng Di.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Grasps the purport of the commentary.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: “Shows decisive judgment.”
The circumstances motivating the various states’ retaliatory warfare differed; the Spring and Autumn Annals establishes standards according to each event. Warfare is one and the same activity, but its rightness or wrongness lies in the particular circumstances. As the standard of right and wrong, could the Spring and Autumn Annals permit these to go undistinguished? I have examined Wei’s attack on Qi, the Di’s rescue of Qi, Jin’s invasion of Cao and attack on Wei, and Chu’s siege of Cai, and have thereby understood how widely human sentiments can diverge in their merits and failings.
Why is this so? With the fortification of Chuqiu, Duke Wen of Wei had already received profound beneficence from Duke Huan of Qi. With their repulse at Niebei, the Di had long harbored resentment against Duke Huan of Qi. Those whose sentiments are generous continually remember others’ kindness without forgetting it; those burdened by selfish partialities brood over petty grievances and will not let them go. How different, then, were Wei and the Di! The former took advantage of Qi’s bereavement to support the younger son and dispossess the elder; the latter pitied Qi’s troubles and led troops to relieve its peril. In one case, resentment outweighed kindness that ought to have been repaid; in the other, righteousness impelled urgent aid to an enemy. What, then, were their respective merits and failings? The gentleman says: “In human sentiment, generosity is prized and meanness abhorred. Meanness leads to callousness…”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而犯順厚則同而無我伐齊之兵其忍心之無
忌救齊之旅其得同物之仁乎故書伐以責衞
書救以許狄者非偏也曲直之不可欺也豈故
伸夷而抑夏歟若塊裸之侮曹衞之獲戾於晉
也可畧宗廟之壞蔡昭之駕禍於楚也實淫夫
心之廣者每矜人之過於不校而無自强之志
者則又委重怨於不圖何晉與楚之異耶一則
懷其侮也而侵伐之必加一則計其暴也而遷
徙之不恕可矜之小過必問終天之重怨不忘
===
其是非果何如耶君子曰心貴乎公而病於私
私則隘而不宏公則正而不拂曹衞之侵其褊
心之所使蔡都之遷其得人情之公乎故書爵
以責晉紀子以予楚者非私也是非之不可枉
也豈故重外而輕內歟是則晉衞俱可惡也而
負德者爲尤楚狄俱可取也而恤患者爲最因
人示法春秋之義精矣抑於是而猶有憾焉無
虧孝公之分可易耶不可易耶桓乃囑人以私
而欲以愛惡定廢置卒之柩方在殯國被危辱
punctuated: 而犯順，厚則同而無我。伐齊之兵，其忍心之無忌；救齊之旅，其得同物之仁乎？故書伐以責衞，書救以許狄者，非偏也，曲直之不可欺也。豈故伸夷而抑夏歟？若塊裸之侮，曹衞之獲戾於晉也可畧；宗廟之壞，蔡昭之駕禍於楚也實淫。夫心之廣者，每矜人之過於不校；而無自强之志者，則又委重怨於不圖。何晉與楚之異耶？一則懷其侮也，而侵伐之必加；一則計其暴也，而遷徙之不恕。可矜之小過必問，終天之重怨不忘，其是非果何如耶？君子曰：「心貴乎公，而病於私。私則隘而不宏，公則正而不拂。」曹衞之侵，其褊心之所使；蔡都之遷，其得人情之公乎？故書爵以責晉，紀子以予楚者，非私也，是非之不可枉也。豈故重外而輕內歟？是則晉衞俱可惡也，而負德者爲尤；楚狄俱可取也，而恤患者爲最。因人示法，《春秋》之義精矣。抑於是而猶有憾焉：無虧、孝公之分，可易耶？不可易耶？桓乃囑人以私，而欲以愛惡定廢置。卒之柩方在殯，國被危辱。
translation_en:
…and offend against the proper order, whereas generosity brings fellowship and freedom from selfishness. Did not the army that attacked Qi display an unrestrained ruthlessness, and the force that rescued Qi attain the benevolence of identifying with others? Thus, recording an “attack” to condemn Wei and a “rescue” to commend the Di is no act of partiality: right and wrong cannot be misrepresented. Could the purpose have been deliberately to exalt the barbarians and disparage the Xia?

As for the affront involving nakedness [?], the offenses by which Cao and Wei incurred Jin’s displeasure could have been overlooked; but the destruction of ancestral temples—the calamity that Duke Zhao of Cai brought upon Chu—was truly excessive. A broad-minded person commonly takes pity on others’ faults and does not hold them to account; yet someone without the resolve to strengthen himself will simply leave a grave grievance unattended. How different were Jin and Chu! The one brooded over its humiliation and insisted on launching an invasion; the other weighed the violence it had suffered and showed no leniency in compelling a relocation. A minor, pardonable fault was invariably called to account, while a grievous wrong, enduring as long as Heaven, was never forgotten. Where, then, did right and wrong actually lie? The gentleman says: “Impartiality is precious in the heart, and selfishness is its affliction. Selfishness makes it narrow and ungenerous; impartiality makes it upright and free of perversity.” Was not the invasion of Cao and Wei prompted by narrow-mindedness, while the relocation of Cai’s capital accorded with the impartial judgment of human feeling? Thus, recording Jin’s ruler by his rank to condemn him, and recording Chu’s ruler as ‘Viscount’ to commend him, is no act of favoritism: right and wrong cannot be distorted. Could the purpose have been deliberately to esteem those outside and slight those within?

Accordingly, Jin and Wei both deserve condemnation, but the one that betrayed kindness deserves it more; Chu and the Di both deserve approval, but the one that relieved distress deserves it most. Through particular people, the Spring and Autumn Annals displays its standards: how subtle its principles are! Yet there remains something regrettable here. Could the distinction in status between Wukui and Duke Xiao be altered, or could it not? Duke Huan privately entrusted his wishes to others, seeking to determine deposition and enthronement according to his own likes and dislikes. In the end, while his coffin still awaited burial, his state suffered danger and humiliation…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
功利之效其及也淺矣若曹衞與蔡之禍固其
自取然歛盂之盟可重絶耶申胥之賢可少無
耶君子以是知棄人不可以大甚而有國家之
責者甚無比之匪人乎
叔孫舍至自晉昭公二十有四年
康建勳
考試官敎諭劉批典雅
考試官敎授林批謹嚴
春秋於大夫之歸國特表其制行以賢之焉夫
===
執禮以維其身懷忠以衞其主舍之所以爲賢
也君子特表之以示勸也爲宜且夫執叔舍者
晉之逆也其歸舍者晉之順也去逆效順晉若
可嘉矣而以之賢叔舍也何賢乎謂其持身有
禮而事君以忠也何則天下之可畏者莫如强
安於靡而罔克自振者辱也遠辱有道禮莫先
焉彼其坐列於邾夷賂責於范鞅晉之無道亦
甚矣怵於其勢者命斯順其誰能抗之而舍則
能秉禮者是故陳之以周制以却其坐也取之
punctuated:
功利之效，其及也淺矣。若曹衞與蔡之禍，固其自取，然歛盂之盟可重絶耶？申胥之賢可少無耶？君子以是知棄人不可以大甚，而有國家之責者，甚無比之匪人乎？
叔孫舍至自晉。昭公二十有四年。
康建勳
考試官敎諭劉批：典雅。
考試官敎授林批：謹嚴。
春秋於大夫之歸國，特表其制行以賢之焉。夫執禮以維其身，懷忠以衞其主，舍之所以爲賢也。君子特表之以示勸也，爲宜。且夫執叔舍者，晉之逆也；其歸舍者，晉之順也。去逆效順，晉若可嘉矣，而以之賢叔舍也，何賢乎？謂其持身有禮，而事君以忠也。何則？天下之可畏者莫如强，安於靡而罔克自振者，辱也。遠辱有道，禮莫先焉。彼其坐列於邾夷，賂責於范鞅，晉之無道亦甚矣。怵於其勢者，命斯順，其誰能抗之？而舍則能秉禮者。是故陳之以周制，以却其坐也；取之
translation_en:
…The effects of pursuing achievement and advantage are shallow in their reach. As for the calamities of Cao, Wei, and Cai, these were indeed of their own making. Yet could the covenant at Lianyu be valued so lightly as to sever it outright [?]? Could the worthiness of Shen Xu be dispensed with even in the slightest? From this the gentleman knows that one must not go too far in abandoning others, and that those charged with responsibility for a state must be especially careful not to associate with unworthy men [?].
“Shusun She arrived from Jin.” The twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.
Kang Jianxun.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Careful and rigorous.”
In recording a grand officer’s return to his state, the Spring and Autumn Annals singles out the discipline of his conduct to commend his worthiness. Holding fast to ritual propriety to govern himself, and cherishing loyalty to protect his ruler: these were what made She worthy. It was fitting that the gentleman should single him out to encourage others. Now, Jin’s detention of Shusun She was contrary to right; its sending She home accorded with right. In abandoning wrongdoing and following what was right, Jin might seem deserving of praise. Yet the record instead commends Shusun She as worthy. What was worthy about him? It was that he conducted himself with ritual propriety and served his ruler loyally. Why is this so? Nothing under Heaven inspires greater fear than superior force. To acquiesce in weakness and prove unable to rouse oneself is disgrace. There is a way to keep disgrace at a distance, and nothing takes precedence over ritual propriety.
He was assigned a seat alongside the Yi of Zhu, and Fan Yang demanded a bribe from him: Jin’s disregard for the Way was indeed extreme. Those intimidated by its power would obey its commands; who among them could resist it? Yet She could hold fast to ritual propriety. Thus he set forth the institutions of Zhou to refuse the seat assigned to him, and drew upon…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以冠法而罔狥其求也蓋曰晉之所以辱我者
勢我之所恃以不辱者禮抗節不回君子之所
以係國輕重者也委靡之風熾矣而猶有不畏
强禦如舍者不亦幸哉天下之可懷者莫如君
志於奸而匪克夾義者亂也遠奸有道忠莫先
焉彼其奪政柄而下移逐主君而外播季之不
軌亦甚矣甘於其黨者謀斯協其誰能折之而
舍則能懷忠者是故責之以逐君以正其奸也
祈之以祝宗而罔受其欺也蓋曰君之所以榮
===
我者爵我之所恃以自榮者忠正色立朝君子
之所以能爲有無者也跋扈之習甚矣而猶有
不忘君父如舍者尚亦利哉夫維觀舍之執禮
而后有以見晉人之無禮觀舍之愛君而后有
以顯意如之無君執足以壯國之勢歸足以係
國之危臣道罔戾厥惟賢哉春秋特表其姓氏
而不比於意如之歸之例者得非彰其賢以示
勸乎雖然國有賢臣惟福之植然而揚州乾侯
之禍終不能免豈賢者無益於人國耶良由昭
punctuated: 以冠法而罔狥其求也。蓋曰：「晉之所以辱我者，勢；我之所恃以不辱者，禮。」抗節不回，君子之所以係國輕重者也。委靡之風熾矣，而猶有不畏强禦如舍者，不亦幸哉？天下之可懷者莫如君，志於奸而匪克夾義者，亂也。遠奸有道，忠莫先焉。彼其奪政柄而下移，逐主君而外播，季之不軌亦甚矣。甘於其黨者，謀斯協，其誰能折之？而舍則能懷忠者。是故責之以逐君，以正其奸也；祈之以祝宗，而罔受其欺也。蓋曰：「君之所以榮我者，爵；我之所恃以自榮者，忠。」正色立朝，君子之所以能爲有無者也。跋扈之習甚矣，而猶有不忘君父如舍者，尚亦利哉！夫維觀舍之執禮，而后有以見晉人之無禮；觀舍之愛君，而后有以顯意如之無君。執足以壯國之勢，歸足以係國之危，臣道罔戾，厥惟賢哉！春秋特表其姓氏，而不比於意如之歸之例者，得非彰其賢以示勸乎？雖然，國有賢臣，惟福之植，然而揚州、乾侯之禍終不能免，豈賢者無益於人國耶？良由昭
translation_en:
…according to the rules governing caps [?], without yielding to their demands. It was as though he said: “What Jin uses to humiliate me is power; what I rely upon to escape humiliation is ritual propriety.” Maintaining his integrity without wavering: this is how a gentleman determines the standing of his state. The prevailing habit of weak submission was rampant, yet there was still someone like She who did not fear the powerful and oppressive. Was this not fortunate?

Among all under Heaven, none deserves greater devotion than one’s ruler. To set one’s purpose on treachery and fail to uphold righteousness is to bring disorder. There is a way to keep clear of treachery, and nothing takes precedence over loyalty. Seizing the reins of government and transferring them to a subordinate, expelling his sovereign and driving him into exile—the lawlessness of Ji was extreme indeed. Those content to belong to his faction joined in his schemes; who could thwart him? Yet She could cherish loyalty. Thus he reproached Ji for expelling his ruler, seeking to correct his treachery; and in the matter of prayers offered through the invocators and ancestral-temple officials [?], he refused to be deceived by him. It was as though he said: “What my ruler uses to honor me is rank; what I rely upon to honor myself is loyalty.” Standing at court with a resolute countenance: this is how a gentleman makes his presence or absence matter. The habit of domineering insubordination was extreme, yet there was still someone like She who did not forget his ruler and father. Was this not a benefit nonetheless!

Only by observing She’s adherence to ritual propriety can one perceive the men of Jin’s lack of propriety; only by observing She’s love for his ruler can one expose Yiru’s disregard for his sovereign. His detention sufficed to strengthen his state’s standing; his return had a bearing on its peril. He did not deviate from the way of a minister—truly, he was worthy! The Spring and Autumn Annals expressly records his surname and personal name, rather than treating his return according to the precedent used for Yiru’s return. Was this not to display his worthiness and encourage others?

Even so, worthy ministers in a state are the foundation of its good fortune, yet the calamities of Yangzhou [?] and Qianhou ultimately could not be avoided. Could it be that worthy men bring no benefit to a state? The true reason lay with Zhao…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
公任之不專信之不篤是以强臣之逼卒不可
制千乘之尊求爲一匹夫而不可得矣噫昭之
弗克厥終不足惜也倂舍之賢而無以自效君
子重爲之三歎焉
禮記
禮之以少爲貴者以其内心也德產之致
也精微觀天下之物無可以稱其德者
如此則得不以少爲貴乎是故君子愼
其獨也
譚維鼎
考試官敎諭劉 批說理詳盡
考試官敎授林 批明整
記者原禮有宜於存誠者因著君子存誠之故
焉夫天地妙生物之德而君子之祀亦難乎其
爲報矣然則不以物而以誠也有以哉禮器君
子蓋謂禮不同或豐或殺惟其稱而已矣是故
君子之行禮也郊以報天而不尚夫多儀社以
神地而不貴於備物者誠以恭敬不足又何牲
punctuated:
公任之不專，信之不篤，是以强臣之逼卒不可制，千乘之尊求爲一匹夫而不可得矣。噫！昭之弗克厥終，不足惜也；倂舍之賢而無以自效，君子重爲之三歎焉。

禮記
禮之以少爲貴者，以其内心也。德產之致也精微，觀天下之物，無可以稱其德者。如此，則得不以少爲貴乎？是故君子愼其獨也。

譚維鼎
考試官敎諭劉批：說理詳盡。
考試官敎授林批：明整。

記者原禮有宜於存誠者，因著君子存誠之故焉。夫天地妙生物之德，而君子之祀亦難乎其爲報矣。然則不以物而以誠也，有以哉！禮器君子蓋謂禮不同，或豐或殺，惟其稱而已矣。是故君子之行禮也，郊以報天而不尚夫多儀，社以神地而不貴於備物者，誠以恭敬不足，又何牲
translation_en:
…Duke Zhao did not entrust him with undivided responsibility or place firm confidence in him. Thus the encroachments of powerful ministers ultimately could not be checked, and the ruler of a thousand chariots could not obtain even the life of an ordinary man. Alas! That Zhao failed to bring his reign to a proper end is not worth lamenting; but that even She, worthy as he was, had no means to prove himself in service makes the gentleman sigh deeply and repeatedly on his behalf.

Book of Rites
“When ritual esteems small quantities, it does so because what matters is the inner heart. The utmost workings of the power that brings things into being are subtle and minute; among all the things under Heaven, none can match that power. This being so, how could ritual fail to esteem small quantities? Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.”

Tan Weiding
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is detailed and exhaustive.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “Clear and orderly.”

The compiler of the Record traces why certain forms of ritual are appropriate for preserving sincerity, and thereby makes clear why the gentleman preserves sincerity. Heaven and Earth possess the wondrous power to bring things into being, and even the gentleman’s sacrifices can scarcely repay them. There is thus good reason to offer sincerity rather than material things! The gentleman in “Ritual Vessels” [?] presumably means that rituals differ: some call for abundance, others for reduction; what matters is simply their appropriateness. Thus, when the gentleman performs ritual, he offers the suburban sacrifice to repay Heaven without esteeming a multiplicity of ceremonies, and sacrifices at the altar of the soil to honor Earth as divine without prizing a full array of offerings. This is truly because, if reverence is insufficient, what can sacrificial animals…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
幣之足云而內志允孚自致神祇之來格矣所
以然者蓋有以見天地之德雖極於至大而無
外而其發育之妙則入於至密而無形故盈天
下之物皆天之所生也然其所以生者孰得而
測其機緘哉皆地之所產也然其所以產者孰
得而窺其蘊奧哉夫天地之德密緻精微如此
縱盡取天下之物以報其功吾見物有盡而功
無窮其能稱其德也乎孰若竭內志之誠以少
為貴使實意孚而幽明達庶或盡吾心焉耳以
===
故行禮君子燔柴於泰壇虛文弗事也瘞埋於
泰折縟禮弗尚也防物訖欲而小心以昭事上
帝者豫養於對越之先閑邪存誠而齋戒以神
明其德者慎獨於駿奔之始則精明之德至而
將享之道盡矣尚何事於盡物也哉由是觀之
則知行禮者不在於儀文而在於誠心之感也
今之君子宜知所法矣抑君子無弗誠也祭祀
為至祭祀無弗誠也郊社為至故禮行於郊而
百神受職禮行於社而百貨可極誠而已矣誠
punctuated: 幣之足云？而內志允孚，自致神祇之來格矣。所以然者，蓋有以見天地之德，雖極於至大而無外，而其發育之妙，則入於至密而無形。故盈天下之物，皆天之所生也，然其所以生者，孰得而測其機緘哉？皆地之所產也，然其所以產者，孰得而窺其蘊奧哉？夫天地之德密緻精微如此，縱盡取天下之物以報其功，吾見物有盡而功無窮，其能稱其德也乎？孰若竭內志之誠，以少為貴，使實意孚而幽明達，庶或盡吾心焉耳。以故行禮君子，燔柴於泰壇，虛文弗事也；瘞埋於泰折，縟禮弗尚也。防物訖欲，而小心以昭事上帝者，豫養於對越之先；閑邪存誠，而齋戒以神明其德者，慎獨於駿奔之始。則精明之德至，而將享之道盡矣，尚何事於盡物也哉？由是觀之，則知行禮者不在於儀文，而在於誠心之感也。今之君子宜知所法矣。抑君子無弗誠也，祭祀為至；祭祀無弗誠也，郊社為至。故禮行於郊，而百神受職；禮行於社，而百貨可極。誠而已矣。誠
translation_en:
…and silk offerings be worth mentioning? When one’s inward intentions are truly sincere, they naturally bring the spirits of Heaven and Earth to draw near. The reason is that, although the virtue of Heaven and Earth reaches such supreme vastness that nothing lies beyond it, the wondrous workings of their generation and nurture penetrate the utmost subtlety and have no visible form. Thus, all the things that fill the world are brought forth by Heaven; yet who can fathom the hidden workings by which it brings them forth? All are produced by Earth; yet who can glimpse the profound mysteries by which it produces them? So intricate, refined, and subtle is the virtue of Heaven and Earth that, even if we took every object in the world to repay their achievements, I see that the objects would be exhausted while those achievements remained inexhaustible. Could such offerings be commensurate with their virtue? How could this compare with fully realizing the sincerity of one’s inward intentions and valuing spareness, so that genuine intentions inspire trust and communication passes between the unseen and visible realms? Only thus might we fully express our hearts.

For this reason, when the gentleman performs the rites, he burns wood upon the great altar to Heaven, without pursuing empty display; he buries offerings at the great square altar to Earth, without prizing elaborate ceremony. Guarding against external enticements and curbing desires [?], he reverently and attentively serves the Lord on High, cultivating himself beforehand, before standing in the divine presence. Warding off depravity and preserving sincerity, he purifies himself through fasting and abstinence so as to make his virtue spiritually luminous, exercising vigilance in solitude before hastening to ritual service. Then the virtue of purity and illumination reaches its fullest, and the proper way of presenting offerings is completely fulfilled. What further need is there to exhaust all material offerings? Viewed in this light, the performance of rites rests upon the power of a sincere heart to move the spirits. Gentlemen today should know what to emulate.

Moreover, the gentleman is sincere in everything, but sincerity finds its highest expression in sacrifice. All sacrifices require sincerity, but its highest expression is in the sacrifices to Heaven in the suburbs and to the gods of the soil. Thus, when the suburban rites are performed, the hundred spirits receive their appointed duties; when the rites at the altar of the soil are performed, material resources of every kind can be fully realized. It is sincerity alone. Sincerity…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則天地斯格矣格則百順斯備矣弗誠弗敬不
能以交人而况鬼神乎書曰鬼神無常享享于
克誠易曰東鄰殺牛不如西鄰之禴祭蓋言誠
也
禮樂皆得謂之有德德者得也
黃榜
考試官敎諭劉批〔典則〕
考試官敎授林批〔理到〕
記者原德之所由名而申其義以見君子知樂
===
之妙也蓋禮樂之道大矣兼而有之則有德之
名歸之矣尚有待於外哉且夫一貫而無二者
禮樂之情同也會通以成德者善體禮樂者也
君子蓋嘗審音知樂而幾於禮矣由是禮之寓
於倫理者匪徒知其物采之施而已也神而明
之有以析其奧樂之發於聲音者匪徒知其器
數之宣而已也默而識之有以通其微夫惟析
禮之奧則有得乎禮矣會道器而體之而治躬
之妙豈有遺乎通樂之微則有得乎樂矣兼情
punctuated:
則天地斯格矣，格則百順斯備矣。弗誠弗敬，不能以交人，而况鬼神乎？《書》曰：「鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」《易》曰：「東鄰殺牛，不如西鄰之禴祭。」蓋言誠也。
禮樂皆得，謂之有德。德者，得也。
黃榜
考試官敎諭劉批〔典則〕
考試官敎授林批〔理到〕
記者原德之所由名，而申其義，以見君子知樂之妙也。蓋禮樂之道大矣，兼而有之，則有德之名歸之矣，尚有待於外哉？且夫一貫而無二者，禮樂之情同也；會通以成德者，善體禮樂者也。君子蓋嘗審音知樂而幾於禮矣。由是禮之寓於倫理者，匪徒知其物采之施而已也，神而明之，有以析其奧；樂之發於聲音者，匪徒知其器數之宣而已也，默而識之，有以通其微。夫惟析禮之奧，則有得乎禮矣，會道器而體之，而治躬之妙豈有遺乎？通樂之微，則有得乎樂矣，兼情
translation_en:
…then Heaven and Earth respond. When they respond, every favorable condition is fully present. Without sincerity and reverence, one cannot establish relations even with other people—how much less with ghosts and spirits! The Book of Documents says: “Ghosts and spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those of one who can be sincere.” The Book of Changes says: “The eastern neighbor’s slaughter of an ox is inferior to the western neighbor’s modest yue sacrifice.” These statements speak of sincerity.

“To attain both ritual and music is called possessing virtue. Virtue (de) means attainment (de).”

Huang Bang

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical and exemplary.〕
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: 〔The reasoning gets to the heart of the matter.〕

The author of the Record of Rites traces the origin of the designation “virtue” and elaborates its meaning to reveal the subtlety of the gentleman’s understanding of music. For great indeed is the Way of ritual and music! When one possesses both, the designation “possessing virtue” belongs to him. What further need has he to depend on anything external? What runs through them as a single thread, without duality, is the shared essential character of ritual and music. Those who integrate them to perfect their virtue are those skilled in embodying ritual and music. The gentleman has indeed examined tones, understood music, and thereby approached an understanding of ritual.

Thus, regarding ritual as it inheres in ethical relationships, he does more than merely understand the deployment of its objects and adornments: through a spiritually penetrating understanding, he can discern its profundities. Regarding music as it issues in sounds, he does more than merely understand its expression through instruments and numerical measures: through silent apprehension, he can comprehend its subtleties. Only by discerning the profundities of ritual does he attain ritual. Bringing together the Way and its concrete implements and embodying them, could he leave out any subtle aspect of disciplining his person? By comprehending the subtleties of music, he attains music. Embracing its inner feeling together with…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文而有之而治心之理其咸備乎合和序於一
致而粹然無偏達於禮而不達於樂者固不得
而擬之也混中和於一途而渾然無迹達於樂
而不達於禮者固不得而名之也不謂之有德
乎然是德也非襲取而強名也蓋至道克篤於
庸行而允蹈實踐各造其精微之域融會貫通
和序之妙其心領之矣至理恒熟於素履而極
深研幾咸達於性安之境交暢洋溢中和之實
其神會之矣故曰德者得也舎是不足以言德
===
矣何以盡知樂之妙也哉大抵禮樂一致也和
序一機也自一身而達之天下皆是物也能全
之者在有諸已而已有諸已則可以察倫可以
知政可以格神可以易俗而其用溥矣否則其
理昧其志荒聽古樂則唯恐卧而心迹之判遠
矣故曰士之所難者在有諸已又曰待其人而
後行
第貳塲
論
punctuated:
文而有之，而治心之理其咸備乎！合和序於一致，而粹然無偏，達於禮而不達於樂者，固不得而擬之也；混中和於一途，而渾然無迹，達於樂而不達於禮者，固不得而名之也。不謂之有德乎？然是德也，非襲取而強名也。蓋至道克篤於庸行，而允蹈實踐，各造其精微之域，融會貫通，和序之妙，其心領之矣；至理恒熟於素履，而極深研幾，咸達於性安之境，交暢洋溢，中和之實，其神會之矣。故曰：「德者，得也。」舎是不足以言德矣，何以盡知樂之妙也哉！大抵禮樂一致也，和序一機也，自一身而達之天下，皆是物也。能全之者，在有諸已而已。有諸已，則可以察倫，可以知政，可以格神，可以易俗，而其用溥矣。否則其理昧，其志荒，聽古樂則唯恐卧，而心迹之判遠矣。故曰：「士之所難者，在有諸已。」又曰：「待其人而後行。」

第貳塲

論
translation_en:
…and outward form together in oneself: would not the principles for governing the mind then be fully present? Uniting harmony and order into a single whole, pure and free from partiality—one who understands ritual but not music certainly cannot compare with such a person. Blending equilibrium and harmony into a single course, wholly integrated and without any trace of contrivance—one who understands music but not ritual certainly cannot describe such a person. Would we not call this possessing virtue? Yet this virtue is not something borrowed from outside and forcibly given that name. The utmost Way is firmly established in everyday conduct and truly put into practice; one reaches the subtle depths of both ritual and music and comprehends their interconnections, grasping in the heart the marvels of harmony and order. The highest principles become thoroughly familiar through habitual conduct; one plumbs their depths and investigates their incipient workings, reaching a state in which one’s nature rests at ease in both. As they freely interpenetrate and overflow, one apprehends in spirit the reality of equilibrium and harmony. Thus it is said: “Virtue means attainment.” Apart from this, one cannot speak adequately of virtue; how, then, could one fully comprehend the marvels of music?

In general, ritual and music form a single whole; harmony and order spring from a single impulse. From one’s own person to all under Heaven, it is everywhere this same thing. To realize it fully depends solely on possessing it within oneself. Possessing it within oneself, one can discern human relationships, understand government, move the spirits, and transform customs: its applications are far-reaching. Otherwise, one’s understanding of its principles is obscured and one’s purpose neglected; when listening to ancient music, one fears only falling asleep, and the gulf between the heart and outward conduct becomes vast. Thus it is said: “What is difficult for a scholar is possessing it within himself.” It is also said: “Only when the right person appears can it be put into practice.”

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
孔子之謂集大成
梁式
同考試官教諭王批以大成為本體足見深造
同考試官教諭劉批俱自胸中流出
同考試官教諭徐批集大成處發得精新似非文
章之士
考試官教諭劉批是學孔孟而有得者
考試官教授林批不蹈襲
夫子之道不可以名言者也夫可名言者則有
===
迹有迹則小不可名言者則無迹無迹則大大
者理也夫子之道具衆理而無迹是以見其用
而不見其體見其出之之時而不見其所以時
出之妙又烏可以名言哉不可名言而謂之曰
孔子之謂集大成而後不可名言者益見矣夫
大成何爲者也孟子以夫子之道至大難形故
借樂以形之而非以爲眞有所成也嘗爲之說
曰可器者則有成不器者則無成有所成者則
泥無所成者則通夫子通乎晝夜之道而知故
punctuated:
孔子之謂集大成
梁式
同考試官教諭王批：以大成為本體，足見深造。
同考試官教諭劉批：俱自胸中流出。
同考試官教諭徐批：集大成處發得精新，似非文章之士。
考試官教諭劉批：是學孔孟而有得者。
考試官教授林批：不蹈襲。
夫子之道，不可以名言者也。夫可名言者則有迹，有迹則小；不可名言者則無迹，無迹則大。大者，理也。夫子之道具衆理而無迹，是以見其用而不見其體，見其出之之時而不見其所以時出之妙，又烏可以名言哉？不可名言，而謂之曰「孔子之謂集大成」，而後不可名言者益見矣。夫大成何爲者也？孟子以夫子之道至大難形，故借樂以形之，而非以爲眞有所成也。嘗爲之說曰：可器者則有成，不器者則無成；有所成者則泥，無所成者則通。夫子通乎晝夜之道而知，故
translation_en:
“Confucius Is Said to Have Brought Together the Great Consummation”
Liang Shi
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “He takes the great consummation as the fundamental substance, fully demonstrating profound attainment.”
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It all flows from his own heart.”
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “His exposition of ‘bringing together the great consummation’ is incisive and fresh. He seems to be more than a mere man of letters.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Here is someone who has studied Confucius and Mencius and attained understanding.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “He does not imitate his predecessors.”
The Master's Way cannot be expressed in words. What can be expressed in words has traces; what has traces is limited. What cannot be expressed in words has no traces; what has no traces is great. This greatness is principle. The Master's Way comprises all principles yet leaves no traces. Thus we see its functioning but not its substance; we see the occasions on which he brings it forth, but not the subtle workings by which he brings it forth at the fitting time. How, then, could it be expressed in words? Though it cannot be expressed in words, once one says, “Confucius is said to have brought together the great consummation,” that which cannot be expressed becomes still more apparent. What, then, is this great consummation? Mencius considered the Master's Way so great that it was difficult to give it form; he therefore borrowed music to represent it, without supposing that it truly involved any fixed accomplishment. I have offered this explanation: what can be made into a vessel has a determinate completion; what is not a vessel has no determinate completion. Having a determinate accomplishment entails confinement; having none allows unrestricted passage. The Master comprehends the Way of day and night and knows it; therefore …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
博學而無所成名惟其無所成名所以爲大成
也非無所成也有所成而不與也猶之樂焉成
於金石者則爲金爲石成於絲竹者則爲絲爲
竹成於匏土革木者則爲匏爲土爲革爲木不
復與金石絲竹更唱而迭用及夫黃鍾一變而
后所謂金石絲竹匏土革木者大小清濁始終
條理惟其所調而不得專其用以歸於黃鍾黃
鍾又無所有焉以全其大何者八音有器黃鍾
則無器焉夫子之道亦猶是也夫子不器故能
===
成其大而伯夷伊尹柳下惠之三子者各有其
器所以卒爲夫子之所有而夫子又未嘗以爲
有也有者有之也有意必固我之心則其清任
和也終不能無執之之心而將反爲清任和之
所執是以行成而名立不若無名者之無所不
成也無所不成則理也中也中無定在是以無
名其諸樂之中氣焉爾也嘗觀記者述夫子之
言曰在天成象在地成形如此則禮者天地之
別也地氣上齊天氣下降陰陽相摩天地相盪
punctuated: 博學而無所成名，惟其無所成名，所以爲大成也。非無所成也，有所成而不與也。猶之樂焉，成於金石者則爲金爲石，成於絲竹者則爲絲爲竹，成於匏土革木者則爲匏爲土爲革爲木，不復與金石絲竹更唱而迭用。及夫黃鍾一變而后，所謂金石絲竹匏土革木者，大小清濁，始終條理，惟其所調，而不得專其用，以歸於黃鍾。黃鍾又無所有焉，以全其大。何者？八音有器，黃鍾則無器焉。夫子之道亦猶是也。夫子不器，故能成其大，而伯夷、伊尹、柳下惠之三子者，各有其器，所以卒爲夫子之所有，而夫子又未嘗以爲有也。有者，有之也。有意必固我之心，則其清任和也，終不能無執之之心，而將反爲清任和之所執。是以行成而名立，不若無名者之無所不成也。無所不成，則理也，中也。中無定在，是以無名，其諸樂之中氣焉爾也。嘗觀記者述夫子之言曰：「在天成象，在地成形，如此則禮者天地之別也。地氣上齊，天氣下降，陰陽相摩，天地相盪，
translation_en:
…broadly learned, yet achieving no particular distinction by which he could be named. Precisely because no particular achievement gave him a name, he constituted the great completion. It was not that he achieved nothing; he achieved, yet did not identify himself with those achievements. Music offers an analogy. What achieves completion in metal and stone remains metal and stone; what achieves completion in silk and bamboo remains silk and bamboo; what achieves completion in gourd, clay, hide, and wood remains gourd, clay, hide, and wood, no longer joining metal, stone, silk, and bamboo in alternating performance and use. But once the Yellow Bell pitch (huangzhong) undergoes a modulation, all these materials—metal, stone, silk, bamboo, gourd, clay, hide, and wood—with their greater and lesser volumes, clear and turbid tones, and ordered beginnings and endings, follow its tuning. None can monopolize its function; all return to the Yellow Bell. Yet the Yellow Bell itself possesses nothing, thereby preserving its greatness whole. Why? The eight classes of musical sound have instruments, whereas the Yellow Bell has no instrument of its own.

The Master's Way is likewise. The Master is no mere vessel and thus can achieve his greatness. The three masters, Bo Yi, Yi Yin, and Liu Xiahui, each have their particular vessel; hence their qualities ultimately become what the Master possesses. Yet the Master has never regarded them as possessions. To possess is to hold something as one's own. If one's mind harbors conjecture, insistence, rigidity, and self-centeredness, then even in one's purity, responsibility, and harmony, one cannot finally escape attachment to these qualities; instead, one becomes bound by them. Thus, establishing one's conduct and gaining a name falls short of the nameless person's capacity to accomplish everything. To accomplish everything is principle; it is the Mean. The Mean has no fixed location and therefore no name. Perhaps it is simply the balanced vital force within music.

I have read how the compiler of the Record recounted the Master's words: “In Heaven, images take shape; on Earth, forms take shape. Thus ritual constitutes the distinctions of Heaven and Earth. Earth's vital force rises, Heaven's vital force descends; yin and yang rub against one another, and Heaven and Earth stir one another…”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨動之以四時煖之以
日月而百化興焉如此則樂者天地之和也是
以禮樂極於天蟠於地行乎陰陽而通乎鬼神
窮高極遠而測深厚樂著大始而禮居成物著
不息者天也著不動者地也一動一靜者天地
之間也噫至矣夫子之道卽雷霆風雨日月之
道雷霆風雨日月之道卽四時之道四時之道
卽陰陽鬼神之道陰陽鬼神之道卽天地一動
一靜之道一動一靜天地之間者不可物也天
===
地之德不可物故以成形成象見其德聖人之
德不可見故先王作樂以象成夫子之成不可
名故假而名之曰大成大成者統同而辨異也
是故夫子之道自其存巳也人斯謂之清矣然
之陳之宋之魯之見南子與互鄉之童子則大
者未嘗變焉君子不謂之清也自其與世也人
斯謂之和矣然佛肸之召陽貨之見夫子雖有
欲仕之心而彼終欲致之而不可得則大者未
嘗變焉君子不謂之和也自其急於仁天下也
punctuated:
鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉。如此，則樂者天地之和也。是以禮樂極於天，蟠於地，行乎陰陽而通乎鬼神，窮高極遠而測深厚。樂著大始，而禮居成物。著不息者，天也；著不動者，地也；一動一靜者，天地之間也。噫，至矣！夫子之道卽雷霆風雨日月之道，雷霆風雨日月之道卽四時之道，四時之道卽陰陽鬼神之道，陰陽鬼神之道卽天地一動一靜之道。一動一靜，天地之間者不可物也。天地之德不可物，故以成形成象見其德；聖人之德不可見，故先王作樂以象成。夫子之成不可名，故假而名之曰大成。大成者，統同而辨異也。
是故夫子之道，自其存巳也，人斯謂之清矣。然之陳、之宋、之魯，之見南子，與互鄉之童子，則大者未嘗變焉，君子不謂之清也。自其與世也，人斯謂之和矣。然佛肸之召，陽貨之見，夫子雖有欲仕之心，而彼終欲致之而不可得，則大者未嘗變焉，君子不謂之和也。自其急於仁天下也，
translation_en:
…They are stirred by thunder, roused by wind and rain, moved by the four seasons, and warmed by the sun and moon, and the myriad transformations arise. Thus music is the harmony of Heaven and Earth. Hence rites and music reach to Heaven, extend throughout Earth, operate through yin and yang, and communicate with ghosts and spirits. They exhaust the heights, reach the farthest distances, and fathom depth and substance. Music manifests the Great Beginning, while rites reside in things brought to completion. What manifests ceaseless activity is Heaven; what manifests immobility is Earth; alternating movement and stillness occur between Heaven and Earth. Ah, how consummate! The Master's Way is the Way of thunder, wind, rain, sun, and moon. Their Way is the Way of the four seasons; the Way of the four seasons is the Way of yin and yang, ghosts and spirits; and their Way is the Way of Heaven and Earth's alternating movement and stillness. This alternation between Heaven and Earth cannot be treated as a thing. The potency of Heaven and Earth cannot be treated as a thing, and so it is made manifest through the formation of shapes and images. The sage's virtue cannot be seen, and so the former kings made music to represent accomplishment. The Master's accomplishment cannot be named, and so we provisionally call it the Great Synthesis. The Great Synthesis unites what is shared while distinguishing what differs.
Thus, regarding the Master's Way, when people consider how he preserved himself [?], they call him pure. Yet when he went to Chen, Song, and Lu, went to see Nanzi, and received the boy from Huxiang, his greater principle never changed. The gentleman therefore does not characterize him as merely pure. When people consider his dealings with the world, they call him harmonious. Yet when Bi Xi summoned him and Yang Huo sought to see him, although the Master wished to take office, they ultimately could not secure his service despite their desire to do so. His greater principle never changed. The gentleman therefore does not characterize him as merely harmonious. When one considers his urgency to bring benevolence to all under Heaven…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人斯謂之任矣然接淅而行明日遂行與不脫
冕而行而卒之以歸魯則大者未嘗變焉君子
不謂之任也不謂之任則人不可識不可識則
無迹而其出也以時其斯之謂大成也已何者
吾心廣大之體本如是也吾心之體無在而無
不在無在故無方無方則神是以大生焉無不
在故無體無體則化是以廣生焉大則不禦廣
則不遺成性存存是以時中出焉以言乎聖人
之道天地之間則備矣或者不知本體之說乃
===
曰夫子集三子之所長而成其大如聚珠然而
不知夫子之道自集自成若有所集而非集於
三子若有所成而非成以三子也若謂集以三
子則三者並畜而不虛縱有所至猶不免於襲
取之弊其清也卽伯夷之清任也卽伊尹之任
和也卽下惠之和而隘與不恭有所不免其爲
成也猶之三子而已豈夫子之道哉夫子之道
孟子所謂聖智者是也智者知也知此本體者
也聖者行也行此本體者也知者行之始行者
punctuated: 人斯謂之任矣。然接淅而行，明日遂行，與不脫冕而行，而卒之以歸魯，則大者未嘗變焉，君子不謂之任也。不謂之任，則人不可識；不可識，則無迹，而其出也以時，其斯之謂大成也已。何者？吾心廣大之體本如是也。吾心之體，無在而無不在。無在故無方，無方則神，是以大生焉；無不在故無體，無體則化，是以廣生焉。大則不禦，廣則不遺，成性存存，是以時中出焉。以言乎聖人之道，天地之間則備矣。或者不知本體之說，乃曰夫子集三子之所長而成其大，如聚珠然，而不知夫子之道自集自成，若有所集而非集於三子，若有所成而非成以三子也。若謂集以三子，則三者並畜而不虛，縱有所至，猶不免於襲取之弊。其清也卽伯夷之清，任也卽伊尹之任，和也卽下惠之和，而隘與不恭有所不免。其爲成也，猶之三子而已，豈夫子之道哉？夫子之道，孟子所謂聖智者是也。智者，知也，知此本體者也；聖者，行也，行此本體者也。知者行之始，行者
translation_en:
…people therefore call him one who assumes responsibility. Yet he departed with his rice still being rinsed, departed the very next day, and departed without removing his ceremonial cap, finally returning to Lu. In all this, what was great in him never changed; hence the gentleman does not characterize him as one who assumes responsibility. If he cannot be so characterized, people cannot fathom him. If he cannot be fathomed, he leaves no fixed traces, and his coming forth accords with the time. This, surely, is what is meant by the “great completion.” Why is this so? The broad and great substance of our own mind is originally just like this. The substance of our mind is nowhere located, yet nowhere absent. Being nowhere located, it has no fixed direction; having no fixed direction, it is numinous, and from this its greatness arises. Being nowhere absent, it has no fixed form; having no fixed form, it transforms, and from this its breadth arises. Being great, it cannot be restrained; being broad, it leaves nothing out. By continually preserving its fully realized nature, it brings forth the Mean appropriate to each moment. Speaking of the sage’s Way, everything between Heaven and Earth is thus complete.

Some, not understanding this account of the original substance, say that the Master gathered the strengths of the three masters and thereby achieved his greatness, as though collecting pearls. They do not understand that the Master’s Way gathers and completes itself: if there is something gathered, it is not gathered from the three masters; if there is something completed, it is not completed by means of the three masters. If one says that he gathered it by means of the three masters, then all three dispositions would be stored together within him, leaving no emptiness. Whatever he might attain, he would still be unable to escape the fault of borrowing and imitation. His purity would simply be Bo Yi’s purity, his assumption of responsibility Yi Yin’s assumption of responsibility, and his harmony Hui of Liu Xia’s harmony; he could not entirely avoid narrowness and irreverence. His completion would amount merely to that of the three masters. How could this be the Master’s Way?

The Master’s Way is what Mengzi calls sageliness and wisdom. Wisdom means knowing: knowing this original substance. Sageliness means acting: putting this original substance into practice. Knowing is the beginning of acting; acting is…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知之成之三子者惟其知之偏是以成之小夫
子之大成所以為大智也故曰知至至之可與
幾也知終終之可與存義也是夫子之言也惜
乎人之偏於見也仁者見之則謂之仁知者見
之則謂之知君子之道鮮矣孟子眞知夫子者
也故曰行之而不著焉習矣而不察焉終身由
之而不知其道衆也蓋歎夫人之不知其體也
至大至剛以直養而無害雖以冉牛閔子顏淵
具聖人之體而不敢安則其所造其大而未化
===
者乎知言養氣集義者其功也
表

蕭來鳳
同考試官敎諭蕭批語健意精非留心本政者
不能作
考試官敎諭劉批清而有味
考試官敎授林批典雅
建炎三年某月某日廣州敎授臣林勲謹
punctuated:
知之成之。三子者，惟其知之偏，是以成之小。夫子之大成，所以為大智也。故曰：「知至至之，可與幾也；知終終之，可與存義也。」是夫子之言也。惜乎人之偏於見也！仁者見之則謂之仁，知者見之則謂之知，君子之道鮮矣。孟子眞知夫子者也，故曰：「行之而不著焉，習矣而不察焉，終身由之而不知其道，衆也。」蓋歎夫人之不知其體也。至大至剛，以直養而無害，雖以冉牛、閔子、顏淵具聖人之體而不敢安，則其所造，其大而未化者乎？知言、養氣、集義者，其功也。
表
擬宋廣州敎授林勲上本政書表，建炎三年。
蕭來鳳
同考試官敎諭蕭批：語健意精，非留心本政者不能作。
考試官敎諭劉批：清而有味。
考試官敎授林批：典雅。
建炎三年某月某日，廣州敎授臣林勲謹
translation_en:
…the completion of knowing [?]. The three masters attained only a limited perfection because their knowledge was partial. The Master's great perfection was therefore great wisdom. Thus it is said: “Knowing the point to be reached and reaching it, one can participate in the incipient workings of things; knowing the end and carrying it through, one can preserve righteousness.” These are the Master's words. How regrettable that people's perceptions are partial! The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. Few comprehend the Way of the gentleman. Mengzi truly understood the Master. Thus he said: “To act without understanding, to become accustomed without examining, and to follow it throughout one's life without knowing its Way—this is how most people are.” He was lamenting people's failure to understand its essential substance. It is supremely great and supremely firm, nourished through uprightness without injury. Even Ran Niu, Minzi, and Yan Yuan, who embodied the essential substance of the sage, did not dare rest content. Had their attainment, then, reached greatness but not yet transformation? Understanding words, nourishing vital energy, and accumulating righteousness constituted their work.

Memorial

A memorial in the person of Lin Xun, Professor in Guangzhou under the Song, submitting his Book on the Fundamentals of Government (Benzheng shu), in the third year of Jianyan [1129].

By Xiao Laifeng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Vigorous language and refined ideas. Only someone who has devoted attention to the fundamentals of government could write this.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Clear, yet rich in flavor.”

Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: “Classical and elegant.”

On a certain day of a certain month in the third year of Jianyan, your servant Lin Xun, Professor in Guangzhou, respectfully…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以所撰本政書上
獻者伏以
賢君觀萬化之原因時立政忠臣思一得之益
隨事昌言稽往牒以成編本生民之急務
敢塵
黼扆庸效芻蕘臣勲誠惶誠恐頓首稽首竊
惟
國保於民
皇建有極所其無逸知小人稼穡之依率由舊
===
章爲王業艱難之故實帝王心法之要爲
民生衣食之源自井牧肇于黃虞經制已
備至貢助行之湯禹法度爲詳以迄成周
尤重民事風歌七月鴻鴈無中澤之哀雅
善三單草莽皆在公之役分田制祿足用
安邊經界正而井地均什一行而頌聲作
慨秦之世阡陌旣開由唐以來兵農遂二
趙過搜粟無補海內空虛陳靖司農祗益
編氓耗竭反裘以負涸澤而漁何有乎正
punctuated:
以所撰《本政書》上獻者。伏以：賢君觀萬化之原，因時立政；忠臣思一得之益，隨事昌言。稽往牒以成編，本生民之急務，敢塵黼扆，庸效芻蕘。臣勲誠惶誠恐，頓首稽首。
竊惟：國保於民，皇建有極。所其無逸，知小人稼穡之依；率由舊章，爲王業艱難之故實。帝王心法之要，爲民生衣食之源。自井牧肇于黃虞，經制已備；至貢助行之湯禹，法度爲詳。以迄成周，尤重民事。風歌《七月》，鴻鴈無中澤之哀；雅善三單，草莽皆在公之役。分田制祿，足用安邊；經界正而井地均，什一行而頌聲作。慨秦之世，阡陌旣開；由唐以來，兵農遂二。趙過搜粟，無補海內空虛；陳靖司農，祗益編氓耗竭。反裘以負，涸澤而漁，何有乎正
translation_en:
…hereby submits the Fundamentals of Government, which he has composed, for Your Majesty’s consideration. I humbly observe: a worthy ruler examines the source of all transformations and establishes government suited to the times; a loyal minister considers the benefit that even a single insight may bring and speaks forthrightly as circumstances require. Examining records of the past to compile this work, I have taken the urgent needs of the people as its foundation. I venture to trouble the imperial throne with it, offering the counsel of a grass-cutter and wood-gatherer. Your servant Xun, in deepest awe and apprehension, bows his head and prostrates himself.
I humbly reflect that the state is preserved through its people, and the sovereign establishes the supreme standard. Taking his place where there is no ease, he understands the farming upon which ordinary people depend; following the old statutes, he takes as his precedents the hardships of founding a royal enterprise. The essentials of the emperors’ and kings’ teachings concerning the mind are the source of the people’s food and clothing. From the beginnings of the well-field system and the allocation of land under the Yellow Emperor and Shun, institutions were already fully established; when the tribute and labor-assistance systems were practiced under Tang and Yu, their regulations became detailed. By the Zhou dynasty, the people’s affairs received still greater attention. Among the Airs, “Seventh Month” was sung, and the wild geese had no cause to lament amid the marshes; among the Court Hymns, the three military divisions were praised, and even those in the wilds performed public service. Fields were apportioned and stipends regulated, ensuring sufficient resources and secure frontiers. Once field boundaries were properly established, well-field allotments were equitable; when the tithe was implemented, songs of praise arose. Alas, in the Qin period the field boundaries were opened up; from the Tang onward, soldiers and farmers became separate groups. Zhao Guo, as Commandant for Grain Collection, did nothing to remedy the empire’s depleted resources; Chen Jing, administering agriculture, merely further exhausted the registered common people. This was like turning a fur coat inside out to carry a burden, or draining a marsh to catch its fish. What place was there for rectifying…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
德利用厚生惡在爲勞來旋定安集潢池
兆釁石壕吏之朘削尤深碩鼠傷殘安上
門之流離具在
近自建炎之歲
上遡開國之初兩稅之征數已增于七倍九
伐之法人不知者百年皆緣經理之疎未
獲雍熈之效惟
明哲以庶績其凝爲泰在農夫以百畝不易爲
憂乆激愚衷曷酬
===
洪造玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
繼天駿命
垂世丕圖民安而視若未安
治先邦本道至而望猶未至
功妙時幾從善如圜進人加膝故自忘其固
陋爰陳本政之書亦願
察於細微壹明王者之制夫一而占田五十
畝井一而爲夫十六人由兵馬以及餘緡
punctuated:
德、利用、厚生？惡在爲勞來、旋定、安集？潢池兆釁，石壕吏之朘削尤深；碩鼠傷殘，安上門之流離具在。近自建炎之歲，上遡開國之初，兩稅之征，數已增于七倍；九伐之法，人不知者百年。皆緣經理之疎，未獲雍熈之效。惟明哲以庶績其凝爲泰，在農夫以百畝不易爲憂。乆激愚衷，曷酬洪造？
玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，繼天駿命，垂世丕圖。民安而視若未安，治先邦本；道至而望猶未至，功妙時幾。從善如圜，進人加膝。故自忘其固陋，爰陳本政之書，亦願察於細微，壹明王者之制。夫一而占田五十畝，井一而爲夫十六人，由兵馬以及餘緡，
translation_en:
…virtue, making resources useful, and enriching the people's livelihood? Where is the effort to encourage them, draw them back, bring them peace, and settle them? Unrest brews by the pools; exactions are even harsher than those of the constable of Shihao. The great rats ravage the people, and the displaced at Anshang Gate are there for all to see. From the more recent Jianyan years [?] back to the founding of the dynasty, the amount levied under the two-tax system has already increased sevenfold; the rules governing the nine kinds of punitive expedition have remained unknown to men for a hundred years. All this results from lax administration, which has failed to achieve harmony and prosperity. The enlightened ruler regards the firm establishment of all undertakings as peace, while the farmer worries that his hundred mu remain untilled. These concerns have long stirred my humble heart. How can I repay your boundless beneficence?
Now, reverently encountering Your Majesty [〇〇〇〇 in the text], who has inherited Heaven's great mandate and bequeaths a grand design to posterity: although the people are secure, you regard them as not yet secure, giving priority in government to the people, the foundation of the state. Although the Way has been attained, you look ahead as though it were not yet attained; your achievements lie in your subtle grasp of the first signs of change. You follow good counsel as readily as a circle turns, and promote men as though drawing them onto your knees. Thus, forgetting my own ignorance and narrowness, I present this writing on the foundations of government. I also hope that you will scrutinize its small details and make fully clear the institutions of a true king. Each man would occupy fifty mu of land, and each well-field unit would comprise sixteen men. From soldiers and horses to the remaining strings of cash…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
自隸農而至匹婦斂散有節適緩急之宜
勞逸相均便分番之直足兵足食有土有
財是謂因略致詳復井田之舊庶幾以人
立政增
祖武之光事在可行言皆有據臣業慙學稼敎
不逮於蘇湖祿過代耕志欲裨於海嶽雖
非
帝籍不刋之典誠爲平生獨得之愚行以十年
化未三代者未之有也伏願
===
===
端本善則
明物察倫
先天下之憂
謹日中之戒
儆於有位
養賢以及萬民
紹乃前聞
雪恥而酬
九廟
punctuated: 自隸農而至匹婦，斂散有節，適緩急之宜；勞逸相均，便分番之直。足兵足食，有土有財，是謂因略致詳，復井田之舊，庶幾以人立政，增祖武之光。事在可行，言皆有據。臣業慙學稼，敎不逮於蘇湖；祿過代耕，志欲裨於海嶽。雖非帝籍不刋之典，誠爲平生獨得之愚。行以十年，化未三代者，未之有也。伏願端本善則，明物察倫，先天下之憂，謹日中之戒，儆於有位，養賢以及萬民，紹乃前聞，雪恥而酬九廟
translation_en:
…from dependent farmers to ordinary women, collections and distributions would be regulated to meet both routine needs and emergencies; toil and rest would be evenly apportioned, facilitating service in rotating shifts. There would be sufficient troops and provisions, land and wealth. This is what is meant by working from a general outline toward detailed arrangements and restoring the old well-field system. In this way, one might establish government through the right people and add lustre to the achievements of Your Majesty’s ancestors.

These measures are practicable, and every statement has a basis. Your servant is ashamed of his meagre competence in farming; his teaching falls short of that of Suzhou and Huzhou. His stipend exceeds what he needs in place of tilling the fields, yet his ambition is to contribute something to Your Majesty’s oceanic and mountainous greatness. Though this is no immutable canon of the imperial records [?], it is indeed the humble insight independently attained over my lifetime. If these measures were implemented for ten years, there could be no failure to attain a moral transformation comparable to that of the Three Dynasties.

I humbly pray that Your Majesty will rectify the foundations and perfect the standards, understand things and discern human relationships, take upon yourself the cares of the realm before others do, heed the warning conveyed by the sun at its zenith, admonish those in office, nurture the worthy and extend this care to all the people, carry forward your former renown, and wipe away humiliation to requite the ancestors in the nine ancestral temples…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
垂衣致治
卑服即功
調玉燭於氤氲占太平之有象
鼓仁風以披拂衍
盛世於無疆臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以本政書十三篇奉
表隨
進以
===
聞
第叄塲
策
第一問
蕭來鳳
同考試官教諭蕭批不但善陳
聖主德且忠愛之心見於言外
考試官教諭劉批大雅之作
考試官教授林批有胸襟
punctuated:
垂衣致治，卑服即功，調玉燭於氤氲，占太平之有象；鼓仁風以披拂，衍盛世於無疆。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以本政書十三篇，奉表隨進以聞。
第叄塲
策
第一問
蕭來鳳
同考試官教諭蕭批：不但善陳聖主德，且忠愛之心見於言外。
考試官教諭劉批：大雅之作。
考試官教授林批：有胸襟。
translation_en:
…With robes hanging loosely, you bring about good government; wearing humble garments, you apply yourself to the work of rule. You harmonize the seasons amid the mingling vital forces, revealing signs of great peace; you stir the breeze of benevolence to spread everywhere, extending this flourishing age without limit. Your servant, looking up to Heaven and reverently admiring Your Majesty, cannot contain his fervent emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit the thirteen chapters of the Book on the Fundamentals of Government (Ben zheng shu), together with this accompanying memorial, for Your Majesty’s attention.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Xiao Laifeng
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Not only does he skillfully expound the sage sovereign’s virtue, but his loyal devotion is also evident beyond the words themselves.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “A work of great elegance.”
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: “He possesses breadth of mind.”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝王之創業垂統也當有以昭曠代之宏
規而其繼體守成也當有以隆中興之大
業夫創業之君嗣王是法必宏規有立而
後人為可繼繼體之君先烈是揚必大業
克隆而前人為益光於乎此我
太祖高皇帝之法古為治而典章文物追蹤於
二帝三王之盛
皇上之經綸大業巍巍足稱中興之盛歟粵昔
秦失其鹿天下競逐漢高起自豐沛手提
===
三尺不五載而成帝業故史臣班彪贊其
所以興者有五曰帝王之苗裔曰體貌多
奇異曰神武有徵應曰寛明而仁恕曰知
人善任使言其取天下於亡秦者以是也
有宋不競元夷猾夏我
太祖高皇帝不階尺土奮起布衣亦不十餘年
而正夫統故
當代文臣宋濂述
聖祖之所以興者有六曰功高萬古曰得國之
punctuated: 帝王之創業垂統也，當有以昭曠代之宏規；而其繼體守成也，當有以隆中興之大業。夫創業之君，嗣王是法，必宏規有立，而後人為可繼；繼體之君，先烈是揚，必大業克隆，而前人為益光。於乎！此我太祖高皇帝之法古為治，而典章文物追蹤於二帝三王之盛，皇上之經綸大業巍巍，足稱中興之盛歟！粵昔秦失其鹿，天下競逐，漢高起自豐沛，手提三尺，不五載而成帝業。故史臣班彪贊其所以興者有五：曰帝王之苗裔，曰體貌多奇異，曰神武有徵應，曰寛明而仁恕，曰知人善任使。言其取天下於亡秦者以是也。有宋不競，元夷猾夏。我太祖高皇帝不階尺土，奮起布衣，亦不十餘年而正夫統。故當代文臣宋濂述聖祖之所以興者有六：曰功高萬古，曰得國之
translation_en:
When emperors and kings found a dynasty and establish its succession, they must make manifest a grand design unmatched across the ages; when they inherit the throne and preserve what has been achieved, they must advance the great undertaking of dynastic restoration. A founding ruler is the model for succeeding kings: his grand design must be established before later generations can carry it forward. A ruler who inherits the throne exalts his predecessors’ glorious deeds: his great undertaking must flourish before their glory can be further enhanced. Ah! Is this not why our Emperor Taizu Gao modeled his government on antiquity, his institutions and cultural achievements matching the flourishing ages of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, while His Majesty’s majestic work of ordering the realm deserves to be called a flourishing dynastic restoration?
In former times, Qin lost its deer—the empire—and all under Heaven competed to pursue it. Gaozu of Han arose from Feng and Pei, wielding a three-foot sword, and in fewer than five years established his imperial rule. Thus the historian Ban Biao praised five reasons for his rise: he was descended from emperors and kings; his physique and appearance bore many extraordinary features; his divine martial prowess was confirmed by signs; he was generous and discerning, humane and forgiving; and he understood men and employed them well. These, Ban Biao said, were the reasons he took the empire from the fallen Qin.
The Song dynasty proved weak, and the Yuan barbarians threw the Chinese realm into turmoil. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, without so much as a foot of inherited territory to build upon, rose from the ranks of commoners and likewise, in no more than a dozen or so years, established the rightful imperial succession. Thus Song Lian, a civil official of his time, set forth six reasons for the Sagely Progenitor’s rise: first, his achievements surpassed those of all ages; second, the manner in which he gained the realm …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
正曰獨稟全智曰敬天勤民曰家法之嚴
曰兵政有統言其復我中國帝王之統者
以是也夫我
太祖高皇帝之取天下得國之正雖與漢高同
而其復華夏於腥羶視起生民於塗炭者
厥功尤偉固非漢高之所可同矣故曰功
高萬古者也然而漢高代秦之興去古未
遠先王之典則尚存六經之遺籍未散高
帝不能收拾補綴其殘壞以追三代之隆
===
而以苟簡之規模自足三章約法之外一
切承襲秦舊無所建明卒使先王典禮湮
而不章論治者不無遺恨於高帝也若我
太祖高皇帝之興乃在亡秦千載之後矣觀其
草創之初首建
宗社以重邦國之本繼立庠序以先郡縣之化
大業既定稽古立法制禮以序倫作樂以
宣化建官以分職明教以齊俗凡所制作
盡反元政典章文物直追前古之隆有非
punctuated:
正，曰獨稟全智，曰敬天勤民，曰家法之嚴，曰兵政有統，言其復我中國帝王之統者以是也。夫我太祖高皇帝之取天下，得國之正雖與漢高同，而其復華夏於腥羶，視起生民於塗炭者，厥功尤偉，固非漢高之所可同矣。故曰功高萬古者也。然而漢高代秦之興，去古未遠，先王之典則尚存，六經之遺籍未散，高帝不能收拾補綴其殘壞，以追三代之隆，而以苟簡之規模自足。三章約法之外，一切承襲秦舊，無所建明，卒使先王典禮湮而不章，論治者不無遺恨於高帝也。
若我太祖高皇帝之興，乃在亡秦千載之後矣。觀其草創之初，首建宗社，以重邦國之本；繼立庠序，以先郡縣之化。大業既定，稽古立法，制禮以序倫，作樂以宣化，建官以分職，明教以齊俗。凡所制作，盡反元政，典章文物直追前古之隆，有非
translation_en:
…the legitimacy of his acquisition of the realm; next, his unique endowment with consummate wisdom; next, his reverence for Heaven and diligent care for the people; next, the strictness of his dynastic household rules; and next, the unified direction of military administration. These, he said, were the reasons he restored the succession of emperors and kings in our Central Realm. Now, in taking All under Heaven, our Emperor Taizu Gao equaled Gaozu of Han in the legitimacy of his acquisition of the realm. Yet his restoration of Huaxia from the reek of flesh and mutton [a disparaging reference to alien rule] was an achievement still greater than rescuing the people from mire and burning coals. It certainly cannot be placed on the same level as Gaozu of Han’s achievement. Thus it is said that his merit surpassed all antiquity. Nevertheless, when Gaozu of Han arose to replace Qin, antiquity was not yet far distant. The institutions and standards of the former kings still survived, and the transmitted writings of the Six Classics had not yet been dispersed. Emperor Gaozu failed to gather and piece together their damaged remains so as to recover the flourishing order of the Three Dynasties. Instead, he was content with makeshift and rudimentary arrangements. Apart from his compact reducing the laws to three articles, he inherited all the old practices of Qin without establishing or elucidating anything anew. In the end, this caused the canonical rites of the former kings to sink into obscurity. Those who discuss government cannot but feel some lingering regret over Emperor Gaozu.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao, by contrast, arose a thousand years after Qin’s fall. Consider the beginning of his founding endeavor: first he established the ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain, giving due weight to the foundations of the state; next he established schools, giving priority to the moral transformation of the prefectures and counties. Once his great enterprise was secured, he examined antiquity and established laws. He instituted rites to order human relationships, created music to spread moral transformation, established offices to distribute duties, and clarified moral instruction to bring customs into accord. Everything he instituted reversed Yuan governance. His statutes, institutions, and cultural achievements directly matched the flourishing ages of antiquity; among them were things that could not…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一時儒臣播誦之所能盡者此豈漢高之
所可得而並論哉所以然者蓋漢高得天
下於馬上不事詩書又嫚而侮人不喜儒
生當時為之議禮者僅以叔孫通鄙儒而
帝方命之曰令易知度吾所能行為之則
帝誠非有復古之心而真知垂統之大計
者其安於苟簡也固宜我
太祖高皇帝本以
天授神聖之資應運而出兵戈倥傯即能延訪
===
鴻儒以置帷幄購求遺書以備
省閱其所得於講論聞見者既深且廣故能
見超千古慮周萬世創制立法盡善盡美
有以昭曠代之宏規也夫作之於前者固
不可無久大之業而守之於後者尤不可
無充拓之功歷觀前代繼體之君如漢之
武帝能表章六經有功斯道矣而窮奢黷
武卒致海內之虛耗唐之憲宗能收復淮
蔡威震強藩矣而驕心一起反令美業之
punctuated:
一時儒臣播誦之所能盡者，此豈漢高之所可得而並論哉？所以然者，蓋漢高得天下於馬上，不事詩書，又嫚而侮人，不喜儒生。當時為之議禮者，僅以叔孫通鄙儒，而帝方命之曰：「令易知，度吾所能行為之。」則帝誠非有復古之心而真知垂統之大計者，其安於苟簡也固宜。我太祖高皇帝本以天授神聖之資，應運而出，兵戈倥傯，即能延訪鴻儒以置帷幄，購求遺書以備省閱。其所得於講論聞見者既深且廣，故能見超千古，慮周萬世，創制立法，盡善盡美，有以昭曠代之宏規也。
夫作之於前者，固不可無久大之業，而守之於後者，尤不可無充拓之功。歷觀前代繼體之君，如漢之武帝，能表章六經，有功斯道矣，而窮奢黷武，卒致海內之虛耗；唐之憲宗，能收復淮蔡，威震強藩矣，而驕心一起，反令美業之
translation_en:
…could fully convey through the praises of the Confucian officials of his time. How could Gaozu of Han possibly be discussed on equal terms with him? The reason is that Gaozu of Han won the realm on horseback, paid no attention to the Odes and Documents, and was moreover arrogant and insulting toward others, disliking Confucian scholars. The man who deliberated on ritual for him at the time was merely that vulgar scholar Shusun Tong, and the emperor instructed him: “Make it easy to understand; devise it according to what you judge I can carry out.” Thus the emperor truly had neither the desire to restore antiquity nor a genuine understanding of the great plan for transmitting his rule to posterity. It was only to be expected that he should remain content with makeshift simplicity. Our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, possessed Heaven-bestowed qualities of divine sagacity and arose in response to the destined time. Even amid the turmoil of warfare, he was able to seek out eminent Confucian scholars and bring them into his command tent, and to purchase surviving books for his own perusal. What he gained through discussion, hearing, and observation was both profound and extensive. Thus his vision surpassed a thousand ages, and his foresight encompassed ten thousand generations. In creating institutions and establishing laws, he attained perfection in every respect, thereby displaying a grand design unequaled through the ages.
Those who establish a foundation must indeed leave an enterprise of enduring greatness; but those who preserve it afterward must all the more accomplish the work of extending and enlarging it. Surveying the rulers of earlier dynasties who inherited the throne, Emperor Wu of Han, for example, honored and promoted the Six Classics and thereby rendered service to this Way. Yet his extravagant excesses and wanton warfare ultimately depleted the resources of the realm. Emperor Xianzong of Tang recovered Huai and Cai, and his might overawed the powerful regional military governors. Yet once pride arose in his heart, he instead caused his splendid enterprise to…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不終宋之神宗銳意更法勵精求治矣而
委用者無經世之學紛紛制作卒釀靖康
之亂惡在其爲中興也我
聖祖創大業於前
列聖紹鴻休於後奕葉相承有隆無替至我
皇上龍飛藩邸運際昌期禀
文武聖神之資備剛健中正之德
御極以來孜孜圖治其所以經綸大業
議禮考文足以建萬世之長策而綿億萬年
===
無疆之休者未能悉數而其卓然爲世大
法度越漢唐宋之君者則有五事可言定
圜丘方澤之制而分祀之議以一也著
明倫大典之書而繼統之禮以明也
留神經術則
經筵日御以研聖賢之旨尊崇孔子則正號
毁像而洗因循之陋察
先朝之遺弊革中官之出鎮若此者皆前人講
求之所未定智慮之所不及或牽於欲而
punctuated:
不終。宋之神宗銳意更法，勵精求治矣，而委用者無經世之學，紛紛制作，卒釀靖康之亂，惡在其爲中興也？
我聖祖創大業於前，列聖紹鴻休於後，奕葉相承，有隆無替。至我皇上龍飛藩邸，運際昌期，禀文武聖神之資，備剛健中正之德。御極以來，孜孜圖治，其所以經綸大業、議禮考文，足以建萬世之長策，而綿億萬年無疆之休者，未能悉數。而其卓然爲世大法、度越漢唐宋之君者，則有五事可言：定圜丘方澤之制，而分祀之議以一也；著《明倫大典》之書，而繼統之禮以明也；留神經術，則經筵日御，以研聖賢之旨；尊崇孔子，則正號毁像，而洗因循之陋；察先朝之遺弊，革中官之出鎮。若此者，皆前人講求之所未定、智慮之所不及，或牽於欲而
translation_en:
…not being brought to completion. Emperor Shenzong of the Song resolutely pursued reforms and devoted himself to achieving good government. Yet those he entrusted with office lacked the learning needed to govern the realm. Their profusion of new institutions ultimately bred the disorders of the Jingkang era. How could this count as a dynastic resurgence?
Our sagely founding ancestor established the great enterprise, and the succession of sage emperors carried forward his magnificent legacy. Generation succeeded generation, with ever greater flourishing and no decline. Then our present emperor rose like a dragon from his princely residence, his accession coinciding with an auspicious age. Endowed with civil and martial gifts, sagacity, and spiritual insight, he possesses the virtues of strength, vigor, balance, and rectitude. Since ascending the throne, he has worked tirelessly for good government. His ordering of the great enterprise, deliberations on ritual, and scrutiny of cultural institutions have established enduring policies for myriad generations and extended boundless blessings for countless ages; these achievements cannot all be enumerated. Yet five matters may be cited in which he has conspicuously established great standards for the age and surpassed the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song. He fixed the institutions of the Circular Mound and Square Marsh altars, thereby bringing agreement to the debate over worshipping Heaven and Earth separately. He compiled the Great Compendium Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian), thereby clarifying the rites governing succession to the imperial line. Attending closely to classical learning, he holds the Classics Colloquium daily to investigate the teachings of the sages and worthies. In honoring Confucius, he rectified his title and destroyed his images, thereby sweeping away the defects of unthinking adherence to precedent. Examining abuses inherited from earlier reigns, he abolished the dispatch of eunuchs to serve as regional overseers. Such measures concern matters that earlier rulers had studied without reaching a resolution, or that lay beyond their wisdom and foresight, or in which they were constrained by their desires and…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不能為或制於内而不敢為者而我
皇上稽古因心右文體道
濬哲淵衷超然遠覽
神謨聖斷毅然裁正有不待儒臣之賛一詞者
猗歟盛哉中興之業前代未之有比也所
以然者蓋我
皇上聰明睿智超越千古而又以
敬一之學上接堯舜禹湯文武周公孔子道
統之傳凡其見諸事天法祖者率皆裁以
===
往聖之心法故能剖析群疑脗合至道考
衷立度盡制盡倫有以隆中興之大業也
愚生生長遐陬沾濡
聖澤其所得於典籍之傳樂育之化者不過如
此何能以鋪張敷揚其萬一哉雖然愚嘗
聞諸先儒韓愈有言曰莫為於前雖美弗
彰莫為於後雖盛弗傳蓋創業者為其可
繼燕翼之仁也守成者光昭前烈繼述之
孝也我
punctuated:
不能為，或制於内而不敢為者。而我皇上稽古因心，右文體道，濬哲淵衷，超然遠覽，神謨聖斷，毅然裁正，有不待儒臣之賛一詞者。猗歟盛哉！中興之業，前代未之有比也。所以然者，蓋我皇上聰明睿智，超越千古，而又以敬一之學，上接堯舜禹湯文武周公孔子道統之傳。凡其見諸事天法祖者，率皆裁以往聖之心法，故能剖析群疑，脗合至道，考衷立度，盡制盡倫，有以隆中興之大業也。

愚生生長遐陬，沾濡聖澤，其所得於典籍之傳、樂育之化者，不過如此，何能以鋪張敷揚其萬一哉！雖然，愚嘗聞諸先儒，韓愈有言曰：「莫為於前，雖美弗彰；莫為於後，雖盛弗傳。」蓋創業者為其可繼，燕翼之仁也；守成者光昭前烈，繼述之孝也。我
translation_en:
…were unable to accomplish, or, constrained from within, dared not undertake. Yet our Emperor consults antiquity and acts from his own heart, honors letters and embodies the Way. With profound wisdom and depth of mind, he surveys matters from a lofty and far-reaching perspective; through inspired plans and sagely decisions, he resolutely judges and rectifies them, sometimes without waiting for even a word of assistance from his Confucian ministers. Ah, how magnificent! The achievement of this restoration has no equal in earlier dynasties. This is because our Emperor’s intelligence and sagely wisdom surpass those of all past ages. Moreover, through his learning of reverent unity, he carries forward the transmission of the succession of the Way from Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. All that he puts into practice in serving Heaven and following his ancestors is judged by the teachings of the former sages concerning the mind. Thus he can resolve the many doubts, accord perfectly with the supreme Way, ascertain the proper mean and establish standards, fully realize institutions and human relationships, and thereby bring the great achievement of restoration to its height.

I, an unworthy student, was born and raised in a distant corner of the realm and have been steeped in the blessings of the sage sovereign. What I have gained from the transmission of the classical writings and the transforming influence of his nurturing instruction amounts to no more than this. How could I possibly expound and extol even one ten-thousandth of his achievements? Nevertheless, I have heard this from the earlier Confucian masters. Han Yu said: “If none acts before, even beauty will not be made manifest; if none acts afterward, even greatness will not be transmitted.” Those who found an enterprise make it capable of being continued: this is the benevolence of providing for their descendants. Those who preserve an established achievement illuminate the glorious deeds of their predecessors: this is the filial devotion of carrying on their purposes and undertakings. Our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝之興有六以建不世之大功我
皇上之度越前代有五以隆萬世之大業其功
大則其德厚而澤遠有以衍無窮之緒仁
之昭也其業隆則其氣振而運昌有以延
無疆之休孝之大也於乎創之以仁守之
以孝我
國家之盛當視成周八百之歷而遠過之矣
詩曰君子萬年永錫祚胤敬爲
皇上頌之雖然愚生又有聞焉昔魏徵事唐太
===
宗於晚年有十漸不克終之陳而太宗實
嘉納之蓋人心易荒於逸樂而至治常虞
於盛隆以數者成之而不足以其一壞之
而有餘我
皇上總攬
乾剛裁決萬幾政權未甞一日下移固無不克
終之漸而愚生私憂過計有不能忘情於
聖明之世者執事儻與其進尚能有言爲
聖天子陳之
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝之興有六，以建不世之大功；我皇上之度越前代有五，以隆萬世之大業。其功大，則其德厚而澤遠，有以衍無窮之緒，仁之昭也；其業隆，則其氣振而運昌，有以延無疆之休，孝之大也。於乎！創之以仁，守之以孝，我國家之盛，當視成周八百之歷而遠過之矣。《詩》曰：「君子萬年，永錫祚胤。」敬爲皇上頌之。
雖然，愚生又有聞焉：昔魏徵事唐太宗，於晚年有十漸不克終之陳，而太宗實嘉納之。蓋人心易荒於逸樂，而至治常虞於盛隆；以數者成之而不足，以其一壞之而有餘。我皇上總攬乾剛，裁決萬幾，政權未甞一日下移，固無不克終之漸。而愚生私憂過計，有不能忘情於聖明之世者。執事儻與其進，尚能有言爲聖天子陳之。
translation_en:
…The rise of Taizu, the Gao Emperor, had six distinguishing features, through which he established achievements unequalled in any age; our present Emperor surpasses previous dynasties in five respects, through which he advances the great enterprise of ten thousand generations. His achievements are great, his virtue abundant, and his beneficence far-reaching, providing the means to perpetuate an inexhaustible legacy: this manifests benevolence. His enterprise flourishes, his vital force is vigorous, and his fortunes prosper, providing the means to prolong boundless blessings: this is the greatness of filial piety. Ah! Founded through benevolence and preserved through filial piety, the flourishing of our dynasty should far surpass even the eight-hundred-year span of Zhou. The Book of Odes says: “May the lord live ten thousand years, and forever be blessed with descendants.” I respectfully offer these words in praise of His Majesty.
Nevertheless, this humble student has also heard the following. When Wei Zheng served Emperor Taizong of Tang, in the latter’s later years he submitted an account of ten gradual failings that threatened his ability to carry his good rule through to the end. Taizong indeed commended and accepted it. For the human heart readily grows neglectful amid ease and pleasure, and even the finest government must constantly guard against danger at the height of its prosperity. Several factors together may be insufficient to bring success, while just one may be more than enough to bring ruin. Our Emperor holds firmly the vigorous authority of Heaven and personally decides the myriad affairs of government. Political authority has never passed into subordinate hands for even a single day; there is certainly no gradual failing that threatens his ability to carry his rule through to the end. Yet this humble student, in his private anxieties and perhaps excessive forethought, cannot cease caring about this age of sagely and enlightened rule. If you, honored examiners, should approve his advancement, he can yet offer words for presentation to the sagely Son of Heaven.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第二問
譚維鼎
考試官敎諭劉批議論根據
考試官敎授林批條荅
執事之問以禮不以刑愚生則曰用禮者
當如用刑焉用禮如刑則禮重禮重則民
心革安處善欲驅之而為惡也不可得已
何哉善固民之心也重之以禮者非强其
所無也特敎之無素則發動之機塞而無
===
以觸其懿美之衷於是乎有物而不化者
苟浸漬之旣乆而又時執其機以振作之
如今之用刑焉民固有勃然興起而日趨
於善者三代敎化之隆率此而已舍此而
徒以法度把縛拘拘於簿書訟獄之間吾
見上繁於刑民敢於悍將有刑之所不能
禁者以此為治終苟而已於乎此禮樂之
所以當興而刑法之不足恃歟請因問而
詳言之天高地下萬物散殊而禮制行矣
punctuated:
第二問
譚維鼎
考試官敎諭劉批：「議論根據。」
考試官敎授林批：「條荅。」
執事之問，以禮不以刑，愚生則曰：用禮者當如用刑焉。用禮如刑，則禮重；禮重，則民心革，安處善，欲驅之而為惡也不可得已。何哉？善固民之心也，重之以禮者，非强其所無也。特敎之無素，則發動之機塞，而無以觸其懿美之衷，於是乎有物而不化者。苟浸漬之旣乆，而又時執其機以振作之，如今之用刑焉，民固有勃然興起而日趨於善者。三代敎化之隆，率此而已。舍此而徒以法度把縛，拘拘於簿書訟獄之間，吾見上繁於刑，民敢於悍，將有刑之所不能禁者。以此為治，終苟而已。於乎！此禮樂之所以當興，而刑法之不足恃歟！請因問而詳言之。天高地下，萬物散殊，而禮制行矣。
translation_en:
Second Policy Question
Tan Weiding
Examiner Liu, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: “The argument is well grounded.”
Examiner Lin, Instructor (jiaoshou), comments: “Answers point by point.”

Your question concerns governing through ritual rather than punishment. This humble student would say that those who employ ritual should do so as they employ punishment. If ritual is employed like punishment, it will carry weight. When ritual carries weight, the people’s hearts will change, and they will rest content in goodness: even if one wished to drive them into wrongdoing, one could not do so. Why? Goodness is inherent in the people’s hearts. Giving it weight through ritual does not force upon them something they do not possess. It is only that, when instruction has not been sustained, the impulse that would set their goodness in motion is blocked, and there is no means of touching the beauty within their hearts. Thus they possess this substance yet remain untransformed [?]. If they have long been steeped in instruction, and one also regularly seizes the opportunity to rouse them, just as punishment is employed today, the people will surely rise vigorously to the occasion and advance daily toward goodness. The flourishing moral instruction of the Three Dynasties followed precisely this course.

If one abandons this and merely binds people with laws and regulations, preoccupied with registers, documents, litigation, and criminal cases, I foresee those above multiplying punishments while the people grow brazen in their defiance. There will then be things that punishment cannot prevent. Government conducted in this way will ultimately be nothing more than expediency. Alas! Is this not why rites and music must be promoted, and penal law cannot be relied upon? Allow me to elaborate in response to your question. Heaven is high and earth is low; the myriad things are dispersed and differentiated, and the ordering of ritual takes effect.…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
流而不息合同而化而樂興焉古先聖王
所以繼天立極垂世立教者莫大於是故
其精神心術之蘊寓於三千三百之儀冠
婚喪祭朝聘鄉射之禮行於君臣父子兄
弟夫婦朋友之間者不過庸言庸行而已
是故形而下也不離於飲食器服之用形
而上也則極於無聲無臭之微由唐虞以
及三代罔不由是損益故當是時教化休
明治隆俗美雖有刑罰無所用之下至亡
===
秦焚滅典籍禮樂崩頹遂使後世言治率
多苟簡在上者畏於檢束或擇令易行或
謙讓未遑既無以脩復古昔節文度數之
詳與夫道德性命之體在下者苟隨時好
或綿蕞雜就或廢罷儀禮亦無以建立萬
世之長策而舉
明主於三代之隆然則刻期簿書而獄訟繁興
穿鑿於俗吏之苟且詐偽萌生而質朴日
消泛濫於刑罰之無極又烏怪乎王吉之
punctuated:
流而不息，合同而化，而樂興焉。古先聖王所以繼天立極、垂世立教者，莫大於是。故其精神心術之蘊，寓於三千三百之儀；冠婚喪祭、朝聘鄉射之禮，行於君臣父子兄弟夫婦朋友之間者，不過庸言庸行而已。是故形而下也，不離於飲食器服之用；形而上也，則極於無聲無臭之微。由唐虞以及三代，罔不由是損益。故當是時，教化休明，治隆俗美，雖有刑罰，無所用之。
下至亡秦，焚滅典籍，禮樂崩頹，遂使後世言治率多苟簡。在上者畏於檢束，或擇令易行，或謙讓未遑，既無以脩復古昔節文度數之詳，與夫道德性命之體；在下者苟隨時好，或綿蕞雜就，或廢罷儀禮，亦無以建立萬世之長策，而舉明主於三代之隆。然則刻期簿書，而獄訟繁興，穿鑿於俗吏之苟且；詐偽萌生，而質朴日消，泛濫於刑罰之無極，又烏怪乎王吉之
translation_en:
…flowing without cease, uniting in harmony and bringing about transformation, music thus arises. Nothing was greater than these in enabling the sage kings of antiquity to carry on Heaven’s work, establish the supreme standard, and transmit their teachings to later ages. Thus, the riches of their spiritual vitality and inner cultivation were embodied in the three thousand minor and three hundred major ritual prescriptions. The rites of capping, marriage, mourning, sacrifice, court audiences, diplomatic visits, village gatherings, and archery, practiced among ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brother, husband and wife, and friends, were nothing more than everyday words and deeds. At the level of concrete forms, they never departed from the uses of food, drink, implements, and clothing; at the level beyond form, they reached the utmost subtlety of that which has neither sound nor scent. From Tang and Yu through the Three Dynasties, all made their reductions and additions on this basis. Hence, in those times, moral instruction flourished brilliantly, government prospered, and customs were admirable. Although punishments existed, there was no occasion to use them.
By the time of the doomed Qin dynasty, the canonical writings were burned and destroyed, and rites and music fell into ruin. Consequently, later discussions of government were generally makeshift and superficial. Those above feared restraint: some selected ordinances that were easy to implement [?], while others deferred modestly, claiming they had no time. They were thus unable to restore either the detailed ceremonial forms and regulations of antiquity or their underlying substance in the Way, virtue, human nature, and Heaven’s mandate. Those below merely followed current tastes: some improvised a patchwork of ceremonies, while others abolished ritual observances. They too could neither establish a lasting plan for all ages nor raise an enlightened ruler to the flourishing heights of the Three Dynasties. Thus, deadlines were imposed for documentary business, while litigation multiplied amid the contrived expedients of petty officials [?].
