Deceit and falsehood sprang up, while simplicity and sincerity dwindled daily, and punishments proliferated without limit. How, then, could one be surprised at Wang Ji’s …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
抗疏乎於乎孫昌胤造朝告卿士以子冠
篤古之士也鄭京兆乃哂其無預我事而
曳笏却立程伊川主司馬文正之喪而品
節周詳守禮大儒也蘇東坡乃譏其父在
不宜學禮習俗之移人乃賢者不免矣况
其下乎執事謂古禮之難復似也然禮終
不可復乎書曰天秩有禮自我五禮有庸
哉禮者上下之紀天地之經緯民之所以
生也道德仁義非禮不成教訓正俗非禮
===
不備分爭辯訟非禮不决君臣上下父子
兄弟非禮不定宦學事師非禮不親班朝
治軍蒞官行法非禮威嚴不行禱祠祭祀
供給鬼神非禮不誠不莊故禮者緣人情
而制之者也禮果不可復乎昔者裴耀卿
守宣州嘗行之一郡矣白華華黍南陔由
庚歌於堂所以明孝子養親萬物遂性之
道也而致宣州之民□□者踴躍聽者感泣
仁孝慈愛之心勃如□□詠歌之下者何哉
punctuated: 抗疏乎？於乎！孫昌胤造朝，告卿士以子冠，篤古之士也。鄭京兆乃哂其無預我事，而曳笏却立。程伊川主司馬文正之喪，而品節周詳，守禮大儒也。蘇東坡乃譏其父在，不宜學禮。習俗之移人，乃賢者不免矣，况其下乎？執事謂古禮之難復，似也。然禮終不可復乎？《書》曰：「天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！」禮者，上下之紀，天地之經緯，民之所以生也。道德仁義，非禮不成；教訓正俗，非禮不備；分爭辯訟，非禮不决；君臣上下、父子兄弟，非禮不定；宦學事師，非禮不親；班朝治軍、蒞官行法，非禮威嚴不行；禱祠祭祀、供給鬼神，非禮不誠不莊。故禮者，緣人情而制之者也。禮果不可復乎？昔者裴耀卿守宣州，嘗行之一郡矣。《白華》《華黍》《南陔》《由庚》歌於堂，所以明孝子養親、萬物遂性之道也。而致宣州之民□□者踴躍，聽者感泣，仁孝慈愛之心勃如□□詠歌之下者，何哉？
translation_en:
…submission of a remonstrance? Alas! Sun Changyin came to court and informed the high officials that his son was to undergo the capping ceremony: he was a man deeply devoted to antiquity. Yet Zheng, the Metropolitan Prefect, scoffed, saying, “This has nothing to do with me,” and withdrew to stand aside, trailing his audience tablet. Cheng Yichuan presided over the funeral of Sima Wenzheng, arranging its ceremonial details with meticulous care: he was a great Confucian scholar who upheld ritual propriety. Yet Su Dongpo mocked him, saying that, while his own father was still alive, he ought not to be learning funeral rites. Even worthy men cannot escape the influence of prevailing customs—how much less those below them! Your assertion that ancient rites are difficult to restore seems reasonable. But can ritual truly never be restored?

The Book of Documents says: “Heaven has established an ordered system of rites; let the five rites be put into practice by us!” Ritual is the ordering principle of those above and below, the warp and weft of Heaven and Earth, and that by which the people live. The Way, virtue, benevolence, and righteousness cannot be perfected without ritual; instruction and the rectification of customs cannot be complete without ritual; disputes and lawsuits cannot be settled without ritual; the relationships between ruler and minister, superior and inferior, father and son, and elder and younger brother cannot be established without ritual. In official training and service to teachers, intimacy cannot be achieved without ritual. In arranging ranks at court, governing armies, holding office, and enforcing laws, authority and dignity cannot prevail without ritual. In prayers, offerings, sacrifices, and service to spirits, there can be neither sincerity nor reverence without ritual. Thus rites are institutions fashioned in accordance with human feelings. Can ritual really not be restored?

In former times, when Pei Yaoqing served as Prefect of Xuanzhou, he put these rites into practice throughout that prefecture. “White Flowers” (Baihua), “Luxuriant Millet” (Huashu), “The Southern Terrace” (Nangai), and “Following the Course” (Yougeng) were sung in the hall to make clear the principles by which filial sons nourish their parents and all things fulfill their natures. This caused those among the people of Xuanzhou who [two illegible characters; ?] to leap with joy, while those listening were moved to tears. Why did feelings of benevolence, filial devotion, kindness, and love surge forth [two illegible characters; ?] amid the chanting and singing?

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蓋禮樂之感於外而精神之發於中也禮
果不可復乎禮之根於人心也大矣聖人
本因其心而制節之固非強世之物也自
後世禮樂之敎不行天下日流於鄙俗之
敝故說者慨夫子之作春秋不存禮樂之
制博士顏復至有虛名失實之歎豈非探
本之論乎古人有見於此斷斷乎以禮之
必可為國民之不可無禮故裴耀卿之在
唐玄宗朝也則請乞令天下大州每年各
===
備禮儀准令式行禮稍加勸奬以示風俗
使民習禮聞樂上奉君親下安鄉族自然
和氣浹洽化理清平而不任刑法矣胡銓
之在宋寧宗朝也則請以司馬光冠婚喪
祭之儀乞詔禮官討論擇其要而易行者
布之民間使耆儒宿學轉相傳授而武夫
悍將亦令通行欲使民知禮則知尊君親
上奉先思孝而天下不足治矣若夫五禮
新儀下頒州郡有司慮其推行之不及也
punctuated: 蓋禮樂之感於外，而精神之發於中也。禮果不可復乎？禮之根於人心也大矣！聖人本因其心而制節之，固非強世之物也。自後世禮樂之敎不行，天下日流於鄙俗之敝。故說者慨夫子之作《春秋》不存禮樂之制，博士顏復至有虛名失實之歎，豈非探本之論乎？古人有見於此，斷斷乎以禮之必可為國、民之不可無禮。故裴耀卿之在唐玄宗朝也，則請乞令天下大州每年各備禮儀，准令式行禮，稍加勸奬，以示風俗，使民習禮聞樂，上奉君親，下安鄉族，自然和氣浹洽，化理清平，而不任刑法矣。胡銓之在宋寧宗朝也，則請以司馬光冠婚喪祭之儀，乞詔禮官討論，擇其要而易行者，布之民間，使耆儒宿學轉相傳授，而武夫悍將亦令通行。欲使民知禮，則知尊君親上，奉先思孝，而天下不足治矣。若夫《五禮新儀》下頒州郡，有司慮其推行之不及也，
translation_en:
This was because rites and music moved them from without, while their spirit responded from within. Can ritual truly not be restored? How deeply ritual is rooted in the human heart! The sages originally followed people's hearts and established measured forms for their expression; ritual was certainly not something imposed forcibly upon the world. In later ages, once instruction in rites and music ceased to be practiced, the world slipped daily into the evils of vulgar customs. Thus commentators lamented that when the Master composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he did not preserve the institutions of rites and music. The Erudite Yan Fu went so far as to lament that empty names remained while their substance was lost. Was this not an argument that sought the root of the matter?

The ancients understood this and were firmly convinced that ritual could indeed be used to govern a state, and that the people could not do without it. Thus, during the reign of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang, Pei Yaoqing petitioned that every large prefecture throughout the realm annually prepare the requisite ceremonies and perform the rites according to the prescribed regulations, with some encouragement and rewards to guide popular customs. This would enable the people to practice ritual and hear music, serving their ruler and parents above and bringing peace to their communities and clans below. A spirit of harmony would naturally pervade society, moral transformation and governance would be orderly and peaceful, and there would be no reliance on penal law.

During the reign of Emperor Ningzong of the Song [?], Hu Quan petitioned concerning Sima Guang's ceremonies for capping, marriage, mourning, and sacrifice. He requested an edict directing the ritual officials to deliberate upon them, select what was essential and easy to practice, and disseminate it among the people. Elderly Confucian scholars and seasoned students were to transmit and teach these ceremonies to one another, and even military men and fierce generals were to be ordered to practice them universally. The intention was that, through knowing ritual, the people would learn to honor their ruler and cherish their superiors, serve their ancestors, and aspire to filial devotion; governing the realm would then be no great matter [?]. As for the New Ceremonies of the Five Rites, when it was promulgated to the prefectures, the responsible officials feared that its implementation would not reach far enough …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乃欲諸州鏤板行屬州委敎授縣委有出
身官旦望就學講習新儀監司歲終保明
具奏察其勤弛以爲懲勸此則通判李新
嘗請於徽宗者焉三禮全書王安石妄廢
儀禮而獨存禮記之科致使學者誦虛文
以供應舉甚變亂也儒臣慮三禮之散失
也乃欲就秘書省關借禮書自行招致學
徒類編三禮以興起廢墜垂之永久使士
知實學以爲制作之助此則先儒朱熹嘗
===
請於寧宗者焉夫此四臣者旣能行之而
各言之矣當時若可以復純王之治然乃
俱付之空言而不臻實効其故何哉蓋其
所遇者唐之玄宗宋之徽寧固非議禮作
樂之君此其治之所以不古復而禮之所
以終不行也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝龍飛淮甸以
大德而受
大命驅除夷狄洗污習而回華風創造之初固
punctuated:
乃欲諸州鏤板行屬，州委敎授，縣委有出身官，旦望就學講習新儀，監司歲終保明具奏，察其勤弛以爲懲勸。此則通判李新嘗請於徽宗者焉。三禮全書，王安石妄廢《儀禮》，而獨存《禮記》之科，致使學者誦虛文以供應舉，甚變亂也。儒臣慮三禮之散失也，乃欲就秘書省關借禮書，自行招致學徒，類編三禮，以興起廢墜，垂之永久，使士知實學，以爲制作之助。此則先儒朱熹嘗請於寧宗者焉。
夫此四臣者，旣能行之，而各言之矣。當時若可以復純王之治，然乃俱付之空言，而不臻實効，其故何哉？蓋其所遇者，唐之玄宗、宋之徽寧，固非議禮作樂之君。此其治之所以不古復，而禮之所以終不行也。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，龍飛淮甸，以大德而受大命，驅除夷狄，洗污習而回華風。創造之初，固
translation_en:
…he therefore proposed that the prefectures cut printing blocks and circulate copies throughout their jurisdictions. Prefectures were to assign instructors, and counties officials holding examination degrees, to go to the schools on the first and fifteenth days of the month [?] to expound and study the New Ceremonies. At the end of each year, the surveillance commissioners were to submit certified reports, examining their diligence or negligence as a basis for punishment and encouragement. This was what Li Xin, an assistant prefect, once requested of Emperor Huizong.
As for the complete corpus of the Three Ritual Classics, Wang Anshi recklessly abolished the examination subject on the Ceremonies and Rites (Yili), retaining only that on the Book of Rites (Liji). This caused students to recite empty texts merely to sit the examinations—a grave disruption of the established order. Concerned that the Three Ritual Classics might become scattered and lost, a Confucian official proposed formally borrowing ritual books from the Palace Library, personally recruiting students, and compiling the Three Ritual Classics by subject. This would revive what had fallen into neglect and transmit it for all time, enabling scholars to understand substantive learning and thereby assist in establishing rites and institutions. This was what the earlier Confucian scholar Zhu Xi once requested of Emperor Ningzong.
These four officials were capable of putting such measures into practice, and each articulated his proposals. It seemed possible at the time to restore the government of true sage kings. Yet all their proposals were consigned to empty words and achieved no practical results. Why was this? The rulers they served were Xuanzong of the Tang and Huizong and Ningzong of the Song, who were certainly not sovereigns capable of determining rites and instituting music. This explains why their government failed to recover the ways of antiquity and why the rites ultimately went unpracticed.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao rose like a dragon from the lands along the Huai River. Through his great virtue he received the great Mandate, expelled the alien peoples, swept away corrupt customs, and restored Chinese ways. At the very beginning of his founding endeavor, he indeed…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘗編輯
大明集禮上自虞夏下及唐宋歷代所行儀文
度數爲之因革損益凡吉凶軍賓嘉之禮
條目具備復以冠履車輅儀仗鹵簿字學
樂律諸目附之於後固已經緯天地貫徹
古今垂一世之大典矣
列聖相承恪遵罔斁肆我
皇上誕膺
寶曆議禮考文勵精圖治又皆本諸
===
躬行漸以膏澤其於儀文大禮固嘗申明校正
而增定焉然
朝廷之上品節雖已詳明而遠郡偏州苟且
尚仍其舊以至鄉飲讀法猶屬虛文日用
常行殊無畫一故時方丱角已衣成服恐
冠禮不舉也鄙俗雜亂不識親迎恐婚禮
不備也火焚水溺拘忌陰陽五服之制輕
重未别恐喪禮之不齊也春秋不知當祭
之時祭日不知早晚之節器皿今古之或
punctuated:
嘗編輯《大明集禮》，上自虞夏，下及唐宋，歷代所行儀文度數，爲之因革損益。凡吉凶軍賓嘉之禮，條目具備，復以冠履車輅、儀仗鹵簿、字學樂律諸目附之於後，固已經緯天地，貫徹古今，垂一世之大典矣。列聖相承，恪遵罔斁。肆我皇上誕膺寶曆，議禮考文，勵精圖治，又皆本諸躬行，漸以膏澤。其於儀文大禮，固嘗申明校正而增定焉。
然朝廷之上，品節雖已詳明，而遠郡偏州，苟且尚仍其舊，以至鄉飲讀法，猶屬虛文，日用常行，殊無畫一。故時方丱角，已衣成服，恐冠禮不舉也；鄙俗雜亂，不識親迎，恐婚禮不備也；火焚水溺，拘忌陰陽，五服之制輕重未别，恐喪禮之不齊也；春秋不知當祭之時，祭日不知早晚之節，器皿今古之或
translation_en:
…had compiled the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming (Da Ming jili). Drawing on the ceremonial forms and prescribed measures practiced under successive dynasties, from Yu and Xia down to Tang and Song, he retained or altered, reduced or supplemented them. Its provisions comprehensively covered the rites for auspicious occasions, mourning, military affairs, receiving guests, and celebrations. Sections on caps and footwear, ceremonial carriages, ceremonial insignia and processional escorts, the study of written characters, and musical pitch standards were appended. It thus ordered Heaven and Earth, encompassed antiquity and the present, and bequeathed a great ritual code for the dynasty. Successive sage emperors scrupulously observed it without flagging. Then our present Emperor received the imperial succession, deliberated on rites and examined cultural forms, and devoted his energies to good government. All this was rooted in his personal practice, through which his beneficence permeated the realm. He has indeed clarified, corrected, supplemented, and settled the ceremonial forms and great rites.
Yet although their distinctions and regulations have been clearly elaborated at court, distant prefectures and outlying subprefectures still carelessly follow their old ways. Even the community drinking ceremony and public readings of the laws remain empty formalities, while everyday practices lack uniformity altogether. Thus children still wearing their hair in paired tufts already wear adult clothing: I fear that the capping rite is not performed. Vulgar customs are confused, and people do not know the rite in which the groom personally receives his bride: I fear that the marriage rites are incomplete. Bodies are burned or submerged in water; people are constrained by prohibitions associated with yin and yang; and the relative degrees of the five grades of mourning are not distinguished: I fear that mourning rites are not uniformly observed. In spring and autumn, people do not know the proper times for sacrifices; on sacrificial days, they do not know the prescribed hours, early or late; as for ritual vessels, ancient and modern practices may…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
異牲牢生熟之不同恐祭禮之不嚴也若
此者夫豈
上德之未敷下民之不率哉固係牧民者不能
宣揚禮樂有如唐宋四臣舉禮以爲敎抑
亦典禮之制未嘗著爲彜式頒行於下有
如刋定律例諸書使臣工悉行遵守耶是
不可以不講也傳曰功成作樂治定制禮
今六府旣脩三事旣和休貺備至功已成
治已定矣申明禮樂以幸天下正在今日
===
曩者四臣之所請其度數散見於典籍可
考也上有
聖天子學古作極是議禮制度之有君矣下有
大臣宰輔夙夜惟寅明法習禮是稽古考
禮之有臣矣爲今之計誠能具疏於
朝請乞禮官將洪武年間頒降孝慈錄諸司
職掌洪武禮制禮儀定式及永樂中頒降
文公家禮等書逐一叅考凡係天下郡縣
家鄕臣民所當行之禮
punctuated:
異，牲牢生熟之不同，恐祭禮之不嚴也。若此者，夫豈上德之未敷、下民之不率哉？固係牧民者不能宣揚禮樂，有如唐宋四臣舉禮以爲敎；抑亦典禮之制未嘗著爲彜式，頒行於下，有如刋定律例諸書，使臣工悉行遵守耶？是不可以不講也。傳曰：「功成作樂，治定制禮。」今六府旣脩，三事旣和，休貺備至，功已成，治已定矣。申明禮樂以幸天下，正在今日。
曩者四臣之所請，其度數散見於典籍，可考也。上有聖天子，學古作極，是議禮制度之有君矣；下有大臣宰輔，夙夜惟寅，明法習禮，是稽古考禮之有臣矣。爲今之計，誠能具疏於朝，請乞禮官將洪武年間頒降《孝慈錄》《諸司職掌》《洪武禮制》《禮儀定式》及永樂中頒降《文公家禮》等書，逐一叅考，凡係天下郡縣家鄕臣民所當行之禮，
translation_en:
…differ, and sacrificial animals are presented variously raw or cooked: one fears that the sacrificial rites are not rigorously observed. Can such things really be due to the sovereign’s virtue not having spread, or the people below refusing to comply? Certainly they stem from those who govern the people failing to propagate rites and music as the four ministers of the Tang and Song did, using rites to instruct the people. Or is it also because ritual regulations have never been compiled into permanent standards and promulgated below, as the statutes, substatutes, and other books have been edited and established, so that all officials might observe them? This must be examined. The Commentary says: “When achievement is complete, music is composed; when governance is settled, rites are instituted.” Now the six resources are well ordered and the three undertakings are harmonious; auspicious blessings have arrived in full. Achievement is complete and governance is settled. This is precisely the time to clarify rites and music for the benefit of all under Heaven.
The detailed prescriptions requested earlier by the four ministers are scattered through the canonical writings and can be investigated. Above, we have a sage Son of Heaven who studies antiquity and establishes the supreme standard: thus there is a ruler to deliberate on rites and establish institutions. Below, we have high ministers and chief councillors, reverent day and night, versed in laws and practiced in rites: thus there are ministers to investigate antiquity and examine ritual. As a plan for the present, if a memorial could indeed be submitted to the court, requesting that the ritual officials consult, one by one, such books as the Record of Filial Piety and Compassion (Xiaoci lu), the Duties of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang), the Hongwu Ritual System (Hongwu lizhi), and the Established Forms of Ritual and Ceremony (Liyi dingshi), promulgated during the Hongwu reign, together with Master Wen’s Family Rituals (Wengong jiali), promulgated during the Yongle reign, then, concerning all rites that officials and common people throughout the realm’s prefectures, counties, households, and villages ought to perform…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
勅翰林儒臣簡節刪潤著爲一書印行天下使
之如
大明律令諸書一體遵守如四臣之所議者又
於學校村社選人習學演行其至要者尤
乞申命銓曹掄選脩德講禮如裴耀卿四
臣輩俾爲州縣正官學校教職各務以身
爲教專一管領而提督學校憲臣
勅書中亦首以此載入俾其按部提督察其勤
惰以爲勸懲緩驅以令使樂而不駭勸曉
===
===
以文使徐而知義則民心惟善之思思則
辨辨則安安則起居動息造次顛沛莫不
在是則四臣之所言不行於昔而得行於
今矣如此而民不革心治不純王者無是
理也綜核考課之法轉移鼓舞之機是在
聖君賢輔精神心術一運用中耳普天率土向
風承式又何患乎專恃法律以逐逐於簿
書獄訟之繁猥也夫王者牧民設刑以輔
理刑非所先也今律民之書一字有易則
punctuated: 勅翰林儒臣簡節刪潤，著爲一書，印行天下，使之如《大明律令》諸書一體遵守。如四臣之所議者，又於學校村社選人習學演行。其至要者，尤乞申命銓曹，掄選脩德講禮如裴耀卿四臣輩，俾爲州縣正官、學校教職，各務以身爲教，專一管領。而提督學校憲臣勅書中，亦首以此載入，俾其按部提督，察其勤惰，以爲勸懲。緩驅以令，使樂而不駭；勸曉以文，使徐而知義。則民心惟善之思，思則辨，辨則安，安則起居動息、造次顛沛，莫不在是。則四臣之所言，不行於昔而得行於今矣。如此而民不革心、治不純王者，無是理也。綜核考課之法，轉移鼓舞之機，是在聖君賢輔精神心術一運用中耳。普天率土，向風承式，又何患乎專恃法律，以逐逐於簿書獄訟之繁猥也？夫王者牧民，設刑以輔理，刑非所先也。今律民之書，一字有易，則
translation_en:
…order the scholarly officials of the Hanlin Academy to abridge, edit, and polish these materials, compiling them into a single book to be printed and circulated throughout the realm, so that it may be uniformly observed like the Great Ming Code and Ordinances and other such books. Following what the four ministers proposed, people should also be selected in schools and village communities to study and practice these rites. Most essential of all, I further beg that renewed orders be issued to the Ministry of Personnel to select men who cultivate virtue and study ritual, like Pei Yaoqing and his fellow ministers among the four, and appoint them as principal officials of prefectures and counties and as school instructors. Each should strive to teach through personal example and take dedicated charge of this work. This should also be entered as the foremost charge in the imperial letters of instruction to the surveillance officials supervising schools, so that, when touring their jurisdictions and overseeing education, they may examine diligence and negligence and use their findings as grounds for encouragement and punishment. Guide the people gently through commands, so that they are happy rather than alarmed; exhort and instruct them through cultural teaching, so that they gradually come to understand righteousness. Then the people’s hearts will think only of goodness. Reflection leads to discernment, discernment to being settled in goodness; once settled in it, whether rising or resting, moving or still, in haste or adversity, they will never depart from it. Thus what the four ministers advocated, though not implemented in the past, can be implemented today. That the people should then fail to reform their hearts, or government fail to conform entirely to the kingly way, is inconceivable.

The methods of comprehensive scrutiny and assessment of officials, and the means of transforming and inspiring people, depend simply on how the sage ruler and his worthy assistants apply their minds and intentions. When all under Heaven turn toward their influence and follow their example, why worry about relying solely on laws and regulations and being perpetually occupied with the burdensome profusion of registers, documents, criminal cases, and litigation? A true king, in tending his people, establishes punishments to assist good government; punishment is not his first priority. Yet today, if even a single character is changed in the books governing the people by law, then…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
監司置郵而下郡縣士民常禮乃反無書
以稽之本末重輕之不稱從可明矣雖然
此非愚生之言也嘗伏讀政要見我
皇祖之諭群臣有曰治天下之道禮樂二者而
已若通於禮而不通於樂非所以淑人心
而出治道達於樂而不達於禮非所以振
紀綱而立大中必禮樂並行而後治化醇
一或者曰有禮樂不可無政刑朕觀政刑
二者不過輔禮樂為治耳苟為治徒務政
===
刑而遺禮樂在上者雖有威嚴之政必無
和平之風在下者雖存苟免之心終無格
非之誠大抵禮樂者治平之膏粱刑政者
救弊之藥石大哉
王言此固千萬世移風易俗之格言也愚也媿
非賢才其於禮樂豈曰能之願學焉舊矣
敢以是為明問復幸轉而聞之
上
第三問
punctuated:
監司置郵而下郡縣，士民常禮乃反無書以稽之，本末重輕之不稱，從可明矣。雖然，此非愚生之言也。嘗伏讀《政要》，見我皇祖之諭群臣有曰：「治天下之道，禮樂二者而已。若通於禮而不通於樂，非所以淑人心而出治道；達於樂而不達於禮，非所以振紀綱而立大中。必禮樂並行，而後治化醇一。或者曰：『有禮樂，不可無政刑。』朕觀政刑二者，不過輔禮樂為治耳。苟為治徒務政刑而遺禮樂，在上者雖有威嚴之政，必無和平之風；在下者雖存苟免之心，終無格非之誠。大抵禮樂者，治平之膏粱；刑政者，救弊之藥石。」大哉，王言！此固千萬世移風易俗之格言也。愚也媿非賢才，其於禮樂，豈曰能之？願學焉舊矣。敢以是為明問復，幸轉而聞之上。

第三問
translation_en:
…the surveillance commissioners transmit it by postal relay down to the prefectures and counties; yet there is no book by which to ascertain the customary rites of scholars and commoners. The disproportion between root and branch, between what is weighty and what is slight, can thus [?] be clearly seen. Nevertheless, these are not merely the words of this foolish student. I once reverently read the Essentials of Government (Zhengyao) and found that our imperial ancestor had admonished his ministers as follows:

“Rites and music: these two alone constitute the way to govern all under Heaven. To understand rites without understanding music is no way to improve people’s hearts and bring forth good government; to comprehend music without comprehending rites is no way to invigorate the guiding principles of order and establish the great mean. Only when rites and music operate together can the transforming influence of government become pure and unified. Some say, ‘Even with rites and music, administration and punishments cannot be dispensed with.’ In my view, administration and punishments merely assist rites and music in governing. If, in governing, one attends solely to administration and punishments and neglects rites and music, those above may exercise an awe-inspiring severity in government, but there will assuredly be no atmosphere of peace and harmony. Those below may harbor the wish merely to escape punishment, but they will never possess the sincerity needed to rectify wrongdoing. Broadly speaking, rites and music are the rich nourishment of orderly and peaceful rule; punishments and administration are the medicines and lancets that remedy its disorders.”

How great are these royal words! They are indeed a maxim for transforming prevailing practices and changing customs for countless generations. Foolish as I am, I am ashamed to fall short of worthy talent. As for rites and music, how could I claim proficiency? Yet I have long wished to study them. I venture to offer this in reply to your discerning question, and hope that you will convey it to His Majesty.

Third Question

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
高士楠
同考試官教諭王批誠非曲士可以語此
同考試官教諭劉批篇末一段尤見忠義
同考試官教諭徐批出處亦甚難言以仁立論得之
考試官教諭劉批有斷制
考試官教授林批論古人心迹處可備參考
攷論古人於千載之上者有二焉亦曰槩
之以常道之正要之以所遇之時爾道也
者中也仁也當理而無私心之謂也古之
===
君子或懼其無以為訓則守正以植萬世
之大經或懼其無以濟時則旁行以權一
時之大義凡以求適於吾心之安而不拂
乎天理之至公至大而已知乎此則古人
出處去就之大節豈不可攷而區區形迹
之似是而非似非而是者舉無所逃矣執
事發策下詢承學而以古昔聖賢出處去
就為問愚生末學何足知之然嘗考之經
傳而得其槩矣紂敗厥德武王伐之所以
punctuated:
高士楠

同考試官教諭王批：誠非曲士可以語此。
同考試官教諭劉批：篇末一段，尤見忠義。
同考試官教諭徐批：出處亦甚難言，以仁立論，得之。
考試官教諭劉批：有斷制。
考試官教授林批：論古人心迹處，可備參考。

攷論古人於千載之上者有二焉：亦曰槩之以常道之正，要之以所遇之時爾。道也者，中也，仁也，當理而無私心之謂也。古之君子，或懼其無以為訓，則守正以植萬世之大經；或懼其無以濟時，則旁行以權一時之大義。凡以求適於吾心之安，而不拂乎天理之至公至大而已。知乎此，則古人出處去就之大節，豈不可攷？而區區形迹之似是而非、似非而是者，舉無所逃矣。執事發策下詢承學，而以古昔聖賢出處去就為問。愚生末學，何足知之？然嘗考之經傳，而得其槩矣。紂敗厥德，武王伐之，所以
translation_en:
Gao Shinan

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Truly, this is not something that can be discussed with a narrow-minded scholar.
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: The final passage especially reveals loyalty and righteousness.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: Taking office or remaining in retirement is indeed difficult to discuss. Grounding the argument in benevolence gets it right.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Shows decisive judgment.
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: The discussion of the intentions and outward conduct of the ancients may serve as a reference.

There are two considerations in examining and judging the ancients who lived a thousand years before us: to measure them against the rectitude of the constant Way, and to assess them in light of the circumstances they encountered. The Way means centrality and benevolence: acting in accordance with principle, without selfish intentions. Among the gentlemen of antiquity, some feared that their conduct would fail to provide a model, and so upheld rectitude to establish the great enduring norm for all ages. Others feared that they would fail to meet the needs of their times, and so departed from the usual course to weigh what greater righteousness required in a particular situation. All sought only to act in a manner that brought peace to their hearts without contravening the utmost impartiality and greatness of Heaven’s principle. Once this is understood, can we not examine the great questions of integrity involved in the ancients’ taking office or remaining in retirement, withdrawing or accepting appointment? Then none of those mere outward actions that seem right but are wrong, or seem wrong but are right, can escape scrutiny.

You, sir, have issued a policy question, condescending to consult us students, and have asked about the ancient sages’ and worthies’ decisions to take office or remain in retirement, to withdraw or accept appointment. An ignorant student of shallow learning, how could I know enough to address this? Yet I have examined the classics and their commentaries and gained a general understanding. Zhou corrupted his virtue, and King Wu attacked him, thereby …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
順天應人無所私也吾固知夷齊微箕之
心與武王之心一而已矣然夷齊義士也
不可干也於是乎有扣馬之諫首陽遯跡
竟爲餓夫蓋所以標表人極以示萬世之
有君者至矣至若微子抱祭器以歸周箕
子就武王而衍極先儒以爲非臣周矣執
事乃復以是爲疑豈眞然哉夫亦以二子
者眞有以見其大而無所滯於心固不必
以臣周之說爲解也自今觀之紂爲無道
===
天命在周商之哲人已罔知其能吉微子
之去遯於荒野而其歸周也乃在武王定
命之後箕子囚奴安於受辱而其陳範也
由釋於武王戎殷之時考之左傳楚子馮
伯答問與武成釋箕子囚之說可知已其
囚遯也以忠其來歸也以道豈直不臣仇
已哉書曰自靖孔曰三仁愚嘗讀此未嘗
不想二子無我之心與天爲一拘拘曲學
之見烏足以知之是故可以觀仁矣裒平
punctuated: 順天應人，無所私也。吾固知夷齊、微箕之心與武王之心一而已矣。然夷齊，義士也，不可干也。於是乎有扣馬之諫，首陽遯跡，竟爲餓夫，蓋所以標表人極，以示萬世之有君者，至矣。至若微子抱祭器以歸周，箕子就武王而衍極，先儒以爲非臣周矣。執事乃復以是爲疑，豈眞然哉？夫亦以二子者眞有以見其大，而無所滯於心，固不必以臣周之說爲解也。自今觀之，紂爲無道，天命在周，商之哲人已罔知其能吉。微子之去，遯於荒野，而其歸周也，乃在武王定命之後。箕子囚奴，安於受辱，而其陳範也，由釋於武王戎殷之時。考之《左傳》楚子馮伯答問，與《武成》釋箕子囚之說，可知已。其囚遯也以忠，其來歸也以道，豈直不臣仇已哉？《書》曰「自靖」，孔曰「三仁」。愚嘗讀此，未嘗不想二子無我之心，與天爲一，拘拘曲學之見，烏足以知之？是故可以觀仁矣。裒平
translation_en:
…to accord with Heaven and respond to the people, without any selfish motive. I certainly know that the hearts of Boyi and Shuqi, Weizi and Jizi were one with King Wu’s. Yet Boyi and Shuqi were men of righteousness whose integrity could not be violated. Thus they grasped his horse’s reins to remonstrate, withdrew into seclusion on Shouyang, and finally died of starvation. In this way they upheld the highest standard of human conduct as an example to all subjects of rulers for ten thousand generations: theirs was the utmost achievement.

As for Weizi carrying the sacrificial vessels to submit to Zhou, and Jizi approaching King Wu to expound the Supreme Standard, earlier Confucian scholars held that they did not thereby become subjects of Zhou. You, sir, nevertheless raise doubts about this again. Is it really so? These two men truly perceived the greater principles and harbored no impediments in their hearts; there is surely no need to explain their conduct in terms of whether they became subjects of Zhou.

Viewed from our own day, Zhou, the last Shang king, lacked the Way, and Heaven’s Mandate rested with Zhou. The wise men of Shang no longer knew how their dynasty could attain a fortunate outcome. When Weizi departed, he withdrew into the wilderness; his submission to Zhou came only after King Wu had secured the Mandate. Jizi, imprisoned and enslaved, accepted humiliation; his exposition of the Great Plan followed his release when King Wu campaigned against Yin. This can be understood by examining the exchange of questions and answers involving the ruler of Chu and Feng Bo [?] in the Zuo Commentary, together with the account of Jizi’s release from imprisonment in “Successful Completion of the War.”

Their imprisonment and withdrawal sprang from loyalty; their coming over in allegiance accorded with the Way. Could this be merely a matter of refusing to serve an enemy? The Book of Documents speaks of “setting oneself at peace,” and Confucius speaks of “three humane men.” Whenever I read these passages, I cannot help imagining the selfless hearts of these two men, united with Heaven. How could the cramped views of narrow scholarship suffice to understand them? Thus, through their conduct one may discern humaneness.

Ai [?] and Ping…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不綱新莽篡位女主革命唐室陵夷蓋飭
已智以奸天位忠臣之所共憤也吾固知
龔勝之心之於梁公之心一而已矣但龔
勝舊臣也無可為也於是乎有二姓之辯
義不受辱絕食以死薰膏不避甘就燒焚
以立一身之節者至矣若夫仁傑之於武
后乃北面俯首不以為非先儒以為心在
唐室矣執事乃復以是為疑豈真然哉夫
亦以仁傑能觀事察體以成其大而無所
===
累於身固不必以心在唐室之言為解也
自今觀之天未厭唐人心思李武三思輩
之不能有成仁傑豈不知之要亦以宗室
雖危廬陵無恙尚屬可為之時舍此不為
恐大唐社稷不血食矣母子之性孜孜左
右以悟其心卒之引薦諸賢委曲周全以
成其志五龍潛授夾日以飛誠有得於旁
行之知而不流者故其撥亂反正動必以
理未嘗挾數術以濟其私今觀史氏所載
punctuated:
不綱，新莽篡位，女主革命，唐室陵夷，蓋飭已智以奸天位，忠臣之所共憤也。吾固知龔勝之心之於梁公之心，一而已矣。但龔勝舊臣也，無可為也，於是乎有二姓之辯，義不受辱，絕食以死，薰膏不避，甘就燒焚，以立一身之節者至矣。
若夫仁傑之於武后，乃北面俯首，不以為非，先儒以為心在唐室矣。執事乃復以是為疑，豈真然哉？夫亦以仁傑能觀事察體，以成其大，而無所累於身，固不必以心在唐室之言為解也。自今觀之，天未厭唐，人心思李，武三思輩之不能有成，仁傑豈不知之？要亦以宗室雖危，廬陵無恙，尚屬可為之時，舍此不為，恐大唐社稷不血食矣。母子之性，孜孜左右，以悟其心。卒之引薦諸賢，委曲周全，以成其志。五龍潛授，夾日以飛，誠有得於旁行之知而不流者。故其撥亂反正，動必以理，未嘗挾數術以濟其私。今觀史氏所載
translation_en:
…the governing order broke down. Wang Mang of the Xin usurped the throne; a female ruler changed the dynasty, and the house of Tang declined. These were instances of deploying one’s own cleverness [?] to encroach upon Heaven’s throne, deeds that loyal ministers universally resented. I certainly recognize that Gong Sheng’s heart and that of the Duke of Liang were one and the same. But Gong Sheng was a minister of the former dynasty, with no possibility of effective action. Thus he declared his distinction between serving two ruling houses: righteousness forbade him to suffer disgrace, and he starved himself to death. Like fragrant oil that does not evade the flame, he willingly submitted to burning. In establishing his personal integrity, he reached the utmost degree.
As for Renjie’s conduct toward Empress Wu, he faced north and bowed his head as her subject, without considering this wrong. Earlier Confucian scholars held that his heart remained with the house of Tang. Yet you, sir, again raise doubts on this account. Can this really be so? Renjie was able to observe events and discern the overall situation, thereby accomplishing the greater purpose without compromising himself. There is certainly no need to explain his conduct merely by saying that his heart remained with the house of Tang. Looking back from the present, Heaven had not yet rejected Tang, and the people’s hearts longed for the Li house. How could Renjie not have known that Wu Sansi and his fellows could not succeed? The essential point was that, although the imperial clan was in peril, the Prince of Luling remained unharmed, so effective action was still possible. If he let this opportunity pass without acting, he feared that the altars of soil and grain of the great Tang would no longer receive blood sacrifices. Appealing to the natural affection between mother and son, he worked tirelessly at her side to awaken her heart. Eventually he recommended worthy men and, through painstaking accommodation and careful provision, fulfilled his purpose. The five dragons secretly received their charge [?] and flew aloft flanking the sun. He truly possessed the wisdom to pursue an indirect course without being swept astray. Thus, in ending disorder and restoring legitimate rule, his actions invariably accorded with principle; he never relied on calculation and intrigue to advance his private interests. Now, considering what the historians recorded…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其議論可知已其始也以權其成也以正
豈直心在唐已哉呂温謂其蒙恥奮忠以
權大謀世亦謂之知言而大儒朱子感興
詩亦曰向非狄張徒誰辦取日功愚嘗觀
此未嘗不服仁傑沉幾潜運獨立物表區
區匹夫之諒烏足以知之是故可以觀智
矣至若元以夷人入主中國此世道大變
之極也當時儒者許衡乃應聘而爲臣劉
因則屢聘而不起以迹擬之劉信高於許
===
矣然戰則爲王降則爲奴渡江賦之所誇
揚似乎欣幸趙宋之亡者劉之心毋乃未
嘗以元夷爲非者耶然以靜脩之賢甘心
爲之不以爲諱而又不爲之臣其在當時
必有所見果合於至公至大之義未可知
也五胡亂華姚弋仲老羌耳尚言胡人之
不當據有中土正朔相承王景略臨終尤
以勸符堅之不當圖晉許以一世大儒得
君行道將欲以華變夷乃曾無一言以存
punctuated:
其議論可知已。其始也以權，其成也以正，豈直心在唐已哉？呂温謂其蒙恥奮忠，以權大謀，世亦謂之知言。而大儒朱子《感興詩》亦曰：「向非狄張徒，誰辦取日功？」愚嘗觀此，未嘗不服仁傑沉幾潜運，獨立物表，區區匹夫之諒，烏足以知之？是故可以觀智矣。
至若元以夷人入主中國，此世道大變之極也。當時儒者許衡乃應聘而爲臣，劉因則屢聘而不起。以迹擬之，劉信高於許矣。然「戰則爲王，降則爲奴」，《渡江賦》之所誇揚，似乎欣幸趙宋之亡者。劉之心，毋乃未嘗以元夷爲非者耶？然以靜脩之賢，甘心爲之，不以爲諱，而又不爲之臣，其在當時必有所見，果合於至公至大之義，未可知也。五胡亂華，姚弋仲老羌耳，尚言胡人之不當據有中土，正朔相承。王景略臨終，尤以勸符堅之不當圖晉。許以一世大儒，得君行道，將欲以華變夷，乃曾無一言以存
translation_en:
…his arguments make this clear. He began with expedient measures and brought the undertaking to completion through rectitude. Was it merely that his heart lay with the Tang? Lü Wen said that he endured disgrace and exerted his loyalty, using expediency to accomplish a great design; people likewise judged these discerning words. The great Confucian master Zhu Xi also wrote in his Poems Inspired by Reflections: “Had it not been for men like Di and Zhang, who could have accomplished the feat of recovering the sun?” Whenever I have considered this, I have admired Di Renjie’s profound grasp of incipient developments, his unobtrusive maneuvering, and his ability to stand above worldly circumstances. How could the petty fidelity of an ordinary man suffice to comprehend him? Thus, in this one may discern wisdom.
As for the Yuan entering and ruling the Central Kingdom as barbarians, this was an upheaval in the course of the world taken to its utmost extreme. The Confucian scholar Xu Heng accepted an invitation to serve and became their subject, whereas Liu Yin repeatedly declined invitations to take office. Judging by their outward actions, Liu was indeed superior to Xu. Yet “Fight and become a king; surrender and become a slave”—what his Rhapsody on Crossing the River extols seems to express delight at the fall of the Zhao house’s Song dynasty. Could it be that, in his heart, Liu never regarded rule by the Yuan barbarians as wrong? Yet a worthy man such as Jingxiu [Liu Yin] willingly wrote this, without considering it something to avoid, and nevertheless refused to become their subject. He must have had some insight into the circumstances of his time; whether it truly accorded with the most impartial and comprehensive moral principles cannot be known.
When the Five Barbarian Peoples threw China into disorder, Yao Yizhong, merely an old Qiang, still said that barbarians ought not to occupy the central lands and perpetuate their own dynastic succession. At his death, Wang Jinglüe particularly urged Fu Jian not to attack the Jin. Xu Heng, a great Confucian scholar of his age, found a ruler under whom he could put the Way into practice, intending to transform the barbarians through Chinese civilization. Yet he never uttered even a single word to preserve…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宋祚夫豈其非耶毋亦有見於天命所在
混一之勢已成人心去宋值時不競而言
之無補耶其在當時必有所見果合於至
公至大之義亦未可知也此皆死生之際
聖賢所處乃其大者隆中高卧管樂自比
諸葛孔明其人也以昭烈三顧而後出披
裘釣澤隱跡富春嚴子陵其人也光武以
三公召之而不出文起八代之衰道濟天
下之溺乃三上宰相書而求出非唐之韓
===
愈乎旣已委質事隋隋亡去官不仕太宗
下詔徵之而終不出非隋之劉子翼乎之
四子者出處之義先儒甞論之矣然愚以
爲出與不出其中有道存焉不可以形迹
辨者學者必能察於仁智之體不爲世俗
之見以先入之議牿其心然后足以識之
顧其心之所主今皆不復致詳但以子陵
之賢后之論者終不足以明其出處之心
愚則不能無說焉夫子陵豈不欲仕者哉
punctuated:
宋祚，夫豈其非耶？毋亦有見於天命所在，混一之勢已成，人心去宋，值時不競，而言之無補耶？其在當時必有所見，果合於至公至大之義，亦未可知也。此皆死生之際，聖賢所處，乃其大者。
隆中高卧，管樂自比，諸葛孔明其人也，以昭烈三顧而後出。披裘釣澤，隱跡富春，嚴子陵其人也，光武以三公召之而不出。文起八代之衰，道濟天下之溺，乃三上宰相書而求出，非唐之韓愈乎？旣已委質事隋，隋亡，去官不仕，太宗下詔徵之而終不出，非隋之劉子翼乎？之四子者，出處之義，先儒甞論之矣。然愚以爲出與不出，其中有道存焉，不可以形迹辨者。學者必能察於仁智之體，不爲世俗之見，以先入之議牿其心，然后足以識之。顧其心之所主，今皆不復致詳。但以子陵之賢，后之論者終不足以明其出處之心，愚則不能無說焉。夫子陵豈不欲仕者哉？
translation_en:
…the continuation of the Song dynasty. Was he therefore in the wrong? Might he instead have perceived where Heaven’s Mandate lay—that the momentum toward unification had already become irresistible, that the people’s allegiance had turned away from the Song, and that, with the dynasty unable to contend against the circumstances of the time, speaking out would accomplish nothing? He must have had some insight at the time; whether it truly accorded with the principle of utmost impartiality and supreme greatness likewise remains uncertain. These were all matters of life and death, among the weightiest situations that sages and worthies faced.
Dwelling in retirement at Longzhong and comparing himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi: this was Zhuge Kongming. Only after Emperor Zhaolie visited him three times did he come forth to serve. Wearing a fur coat and fishing by the waters, concealing his whereabouts at Fuchun: this was Yan Ziling. Emperor Guangwu summoned him to serve as one of the Three Dukes, yet he did not come forth. Through his writing he reversed the decline of eight dynasties, and through his Way he rescued the world from drowning; yet he submitted letters to the chief councilor three times, seeking to enter service. Was this not Han Yu of the Tang? Having pledged himself to serve the Sui, he left office when the Sui fell and served no more; although Emperor Taizong issued an edict summoning him, he never came forth. Was this not Liu Ziyi of the Sui? Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed the principles governing these four men’s decisions to serve or withdraw. Yet I believe that whether one comes forth or remains in retirement, there is a Way underlying the decision that cannot be discerned from outward conduct. Students must be able to perceive the essential nature of benevolence and wisdom, and must not let conventional views and preconceived judgments constrain their minds; only then can they understand it. As for the guiding purposes within these men’s hearts, I shall not examine them all further here. But worthy as Ziling was, later commentators have ultimately failed to illuminate his intentions in serving or withdrawing, and I cannot refrain from offering an explanation. Was Ziling really someone who had no desire to serve?

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
光武以帝室之胄憤世艱危無以自拔子
陵乃與之周旋於草莽之間以强其志定
大謀卒之光復漢室克成中興之功此其
大者人所不見或者以為隱士出山而成
伊傅之業是矣然以其抗世祖而不屈也
遂謂之薄三公而不為子陵豈薄三公者
哉觀其譏切侯霸之語懷仁抱義純確無
疵苟非養之有素深有得於學力者不能
或者多其高尚之節至與周黨等並觀則
===
非矣何者兇奸掃定其忠攄矣寓釣富春
其道隱矣召之而至其出時矣柔道致理
其幾見矣三公不就其志弘矣士各有志
其詞遜矣此其進退出處從容道義無可
議者而亦無知之者此愚之所謂世俗之
見也噫豈獨子陵哉夫出處去就一道也
道者仁也仁則不私不私則公公則大其
用舍也以時而巳不與焉此孔子之所以
獨與顏淵者也苟有係吝之心存乎□□
punctuated:
光武以帝室之胄，憤世艱危，無以自拔。子陵乃與之周旋於草莽之間，以强其志，定大謀。卒之光復漢室，克成中興之功，此其大者，人所不見。或者以為隱士出山而成伊傅之業，是矣。然以其抗世祖而不屈也，遂謂之薄三公而不為。子陵豈薄三公者哉？觀其譏切侯霸之語，懷仁抱義，純確無疵，苟非養之有素、深有得於學力者不能。或者多其高尚之節，至與周黨等並觀，則非矣。何者？兇奸掃定，其忠攄矣；寓釣富春，其道隱矣；召之而至，其出時矣；柔道致理，其幾見矣；三公不就，其志弘矣；士各有志，其詞遜矣。此其進退出處，從容道義，無可議者，而亦無知之者。此愚之所謂世俗之見也。
噫！豈獨子陵哉？夫出處去就，一道也。道者，仁也。仁則不私，不私則公，公則大。其用舍也以時，而巳不與焉。此孔子之所以獨與顏淵者也。苟有係吝之心存乎□□……
translation_en:
…Guangwu, a descendant of the imperial house, was distressed by the perilous troubles of the age and could find no way out. Ziling then associated with him amid the wilderness, strengthening his resolve and settling his great plans. In the end, Guangwu restored the Han imperial house and accomplished its resurgence. This was Ziling’s great contribution, which others failed to see. Some say that he was a recluse who came down from the mountains and achieved deeds like those of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. This is correct. Yet because he stood firm before Shizu [Guangwu] and would not yield, they consequently say that he disdained the offices of the Three Dukes and refused to serve. Could Ziling really have disdained the Three Dukes? Consider his sharply admonitory words to Hou Ba: he cherished benevolence and upheld righteousness, pure and steadfast, without blemish. Only someone who had long cultivated himself and gained profound understanding through diligent learning could have done this. Some so esteem his lofty integrity that they place him alongside Zhou Dang and others; this is mistaken. Why? With the wicked and treacherous swept away, his loyalty had found expression. Lodging and fishing at Fuchun, he kept his Way concealed. Coming when summoned, he emerged at the proper time. With orderly government achieved through a gentle approach, his discernment of incipient developments became evident. In declining office among the Three Dukes, he showed the breadth of his aspirations. In saying that each scholar had his own aspirations, he spoke modestly. Thus, in advancing or withdrawing, serving or retiring, he acted with ease in accordance with the Way and righteousness. There is nothing to criticize, yet no one understands him. This is what I mean by the views of the common world.
Alas! Is this true only of Ziling? Serving and retiring, departing and accepting office, all follow one Way. The Way is benevolence. Benevolence excludes selfishness; freedom from selfishness brings impartiality; impartiality brings greatness. Whether one is employed or set aside depends on the time, without the self intervening [?]. This is why Confucius gave his approval to Yan Yuan alone. If a mind attached to things and reluctant to let go should remain in □□ [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則行為貪位藏為獨善其有不為貪位獨
善者而亦不自知其所以出處之故是故
知德者鮮矣不明於德而拘於曲學俗士
之說吾見以存祀傳道之名托迹於微子
箕子而忘宗以事讎者靡極也其亦將為
仁乎無仁傑之心藉口於旁行濟時包羞
苟祿以屈節於惡人之朝者靡極也其亦
將為智乎身陷夷戎不顧華夷之辯包藏
二心甘出犬馬之儔又安知非曲說之惑
===
人而俾流禍之接踵也哉愚也草莽之見
固欲竊效於古之君子以自處其身唯執
事進而教之
第四問
蒙詔
同考試官教諭甘批有志之士出言自是不苟
同考試官教諭陳批此子策俱優至於言理處尤詳
考試官教諭劉批學有考究
考試官教授林批知學然更有進步處
punctuated:
則行為貪位，藏為獨善。其有不為貪位、獨善者，而亦不自知其所以出處之故。是故知德者鮮矣。不明於德，而拘於曲學俗士之說，吾見以存祀傳道之名，托迹於微子、箕子，而忘宗以事讎者靡極也。其亦將為仁乎？無仁傑之心，藉口於旁行濟時，包羞苟祿，以屈節於惡人之朝者靡極也。其亦將為智乎？身陷夷戎，不顧華夷之辯，包藏二心，甘出犬馬之儔，又安知非曲說之惑人，而俾流禍之接踵也哉？愚也草莽之見，固欲竊效於古之君子，以自處其身，唯執事進而教之。
第四問
蒙詔
同考試官教諭甘批：有志之士，出言自是不苟。
同考試官教諭陳批：此子策俱優，至於言理處尤詳。
考試官教諭劉批：學有考究。
考試官教授林批：知學，然更有進步處。
translation_en:
…then taking office becomes grasping after position, and withdrawing becomes cultivating one’s own goodness alone. Even among those who do neither, some do not themselves understand their reasons for taking office or remaining in retirement. Thus few understand virtue. Failing to comprehend virtue and constrained by the doctrines of distorted learning and conventional scholars, people invoke the preservation of ancestral sacrifices and the transmission of the Way, claiming to follow Weizi and Jizi, yet forget their ancestral line and serve its enemies: I see no end to such people. Can this, then, count as benevolence? Without Renjie’s heart, they make a pretext of acting indirectly to meet the needs of the times, swallowing shame and clinging to their stipends, compromising their integrity at an evil man’s court: there is no end to such people. Can this, then, count as wisdom? Having fallen among the Yi and Rong, they disregard the distinction between Chinese and barbarians, harbor divided loyalties, and willingly join the ranks of dogs and horses. How can we know that it is not distorted doctrines that delude people and cause calamities to follow one upon another? These are my humble views as a man outside official life. I would indeed seek to emulate the gentlemen of antiquity in conducting myself. I ask only that you, sir, guide me forward with your instruction.
Fourth Question
Meng Zhao
Associate Examiner Gan, Instructor, comments: “A man of aspiration is naturally never careless in what he says.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “This candidate’s policy essays are all excellent; his discussions of principle are especially thorough.”
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “His learning shows careful investigation.”
Examiner Lin, Professor, comments: “He understands how to learn, though there is still room for further progress.”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有見而知之者則必有聞而知之者此固
氣機之潛運而上下之相爲感者尤不可
誣也是故上有隆儒重道之君而後下有
懷道秉德之士上得其人而聖人之道行
天下不患無善治下得其人而聖人之學
傳天下不患無眞儒同時者得於見知之
的後時者亦得上有所考而與聞乎心法
之要焉此其所以上下同德而世教休美
也有以哉執事策試諸生而以當世道統
===
之傳下詢蓋有望於諸生者不淺也夫道
何統乎堯之授舜曰惟精惟一允執厥中
此千聖傳心之要法而道之所由宗也然
聖賢不世出則其出也有時故孟軻氏曰
五百年必有王者興其間必有名世者由
堯舜至於湯五百餘歲若禹臯陶見而知
之若湯聞而知之由湯至於文王五百餘
歲若伊尹萊朱見而知之若文王聞而知
之由文王至於孔子五百餘歲若太公望
punctuated: 有見而知之者，則必有聞而知之者，此固氣機之潛運，而上下之相爲感者，尤不可誣也。是故上有隆儒重道之君，而後下有懷道秉德之士。上得其人，而聖人之道行，天下不患無善治；下得其人，而聖人之學傳，天下不患無眞儒。同時者得於見知之的，後時者亦得上有所考，而與聞乎心法之要焉。此其所以上下同德，而世教休美也，有以哉！執事策試諸生，而以當世道統之傳下詢，蓋有望於諸生者不淺也。夫道何統乎？堯之授舜曰：「惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此千聖傳心之要法，而道之所由宗也。然聖賢不世出，則其出也有時。故孟軻氏曰：「五百年必有王者興，其間必有名世者。」由堯舜至於湯，五百餘歲，若禹、臯陶，見而知之；若湯，聞而知之。由湯至於文王，五百餘歲，若伊尹、萊朱，見而知之；若文王，聞而知之。由文王至於孔子，五百餘歲，若太公望
translation_en:
Where there are those who understand through seeing, there must also be those who understand through hearing. This is indeed the unseen operation of the vital forces; still less can the mutual responsiveness of those above and below be denied. Thus, only when there is a ruler above who exalts Confucian scholars and esteems the Way are there men below who cherish the Way and uphold virtue. When the right person is found above, the Way of the sages prevails, and there need be no fear that the realm will lack good government. When the right person is found below, the learning of the sages is transmitted, and there need be no fear that the realm will lack true Confucian scholars. Contemporaries acquire certain knowledge through seeing; those of later times, too, can seek evidence in the past and come to hear the essentials of the teaching of the mind. There is good reason why those above and below thus share the same virtue, and why moral instruction in the world flourishes! You, honored examiners, have tested us students with a policy question, asking us about the transmission of the succession to the Way in our own age. Surely your expectations of us are considerable.

What, then, constitutes the succession to the Way? In handing down his teaching to Shun, Yao said: “Be discerning, be single-minded, and sincerely hold fast to the mean.” This is the essential method by which all the sages transmitted the teaching of the mind, and the guiding principle of the Way. Yet sages and worthies do not appear in every generation; their emergence has its appointed times. Thus Meng Ke said: “Every five hundred years a true king must arise, and in the interval there must be men renowned in their age.” From Yao and Shun to Tang there were more than five hundred years. Men such as Yu and Gao Yao understood through seeing them; Tang understood through hearing of them. From Tang to King Wen there were more than five hundred years. Men such as Yi Yin and Lai Zhu understood through seeing him; King Wen understood through hearing of him. From King Wen to Confucius there were more than five hundred years. Men such as Taigong Wang…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
散宜生見而知之若孔子聞而知之軻嘗
私淑於孔子之門人蓋與乎見而知之者
矣軻之死不得其傳秦漢以來天下之士
莫知所以為學是以天理不明而人欲熾
正學不傳而異端起彞倫之在人心者雖
不可泯而斯道一脉亦且不絶如綫矣延
至有宋一元協運五星聚奎上之人知所
以教下之人知所以學濂溪周敦頤作著
太極圖通書以示學者刋落繁蕪直究道
===
===
體真有以闡夫陰陽五行之奥而天下之
為中正仁義者得以知其所自來言聖學
之有要而下學者知勝私復禮之可以馴
致於上達明天下之有本而言治者知誠
心端緒之可以舉而措之於天下其所以
上接洙泗千載之統下啓河洛百世之傳
者脉絡分明規模亦宏遠矣由宋迄今適
逢其會胡元運竭
聖人篤生於是我
punctuated: 散宜生見而知之，若孔子聞而知之。軻嘗私淑於孔子之門人，蓋與乎見而知之者矣。軻之死，不得其傳。秦漢以來，天下之士莫知所以為學，是以天理不明而人欲熾，正學不傳而異端起。彞倫之在人心者雖不可泯，而斯道一脉亦且不絶如綫矣。延至有宋，一元協運，五星聚奎，上之人知所以教，下之人知所以學。濂溪周敦頤作，著《太極圖》《通書》以示學者，刋落繁蕪，直究道體，真有以闡夫陰陽五行之奥，而天下之為中正仁義者得以知其所自來。言聖學之有要，而下學者知勝私復禮之可以馴致於上達；明天下之有本，而言治者知誠心端緒之可以舉而措之於天下。其所以上接洙泗千載之統，下啓河洛百世之傳者，脉絡分明，規模亦宏遠矣。由宋迄今，適逢其會，胡元運竭，聖人篤生，於是我
translation_en:
…San Yisheng knew it through seeing him, whereas Confucius knew it through hearing of him. Meng Ke once privately cultivated himself through the teachings of Confucius’s disciples and thus may be counted among those who knew it through seeing. When Meng Ke died, no one received his transmission. From the Qin and Han onward, scholars throughout the realm did not know how to pursue learning. Consequently, heavenly principle was obscured and human desires blazed; orthodox learning went untransmitted and heterodox teachings arose. Although the enduring moral relationships could not be effaced from human hearts, the single line of this Way survived only as a tenuous thread.

This continued until the Song, when the primal force brought the cosmic cycles into harmony and the five planets gathered in the constellation Kui. Those above knew how to teach, and those below knew how to learn. Zhou Dunyi of Lianxi arose and composed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and the Book of Penetration to instruct students. Pruning away tangled profusion, he investigated directly the substance of the Way. He truly elucidated the mysteries of yin and yang and the Five Phases, enabling all under Heaven who practiced centrality, correctness, humaneness, and righteousness to understand their source. He explained that sagely learning has an essential core, so that those engaged in elementary learning knew that overcoming selfishness and returning to ritual propriety could gradually lead them to higher understanding. He made clear that all under Heaven has a foundation, so that those who discussed governance knew that the beginnings of sincerity in the heart could be extended and applied throughout the realm. In thus connecting above with the thousand-year succession of the Zhu and Si rivers—the tradition of Confucius—and opening below the transmission of the He and Luo rivers—the Song masters’ tradition—for a hundred generations, his lines of connection were clear, and his scope was vast and far-reaching.

From the Song down to the present, the fitting conjunction of circumstances arrived: the allotted fortune of the non-Han Yuan was exhausted, and a sage was born richly endowed. Thereupon, our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝龍飛九五作萬世君師之極嘗謂
禮部侍郎曾魯曰帝王之治莫盛於堯舜
觀其授受其要在允執厥中而病儒者講
之雖精未免背馳於行事又曰人君一心
治化之本存於中者無堯舜之心欲施於
治者有堯舜之治決不可得而務存心立
政以成堯舜之事功
成祖文皇帝繼統尤切儆戒其覽學士解縉進
呈大學正心章講義則曰人君誠不可有
===
所好樂一有好樂泥而不返則慾必勝理
若心能靜虛事來則應事去如明鏡止水
自然純是天理朕每朝默坐未嘗不思管
束此心爲切要皇哉
祖宗創業垂統之初即有以啓斯道之眞傳於
上而其所以明世敎淑人心者有以媲美
於唐虞矣
列聖相承躬行體道代有
制作蓋獨步千古而莫之與京洪惟我
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝龍飛九五，作萬世君師之極。嘗謂禮部侍郎曾魯曰：「帝王之治，莫盛於堯舜。觀其授受，其要在允執厥中。」而病儒者講之雖精，未免背馳於行事。又曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，欲施於治者有堯舜之治，決不可得。」而務存心立政，以成堯舜之事功。
成祖文皇帝繼統，尤切儆戒。其覽學士解縉進呈《大學》正心章講義，則曰：「人君誠不可有所好樂。一有好樂，泥而不返，則慾必勝理。若心能靜虛，事來則應，事去如明鏡止水，自然純是天理。朕每朝默坐，未嘗不思管束此心爲切要。」皇哉！祖宗創業垂統之初，即有以啓斯道之眞傳於上，而其所以明世敎、淑人心者，有以媲美於唐虞矣。
列聖相承，躬行體道，代有制作，蓋獨步千古，而莫之與京。洪惟我
translation_en:
…Taizu, the Gao Emperor, ascended like a dragon to the sovereign’s place and established the supreme standard of ruler and teacher for all ages. He once told Zeng Lu, Vice Minister of Rites: “No imperial rule has surpassed that of Yao and Shun. Looking at their transmission and reception of sovereignty, its essential principle lay in faithfully holding fast to the Mean.” Yet he deplored how Confucian scholars, though refined in their exposition of this principle, nevertheless departed from it in practice. He also said: “The ruler’s single mind is the root of government and moral transformation. If what he holds within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes to achieve the government of Yao and Shun in his administration, this is utterly impossible.” He therefore devoted himself to preserving his mind and establishing good government, so as to accomplish deeds like those of Yao and Shun.
Chengzu, the Wen Emperor, succeeded to the imperial line and was especially earnest in vigilance and self-admonition. On reading the exposition of the chapter on rectifying the mind in the Great Learning submitted by Academician Xie Jin, he said: “A ruler truly must not have particular likes and pleasures. Once he has such attachments and becomes mired in them without turning back, desire will inevitably overcome principle. If the mind can remain tranquil and empty, it responds when affairs arise; when they pass, it is like a bright mirror or still water, naturally consisting wholly of heavenly principle. Every morning I sit silently, and never fail to reflect that keeping this mind under control is of the utmost importance.” How august! At the very beginning, when our imperial ancestors founded the enterprise and established the succession, they already brought forth the true transmission of this Way at the summit of government. In illuminating moral teaching in the world and improving people’s minds, they thus rivaled the ages of Yao and Shun.
The successive sage emperors embodied the Way in their own conduct, each reign producing its own institutions and ordinances. They indeed stand unrivaled through the ages, with none their equal. We reverently reflect upon our…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上聰明睿智
文思溫恭
聖學本乎天縱至道得於心傳
御製敬一箴勒石兩京國學及天下府州縣學
以開示心學之全有曰敬者存其心而不
忽之謂一者純乎理而不雜之謂又曰其
敬維何怠荒必除
郊崇恭敬
廟嚴孝思肅於朝廷愼於閒居省躬察咎儆戒
===
無虞曰一維何純乎天理勿參以三勿貳
以二行顧其言終如其始靜思無欲日新
不已於乎大哉
王言一哉
王心揆之精一執中之訓豈非同條而共貫者
哉執事所謂發前聖之所未發眞猶湯之
於堯文之於湯也已夫以道統之傳
列聖相承後先不墜我
皇上則又默契而光大之如日中天則所以勉
punctuated: 皇上聰明睿智，文思溫恭，聖學本乎天縱，至道得於心傳。御製《敬一箴》，勒石兩京國學及天下府州縣學，以開示心學之全。有曰：「敬者，存其心而不忽之謂；一者，純乎理而不雜之謂。」又曰：「其敬維何？怠荒必除。郊崇恭敬，廟嚴孝思，肅於朝廷，愼於閒居，省躬察咎，儆戒無虞。」曰：「一維何？純乎天理，勿參以三，勿貳以二，行顧其言，終如其始，靜思無欲，日新不已。」於乎！大哉，王言！一哉，王心！揆之精一執中之訓，豈非同條而共貫者哉？執事所謂發前聖之所未發，眞猶湯之於堯、文之於湯也已。夫以道統之傳，列聖相承，後先不墜。我皇上則又默契而光大之，如日中天，則所以勉
translation_en: …His Majesty is discerning and wise, accomplished and thoughtful, gentle and reverent. His sagely learning rests upon gifts bestowed by Heaven, and he has attained the supreme Way through transmission from mind to mind. His imperially composed Admonition on Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi zhen) has been engraved on stone at the National Universities in both capitals and at the prefectural, subprefectural, and county schools throughout the realm, to disclose the full scope of the learning of the mind. It states: “Reverence means preserving one’s mind and never neglecting it; oneness means being wholly in accord with principle, without admixture.” It further states: “What is this reverence? Indolence and negligence must be eliminated. At the suburban sacrifices, exalt respect and reverence; in the ancestral temple, solemnly cherish filial thoughts. Be solemn at court and cautious in private. Examine yourself and scrutinize your faults; remain vigilant even when there is no cause for apprehension.” It states: “What is oneness? Be wholly in accord with Heaven’s principle. Do not complicate it with three or divide it with two. Let your conduct accord with your words, and finish as you began. Reflect quietly, free of desires, and renew yourself daily without cease.” Ah, how great are the sovereign’s words! How single-minded is the sovereign’s heart! Measured against the teaching to be discerning and single-minded and to hold fast to the Mean, do they not belong to the same lineage and share one continuous thread? As you, honored sir, have said, he has brought to light what earlier sages had not yet brought to light—truly like Tang in relation to Yao, or King Wen in relation to Tang. As for the transmission of the succession of the Way, the successive sage emperors have inherited it from one another, never allowing it to lapse. Our emperor, moreover, has inwardly grasped it and made it shine more broadly, like the sun at the zenith. Thus, the means by which he strives…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
勉綱紀以造就乎四方者深矣然漸濡
聖化者乃未甞有得於禹臯伊傅之緒以為名
世之望成見知之盛者豈有之而未見耶
抑尚有待於薰陶之既久而後出耶夫天
理民彝不可泯沒況上有累朝
列聖作人之功今日
皇上躬行之化百七十餘年間儒臣隱逸豈無
造詣誠確神會心得以垂衍斯道之一脉
者乎近世儒臣楊廉獨識此意乃歷考當
===
時諸臣如力行好古進趨有程有若河津
之薛瑄堅忍貧賤進脩不倦有若崇仁之
吳與弼或仕或不仕皆銳志理學而潜心
於聖賢者也端嘿沉靜慕回如愚有若布
衣陳真晟學求自得勿助勿忘有若白沙
陳獻章或著作與不著作皆絶意舉業而
返求於心學者也以至胡居仁之議論的
當根據程朱布政使陳選之講明正學務
實近裏侍郎張元禎之反躬研理侍講納
punctuated: 勉綱紀以造就乎四方者深矣。然漸濡聖化者，乃未甞有得於禹臯伊傅之緒，以為名世之望、成見知之盛者，豈有之而未見耶？抑尚有待於薰陶之既久而後出耶？夫天理民彝不可泯沒，況上有累朝列聖作人之功、今日皇上躬行之化，百七十餘年間，儒臣隱逸豈無造詣誠確、神會心得，以垂衍斯道之一脉者乎？近世儒臣楊廉獨識此意，乃歷考當時諸臣：如力行好古、進趨有程，有若河津之薛瑄；堅忍貧賤、進脩不倦，有若崇仁之吳與弼。或仕或不仕，皆銳志理學而潜心於聖賢者也。端嘿沉靜、慕回如愚，有若布衣陳真晟；學求自得、勿助勿忘，有若白沙陳獻章。或著作與不著作，皆絶意舉業而返求於心學者也。以至胡居仁之議論的當、根據程朱，布政使陳選之講明正學、務實近裏，侍郎張元禎之反躬研理，侍講納
translation_en:
…his diligent ordering of the guiding principles, through which he nurtures talent throughout the realm, has profound significance. Yet among those steeped in the sage’s transforming influence, there have never been men who have grasped the legacy of Yu, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue, become the hope of their age, and brought about a flourishing of sages recognized by their contemporaries. Could such men exist but remain unseen? Or must they emerge only after a longer period of cultivation? Heaven’s principles and the constant moral norms of the people cannot be effaced. Moreover, above us stand the achievements of the successive sage emperors in nurturing men, and today the transforming influence of His Majesty’s personal conduct. Over these more than one hundred and seventy years, could there have been no Confucian officials or recluses whose attainments were sincere and sound, who understood inwardly and grasped in their hearts the means to perpetuate this single line of transmission of the Way?

Among recent Confucian officials, Yang Lian alone discerned this intention and systematically examined the officials of the period. For vigorous practice, love of antiquity, and methodical progress, there was Xue Xuan of Hejin; for steadfast endurance of poverty and humble circumstances, and tireless self-cultivation, there was Wu Yubi of Chongren. Whether they served in office or did not, all resolutely devoted themselves to the Learning of Principle and immersed themselves in the teachings of the sages and worthies. For dignified silence and profound tranquility, admiring Yan Hui’s seeming foolishness, there was the commoner Chen Zhensheng; for seeking personal understanding through learning, neither forcing its growth nor neglecting it, there was Chen Xianzhang of Baisha. Whether they produced writings or did not, all abandoned examination studies and turned inward to pursue the learning of the mind. Further examples include Hu Juren, whose judgments were precise and sound, grounded in the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi; Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xuan, who elucidated orthodox learning and devoted himself to substantial, inward cultivation; Vice Minister Zhang Yuanzhen, who examined himself and investigated principle; and Expositor-in-waiting Na…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忠聞望輝映於後先也羅倫之氣節奇偉
任道甚力布政使周瑛之每事檢心學求
自得郎中莊㫤之博學大志溫醇和易互
相為羽翼也以至急流引退究心理學則
有重內輕外篤信朱子如章懋飭躬勵行
深明易理如蔡清者焉遭時星變抗疏直
言則有卓然自立如張吉篤志聖賢如鄒
智名並四諫竒氣疎節如黃仲昭者焉凡
一十五人撮其行實各為編次名之曰
===
皇明理學名臣言行錄其意蓋亦慮夫理學之
失傳而所以扶持世道於不廢者就中論
之如薛瑄之學貴踐履性與天通陳獻章
之主一養心造詣充裕以至吳與弼之分
別聖學俗學是皆奮起乎百世之下倡明
斯道之統以為天下法程雖若不敢遽謂
其俱有見知之實然考其脩身慎行明道
立言由下學以至上達卑不遺於事物高
不淪於空虛粹然一出於正回視游黃諸
punctuated:
忠，聞望輝映於後先也。羅倫之氣節奇偉，任道甚力；布政使周瑛之每事檢心，學求自得；郎中莊㫤之博學大志，溫醇和易：互相為羽翼也。以至急流引退，究心理學，則有重內輕外，篤信朱子如章懋；飭躬勵行，深明易理如蔡清者焉。遭時星變，抗疏直言，則有卓然自立如張吉，篤志聖賢如鄒智，名並四諫、竒氣疎節如黃仲昭者焉。凡一十五人，撮其行實，各為編次，名之曰《皇明理學名臣言行錄》。其意蓋亦慮夫理學之失傳，而所以扶持世道於不廢者。

就中論之，如薛瑄之學貴踐履，性與天通；陳獻章之主一養心，造詣充裕；以至吳與弼之分別聖學俗學：是皆奮起乎百世之下，倡明斯道之統，以為天下法程。雖若不敢遽謂其俱有見知之實，然考其脩身慎行，明道立言，由下學以至上達，卑不遺於事物，高不淪於空虛，粹然一出於正。回視游黃諸
translation_en:
…loyal counsel; their reputations shone across successive generations. Luo Lun possessed extraordinary integrity and devoted himself vigorously to upholding the Way. Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhou Ying examined his mind in every matter and sought understanding through his own learning. Bureau Director Zhuang Chang combined broad learning and lofty aspirations with a gentle, generous, and affable disposition. They lent one another support.

Among those who withdrew from office amid the rushing current of affairs and devoted themselves to investigating the Learning of Principle were Zhang Mao, who valued inner cultivation above external things and firmly trusted Master Zhu, and Cai Qing, who disciplined himself, cultivated his conduct, and deeply understood the principles of the Book of Changes. Among those who responded to celestial anomalies by boldly submitting outspoken memorials were Zhang Ji, who stood resolutely on his own; Zou Zhi, whose aspirations were firmly directed toward the sages and worthies; and Huang Zhongzhao, whose name ranked among the Four Remonstrators and who possessed an extraordinary spirit and a lofty, untrammeled character. Fifteen men in all were included. Accounts of their conduct and deeds were excerpted and arranged individually in a compilation entitled Record of the Words and Deeds of Eminent Ministers of the Learning of Principle in the August Ming. Its purpose was presumably also to guard against the loss of this learning’s transmission and thereby sustain the moral order of the world without letting it lapse.

Considering these men individually, Xue Xuan’s learning prized putting principles into practice, and his nature was in communion with Heaven. Chen Xianzhang nurtured his mind through concentration on unity, attaining a rich and ample understanding. Wu Yubi distinguished the learning of the sages from conventional learning. All these men arose a hundred generations later to proclaim and elucidate the succession of this Way, providing standards for all under Heaven. Although one might hesitate to assert that they all truly possessed the understanding gained through direct acquaintance with sages, an examination of their self-cultivation, care in conduct, elucidation of the Way, and formulation of teachings shows that they proceeded from learning below to understanding above. At the ordinary level they neglected no concrete affairs or things; at the elevated level they did not lapse into emptiness. Their learning issued wholly and purely from what was correct. Looking back by comparison at Masters You, Huang, and the other…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
子親炙程朱之門而其後不能無少謬者
殆為過之暨如羅倫之好善惡惡心事如
青天白日胡居仁之學主忠信排斥異端
章懋之精極義理身體力行莊㫤之慷慨
豪邁樂取人善以及鄒智之雅負竒氣守
義據經皆卓然有以自立以為四方表雖
若不敢盡謂其涵養弘深各造其極然尚
論一時之清風勁節才識忠款志之必為
君子而不為小人學之必為道德而不苟
===
利禄端使海內之士想望風采可仰而不
可及回視陳同父輩之出入於義利王伯
之間而不免以豪傑自逞者其不猶有可
議矣乎於乎道之不明也久矣流俗之難
挽人心之難覺也今世果無其人乎固有
篤於深造而不求人知者蓋偶未之見耳
昔周敦頤肇開宋學之源當時見其政事
精絕者則以為宦業過人見其有山林之
志者則以為襟懷灑落世有知其學者則
punctuated:
子親炙程朱之門而其後不能無少謬者，殆為過之。暨如羅倫之好善惡惡，心事如青天白日；胡居仁之學主忠信，排斥異端；章懋之精極義理，身體力行；莊㫤之慷慨豪邁，樂取人善；以及鄒智之雅負竒氣，守義據經，皆卓然有以自立，以為四方表。雖若不敢盡謂其涵養弘深，各造其極，然尚論一時之清風勁節、才識忠款，志之必為君子而不為小人，學之必為道德而不苟利禄，端使海內之士想望風采，可仰而不可及。回視陳同父輩之出入於義利王伯之間，而不免以豪傑自逞者，其不猶有可議矣乎？
於乎！道之不明也久矣！流俗之難挽，人心之難覺也！今世果無其人乎？固有篤於深造而不求人知者，蓋偶未之見耳。昔周敦頤肇開宋學之源，當時見其政事精絕者，則以為宦業過人；見其有山林之志者，則以為襟懷灑落；世有知其學者，則
translation_en:
…masters who received instruction personally in the schools of Cheng and Zhu, yet later could not avoid some small errors: they probably surpassed them. Then there were Luo Lun, who loved goodness and hated evil, whose thoughts and deeds were as clear as the blue sky and bright sun; Hu Juren, whose learning took loyalty and trustworthiness as its foundation and rejected heterodox teachings; Zhang Mao, who investigated moral principles to their utmost refinement and put them into practice himself; Zhuang Chang, who was spirited and bold, and delighted in adopting the good qualities of others; and Zou Zhi, who had long possessed an exceptional spirit, upheld righteousness, and grounded himself in the Classics. All stood independently and with distinction, serving as exemplars throughout the realm. Although one might hesitate to say that their moral cultivation was in every case broad and deep, or that each attained its highest limit, consider their pure influence and unbending integrity, their ability and discernment, and their loyal sincerity in their own time. They resolved firmly to become gentlemen rather than petty men, and pursued learning for the sake of the Way and virtue, never heedlessly seeking profit and official emoluments. They truly caused scholars throughout the empire to yearn for their noble bearing, which could be admired but scarcely equaled. Looking back at Chen Tongfu and his like, who moved between righteousness and profit, between the ways of true kings and hegemons, and could not avoid vaunting their own heroic prowess, do they not still leave grounds for criticism?
Alas! The Way has long remained obscure! How hard it is to turn back prevailing vulgar habits and awaken people’s hearts! Does the present age truly lack such men? Surely there are those devoted to profound attainment who do not seek recognition from others; it is merely that we happen not to have encountered them. Formerly, when Zhou Dunyi first opened the wellspring of Song learning, those of his contemporaries who saw the exceptional excellence of his administration thought that his official accomplishments surpassed those of others; those who saw his aspiration to retreat among mountains and forests thought him free and untrammeled in spirit. As for those in his day who knew of his learning, they…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
又或疑其出於希夷而未嘗知其有道必
至身沒而后道始章名始定今之論者母
亦類此歟然則論我
朝見知之學而有以得其正傳者詢名責實
固有俟於後之君子也方今
聖天子學有緝熈凡所
講明制作以昭著於天下者無非斯道之實
用公卿而下以及士庶沾濡
聖澤者亦皆丕變維新凡所措之身心以為化
===
民成俗之本者亦皆體道之實功將見上
有善治以行聖人之道致天下於仁義禮
樂之域下有真儒以明聖人之學上接夫
周程張朱道統之傳固當應期而出以徴
柔
一代治教之盛者矣愚何幸身親見之
第五問
魯迪
考試官教諭劉批非泛言者
punctuated:
又或疑其出於希夷，而未嘗知其有道，必至身沒而后道始章，名始定。今之論者，母亦類此歟？然則論我朝見知之學，而有以得其正傳者，詢名責實，固有俟於後之君子也。方今聖天子學有緝熈，凡所講明制作，以昭著於天下者，無非斯道之實用。公卿而下，以及士庶，沾濡聖澤者，亦皆丕變維新。凡所措之身心，以為化民成俗之本者，亦皆體道之實功。將見上有善治，以行聖人之道，致天下於仁義禮樂之域；下有真儒，以明聖人之學，上接夫周程張朱道統之傳，固當應期而出，以徴柔一代治教之盛者矣。愚何幸身親見之！
第五問
魯迪
考試官教諭劉批：非泛言者。
translation_en:
…some also suspected that his learning derived from Xiyi [Chen Tuan], without ever recognizing that he possessed the Way. Only after his death did his Way become manifest and his reputation become settled. Might those who judge today be much the same? Thus, to assess the learning of those in our dynasty who understand the Way through witnessing it, and who have grasped its authentic transmission—to investigate their reputations and demand corresponding substance—we must indeed await the gentlemen of later ages.
At present, our sagely Son of Heaven continually advances in luminous learning. Everything he elucidates and establishes, making it manifest throughout the realm, is a practical application of this Way. From the dukes and ministers down to scholars and commoners, all who are steeped in his sagely beneficence have likewise undergone profound transformation and renewal. Everything they put into practice in their own persons and minds, as the foundation for transforming the people and perfecting customs, is likewise real work in embodying the Way. We shall see good government above putting the sages’ Way into practice and bringing all under Heaven into the realm of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music; below, true Confucians will elucidate the sages’ learning and carry forward the lineage of the Way transmitted by Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi. Surely they will emerge when their time comes, attesting to [?] the flourishing government and instruction of this dynasty. How fortunate I am to witness this in person!
Fifth Policy Question
Lu Di
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “This is no mere talk in generalities.”

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授林批有見
用人者貴於公天下之法而不必盡天下
之情入仕者在於端致用之本而不可計
一身之利蓋人有不可盡之情而法無可
必盡之術吾惟持之以公則情之不得盡
者與我皆無憾也而又何嫌於法耶士有
欲用世之志而法無可倖進之理吾惟俟
之以正則身之難於進者於法固相安也
而又何急於利耶審如此則入仕者不患
===
其居閑之日多而掌銓者亦何憂其積壅
之日深也哉維昔羲后以物命官推擇之
典邈矣無聞爰洎唐虞建官惟百夏商官
倍當其時疇咨明揚考言詢事旁招俊乂
列于庶位上以道求下以行應無常法也
逮于成周大司徒以鄕三物敎萬民攷其
德行道藝而賓之于王曰選士曰俊士曰
造士曰進士論定而後官任官而後爵位
定而後祿擇才取士始爲詳矣然猶未有
punctuated:
考試官敎授林批：有見。

用人者貴於公天下之法，而不必盡天下之情；入仕者在於端致用之本，而不可計一身之利。蓋人有不可盡之情，而法無可必盡之術。吾惟持之以公，則情之不得盡者與我皆無憾也，而又何嫌於法耶？士有欲用世之志，而法無可倖進之理。吾惟俟之以正，則身之難於進者於法固相安也，而又何急於利耶？審如此，則入仕者不患其居閑之日多，而掌銓者亦何憂其積壅之日深也哉！維昔羲后以物命官，推擇之典邈矣無聞。爰洎唐虞，建官惟百，夏商官倍。當其時，疇咨明揚，考言詢事，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。上以道求，下以行應，無常法也。逮于成周，大司徒以鄕三物敎萬民，攷其德行道藝而賓之于王。曰選士，曰俊士，曰造士，曰進士。論定而後官，任官而後爵，位定而後祿，擇才取士始爲詳矣。然猶未有
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Lin, Professor: “Insightful.”

Those who employ men should above all administer the laws of the realm impartially; they need not satisfy every individual’s wishes. Those entering official service must set right the foundations of their usefulness, rather than calculate their personal advantage. People have wishes that cannot all be satisfied, and the law has no means of ensuring that all are fulfilled. If I merely uphold it impartially, then neither those whose wishes remain unfulfilled nor I will have any regrets. What resentment toward the law could there then be? Scholars aspire to serve the world, but the law provides no justification for advancement through undeserved good fortune. If I merely await appointment with rectitude, then even when advancement is difficult, I can remain at peace with the law. Why, then, be impatient for personal advantage? If this is indeed so, those entering service will not worry about spending many days without an appointment; and why should those responsible for personnel selection worry that the backlog grows ever greater?

Long ago, the sovereign Xi named offices after things; the institutions governing recommendation and selection are so remote that nothing is known of them. By the time of Tang and Yu, only a hundred offices were established; under Xia and Shang, their number doubled. In those days, inquiries were made and worthy men publicly recommended; their words were examined and their deeds investigated. Men of outstanding ability were recruited from far and wide and placed in the various offices. Those above sought them according to the Way, and those below responded through their conduct: there were no fixed regulations.

By the Zhou dynasty, the Minister of Education taught the people through the three subjects of local instruction, examined their virtue, conduct, learning, and skills, and presented them to the king as honored guests. They were called ‘selected scholars,’ ‘outstanding scholars,’ ‘accomplished scholars,’ and ‘advanced scholars.’ Only after assessment was settled were they given office; only after appointment to office were they granted rank; and only after their positions were determined were they granted emoluments. The selection of talented men and recruitment of scholars thus began to become detailed. Yet there was still no…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
銓選之法也至漢成帝立常侍曹尚書一
人以主公卿之選立二千石曹尚書一人
以主郡國之選而選法始起光武改常侍
曹爲吏部尚書以總三曹之事而選法專
隸之吏部矣自時厥後魏有九品中正之
法唐有三曹選法宋有國初之選法有元
豐之銓法然皆愈詳愈敝愈敝愈變用中
正者膏梁閥閱坐登仕版而寒素有不得
進之滯循資格者闒茸讒諂立升要路而
===
豪傑有不得伸之歎故崔亮嘗變中正矣
而停解之法賢愚同貫或咎亮之失才魏
玄同張九齡嘗欲停資格矣而選擧之制
迄不可復終莫能遂其志此宋人調停之
說所由起也恭惟我
朝稽古定制設吏部尚書佐以侍郎有郎中
員外郎主事爲之屬有文選司以掌文官
銓選之法蓋古之資格也用之
累朝得人爲治至我
punctuated:
銓選之法也。至漢成帝，立常侍曹尚書一人，以主公卿之選；立二千石曹尚書一人，以主郡國之選，而選法始起。光武改常侍曹爲吏部尚書，以總三曹之事，而選法專隸之吏部矣。自時厥後，魏有九品中正之法，唐有三曹選法，宋有國初之選法，有元豐之銓法。然皆愈詳愈敝，愈敝愈變。用中正者，膏梁閥閱坐登仕版，而寒素有不得進之滯；循資格者，闒茸讒諂立升要路，而豪傑有不得伸之歎。故崔亮嘗變中正矣，而停解之法，賢愚同貫，或咎亮之失才。魏玄同、張九齡嘗欲停資格矣，而選擧之制迄不可復，終莫能遂其志。此宋人調停之說所由起也。
恭惟我朝稽古定制，設吏部尚書，佐以侍郎，有郎中、員外郎、主事爲之屬，有文選司以掌文官銓選之法，蓋古之資格也。用之累朝，得人爲治。至我
translation_en:
…a system for selecting and appointing officials. Under Emperor Cheng of the Han, one Director of the Section for Regular Attendants was established to oversee the selection of the highest ministers, and one Director of the Section for Officials of Two Thousand Bushels to oversee selection for the commanderies and kingdoms. Thus a system of selection began. Emperor Guangwu changed the Section for Regular Attendants into the office of Minister of Personnel, with overall responsibility for the affairs of the three sections, and the selection system became the exclusive responsibility of the Ministry of Personnel. Thereafter, the Wei had the nine-rank system of Rectifiers; the Tang had a selection system administered by three sections; and the Song had both the selection system of its founding period and the appointment system of the Yuanfeng era. Yet the more elaborate these became, the more abuses arose; the more abuses arose, the more they were changed. Under the Rectifier system, men from wealthy and distinguished families entered the official registers without effort, while men of humble background were held back, unable to advance. Under systems governed by seniority and qualifications, the base, incompetent, slanderous, and flattering immediately rose to important posts, while outstanding men lamented their inability to realize their abilities. Thus Cui Liang once changed the Rectifier system, but his “tingjie” system [?] treated the worthy and the foolish alike, and some blamed Liang for failing to recruit talent. Wei Xuantong and Zhang Jiuling once sought to abolish reliance on seniority and qualifications, but the system of selection by recommendation could never be restored, and neither ultimately achieved his aim. This was the origin of the Song proposal to reconcile the two approaches.
We reverently consider how our dynasty consulted antiquity in establishing its institutions. It established a Minister of Personnel, assisted by Vice Ministers, with Bureau Directors, Vice Directors, and Secretaries as subordinate officials, and a Bureau of Civil Appointments to administer the selection and appointment of civil officials. This is essentially the ancient system of seniority and qualifications. Through its use over successive reigns, suitable men have been obtained to carry out government. Coming now to our …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上殫心化理尤愼用人冢宰之官不輕授任
常慮選法爲滯重以
天語丁寧宜乎仕路清通人才彙進矣而執事
猶曰赴部待選動至數千給假家居恒逾
二萬至有白首不得一命幸而得之亦皆
垂老志得之年深歎夫壅滯之弊而欲求
變通之計者何也將謂入仕之源有未清
歟愚觀今
國家入仕之途不過歲貢科舉吏員三者而
===
已外此則有蔭補之胄納粟之例而已然
歲貢科舉定額未增于舊蔭補胥吏資格
不混其常納貲入監非爲常例其視上官
均之所謂四弊曰雜流曰特奏曰資蔭曰
入流者不待去而自無惡在其爲仕源之
不清也將謂冗濫之員未盡去歟考自
皇上臨治以來屢
勑吏部通查天下凡官之事簡可兼及因時添
設者盡從裁革至今停選而又有六察嚴
punctuated: 皇上殫心化理，尤愼用人，冢宰之官不輕授任，常慮選法爲滯，重以天語丁寧，宜乎仕路清通，人才彙進矣。而執事猶曰：「赴部待選，動至數千；給假家居，恒逾二萬。至有白首不得一命，幸而得之，亦皆垂老志得之年。」深歎夫壅滯之弊，而欲求變通之計者，何也？將謂入仕之源有未清歟？愚觀今國家入仕之途，不過歲貢、科舉、吏員三者而已。外此則有蔭補之胄、納粟之例而已。然歲貢、科舉定額未增于舊，蔭補、胥吏資格不混其常，納貲入監非爲常例。其視上官均之所謂四弊，曰雜流，曰特奏，曰資蔭，曰入流者，不待去而自無，惡在其爲仕源之不清也？將謂冗濫之員未盡去歟？考自皇上臨治以來，屢勑吏部通查天下，凡官之事簡可兼及因時添設者，盡從裁革，至今停選，而又有六察嚴
translation_en:
…His Majesty devotes his utmost attention to government and moral transformation and is particularly careful in employing men. He does not lightly entrust anyone with the office of Minister of Personnel. Constantly concerned that the selection procedures cause delays, he has repeatedly issued earnest imperial admonitions. Surely the paths into office should therefore be clear and unobstructed, and talented men should advance in numbers. Yet you still say: “Those who come to the ministry awaiting selection frequently number several thousand; those granted leave to remain at home regularly exceed twenty thousand. Some reach white-haired old age without receiving a single appointment. Even those fortunate enough to obtain one achieve their ambition only when approaching old age.” Why do you lament so deeply the evils of this congestion and seek a means of adapting the system? Would you say that the sources of recruitment into office have not yet been purified?

In my humble view, the state's present routes into office amount to only three: annual tribute students, the civil-service examinations, and clerical service. Beyond these there are merely descendants appointed through hereditary privilege and the provision for appointments through grain contributions. Yet the established quotas for annual tribute students and the examinations have not increased over their former levels; the qualifications governing hereditary privilege and clerical service retain their customary distinctions; and admission to the Directorate of Education through monetary contributions is not a regular practice. As for what Shangguan Jun called the four abuses—miscellaneous recruitment channels, special recommendations to the throne, hereditary privilege, and admission to ranked official service—these are absent of themselves, without needing to be eliminated. Where, then, is the alleged impurity in the sources of recruitment?

Would you say that redundant and excessive posts have not all been eliminated? Looking back over the period since His Majesty began to rule, he has repeatedly commanded the Ministry of Personnel to conduct a comprehensive review throughout the realm. All posts whose duties were light enough to be combined with others, and those added to meet particular circumstances, were to be abolished. Selection for these posts remains suspended to this day. Moreover, the six inspecting authorities [?] strictly…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
糾劾於監臨吏部明考察於朝
覲其視歐陽脩之所謂四色曰年老曰患病曰
貪汙曰不才者已皆汰而不留烏在其爲
冗員之未去也然則變通之法將無用乎
愚嘗思之厥初生民寡鮮大地爲墟爰自
三代養育以迄于今齒類益繁猶皆各奠
攸居未聞有巢棲而穴處者乘除消長之
數天固有自然之妙而非人之所能與也
銓選之法何以異是嘗觀今之需選者科
===
貢率十餘年而得官胥吏十五年而得官
蔭補者半之若進士之選則又速矣循資
之外又有揀選遠方之例家貧親老者得
就此以申其願若不爲壅矣其間歲貢出
身之人容或有皓首膺命之悲蓋其所成
之時則然也固無害其爲選法之通矣又
竊嘗觀之天之生物洪纖巨細各惟其質
遲速榮悴各惟其時夭札乆固各惟其氣
不能强之而使同是雖父母之於子有不
punctuated:
糾劾於監臨，吏部明考察於朝覲。其視歐陽脩之所謂四色，曰年老，曰患病，曰貪汙，曰不才者，已皆汰而不留，烏在其爲冗員之未去也？然則變通之法將無用乎？
愚嘗思之：厥初生民寡鮮，大地爲墟。爰自三代養育，以迄于今，齒類益繁，猶皆各奠攸居，未聞有巢棲而穴處者。乘除消長之數，天固有自然之妙，而非人之所能與也。銓選之法何以異是？嘗觀今之需選者，科貢率十餘年而得官，胥吏十五年而得官，蔭補者半之。若進士之選，則又速矣。循資之外，又有揀選遠方之例，家貧親老者得就此以申其願，若不爲壅矣。其間歲貢出身之人，容或有皓首膺命之悲，蓋其所成之時則然也，固無害其爲選法之通矣。
又竊嘗觀之：天之生物，洪纖巨細，各惟其質；遲速榮悴，各惟其時；夭札乆固，各惟其氣。不能强之而使同，是雖父母之於子，有不
translation_en:
…impeach offenders in the exercise of supervision, while the Ministry of Personnel conducts rigorous evaluations during the court audiences. As for what Ouyang Xiu called the four categories—the aged, the ill, the corrupt, and the incompetent—all have already been weeded out, with none retained. How, then, can it be said that superfluous officials have yet to be removed? Does this mean that measures for adapting existing procedures would serve no purpose?
I have often reflected on this: when humankind first arose, people were few, and the vast earth lay empty. From the nurturing of the people under the Three Dynasties down to the present, the population has grown ever more numerous. Yet everyone still has a settled dwelling; we do not hear of people having to nest in trees or live in caves. In the patterns of increase and decrease, decline and growth, Heaven possesses a spontaneous subtlety in which human beings cannot intervene. How are the procedures for selecting and appointing officials any different? I have observed that, among those now awaiting selection, candidates qualified through examinations or tribute generally obtain office after more than ten years, and clerks after fifteen years; those appointed through hereditary privilege wait half as long. For metropolitan graduates (jinshi), selection is still faster. Besides appointment according to seniority, there is also a provision for selecting men for distant posts. Those whose families are poor and whose parents are aged can use this provision to fulfill their wishes, so the process seems free of obstruction. Among those qualified as annual tribute students, some may indeed suffer the sorrow of receiving an appointment only when their hair has turned white. But this results from the time at which they attained their qualification; it certainly does not impair the effective operation of the selection procedures.
I have also privately observed that, when Heaven brings living things into being, their magnitude or minuteness, their size or smallness, depends on their individual substance; whether they flourish or wither early or late depends on their appointed time; and whether they die prematurely or endure in vigor depends on their vital force. They cannot be compelled to be alike. Even parents, in dealing with their children, have things they cannot…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
能爲之謀者況以天下之欲仕者年有壯
老地有遠近家有貧裕資有深淺各挾其
情以求伸於銓部三尺之法而掌銓者欲
遷常法以曲成則物議未孚欲盡詢察以
從事則聰明有限何以盡使之各得其情
而無失所之歎雖有智者亦不能爲之法
矣故曰冢宰者天官也天之於物惟付之
無心而已無心者至公也故掌銓者必至
公如天進退遲疾一惟其法而毫髮巳私
===
無所容又能揭示奸弊如魯宗道不使吏
升堂如杜衍則虛明之下自得其平有不
能適當其情者乃其所遇之窮於我固未
嘗有心也如此則蘇軾之所謂天下安危
所係而欲變而通之者不足慮於下矣而
其入仕者亦必守正俟命進用則經國爲
民推行所蘊居閑則孝弟力田無求於上
苟年垂衰暮圖報無時則寧受服飾如尹
洙之言若陳襄之與折資差遣李東之與
punctuated: 能爲之謀者。況以天下之欲仕者，年有壯老，地有遠近，家有貧裕，資有深淺，各挾其情，以求伸於銓部三尺之法。而掌銓者欲遷常法以曲成，則物議未孚；欲盡詢察以從事，則聰明有限。何以盡使之各得其情，而無失所之歎？雖有智者，亦不能爲之法矣。故曰：「冢宰者，天官也。」天之於物，惟付之無心而已。無心者，至公也。故掌銓者必至公如天，進退遲疾，一惟其法，而毫髮巳私無所容；又能揭示奸弊，如魯宗道；不使吏升堂，如杜衍。則虛明之下，自得其平。有不能適當其情者，乃其所遇之窮，於我固未嘗有心也。如此，則蘇軾之所謂天下安危所係，而欲變而通之者，不足慮於下矣。而其入仕者，亦必守正俟命，進用則經國爲民，推行所蘊；居閑則孝弟力田，無求於上。苟年垂衰暮，圖報無時，則寧受服飾，如尹洙之言。若陳襄之與折資差遣，李東之與
translation_en:
…things for which they cannot devise a plan. How much more is this so with all those throughout the realm who seek office! Some are young and vigorous, others old; some live far away, others nearby; their families are poor or affluent, and their seniority varies. Each brings his own circumstances, seeking accommodation under the statutory rules of the Ministry of Personnel. If those responsible for appointments wish to alter the standing rules to accommodate particular cases, public opinion is unconvinced; if they wish to investigate every circumstance before acting, their powers of discernment are limited. How can they ensure that everyone’s circumstances are accommodated and that none laments being left without a proper place? Even a wise person could not devise rules to achieve this.

Thus it is said: “The Minister of Personnel is the Official of Heaven.” In dealing with things, Heaven simply leaves them to their course, without personal intention. To have no personal intention is to be utterly impartial. Those responsible for appointments must therefore be as impartial as Heaven. Advancement and dismissal, delay and speed must all follow the rules, leaving no room for the slightest private interest. If they can also expose fraud and abuses, as Lu Zongdao did, and prevent clerks from ascending into the hall, as Du Yan did, then impartiality and clarity will naturally produce equitable treatment. If anyone’s particular circumstances cannot be accommodated, this is a limitation of his lot; on my part, there has certainly been no deliberate intention against him. In this way, what Su Shi described as bearing upon the security or peril of the realm, and therefore wished to reform to make it workable, need cause no anxiety among those below.

Those entering official service must likewise uphold what is right and await their allotted fate. When appointed, they should administer the state for the people and put their accumulated learning into practice; when out of office, they should practise filial piety and fraternal respect, work diligently at farming, and seek nothing from their superiors. If they are approaching decrepit old age and have no time left to repay imperial favour through service, they should prefer to receive robes and insignia, as Yin Zhu proposed. As for Chen Xiang’s granting of assignments at reduced seniority requirements [?], and Li Dong’s granting of…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
監臨物務以利誘人者不以自待其身則
靖恭之下行誼已章雖終身未沾一命而
其所榮者不旣多乎如此則蘇軾之所謂
以莅官之所得爲居閑仰給之資者非所
恤於上矣然而掌銓者何難於用法也昔
在唐宋有墨勅之官有內降之除皆自宮
闈而出倖濫之輩溷我清流此猶可諉曰
衡之未平天子奪之也今
皇上於吏部尚書簡任責成未嘗侵職慎惜名
===
器不輕授予而今之士人猶有囂囂於銓
部者豈所居之者敦尚勤儉甄別清通如
毛玠山濤者未得其人耶抑豈所謂天地
之大人猶有所憾者耶嗚呼吾果至公如
天則人言不恤可也如或未然得無有厪
於位乎而入仕者又何難於守正也古之
時公卿大夫之子弟皆自幼年入學至四
十方仕士脩其學學至而君求之故其行
備業全事理績茂秦漢以降乃異於斯其
punctuated:
