監臨物務，以利誘人者，不以自待其身，則靖恭之下，行誼已章。雖終身未沾一命，而其所榮者不旣多乎？如此，則蘇軾之所謂以莅官之所得爲居閑仰給之資者，非所恤於上矣。
然而掌銓者何難於用法也？昔在唐宋，有墨勅之官，有內降之除，皆自宮闈而出，倖濫之輩溷我清流。此猶可諉曰：「衡之未平，天子奪之也。」今皇上於吏部尚書，簡任責成，未嘗侵職，慎惜名器，不輕授予。而今之士人猶有囂囂於銓部者，豈所居之者敦尚勤儉、甄別清通，如毛玠、山濤者，未得其人耶？抑豈所謂天地之大，人猶有所憾者耶？嗚呼！吾果至公如天，則人言不恤可也；如或未然，得無有厪於位乎？
而入仕者又何難於守正也？古之時，公卿大夫之子弟皆自幼年入學，至四十方仕。士脩其學，學至而君求之，故其行備業全，事理績茂。秦漢以降，乃異於斯，其
translation_en:
…supervising material affairs, using profit to entice people—if a man does not seek such treatment for himself, then through quiet reverence his virtuous conduct will already be manifest. Even if throughout his life he never receives a single official appointment, will he not already have much in which to take pride? In this way, what Su Shi described as using the proceeds of holding office to provide support while out of office need no longer concern those above.
Yet why should those responsible for selecting officials find it difficult to apply the rules? Formerly, under the Tang and Song, there were officials appointed by “ink-written decrees” and appointments issued from within the palace. All came from the palace quarters, and men who gained favor and undeserved advancement sullied our ranks of upright officials. In such cases, one could still offer the excuse: “The scales were not balanced because the Son of Heaven took the decision out of our hands.” Now His Majesty carefully selects and appoints the Minister of Personnel and holds him responsible for results, never encroaching upon his duties. He jealously guards official titles and insignia, never bestowing them lightly. Yet scholars today still clamor against the Ministry of Personnel. Is it because the right men have not been found to occupy its posts—men like Mao Jie and Shan Tao, who prized diligence and frugality and distinguished candidates with integrity and discernment? Or is this what is meant by saying that, vast as Heaven and Earth are, people still find grounds for dissatisfaction? Alas! If I am indeed as utterly impartial as Heaven, I may disregard what people say. But if I am not, ought I not to feel concern about occupying my position [?]?
And why should those entering official service find it difficult to hold to what is right? In antiquity, the sons and younger kinsmen of dukes, ministers, and grandees all entered school in childhood and did not take office until forty. A scholar cultivated his learning; when his learning was mature, the ruler sought him out. Thus his conduct was fully formed and his preparation complete, affairs were well ordered, and his achievements abundant. From the Qin and Han onward, things became different from this; their…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
行敎也不深其取材也務速人才愈多治
功愈壞職此之由今之需選於銓部者胥
吏雜流無容深議其出於科貢入貲者皆
謂之士人我
國家旣養之於庠序董之以憲臣比其有成
則又晉之國學廣其聞見敎之不爲不豫
矣而猶有汲汲於求仕敗德於授官者豈
所敎之者身先孝弟敦尚行實如陽城安
定者未得其人耶抑亦執德不固見義未
===
明脩之於家而壞之於庭耶嗚呼吾知窮
達有命則守正以俟可也如其未然得無
有負於敎乎執事曰變通之法以疏壅滯
愚則曰非壅滯之足患也要在掌銓者之
秉其公執事曰莅官之資以給居閑愚則
曰非資給之足恤也要在入仕者之安於
義然則銓選之法終無可言乎曰入貲之
例以濟時艱不宜於數開田里之賢盡收
科目無庸於辟舉資格以待常品則不亂
punctuated:
行敎也不深，其取材也務速，人才愈多，治功愈壞，職此之由。今之需選於銓部者，胥吏雜流無容深議，其出於科貢、入貲者，皆謂之士人。我國家旣養之於庠序，董之以憲臣，比其有成，則又晉之國學，廣其聞見，敎之不爲不豫矣。而猶有汲汲於求仕、敗德於授官者，豈所敎之者，身先孝弟、敦尚行實，如陽城、安定者，未得其人耶？抑亦執德不固，見義未明，脩之於家而壞之於庭耶？嗚呼！吾知窮達有命，則守正以俟可也。如其未然，得無有負於敎乎？
執事曰：「變通之法，以疏壅滯。」愚則曰：「非壅滯之足患也，要在掌銓者之秉其公。」執事曰：「莅官之資，以給居閑。」愚則曰：「非資給之足恤也，要在入仕者之安於義。」然則銓選之法，終無可言乎？曰：「入貲之例，以濟時艱，不宜於數開；田里之賢，盡收科目，無庸於辟舉；資格以待常品，則不亂
translation_en:
…their instruction is not thorough, and their recruitment of talent seeks speed. The more numerous the men of talent, the worse the achievements of government: this is precisely the cause. Among those now awaiting selection by the Ministry of Personnel, clerks and candidates from miscellaneous channels need not be discussed at length. Those who come through examinations, tribute recommendation, or monetary contributions are all called scholars. Our dynasty has already nurtured them in the schools and placed them under the supervision of surveillance officials. Once they have attained some accomplishment, it further advances them to the Directorate of Education to broaden their knowledge and experience. Their education can hardly be said to lack advance preparation. Yet some still pursue office impatiently and corrupt their virtue upon receiving appointments. Is this because their teachers have not been men like Yang Cheng and Anding, who personally set an example of filial piety and fraternal respect and earnestly valued conduct and substance? Or is it because these scholars hold to virtue insecurely and perceive righteousness unclearly, cultivating themselves at home only to fall into corruption at court? Alas! If I know that adversity and success are allotted by fate, I need only maintain my integrity and wait. If I fail to do so, am I not betraying my education?
You speak of “methods of adapting established practice to relieve the backlog.” I humbly reply: “It is not the backlog that warrants concern; the essential thing is that those responsible for official selection uphold impartiality.” You speak of “the resources obtained in office to provide for periods without appointment.” I humbly reply: “It is not material provision that warrants anxiety; the essential thing is that those entering office rest content in righteousness.” Does this mean, then, that there is ultimately nothing to say about methods of official selection? My answer is: “The provision for monetary contributions serves to relieve the difficulties of the times and should not be opened repeatedly. Worthy men from the countryside are all gathered through the examinations, so there is no need for recruitment by invitation or recommendation. If eligibility and seniority govern the treatment of men of ordinary ability, this will not disrupt…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
序於私親超用以待異才匪為徇法於權
貴獎拔恬退則奔競者自抑崇尚清節則
請謁者羞為此在掌銓者加之意而已若
夫慎簡其人是在吾
君吾相之權衡人物也草茅之言不知忌諱惟
執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 序於私親；超用以待異才，匪為徇法於權貴。獎拔恬退，則奔競者自抑；崇尚清節，則請謁者羞為。此在掌銓者加之意而已。若夫慎簡其人，是在吾君吾相之權衡人物也。草茅之言，不知忌諱，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …the established order for the sake of personal connections and relatives. Exceptional advancement should accommodate extraordinary talent, not bend the rules for the powerful and eminent. If those who are unassuming and refrain from seeking advancement are rewarded and promoted, those who scramble for office will restrain themselves. If purity and integrity are esteemed, those who solicit favors will be ashamed to do so. This requires only that those responsible for official selection give it their attention. As for carefully choosing the people entrusted with this responsibility, that rests upon our sovereign and our chief ministers’ assessment of men. These words from a man of the countryside show no awareness of what ought not to be said. I would be most fortunate if you, sir, would receive me and instruct me.

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
嘉靖十九年秋八月廣東鄉
試錄成康以執事當序諸末
簡乃復申勗多士曰古稱虎
嘯而風冽龍興而致雲世有
明聖之君必有賢良之臣睹
諸虞夏商周可尚也已惟我
===
皇明列聖繼作禮樂聲敎之澤漸
濡浸潤積百有數十餘年今
上紹承鴻緒
文明濬哲道化丕隆溢於四海章
逢之士衣被薰育雖在疏逖
莫不窮經學古磨濯淬礪以
賢良事業自期待易曰聖人
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

嘉靖十九年秋八月，廣東鄉試錄成。康以執事，當序諸末簡，乃復申勗多士曰：古稱虎嘯而風冽，龍興而致雲。世有明聖之君，必有賢良之臣，睹諸虞夏商周，可尚也已。惟我皇明列聖繼作，禮樂聲敎之澤漸濡浸潤，積百有數十餘年。今上紹承鴻緒，文明濬哲，道化丕隆，溢於四海。章逢之士，衣被薰育，雖在疏逖，莫不窮經學古，磨濯淬礪，以賢良事業自期待。《易》曰：「聖人
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In autumn, in the eighth month of the nineteenth year of Jiajing [1540], the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination was completed. I, Kang, having served as an examination official, was charged with composing a postface on its final leaves. I therefore once again exhorted the assembled scholars, saying: The ancients said that when the tiger roars, the wind blows keenly, and when the dragon rises, clouds gather. When the world has an enlightened and sage ruler, it must also have worthy and capable ministers. We see this in the reign of Shun and in the Xia, Shang, and Zhou dynasties: how worthy of esteem!

In our august Ming dynasty, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another. The beneficent influence of ritual, music, and moral instruction has gradually permeated the realm for more than a hundred and several tens of years. His present Majesty has inherited this magnificent succession. Cultured, enlightened, and profoundly wise, he has brought transformation through the Way to great flourishing, extending throughout the Four Seas. Scholars in their learned attire [?], sheltered and nurtured by this influence, even in distant places, all thoroughly investigate the classics and study antiquity, polishing and tempering themselves, aspiring to the accomplishments of worthy and capable men. The Book of Changes says: “The sage …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
久於其道而天下化成其弗
信矣乎今獲選而進之
天子之庭奮庸熙載固其會也康
於多士竊猶有餘懼焉夫文
辭藝也道德實也古之進也
以道德今之進也以辭章爾
多士以辭章進自今觀之固
===
有光明俊偉建功樹業庶幾
豪傑者出乎其間亦豈無脂
韋涊忍與時乾没始慎而終
以悖謬者是非辭章之罪不
善用者之過也夫聖人之道
入乎耳存乎心蘊之爲德行
行之爲事業故六經爲文之
punctuated: 久於其道，而天下化成。」其弗信矣乎？今獲選而進之天子之庭，奮庸熙載，固其會也。康於多士，竊猶有餘懼焉。夫文辭，藝也；道德，實也。古之進也以道德，今之進也以辭章爾。多士以辭章進，自今觀之，固有光明俊偉、建功樹業、庶幾豪傑者出乎其間，亦豈無脂韋涊忍、與時乾没、始慎而終以悖謬者？是非辭章之罪，不善用者之過也。夫聖人之道，入乎耳，存乎心，蘊之爲德行，行之爲事業。故六經爲文之
translation_en: …“endures in his Way, and the world is transformed and brought to perfection.” Can this indeed be doubted? Now that these men have been selected to advance to the Son of Heaven’s court, this is surely their opportunity to exert their abilities and bring their appointed work to fruition. Yet I, Kang, still privately harbor some apprehension concerning these scholars. Literary expression is an art; moral character is the substance. In antiquity, men advanced through moral character; today, they advance through literary composition alone. Among these scholars who advance through literary composition, judging from the present, there will certainly emerge men of integrity and outstanding ability, who establish achievements and undertakings and approach the stature of heroes. Yet will there not also be those who are pliant and shamelessly forbearing, who pursue gain as circumstances permit, and who begin cautiously but end in perversity and error? This is no fault of literary composition, but the fault of those who fail to put it to good use. The Way of the sages enters through the ears and abides in the heart. Stored within, it becomes virtuous conduct; put into practice, it becomes achievement. Thus the Six Classics are, for literary composition, the …

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宗孔孟爲道德之宗皐夔稷
契伊傅周召爲事業之宗諸
士子亦旣明六經誦法孔孟
欲見諸事業矣究其所用或
昧焉康也能無懼乎今夫句
粤之簳鏃礪羽括遇射疏及
遠則有功以之掊箠則與槁
===
樸無擇也湛盧干將之劍氣
凌紫蜺煇奪白日遇斷犀象
蕩爭寇則有功以之刲穫則
與鉛刀無擇也是故器一也
用之於此則善於彼則不善
諸士產於粤猶粤簳神劍也
不務道德而第以辭章爲工
punctuated: 宗，孔孟爲道德之宗，皐夔稷契伊傅周召爲事業之宗。諸士子亦旣明六經，誦法孔孟，欲見諸事業矣。究其所用，或昧焉，康也能無懼乎？今夫句粤之簳，鏃礪羽括，遇射疏及遠則有功，以之掊箠，則與槁樸無擇也。湛盧干將之劍，氣凌紫蜺，煇奪白日，遇斷犀象、蕩爭寇則有功，以之刲穫，則與鉛刀無擇也。是故器一也，用之於此則善，於彼則不善。諸士產於粤，猶粤簳神劍也。不務道德，而第以辭章爲工，
translation_en:
…the fountainhead of literary composition; Kongzi and Mengzi are the fountainhead of morality; Gao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao are the fountainhead of practical achievement. You scholars have already understood the Six Classics, recited and taken as your models Kongzi and Mengzi, and wish to give these teachings expression in practical achievements. Yet when we examine how you put them to use, there may be some uncertainty. Can I, Kang, be without apprehension?

Consider the bamboo shafts of Gouyue: fitted with sharpened arrowheads, feathered, and notched, they prove effective when shooting at distant targets [?]; used for beating and cudgeling, they are no different from dry pieces of wood. The swords Zhanlu and Ganjiang have an aura that rises above the purple rainbow and a radiance that outshines the sun. They prove effective when cleaving rhinoceroses and elephants or sweeping away contending foes [?]; used for cutting crops, they are no different from leaden knives. Thus the implement is the same: put to one use it serves well, but put to another it does not. You scholars born in Yue are like its bamboo shafts and divine swords. If you do not devote yourselves to morality, but merely seek skill in literary composition…

title: 嘉靖十九年廣東鄉試錄
text:
吾懼其進爲槁樸鉛刀也詩
曰靡不有初鮮克有終爾多
士勗哉
河南汝寧府西平縣儒學敎
諭劉康謹序
punctuated:
吾懼其進爲槁樸鉛刀也。《詩》曰：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」爾多士勗哉！
河南汝寧府西平縣儒學敎諭劉康謹序。
translation_en:
…I fear that they will go on to become mere withered wood and leaden blades. The Book of Odes says: “All make a beginning; few can carry through to the end.” You scholars, strive diligently!
This preface is respectfully composed by Liu Kang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Xiping County, Runing Prefecture, Henan.
